name: asmlib (Agner Fog): assembly memcpy, memmove, memset, strlen, strcpy and related replacements
license: GPL-3.0-or-later (commercial licences available on request from the author)
baseline: glibc 2.7/2.8 memcpy and strlen (32-bit and 64-bit builds), plus MSVC 2008, CodeGear, Intel C++ 10.1 and Mac Darwin8 libraries
one_liner: Agner Fog's CPU-dispatched x86 assembly memcpy, memset, strlen and string routines; beat 2008-era glibc, MSVC and Intel CRTs.

name: SRELL
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Header-only ECMAScript regex engine with the std::regex class design; a 2023 competitor shootout timed it far ahead of std::regex.

name: AMD C++ Compiler (AOCC)
license: Proprietary AMD EULA, binary-only (the Spack recipe declares LicenseRef-AMD-Proprietary, redistribute(source=False, binary=False) and needs +license-agreed)
baseline: GCC 11.2 (also compared with LLVM Clang 14.0)
one_liner: AMD's closed-source LLVM/Clang-based C/C++/Fortran compiler for Zen whose binaries ran about 8% faster than GCC 11.2's.

name: BeeCrypt
baseline: Java multiprecision-integer modular exponentiation (JVM 1.2.2 to 1.4.0; the file says only 'Java', presumably java.math.BigInteger)
one_liner: Portable LGPL C crypto library with per-CPU assembler bignum code; 2003-era tables show 2-4.6x faster modexp than Java BigInteger.

name: ujson (µjson)
baseline: nlohmann/json v2.0.3 (as pinned by nativejson-benchmark)
one_liner: Small C++11 UTF-8 JSON DOM library with an re2c scanner; parses about 2x and prints 3.5-4.5x faster than nlohmann/json 2.0.3.

name: Blaze
baseline: Eigen, Intel MKL/BLAS and other C++ linear-algebra libraries: the Blazemark suite's Configfile has switches for BLAS (MKL), Boost uBLAS, Blitz++, GMM++, Armadillo, FLENS, MTL and Eigen. The result pages (Bitbucket Benchmarks wiki) were unreachable, so the comparison set actually published is unconfirmed.
one_liner: Header-only C++14 dense/sparse linear-algebra library with smart expression templates; claims Eigen/MKL-class speed, but no checkable numbers.

name: fastfilter (hexops)
baseline: xor filter
one_liner: Zig binary fuse and xor filters; binary fuse builds 1.7-3.8x faster than xor, with smaller filters and equal lookups.

name: zrep (grep-zg, Zig grep clone)
baseline: GNU grep 3.12 (C); the same table also lists ripgrep 15.1.0
one_liner: Hobby multithreaded AVX2 grep in Zig (zrep); self-reported 9.6x faster than GNU grep 3.12 on one log, near ripgrep.

name: static_maps
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: C++23 consteval FKS perfect-hash unordered_map for compile-time keysets; 1.4-2.9x faster than std::unordered_map in three paper demos.

name: Ed25519 (original amd64-64-24k SUPERCOP/eBATS submission)
baseline: OpenSSL ECDSA (NIST P-256), benchmarked as SUPERCOP/eBATS entry 'ecdonaldp256' (an OpenSSL-based ECDSA wrapper)
one_liner: The original 2011 public-domain Ed25519 amd64 assembly in SUPERCOP. On Westmere it signs about 20x and verifies about 7.6x faster than OpenSSL-based P-256 ECDSA.

name: yxml
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Tiny (6 KB) malloc-free C streaming XML parser; about 2.2-2.4x faster than a stripped-down libxml2 on large dumps.

name: Java HotSpot vs g++ -O3 virtual-call microbenchmark (gist)
baseline: C++ virtual dispatch compiled with g++ 4.0.1 -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -march=pentium4
one_liner: 2009 gist: HotSpot Java 6 runs an alternating two-class virtual-call loop 2.3x faster than 32-bit g++ 4.0.1 -O3.

name: fast-strlen.c (bjourne gist): multi-threaded memchr-based strlen
baseline: libc strlen (labelled 'strlen' in the gist's printed output; libc implementation and version not stated, glibc presumed on Linux)
one_liner: Benchmark-stunt strlen: finds an upper bound by deliberately faulting, then runs memchr on every core; 2.6x over single-threaded libc strlen.

name: xoshiro8x256pp (8-way SIMD xoshiro256++ gist)
baseline: xoshiro256++ (also PCG64)
one_liner: A 15-line C function running eight xoshiro256++ streams in lockstep for compiler auto-vectorization; ~1.9x scalar xoshiro256++, ~3x PCG64.

name: memcpy_threaded / memset_threaded (Carandiru0 mem.h gist)
baseline: MSVC compiler-intrinsic memcpy and memset (the gist declares #pragma intrinsic(memcpy) and #pragma intrinsic(memset), i.e. the compiler/CRT built-ins), single-threaded and also run multithreaded; MSVC version not stated
one_liner: MSVC/Windows header that splits huge memcpy and memset across Intel TBB threads using AVX2 non-temporal loads and stores.

name: Faster CRC32 on Apple M1 (dougallj, PMULL multi-chain)
baseline: zlib crc32() function
one_liner: Single-file C++17 AArch64 CRC-32/CRC-32C kernel with 12 PMULL folding chains; about 2.5x zlib's crc32 on Apple M1.

name: Memset by memcpy doubling (riteme gist: 'Memcpy is faster than memset on Intel i7 12700 with glibc 2.36')
baseline: glibc 2.36 memset()
one_liner: A 20-line memset wrapper that fills huge buffers by memcpy-doubling an 8 MiB block, 2.47x faster than glibc 2.36 memset.

name: LuaJIT vs C and C++ hash-table word count (spion gist)
baseline: C (hand-written chained hash table, gcc -O3) and C++ (std::unordered_map<string,int> with a custom hash, g++ -O3 -std=gnu++0x)
one_liner: 2012 gist where LuaJIT's plain table counts words from a 19-word sentence faster than naive C and std::unordered_map versions.

name: jaq
baseline: jq 1.8.1 (also compared against gojq 0.12.18)
one_liner: Rust reimplementation of the jq language and CLI; faster than jq 1.8.1 on 23 of 30 author filter benchmarks.

name: ropus (Rust port of libopus)
license: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE is the upstream Xiph libopus BSD text plus a 2026 copyright line for the Rust port additions; ropus/Cargo.toml declares BSD-3-Clause)
baseline: libopus 1.5.2 C reference as built by the repo's own harness (harness/build.rs via the cc crate): fixed-point (FIXED_POINT=1 in harness/config.h), no DNN, x86 runtime dispatch limited to SSE/SSE2/SSE4.1 (no AVX2 sources); the Apple M1 Pro rows use upstream AArch64 NEON intrinsics. Not the stock float build most distributions ship.
one_liner: Pure-Rust, bit-exact port of fixed-point libopus 1.5.2; runs at about parity with the C reference, not faster.

name: ttf2woff2-wasm (@0x6b/ttf2woff2-wasm)
baseline: nfroidure/ttf2woff2 v8 (vendored 2013-2015 C++ Brotli encoder and woff2 snapshot; may have run its Emscripten fallback rather than the node-gyp native build)
one_liner: Pure-Rust TTF-to-WOFF2 converter compiled to WebAssembly for Node; 2.0-2.7x faster than the ttf2woff2 npm package at Brotli quality 11.

name: CryptOpt
baseline: GCC 12.1.0 and Clang 15.0.6 compiling Fiat Cryptography's generated C at -O3 -march=native -mtune=native; also hand-optimized assembly (OpenSSL fe-51/fe-64, libsecp256k1 asm, HACL* fe-64)
one_liner: Randomized-search optimizer emitting formally verified x86-64 assembly for finite-field multiply/square; beats GCC 12 and Clang 15 on Fiat C.

name: hwc (Haskell wc)
baseline: GNU coreutils wc (C, single-threaded)
one_liner: Single-threaded Haskell wc (GHC LLVM backend, mmap input) that claims 4-6x over GNU coreutils wc, using ASCII-only word and width rules.

name: evm.zig (evmz, Zig EVM execution engine)
baseline: evmone (v0.23.0, baseline and advanced interpreters) and revm (=43.0.2 raw interpreter, Interpreter::run_plain)
one_liner: Pre-1.0 Zig EVM with tail-call dispatch; first-party runs beat evmone baseline and revm on storage and snailtracer fixtures.

name: fflate
baseline: pako (JavaScript port of zlib); README also says its compressor beats Info-ZIP and often zlib's ratio
one_liner: Pure-JavaScript DEFLATE/gzip/zlib/ZIP codec, up to 25% faster decode and 50% faster encode than pako.

name: liburing_b3sum
baseline: official Rust b3sum (read/mmap based) and cat to /dev/null
one_liner: Demo BLAKE3 file hasher in C/C++ that reads through io_uring and beats Rust b3sum on cold-cache NVMe reads.

name: rsmod-pathfinder
language: Rust (wasm-pack), with AssemblyScript and TypeScript variants benchmarked
baseline: TypeScript implementation of the same rsmod pathfinder on Node.js (the package's own 4.2.5 TypeScript release, commit 1114386, built with tsc); also the package's 5.0.x AssemblyScript WebAssembly release (commit 8ff4033)
one_liner: Rust/wasm port of rsmod's BFS tile pathfinder; about 5.5x faster per path than its earlier TypeScript build on Node.

name: 200sc/bebop (Go)
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Go code generator and runtime for the Bebop binary format; ~3x faster marshal/unmarshal than protobuf-go on a small struct.

name: Bebop
baseline: Protocol Buffers, MessagePack
one_liner: Schema-first binary serializer with C#, TypeScript, Rust and C++ codegen; its C# decoder beat Google.Protobuf and MessagePack 4-9x.

name: KinoWASM (KinoRuntime)
baseline: WAMR iwasm fast interpreter (also compared against wasm3)
one_liner: Embeddable C WebAssembly interpreter (tail-call threaded, register-TOS); first-party CoreMark 2.5x WAMR fast-interp, 1.2x wasm3 on Windows.

name: aadomn/aes (fixsliced constant-time AES in Cortex-M and RV32I assembly)
language: ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V RV32I assembly, with C reference (opt32)
baseline: previous bitsliced and constant-time AES implementations on Cortex-M and RISC-V cited by the TCHES 2021 paper (not shown on the repo page); the repo's own portable C opt32 versions
one_liner: Fixsliced and barrel-shiftrows constant-time AES-128/256 in Cortex-M and RV32I assembly; claims bitsliced AES speed records on 32-bit microcontrollers.

name: Nerdbank.MessagePack
baseline: MessagePack-CSharp
one_liner: NativeAOT-ready .NET MessagePack serializer; ~1.2x faster than MessagePack-CSharp on array-encoded small objects, ~5% slower on maps.

name: wavelet_forest
baseline: SDSL Huffman-shaped wavelet tree (sdsl-lite), uncompressed bitvectors
one_liner: Research code for the SPIRE 2024 wavelet-forest paper: per-block SDSL Huffman wavelet trees instead of one global tree.

name: lsm-tree-go
baseline: BoltDB
one_liner: Small learning-project LSM-tree KV store in Go; beats bbolt only on batched random writes, loses reads and sequential writes.

name: transpose-scale (hpit)
baseline: Intel MKL 2025.1.0 mkl_simatcopy (in-place transpose with scale); cblas_simatcopy from OpenBLAS on ARM
one_liner: Single-file SIMD kernel for in-place square float transpose with scaling; 3-6x faster than MKL mkl_simatcopy at N>=64.

name: asmlib (abiiranathan)
language: Assembly (NASM x86-64 AVX2/BMI2; GNU as AArch64 NEON) with a C header and a portable C/wasm backend
baseline: glibc 2.44 memcpy/memset/memcmp/strlen/memchr/strstr/memmem, malloc/free, snprintf, sscanf and libm
one_liner: Young MIT libc subset in NASM/AVX2 and AArch64 NEON assembly; its arena and malloc heap beat glibc on burst workloads, string routines mostly parity.

name: s7 Scheme
baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (the copy vendored in scriptorium's javascript/duktape; PUC Lua at 1.341 s in the same table is faster than s7)
one_liner: Single-file embeddable Scheme interpreter (s7.c + s7.h); ran recursive fib(34) about 4.5x faster than Duktape 1.2.2 in Scriptorium 2015.

name: abseil (absl::flat_hash_map, Swiss tables)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: SwissTable-based hash map beating std::unordered_map on build, find, churn, and iteration speed.

name: nexus-async-rt / nexus-async-web
baseline: tokio-tungstenite (Tokio-based WebSocket library)
one_liner: Sans-IO, zero-copy async WebSocket/REST library for Tokio; receives small TLS frames 2-3x faster than tokio-tungstenite.

name: Easylogging++
baseline: glog
one_liner: Archived feature-heavy synchronous C++ stream logger; 6-9% faster than glog at 1-10 threads in spdlog's old bench, 4x slower at 100.

name: OpenEXR
baseline: TinyEXR v3 (pure-C11 EXR codec by the TinyEXR author). OpenEXR's leads are against TinyEXR's dependency-free in-tree build (DEFLATE=intree, the freestanding/WASM path) and against TinyEXR's HTJ2K codec; TinyEXR's hosted default (DEFLATE=auto, vendored libdeflate 1.25, the same backend OpenEXR uses) matches or beats OpenEXR on ZIP/ZIPS/PXR24.
one_liner: Reference C/C++ EXR library; faster than TinyEXR's dependency-free build on ZIPS, PXR24 and HTJ2K, not its libdeflate build.

name: OpenImageIO
baseline: ImageMagick 7.1.1 (magick, convert)
one_liner: VFX-industry image I/O and processing library; its oiiotool ran a crop, resize and convolve job 1.3x faster than ImageMagick 7.

name: rust-sort (Rust GNU sort replacement)
baseline: macOS system /usr/bin/sort (Apple's BSD-derived sort shipped with macOS 15.5), labelled 'GNU sort (system)' in the README; benchmark.sh defaults REFERENCE_SORT to the system 'sort' and its own usage text labels /usr/bin/sort as BSD and /usr/local/bin/gsort as GNU. uutils (rust_coreutils) sort is a second column. Current GNU coreutils sort was not measured.
one_liner: Rust `sort` clone (crate gnu-sort) with rayon, mmap and an integer radix path; timed only against the macOS system sort.

name: spair
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript (vanillajs-keyed)
one_liner: Rust/WebAssembly single-page-app framework without a virtual DOM; its 2022 build runs the js-framework-benchmark about 1.5x faster than React 19.2 hooks.

name: ActiveJ
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Java NIO event-loop platform whose HTTP server beat actix-web by ~9% on the-benchmarker's empty GET test.

name: actix-web
baseline: Drogon (C++) in the HttpArena suite; nginx (C) in two other benchmarks, with mixed results
one_liner: Full-featured Rust HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 web framework; in HttpArena it beats Drogon and Cutelyst (C++) but trails nginx and h2o.

name: ActualLab.Rpc (part of ActualLab.Fusion)
baseline: gRPC
one_liner: .NET RPC library (Fusion's transport) that multiplexes calls over one WebSocket; vendor loopback benchmark shows 5-8x grpc-dotnet call throughput.

name: Ada (WHATWG URL parser)
baseline: libcurl URL parser
one_liner: WHATWG-compliant C++20 URL parser used by Node.js; about 7.8x faster than libcurl's URL API on real-world URLs.

name: ada-url/idna
baseline: ICU
one_liner: C++20 IDNA to_ascii/to_unicode (UTS #46) domain-name encoder, about 1.26x faster than ICU.

name: HyperSerializer
baseline: Protocol Buffers (protobuf-net 3.1.26), MessagePack (MessagePack-CSharp 2.4.59)
one_liner: Contract-less .NET binary serializer built on runtime-compiled Span/MemoryMarshal proxies; ~16x faster than protobuf-net and MessagePack-CSharp in its author's benchmark.

name: faster (Rust SIMD iterators)
baseline: scalar Rust iterators
one_liner: Rust iterator-style explicit SIMD (simd_iter/simd_map/simd_reduce) with scalar polyfills; author's 2017-18 runs beat scalar iterators 1.15-8x.

name: fastgron
baseline: gron
one_liner: C++20 simdjson-based CLI that flattens JSON into greppable gron assignments and back; ~50-80x faster than gron.

name: Unformat
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Single-header scanf-style '{}' field extractor for fixed-shape strings; beats std::regex when regex is overkill.

name: KmStrSearch (Windows kernel UTF-8 and UTF-16 substring search)
baseline: Windows kernel CRT strstr and wcsstr (MSVC runtime; not glibc or musl)
one_liner: Windows kernel-mode UTF-8/UTF-16 substring search (last-character SIMD scan plus BMH/SWAR fallback) beating kernel CRT strstr/wcsstr on buffers above 6 KB.

name: jist
baseline: jq
one_liner: Rust CLI that pulls one value by exact key/index path from multi-GB JSON files, far faster than jq.

name: ademakov/bzero
language: Assembly (x86 SSE/AVX, GNU as) with C test harness
baseline: libc memset (bzero_0 in the harness) and the author's trivial and unrolled C versions compiled with gcc -O2
one_liner: Public-domain x86-64 SSE and AVX assembly zero-fill routines that beat 2017-era libc memset on small buffers.

name: Ragel State Machine Compiler
baseline: flex
one_liner: State-machine compiler that generates FSM-based scanners/parsers in 13 host languages; beats flex on one old, unmeasured example.

name: Bitsliced AEGIS-128L / AEGIS-128X2 (constant-time, no-AES-NI platforms)
baseline: OpenSSL AES-GCM / BoringSSL AES-GCM (side-channel-protected/bitsliced builds)
one_liner: Constant-time bitsliced C AEGIS for CPUs without AES instructions; beats bitsliced AES-GCM by 1.4-6x.

name: libaegis (AEGIS-128L, AEGIS-128X/256X)
baseline: AES-256-GCM (SUPERCOP aes256gcmv1; on this host the fastest implementation is Romain Dolbeau's VAES code; the OpenSSL wrapper 'opensslnew' is also measured and is slower)
one_liner: Portable C library for the AEGIS AEAD family (RFC 10032), roughly 3x AES-GCM throughput on AES-NI/VAES CPUs.

name: Fadec
baseline: libopcodes, Capstone and Zydis (x86 decoding libraries)
one_liner: Small freestanding C table-driven x86-32/x86-64 decoder plus x86-64 encoder; claims, unmeasured, to beat Capstone, Zydis and libopcodes.

name: Instrew
baseline: QEMU and HQEMU (LLVM-based dynamic binary translation)
one_liner: LLVM-based user-mode dynamic binary translator for Linux (x86-64, AArch64, RISC-V64 guests); paper reports far lower overhead than QEMU and HQEMU.

name: Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Code generator for FIX SBE fixed-layout binary messages; C++ flyweight codecs beat Protobuf ~9x encode, ~7x decode (one small-message test).

name: Imprint
baseline: Protobuf (Rust prost 0.12 implementation, per the since-removed benches/Cargo.toml)
one_liner: Rust row format with a sorted field-offset directory, so records merge or project without decoding; ~4x faster than prost merges.

name: DobLIX
license: BSD-3-Clause (RocksDB 5.x-era 'BSD License For rocksdb software' LICENSE text; GitHub reports NOASSERTION) plus Facebook PATENTS file (Additional Grant of Patent Rights Version 2)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Research RocksDB fork replacing the SST index with a block-aware learned string index; paper: 2.21x read-only throughput vs RocksDB.

name: matchedfilter (formerly peak-fft)
language: C core with Python bindings; GPU kernels in Slang (Vulkan/Metal)
baseline: FFTW (inverse transform only, timed through pyFFTW); on GPU rocFFT / MLX FFT inverse-only references
one_liner: Fused batched matched filter (spectral product, inverse FFT, peak scan) for data x template banks; peak-only mode beats FFTW's inverse-only time.

name: zog (Zig SIMD JSONL search)
baseline: jq (C); the README row is labelled 'jq/jaq' so it is not clear which of the two produced each number; ripgrep (Rust) is also compared
one_liner: Zig CLI that filters, extracts and aggregates JSONL by raw byte scanning; README claims 20-50x over jq/jaq.

name: minfft
baseline: KissFFT (the README also plots PocketFFT and FFTW with SSE2 for reference)
one_liner: Two-file C89 power-of-two FFT/DCT/DST library, about 2x KissFFT's speed; still slower than PocketFFT and FFTW.

name: mmemmove (AJ528): memmove in ARM Cortex-M assembly
language: ARM Thumb assembly (Cortex-M4 and M0+) with a C test harness
baseline: newlib generic memmove.c (byte loop under -Os; newlib ARM ships no assembly memmove)
one_liner: Hand-written Thumb-1 memmove for Cortex-M0+/M4 that beats newlib-nano's byte-loop memmove; separate memmove_() symbol.

name: Jansson
baseline: JsonCpp 1.0.0 (stringify also beats nlohmann/json 2.0.3)
one_liner: Dependency-free C library for a mutable, reference-counted JSON tree; stringified 1.35x faster than JsonCpp 1.0.0 in a 2016 independent run.

name: memx-cdy (C ABI of the Rust memx crate: memchr, memmem, memcmp, memcpy, memset)
language: Rust (C ABI shared and static library, LD_PRELOAD capable)
baseline: glibc and musl libc memchr, memmem, memcmp, memcpy and memset (called from Rust through FFI as libc_* rows), alongside Rust std and the memchr crate
one_liner: C-ABI (LD_PRELOAD-able) build of the Rust memx crate; memmem 2.7-5.9x faster than glibc/musl, other mem* mixed.

name: aklomp/base64 (SIMD Base64 C99 library)
baseline: base64
one_liner: Portable C99 SIMD base64 codec with runtime CPU dispatch; the Muła–Lemire paper measured its decoder about 4x faster than Chrome's.

name: woid
baseline: std::function
one_liner: Header-only C++23 type-erasure toolkit; woid::Fun beats std::function via configurable SBO storage and const/noexcept-correct signatures.

name: Pogreb
baseline: goleveldb (pure-Go port of LevelDB; the C++ LevelDB was not tested)
one_liner: Pure-Go embedded key-value store with an on-disk hash index; roughly 10-23x goleveldb random-lookup throughput in the author's chart.

name: Squirrel
baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (the copy vendored in scriptorium's javascript/duktape; PUC Lua at 1.341 s in the same table is faster than Squirrel)
one_liner: Small embeddable C++ bytecode VM for a Lua-like language with classes; ran fib(34) about 4.5x faster than Duktape 1.2.2 in 2015.

name: Albumentations
baseline: torchvision, Kornia, imgaug and AugLy (CPU image-augmentation transforms)
one_liner: Python image-augmentation library on OpenCV and LUT kernels; 1.2-13x the throughput of torchvision, Kornia, imgaug and AugLy per transform.

name: buffet
baseline: std::string
one_liner: C buffer type with SSO and refcounted views beating std::string on append, but not on plain memcopy or views.

name: qoi (qoi-rust)
baseline: QOI reference C implementation (phoboslab/qoi qoi.h, commit 00e34217 as of the 2022-01-06 measurement; the README later relabelled it 8d35d93 without re-measuring)
one_liner: Safe-Rust QOI image codec (crate qoi) that decoded about 1.5x and encoded about 1.3x faster than reference qoi.h.

name: alpha-wrap (CGAL-free Alpha Wrapping)
baseline: CGAL 6.x CGAL::alpha_wrap_3 (Alpha_wrap_3), GMP-free build
one_liner: MIT clean-room C++17 alpha wrapping (TOG 2022) without CGAL; about 2x faster than a GMP-free CGAL::alpha_wrap_3 build.

name: qdf (Quick Data Format)
baseline: Protocol Buffers, FlatBuffers, MessagePack (wire size); MessagePack and Go encoding/json (encode/decode speed)
one_liner: Go-only schemaless binary format: record batches 29-68% smaller than Protobuf, ~7x faster decode than encoding/json.

name: contention_free_shared_mutex (AlexeyAB/object_threadsafe safe_ptr library)
baseline: std::shared_mutex
one_liner: Per-thread sharded reader-writer lock and object wrapper claiming up to ~10x std::shared_mutex throughput under read-heavy contention.

name: ab_glyph
baseline: rusttype 0.9 (Rust OpenType/TrueType glyph layout and rasterization crate, which describes itself as a pure Rust alternative to FreeType)
one_liner: Pure-Rust glyph loading, scaling, positioning and rasterization crate; rewrite of rusttype with cheaper per-glyph layout, especially for CFF fonts.

name: ALP/GraphBLAS (nonblocking backend)
baseline: SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS and Eigen
one_liner: C++ GraphBLAS framework whose nonblocking backend fuses chained sparse ops at run time; paper reports beating SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS and Eigen.

name: apxchol (parallel approximate-Cholesky PCG for Laplacian and SDDM systems)
baseline: hypre BoomerAMG (CPU and GPU builds); AMGCL, RCHOL and ParAC are also in the comparison
one_liner: Parallel randomized approximate-Cholesky PCG for graph-Laplacian and SDDM systems; beats hypre BoomerAMG on total solve time.

name: async_simple (Lazy)
baseline: folly::coro::Task (folly coroutines) and cppcoro::task
one_liner: Alibaba's C++20 Lazy coroutine task type; about 3x faster than folly::coro::Task on call-chain and fan-out microbenchmarks, near-parity with cppcoro.

name: MNN
baseline: TensorFlow Lite, NCNN, MACE, CoreML (MLSys 2020 paper)
one_liner: Alibaba's on-device inference/training engine with hand-written ARM/x86 assembly and GPU backends; beat TF-Lite, NCNN, MACE on 2020 phones.

name: PhotonLibOS
baseline: boost::asio
one_liner: Alibaba's stackful-coroutine C++ I/O runtime (epoll/io_uring/kqueue); its echo server beats boost::asio on single-core QPS.

name: struct_pack (yalantinglibs)
baseline: protobuf
one_liner: Header-only C++ binary serializer that reflects plain structs at compile time, no .proto or macros; ~2-20x faster than protobuf.

name: Zvec
baseline: Milvus 2.5.11 (sq8) and Milvus 2.2.12 (HNSW), plus Zilliz Cloud (managed Milvus) 8cu-perf v2025.6, via VectorDBBench
one_liner: Embedded (in-process) C++ vector database with HNSW and int8 quantization; about 2x Zilliz Cloud QPS at matched recall in its own VectorDBBench run.

name: ECM-ELF (ECM stage 1, AVX-512 IFMA 8-curve batch backend)
language: C/C++ (GitHub lists C as primary; the AVX-512 kernels are .cpp; CUDA and OpenCL backends also exist)
baseline: GMP-ECM 7.0.6 (ecm-zen3.exe, built on GMP, curve family -param 0); the same table also compares Prime95 v31.04b05 (GWNUM FFT)
one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA ECM stage 1 running 8 curves per core; 2.3-3x faster per curve than GMP-ECM on Mersenne numbers.

name: evm2 (alloy-rs)
baseline: revm (Rust EVM interpreter)
one_liner: Customizable Rust EVM from alloy-rs with a tail-call, static-table interpreter; claims up to 2x over revm, unpublished numbers.

name: Almide
language: Almide (statically typed language compiling to Rust and WebAssembly)
baseline: Ordinary hand-written Rust (Box-linked recursive enum, no arena, rustc 1.96.1 opt-level=3, LTO, 1 codegen unit)
one_liner: LLM-oriented statically typed language that compiles to Rust and WebAssembly; its native output beats Box-per-node Rust on two tree-allocation benchmarks.

name: rhet_RNG (xromu2jr, winner of the PRNG Battle Royale)

baseline: std::string::find

name: gDel3D
baseline: CGAL 3D Delaunay triangulation (CGAL 4.2, sequential)

name: midint-arithmetic-division (GPU multi-precision division)
baseline: GMP

name: AsmJit
baseline: PostgreSQL LLVM JIT (llvmjit) in the pg_jitter shootout

name: AssemblyScript (TypeScript-like to Wasm compiler)
baseline: JavaScript on V8 (Node.js v18.7.0), same n-body source compiled with tsc

name: libfoxenflac
baseline: flac command-line reference decoder application (Xiph flac, built on libFLAC); no comparison against libFLAC's API, FFmpeg or dr_flac is published
one_liner: Tiny C99 FLAC decoder with no libc and no heap use; author claims about 25% faster than the flac CLI.

name: Ruff
baseline: Flake8 (linting); Black (formatting); also compared to pycodestyle, pyflakes, pylint
one_liner: Rust linter and formatter replacing Flake8, Black, isort, pyupgrade, and more with one fast CLI.

name: ty
baseline: mypy; Pyright
one_liner: Rust-based Python type checker and language server from Astral; 10-100x faster cold checks than mypy and Pyright.

name: lute
baseline: phf (rust-phf) static compile-time hash maps
one_liner: Rust no_std perfect-hash immutable Map/Set (up to 65,535 keys) with 1.9x-16.9x lower query time than phf.

name: angelsea (MIR-based AngelScript JIT)
baseline: AngelScript interpreter (stock bytecode VM, JIT instructions off); also BlindMindStudios AngelScript JIT
one_liner: Alpha MIR-based AngelScript JIT; author reports about 5x over the stock interpreter on call loops, 0-40% over BMS JIT.

name: sha256mb

name: fast-vad
baseline: webrtcvad (Google WebRTC voice activity detector, C)

name: asmjson
language: Rust crate with hand-written x86-64 AVX-512BW assembly
baseline: sonic-rs (AVX2 lazy Value), simd-json and serde_json
one_liner: Experimental Rust JSON parser with a hand-written AVX-512BW assembly inner loop; about 1.6x sonic-rs on string-heavy synthetic JSON.

name: FastPLBF (fast PLBF / fast PLBF++)
baseline: PLBF (Partitioned Learned Bloom Filter)
one_liner: Python reference code for fast PLBF and PLBF++, which cut partitioned learned Bloom filter construction time 34x-761x versus PLBF.

name: KANN
baseline: Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 1.2.2 (CPU, MKL); also TensorFlow 1.0.0 (CPU) and tiny-dnn
one_liner: Four-file C library for training small MLPs, CNNs and RNNs on CPU; beat 2017 Theano+Keras and tiny-dnn in its own runs.

name: klib khash (khash.h)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Single-header C macro hash table (open addressing, 2-bit flags); about 4x less CPU and 3x less memory than std::unordered_map on integer counting.

name: custom-memory-allocator (atul-singh-as)
baseline: malloc/free (macOS system allocator)
one_liner: Educational C++20 fixed-size pool and first-fit free-list allocators; the pool beats macOS malloc/free on bulk 16 B allocation.

name: aubio
baseline: audioread (FFmpegAudioFile for the load benchmark, audioread.audio_open with its auto-selected backend for the metadata benchmark; compressed formats decode through an ffmpeg subprocess)
one_liner: GPL C audio-analysis library whose Python aubio.source loads compressed audio 1.5-2.3x faster than audioread's ffmpeg subprocess.

name: FastNoise2
baseline: FastNoise Lite (scalar C++), FastNoise legacy, libnoise, stb_perlin
one_liner: C++17 SIMD node-graph noise library (Perlin, Simplex, Value, Cellular) that generates arrays 4-8x faster than scalar FastNoise Lite.

name: FastNoiseSIMD
baseline: libnoise (also the author's scalar FastNoise)
one_liner: SIMD 3D coherent-noise generator (Perlin, simplex, value, cellular, cubic) filling float grids 4-45x faster than libnoise.

name: intel-intrinsics (inteli, SIMD library for D)
baseline: Phobos std.digest.sha sha256Of (scalar D standard-library SHA-256)
one_liner: D library exposing the Intel _mm_* intrinsics API (MMX to AVX2, SHA, BMI2) on LDC, DMD and GDC, emulated on ARM.

name: vger (Audulus)
baseline: nanovg
one_liner: Small Metal GPU renderer for immediate-mode UIs (Apple only); its author reports 120 fps where nanovg managed 30 fps.

name: LeMac
baseline: AES-GCM in associated-data-only mode (GHASH/GMAC-style authentication), using Romain Dolbeau's public-domain AES-NI/PCLMUL implementation (benchmark/GCM/aesenc-int.c, from SUPERCOP), not OpenSSL
one_liner: Designers' AES-NI C code for LeMac, a nonce-based AES-round MAC about 4-7x faster than AES-128-GCM's GHASH on long messages.

name: Blaze (aurimasg/blaze)
baseline: Blend2D, Skia (CPU), Apple CoreGraphics
one_liner: Research-grade multi-threaded CPU rasterizer for solid-color path fills; the author reports 2.6x faster than multi-threaded Blend2D (2023 version) on an M1 Max.

name: XAD
baseline: CppAD, Adept 2, autodiff (C++ AD libraries), finite differences
one_liner: Operator-overloading C++ AD library whose adjoint tape beats Adept 2 and CppAD by 1.1-2.3x on quant-finance gradients.

name: JSONSki
baseline: RapidJSON, simdjson
one_liner: Streaming JSONPath engine that skips irrelevant JSON with bit-parallel fast-forwarding; ~4.8x faster than simdjson parse+query (ASPLOS'22).

name: Pison
baseline: RapidJSON, simdjson
one_liner: Multithreaded SIMD structural-index builder and path iterator for single huge JSON records; beats simdjson/RapidJSON end-to-end using 8 threads.

name: Harper
baseline: LanguageTool (Java grammar checker)
one_liner: Rule-based English grammar and spell checker in Rust (native, LSP, WebAssembly); claims millisecond lints versus LanguageTool's seconds, unmeasured.

name: Automerge (Rust core compiled to WebAssembly, 2.x)
language: Rust (WebAssembly build) with JavaScript bindings; also a C API
baseline: Automerge 0.14.1, the earlier pure-JavaScript implementation (Yjs 13.6.11 shown as the JS reference)

name: AutoMQ
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: Kafka 3.9 fork with S3-backed stateless brokers; beat Kafka's publish latency only with a now-commercial EBS WAL.

name: optimize-cnn (hand-written NEON tiny CNN inference)
baseline: ONNX Runtime 1.27.1, ncnn 20260526 and TensorFlow Lite 2.20.0 (tuned by the author)
one_liner: Hand-written NEON inference for one tiny Fashion-MNIST CNN on a Raspberry Pi 4B; 2.1-3.1x faster than tuned TFLite, ncnn and ONNX Runtime.

name: optimize-gemm (Avafly)
baseline: OpenBLAS 0.3.28 and Eigen 3.4.0 (BLIS 0.9.0-156 and GSL 2.8 also measured)

name: a5hash
baseline: wyhash, xxHash (xxhash64)
one_liner: Tiny header-only C hash for hash-map keys; beats XXH64 and edges wyhash on short keys, but slow on bulk data.

name: AVIR / LANCIR (Aleksey Vaneev)
baseline: No third-party incumbent timed; LANCIR is compared only with the project's own AVIR algorithm

name: komihash
baseline: xxHash (XXH3_64 / XXH64) and wyhash_final4
one_liner: Header-only, non-cryptographic 64-bit hash beating wyhash and xxHash on short keys (0-31 bytes) via full 128-bit multiply accumulation.

name: LZAV
baseline: Snappy
one_liner: Single-header C99 LZ77 codec: about 16% smaller output than LZ4/Snappy at Snappy-class compress speed.

name: r8brain-free-src
baseline: libsamplerate 0.2.2 (Secret Rabbit Code, MEDIUM and BEST converters)
one_liner: Header-only MIT C++ audio sample-rate converter; 3.4x to 8.8x libsamplerate's stereo throughput in a third-party near-unity benchmark.

name: oss-nvjpg
baseline: libjpeg-turbo
one_liner: C++20 driver for the Tegra X1 NVJPG hardware JPEG decoder; README shows 3-4x lower latency than libjpeg-turbo on the A57 cores.

name: savefile
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Rust derive-based, versioned binary format for saving structs to disk; serializes 4.7-41x faster than prost.

name: crc-fast (Rust core, C/C++ compatible) — generic SIMD CRC-16/32/64

name: statico
baseline: nginx (static in-memory 'return' response)
one_liner: Rust benchmarking stub that returns one fixed HTTP response; its README table puts it ahead of nginx 'return 200'.

name: fastgrep (Rust grep)

name: MarkupEver
baseline: BeautifulSoup4 (html.parser and lxml backends) and html5lib

name: sha2-with-c-intrinsic (AWS Crypto Algorithms Group)
baseline: OpenSSL SHA-256/SHA-512 x86-64 perlasm assembly (AVX and AVX2 paths, plus the SHA-NI path for SHA-256 only), copied into the repo from OpenSSL master as of Feb 24 2020 (README link text says 13c5d744, but the URL points to commit e32c608e)
one_liner: C-intrinsics SHA-256/SHA-512 kernels from AWS; only the SHA-NI SHA-256 path beats OpenSSL's assembly, by 5-8%.

name: AWS-LC

baseline: OpenSSL

name: aws-lc-rs
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Rust crypto crate with a ring-style API over AWS-LC and optional FIPS module; beat OpenSSL in wtx handshake runs.

name: LLRT (Low Latency Runtime)
baseline: Node.js 20 (V8) on AWS Lambda
one_liner: AWS Labs JavaScript runtime for Lambda (Rust plus QuickJS-NG, no JIT) that cuts Node.js 20 cold starts.

name: libblur
baseline: OpenCV (Gaussian blur, stack blur and median blur)

name: moxcms
baseline: Little CMS 2 (lcms2); also qcms

name: pic-scale

name: sparkyuv
baseline: libyuv

name: liburing
baseline: libaio
one_liner: Userspace wrapper around Linux's io_uring ring-buffer syscall interface; beats libaio and POSIX-AIO on IOPS and syscall overhead.

name: xorf (Rust xor / binary fuse filter crate)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Rust static xor/binary-fuse filters: about 9 bits/key at 0.4% FPP versus about 11.5 for an optimal Bloom.

name: wasm-runtime-performance (boost::graph Floyd-Warshall via Emscripten)
language: C++ (Boost.Graph, std::priority_queue) compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten
baseline: graphlib.js alg.floydWarshall (JavaScript, in the browser JS engine)
one_liner: 2017 browser benchmark: Boost.Graph Floyd-Warshall compiled to wasm by Emscripten versus graphlib.js; std::priority_queue loses to JS heaps.

name: B2R2 (binary analysis framework, disassembler front-end)

name: EigenRand
baseline: C++ <random> distributions (std::normal_distribution, std::uniform_real_distribution, std::uniform_int_distribution, etc.) and Eigen::DenseBase::Random

name: DAW JSON Link

name: Bolt

name: Mobius

baseline: OpenSSL (ECDSA_verify / o2i_ECPublicKey on secp256k1)
one_liner: Bitcoin Core's secp256k1-only C signature library; ECDSA verification 2.5-5.5x faster than the 2015-era OpenSSL it replaced.

name: tiny-secp256k1 (WASM build)
language: Rust (wrapping the C libsecp256k1) compiled to WebAssembly, TypeScript wrapper
baseline: elliptic (pure JavaScript, the fallback of tiny-secp256k1 1.1.6); the Rust native addon is faster than the WASM build
one_liner: bitcoin-core libsecp256k1 compiled to WebAssembly with a TypeScript API; about 2-4x faster than elliptic, but slower than native addons.

name: bddisasm
baseline: Capstone (decode+format throughput); Intel XED, diStorm, iced, yaxpeax-x86, Sleigh and the other listed decoders are measured in the same harness
one_liner: Bitdefender's x86/x64 instruction decoder in C with rich operand metadata; decode+format 1.4-1.8x Capstone's throughput in disas-bench.

name: RISVM
baseline: Lua 5.3 and CPython 3.6.6
one_liner: Tiny untyped 32-bit register bytecode VM in about 1000 lines of C++; one hand-written assembly benchmark ran 1.45x faster than Lua 5.3.

name: glam
baseline: cgmath and nalgebra (scalar Rust linear algebra crates, as measured by mathbench)
one_liner: Rust f32/f64 3D game-math crate with SSE2/NEON storage; 2.5x faster Mat4 inverse than cgmath in mathbench.

name: compressed_map ApproxSet (frayed ribbon filter)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Research Rust crate: static approximate set built on frayed ribbon filters, about 30% smaller than Bloom at equal FPR.

name: Mino
baseline: ZeroMQ
one_liner: C++20 shared-memory pub/sub framework passing slab handles over SPSC rings; beat Protobuf+ZeroMQ in author's six-process pipeline benchmark.

name: BitLib
baseline: std::vector<bool>
one_liner: Header-only bit_vector and STL-style bit algorithms that beat std::vector<bool> by operating word-at-a-time instead of bit-at-a-time.

name: Nowa
baseline: Cilk Plus and TBB lock-based continuation stealing; OpenMP tasks (libomp)
one_liner: Research C runtime for wait-free continuation-stealing fork/join, reported faster than lock-based Cilk Plus/TBB and OpenMP tasks.

name: BLAKE3
license: CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
baseline: SHA-256 and SHA3-256: the fastest of SUPERCOP's implementations, whose candidates include OpenSSL-backed ones. BLAKE2b is also compared. The project's own chart used OpenSSL 1.1.1d SHA-256/SHA3-256 and BLAKE2b via blake2b_simd.
one_liner: Official Rust/C implementation of BLAKE3, a Merkle-tree hash/XOF/MAC about 4x faster than SHA-256 on long single-core inputs.

name: llcpp
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Header-only C++17 synchronous binary logger: writes format string plus raw argument bytes, about 4x lower median latency than spdlog.

name: Blend2D
baseline: Skia (CPU pipeline) and Cairo; also AGG, JUCE, Qt6, CoreGraphics
one_liner: Zlib-licensed C/C++ CPU 2D vector renderer with JIT-compiled pipelines; about 4x Skia's and 7x Cairo's raster throughput.

name: KVell
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: SOSP'19 research key-value store for NVMe/Optane SSDs that has no LSM compaction; 2-8x RocksDB throughput on YCSB point workloads.

name: AngelScript JIT Compiler (BlindMindStudios)
baseline: AngelScript bytecode interpreter (same SDK, no JIT)
one_liner: x86/x86-64 JIT plug-in for AngelScript 2.31.0 that turns bytecode into native code; about 1.10x over the interpreter on scriptorium fib(34).

name: Bloodmoon001/memory-allocator
baseline: malloc/free
one_liner: Header-only C++17 fixed-capacity, single-type pool with intrusive free list; about 10x faster than MSVC malloc/free on alloc-free pairs.

name: Blosc (c-blosc)
baseline: memcpy (single ctypes.memmove call; Blosc's own named baseline)
one_liner: Blocked, multithreaded meta-compressor (shuffle/bitshuffle plus BloscLZ, LZ4, Zstd, zlib) for typed numeric arrays; can outrun memcpy on compressible data.

name: c-blosc2 (Blosc2 shuffle+lz4)
baseline: memcpy (uncompressed copy); inner codecs lz4/zstd/zlib are components, not rivals
one_liner: Blocked, multithreaded meta-compressor (shuffle/bitshuffle filters plus LZ4, Zstd, zlib or BloscLZ) for typed binary arrays; outruns memcpy on compressible data.

name: revm
baseline: go-ethereum (Geth) EVM, py-evm and ethereumjs
one_liner: The standard Rust EVM; about 2.8x faster than Geth's EVM on evm-bench, but slower than C++ evmone.

name: skani
baseline: FastANI 1.33 (C++) and Mash 2.3 (C++), bioconda builds pinned in skani-test/env.yml
one_liner: Rust ANI and aligned-fraction calculator for genomes and MAGs; 20-50x faster than FastANI (C++), slower than Mash at querying.

name: sylph
baseline: Kraken2 (C++)
one_liner: Rust k-mer-sketch metagenome profiler giving species abundances and containment ANI with far less CPU and memory than Kraken2.

name: Courierust
baseline: tokio-tungstenite / tungstenite
one_liner: Zero-dependency Rust HTTP/WebSocket stack; its WebSocket codec encodes small masked frames ~2.5x faster than tungstenite.

name: mp++
baseline: GMP (mpz_t)
one_liner: C++ multiprecision integer/rational/float types over GMP with inline small-value storage; 4-8x faster than raw GMP on 1-limb operands.

name: glibc (libc string functions, qsort, regexec, strtod, malloc)
baseline: musl libc as shipped by zig 0.15.2 (string functions replaced by Zig code), single run
one_liner: GNU C library; its CPU-dispatched string routines, malloc, qsort, regexec and strtod beat zig-bundled static musl in most micro-benchmarks.

name: SpookyHash V2 (Bob Jenkins' official repo)
baseline: xxHash64 (XXH64)
one_liner: Bob Jenkins' own reference C++ SpookyV2, a 128-bit non-cryptographic hash about 1.2x faster than XXH64 on large buffers.

name: Graaf
baseline: Boost Graph Library (Boost.Graph 1.84.0, via the perf/boost benchmarks for Dijkstra, BFS, Kruskal, Prim, greedy and Welsh-Powell colouring)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 graph library positioned as a lighter Boost.Graph alternative; measured slower than Boost.Graph on every benchmarked algorithm.

name: TFT_eSPI
baseline: Adafruit_GFX (Adafruit-GFX-Library) with the Adafruit_ILI9341 driver
one_liner: Arduino TFT driver plus drawing library for ESP32, RP2040, ESP8266 and STM32; 1.3x to 4.7x faster than Adafruit_GFX on an ILI9341 at 40 MHz.

name: Bodo DataFrames
language: Python (JIT-compiled to native code via an MPI-based C++ runtime)
baseline: polars
one_liner: Pandas-API DataFrame library and Numba-based JIT compiling pandas code to MPI-parallel native code; beats Polars on a UDF-heavy vendor benchmark.

name: ptpng
license: None stated: no LICENSE file (raw LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and COPYING all return 404), the GitHub page shows no license, and README.md, include/ptpng.h and CMakeLists.txt give no terms
baseline: Decoder: libpng 1.6 (vendored libpng16 branch) with zlib-ng 2.2.4 in ZLIB_COMPAT mode. Encoder: libpng with the vendored stock zlib (develop branch) at level 6 and libpng with zlib-ng 2.2.4 at level 6, both with PNG_ALL_FILTERS adaptive filtering.
one_liner: Unlicensed C11 PNG decoder and encoder with AVX2/NEON kernels; decodes 1.5-1.8x faster than libpng with zlib-ng on synthetic images.

name: BoltFFI
baseline: wasm-bindgen (Rust-to-JavaScript glue); on native targets UniFFI
one_liner: Rust multi-language bindings generator; returns arrays of structs to JS or Swift far faster than wasm-bindgen class handles or UniFFI.

name: [Boost].UT (boost-ext/ut)
baseline: GoogleTest 1.10.0, Catch2 2.10.2, Boost.Test 1.71.0, doctest 2.3.5 (compile time of test code using each framework)
one_liner: Macro-free C++20 single-header/module unit-testing framework whose 2019 benchmark compiled faster than Boost.Test, GoogleTest and Catch2.

name: Boost.Algorithm Boyer-Moore / Boyer-Moore-Horspool searchers
baseline: std::search
one_liner: Header-only Boyer-Moore / Boyer-Moore-Horspool string searchers, ~4-5x faster than std::search on long patterns.

name: Boost.Bloom (block / multiblock filter configurations)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Header-only C++11 Boost filter template whose cache-local block and SIMD multiblock subfilters run 2.6-5x faster than a classical Bloom filter.

name: Boost.Charconv
baseline: std::to_chars, std::from_chars
one_liner: Portable std::to_chars/from_chars reimplementation for pre-C++17 toolchains and MSVC, winning there and near-parity on GCC.

name: Boost.Cobalt
baseline: Boost.Asio stackful coroutines (spawn on Boost.Context) and asio::awaitable
one_liner: Boost library of C++20 coroutine primitives on Boost.Asio; beats asio stackful spawn and, on channels, asio::awaitable.

name: boost::container::flat_set / flat_map
baseline: std::set
one_liner: Vector-backed sorted set/map beating std::set on insert+remove at small sizes, up to ~256 elements.

name: Boost.Context
baseline: glibc ucontext_t user-space context switch (::swapcontext/makecontext), as wrapped by Boost.Context's own continuation_ucontext.hpp backend (b2 context-impl=ucontext), run through the same callcc()/continuation benchmark
one_liner: Boost's assembly-backed stackful context switch (fiber, callcc/continuation): about 9 ns per switch versus 547 ns for glibc swapcontext.

name: Boost.Fiber
baseline: std::thread, std::async
one_liner: Cooperative user-space fibers with a std::thread-like API, spawning and context-switching orders of magnitude cheaper than std::thread/std::async.

name: Boost.JSON
baseline: nlohmann/json, RapidJSON
one_liner: Mutable C++11 JSON DOM with an SSE2-assisted streaming parser; median ~2.6x faster parsing than nlohmann/json, roughly ties RapidJSON.

name: Boost.Lockfree
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Boost's lock-free MPMC/SPSC queue and stack family; beats std::mutex on latency, not contended MPMC throughput.

name: Boost.Log
baseline: std::fstream with std::flush after every line (also stdio fprintf+fflush and g3log 1.3.2)
one_liner: Boost's attribute-based logging framework; beats a flush-every-line std::fstream only under multithreaded or disk-stalled load.

name: Boost.Multiprecision (cpp_int fixed-precision)
baseline: GMP (mpz_int via gmp_int backend)
one_liner: Header-only C++ big-number types; fixed-width cpp_int (128-bit) beats GMP's mpz on basic arithmetic by 1.5-6x.

name: Boost.Polygon (Voronoi diagram builder)
baseline: CGAL (Delaunay triangulation of points / segment Delaunay graph; CGAL-4.3-beta1 in the benchmark)
one_liner: Header-only Boost sweep-line Voronoi builder for integer points and segments; beats CGAL's segment Delaunay graph, loses on points.

name: Boost.Regex
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Header-only successor to std::regex: same backtracking engine, hand-tuned matcher and pooled allocation for real throughput gains.

name: Boost.Serialization
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Boost's C++ object-graph serializer; its native binary archive round-tripped a ~17 KB record ~1.9x faster than Protobuf.

name: Boost.Sort — spreadsort
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Hybrid radix/comparison sort in Boost; beats std::sort on large random integers, strings, and objects.

name: Boost.Unordered (boost::unordered_flat_map)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only SIMD open-addressing hash map/set for Boost; unordered_flat_map is 2.7x-11.6x faster than std::unordered_map.

name: Marlin renderer (Java 2D)
baseline: OpenJDK 8 Pisces and Oracle JDK 8 Ductus (the Java 2D antialiasing rasterizers)
one_liner: Pure-Java antialiasing shape rasterizer for Java 2D that replaced Pisces and Ductus; OpenJDK's default renderer since JDK 9.

name: BusterMQ
baseline: NATS Server (nats-server, Go, epoll-based via Go's netpoller)
one_liner: Zig thread-per-core io_uring server for the core NATS pub/sub protocol; ~1.4x Go nats-server publish rate in its own benchmark.

name: Tessera
baseline: pandas
one_liner: Small .NET 9 columnar library whose sorted merge-sweep as-of join is about 14x faster than pandas.merge_asof on 1M x 1M rows.

name: CPath
baseline: find (GNU findutils), TinyDir, Cute Files, Python os.walk
one_liner: Single-header C directory traversal library; faster than `find`, TinyDir, Cute Files, and Python os.walk on recursive walks.

name: libutf
baseline: ICU 78.3 (ICU4C: ubrk grapheme break iterator, unorm2 NFC, ucol DUCET collation)
one_liner: Small malloc-free C11 library for NFC, DUCET collation and grapheme clusters on raw UTF-8; first-party numbers beat ICU on short strings.

name: XLSX I/O (xlsxio)
baseline: openpyxl (read_only=True, list(ws.iter_rows())); also xlrd (a pre-2.0 release, since xlrd 2.0 dropped .xlsx) and sxl in the same table. The table's xlsx2csv rows actually time openpyxl (copy-paste bug in benchmark.py), so xlsx2csv was never measured.
one_liner: C library that streams .xlsx worksheet values through expat; its Python wrapper reads about 5.8x faster than openpyxl read-only.

name: mosdepth (Nim BAM/CRAM depth calculator)
baseline: samtools depth (C, htslib); README table also lists bedtools genomecov (C++) and sambamba depth (D)
one_liner: Nim command-line tool for BAM/CRAM coverage; about 2x faster per-base than the pre-2021 pileup-based samtools depth.

name: ring
license: Apache-2.0 AND ISC (ring's own code ISC; BoringSSL-derived code Apache-2.0 per LICENSE-BoringSSL; once_cell polyfill Apache-2.0/MIT)
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Rust crypto-primitives crate (BoringSSL-derived C/asm) behind rustls; beat OpenSSL 1.5-3.7x on whole-process TLS handshake runs.

name: md5-wasm (hand-written WebAssembly MD5)
language: WebAssembly text format (.wat) with JavaScript wrapper
baseline: md5 npm package (pure JavaScript MD5, 'the most popular md5 utility')
one_liner: Promise-based MD5 for Node and browsers with a hand-written WAT core; about 39x faster than md5 npm on 37 MB.

name: mtpng (parallel PNG encoder with C API)
baseline: libpng
one_liner: Multithreaded Rust PNG encoder with a C API; chunked zlib deflate gives libpng-like file sizes, several times faster on many cores.

name: blake3-jit
baseline: @napi-rs/blake-hash (native Rust BLAKE3 Node addon)
one_liner: BLAKE3 in TypeScript with a runtime-generated WASM SIMD module; beats the native napi-rs addon only on inputs under 4 KB.

name: @napi-rs/image
baseline: sharp (Node.js binding over libvips with libwebp and libavif)
one_liner: Rust napi-rs addon for Node.js image resize and WebP/AVIF/JPEG/PNG encoding; edges out sharp on small-thumbnail throughput.

name: metal-json
baseline: simdjson
one_liner: Rust crate that parses JSON to a simdjson-format tape on Apple Silicon GPUs (Metal); beats C++ simdjson above ~4-5 MiB.

name: Decoding Attention (Bruce-Lee-LY)
baseline: Flash-Decoding (FlashAttention v2.6.3) and FlashInfer v0.1.6 decode attention
one_liner: CUDA-core decode-attention kernel for LLM inference; beats Flash-Decoding and FlashInfer only at short KV lengths.

name: geogram (ParallelDelaunay3d)
baseline: CGAL 3D Delaunay / regular triangulation, single-threaded and CGAL Parallel; the paper also has SciPy, Voro++, HXT (Gmsh) and gDel3D (GPU) columns
one_liner: BSD-licensed C++ geometry library whose multithreaded 3D Delaunay/regular triangulation (PDEL) outruns CGAL on large point sets.

name: LC Scheme BBV JIT (bsaleil/lc)
baseline: Gambit Scheme v4.9.3 and Chez Scheme v9.5.2 (mature AOT Scheme compilers, safe and unsafe modes); also Pycket (February 2019 build, Racket tracing JIT on RPython) for total time
one_liner: Research Scheme JIT using lazy basic-block versioning; generated code edges out Gambit and Chez on 38 classic benchmarks.

name: BS::thread_pool
baseline: std::thread
one_liner: Single-header C++17/20/23 thread pool that reuses worker threads to avoid std::thread's per-task creation overhead.

name: jsonparser (buger)
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Zero-allocation, path-based JSON field extractor for Go; 3-6.5x faster than encoding/json struct unmarshal on the project's benchmarks.

name: Bullet Physics (bullet3)
baseline: DART (also Simbody; ODE for comparison)
one_liner: Zlib-licensed C++ rigid/soft-body physics and collision SDK (PyBullet's core); beat DART and Simbody inside Gazebo-classic, not ODE.

name: Bundy-DNS (l1cache experimental branch)
baseline: BIND
one_liner: Bundy's unpublished l1cache experiment: pre-rendered wire-format DNS answer cache, claimed 180K vs 41K qps over BIND 9.9.2.

name: memchr (Rust crate)
baseline: Rust standard library substring search (rust/std/memmem: str::find / str::matches); the same rebar records also run glibc memmem and memchr through the libc engine (libc/memmem/oneshot, libc/memchr/oneshot)
one_liner: Rust crate of SIMD byte and substring search (memchr, memchr2/3, memrchr, memmem); about 4-6x faster than str::find, 2x faster than glibc memmem.

name: ripgrep
baseline: GNU grep, ag, git grep (mmap vs buffered read strategy)
one_liner: Recursive regex search CLI in Rust; beats GNU grep, git grep, ag and ugrep on code trees and large files.

name: snap (Rust Snappy, BurntSushi/rust-snappy)
baseline: Snappy C++ reference implementation (google/snappy 1.1.8)
one_liner: Pure-Rust Snappy (raw and frame formats) that roughly matches C++ Snappy 1.1.8: within about 10% either way per file.

name: Caffe
baseline: Torch-7 native CUDA convolution (cunn SpatialConvolutionMM)
one_liner: Berkeley's C++/CUDA layer-based deep learning framework; its native im2col+cuBLAS convolutions edged Torch-7's native kernels by 3-7% in 2015.

name: go-and (bwesterb)
language: Go (AVX2 and NEON assembly, generated with avo)
baseline: naive one-byte-at-a-time Go for loop (and a uint64-wise pure-Go version, build tag purego), both compiled by the Go gc compiler
one_liner: Go package of AVX2/NEON assembly kernels for and/or/xor/andnot/not, any-bit and popcount over []byte; beats Go loops 5-20x.

name: WebAssembly Micro Runtime (WAMR)
baseline: Wasmtime Pulley interpreter (A-tier numbers); Wasmtime, Wasmer and V8 JIT/AOT (libsodium suite)
one_liner: Small, build-time-configurable C WebAssembly runtime whose fast interpreter beats Wasmtime's Pulley interpreter by about 1.2-1.3x geomean.

name: Cranelift code generator (Bytecode Alliance Wasmtime)
baseline: V8 (TurboFan) for generated-code speed; WAVM (LLVM-based Wasm engine) for compile speed
one_liner: Cranelift, Wasmtime's Rust code generator: in a 2021 paper it compiled WebAssembly 7-10x faster than LLVM-based WAVM, with code about 14% slower.

name: weval
baseline: generic SpiderMonkey (StarlingMonkey) JavaScript interpreter running on Wasmtime
one_liner: Wasm partial evaluator that turns an annotated interpreter into an AOT compiler; about 3.6x over SpiderMonkey's interpreter on Richards.

name: Wizer
baseline: Wasmtime instantiating and running the same module without Wizer pre-initialization (the benches build a 'control' module and a wizened one on a wasmtime Engine; Wizer embeds Wasmtime)
one_liner: Build-time Wasm pre-initializer: snapshots a module's initialized memory and globals so startup skips init (1.35x-6.00x vs plain Wasmtime).

name: ByteTransformer
baseline: PyTorch 1.13.0, TensorFlow, FasterTransformer, DeepSpeed (BERT-base inference)
one_liner: Padding-free fp16 BERT encoder inference on NVIDIA GPUs; first-party A100 numbers show about 2x over PyTorch and 1.8x over FasterTransformer at long, variable lengths.

name: LightSeq
baseline: PyTorch fp16 mixed precision (training and inference), PyTorch QAT
one_liner: Fused CUDA Transformer layers for training and beam-search inference; 1.4-2.1x faster training than PyTorch fp16 AMP on A100.

name: monoio
baseline: epoll (via Tokio's mio-based reactor)
one_liner: Thread-per-core Rust async runtime on io_uring (epoll/kqueue fallback); ~1.9x Tokio's peak echo QPS on 4 cores.

name: Sonic
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: ByteDance's JIT- and SIMD-accelerated Go JSON library; about 1.9-3.4x the throughput of encoding/json on amd64.

name: Sonic-Cpp
baseline: RapidJSON (also nlohmann/json and taocpp/json in the nativejson-benchmark chart; simdjson, yyjson, cJSON and JsonCpp in the project's own benchmark)
one_liner: Header-only SIMD JSON DOM parser and serializer for C++ with a RapidJSON-style API, about 2x RapidJSON on nativejson-benchmark files.

name: @bytedance/tar-wasm
language: Rust compiled to WebAssembly (Cargo.toml in repo) with a TypeScript wrapper
baseline: tar-js and tarts (pure-JavaScript tar writers on npm)
one_liner: Rust tar crate compiled to WebAssembly behind a TarBuilder JS class; builds in-memory tars 50-160x faster than tar-js and tarts.

name: TerarkDB
baseline: RocksDB v6.12 (TerarkDB is a fork/drop-in replacement of RocksDB v5.18.3)
one_liner: ByteDance's RocksDB 5.18 fork with no-writeback key-value separation and lazy compaction; ~1.7x db_bench QPS vs RocksDB 6.12.

name: ConsensusRecSplit
baseline: RecSplit
one_liner: Minimal perfect hash function close to the 1.443 bits/key bound; builds about 100x faster than RecSplit at lower space.

name: SimdRecSplit / GpuRecSplit
baseline: BBHash
one_liner: SIMD, multicore and GPU construction of RecSplit minimal perfect hashes; single-threaded builds about 4x faster than BBHash at similar space.

name: LeMonHash
baseline: Prior monotone MPHF implementations: the Grossi-Ottaviano C++ Centroid Hollow Trie, Hollow Trie and Path Decomposed Trie (ot/path_decomposed_tries), plus the Belazzougui et al. Java implementations from Sux4J of the Hollow Trie Distributor, Hollow Trie, ZFast Trie, LCP, LCP 2-step, PaCo, VLLCP and VLPaCo
one_liner: Learned monotone minimal perfect hash (key to sorted rank): about 3-5 bits/key and 7-19x faster queries than trie-based MMPHFs.

name: ShockHash
baseline: RecSplit
one_liner: C++ minimal perfect hash: RecSplit with cuckoo-hashing leaves, building 1.56-1.58 bits/key MPHFs 15-160x faster than RecSplit/SIMDRecSplit.

name: SicHash
baseline: BBHash
one_liner: Cuckoo-hashing-plus-retrieval (minimal) perfect hash for static key sets: about 2.1 bits/key against BBHash's 3.3-3.7, with faster queries.

name: DBX
baseline: SQLite
one_liner: Beta pure-Rust HTAP embedded database whose key-value API edges out in-memory SQLite on a 10,000-row first-party benchmark.

name: fc_malloc
baseline: glibc malloc and jemalloc
one_liner: 2013 proof-of-concept thread-caching allocator with a dedicated free-recycling thread; README claims about 2x faster than glibc and jemalloc.

name: cligen/dents (c-blake, Nim fast directory walker behind find, ls and du)
baseline: GNU find, GNU ls -1AUR and GNU du (C); BSD find and fd are also named for find
one_liner: Nim getdents64/openat tree walker (cligen/dents) whose find, ls -R and du demos claim 1.4-4.5x over GNU tools.

name: procs (c-blake, Nim ps, pgrep and pkill replacement: pd, pf, pk)
baseline: procps ps ('/bin/ps ax'), pgrep and pkill (C)
one_liner: Nim /proc query toolkit whose pd/pf/pk read fewer /proc files than procps ps, pgrep and pkill.

name: wasman
baseline: wazero v1.12 (interpreter mode and compiler mode); also wagon v0.4 and life
one_liner: Pure-Go, dependency-free WebAssembly MVP interpreter with an optional arm64/amd64 JIT; beats wazero's interpreter 1.1-1.8x on micro-loops.

name: wtx (gRPC server)
baseline: gRPC (grpc-go, official google.golang.org/grpc implementation)
one_liner: Rust crate with its own HTTP/2 and gRPC stack. Its unary gRPC server served 3.7-5.5x grpc-go's req/s on HttpArena.

name: CWIST
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Plain-C17 web framework and app server; about 2.1-2.3x Go net/http's plaintext req/s in one independent suite run.

name: Cachelot
baseline: memcached
one_liner: Single-threaded C++ LRU cache library plus a memcached-text-protocol server that fits 7-16% more data than Memcached in the same RAM.

name: Caddy
baseline: nginx (C), HTTPS reverse proxy
one_liner: Go web server and reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS; claimed to beat nginx, but measured 4-14x slower in HttpArena.

name: lbzip2 (maintained fork)
baseline: bzip2 (bzip2 1.0.8)
one_liner: Maintained fork of lbzip2, a parallel bzip2-compatible compressor; single-threaded it already beats bzip2 1.0.8 by about 1.3x to 1.8x.

name: fasthex
baseline: xxd
one_liner: Rust CLI hex dumper that uses multiple threads, SIMD and mmap to dump large files far faster than xxd, hexyl and hexdump.

name: cauldron random.h (ziggurat normal distribution)
baseline: std::normal_distribution (driven by std::minstd_rand in the benchmark's cpp11random entry)
one_liner: Single-header C (C++-compatible) RNG library whose ziggurat standard-normal sampler measured 2.2x (float) and 4.2x (double) faster than std::normal_distribution.

name: rvv-bench (RISC-V Vector memcpy, memset and strlen assembly)
language: Assembly (RISC-V Vector 1.0) with a C harness
baseline: libc memcpy, memset and strlen of the benchmarked RISC-V board (hosted libc, version not stated); the same harness also times musl's C memcpy/strlen, a byte-wise scalar loop and a compiler auto-vectorized scalar loop
one_liner: Hand-written RISC-V Vector 1.0 memcpy, memset and strlen kernels; memcpy averages 2x a board's scalar libc in cache.

name: moodycamel::ConcurrentQueue
baseline: boost::lockfree::queue
one_liner: Lock-free MPMC C++11 queue with per-producer sub-queues and bulk ops, beating boost::lockfree::queue on throughput.

name: moodycamel::ReaderWriterQueue
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Header-only lock-free SPSC queue for C++11; beats a mutex-guarded queue by ~7x in ping-pong latency.

name: cmp
baseline: msgpack-c (msgpack C API, v1.3.0 in the shootout)
one_liner: Tiny allocation-free C89 MessagePack reader/writer; smaller than msgpack-c but 13-30% slower on write in the only shootout.

name: xutf
baseline: simdutf
one_liner: SIMD Rust UTF-8/16/32 transcoder beating simdutf on most inputs, plus allocation-free grapheme/width/wrap terminal-text primitives.

name: Porffor (AOT JavaScript/TypeScript to Wasm and C)
baseline: QuickJS and Node --jitless (V8 interpreter only); Node and Bun with JIT are NOT beaten

name: halloc

baseline: CUDA device-side malloc (in-kernel allocator)

name: Cap'n Proto
baseline: JSON serialization (RapidJSON)

name: cpu_gemm_opt
baseline: OpenBLAS 0.3.4 sgemm (README: 'most of the size exceed openblas(0.3.4)'; the driver times cblas_sgemm from the OpenBLAS it links)
one_liner: Single-core AVX2 SGEMM study (BLIS-style 6x16 asm kernel, per-size tuned blocking) about 4-9% ahead of OpenBLAS 0.3.4.

baseline: raw liburing C echo server (CarterLi/io_uring-echo-server, io_uring RECV-SEND); epoll echo server only indirectly

name: FastMap

name: otfcc

name: ICBC (high quality SIMD BC1 encoder)

name: WAMR in Zig (cataggar/wamr)
baseline: wasmtime run (default Cranelift JIT)

name: CatBoost
baseline: XGBoost 0.80 and LightGBM 2.2.1 (gradient boosted tree model prediction on CPU)

name: Snowshoe (catid/snowshoe)
baseline: OpenSSL 1.0.1e (NIST P-256 elliptic-curve math, ecp_nistp256.c)

name: Wirehair
baseline: CM256 (catid/cm256, O(N^2) Cauchy-matrix MDS Reed-Solomon codec; Longhair measured alongside)

name: Zpng
baseline: libpng
one_liner: Zstd-backed lossless RGB/RGBA image format that encodes about 23x and decodes 4.6x faster than libpng, with smaller files.

name: uring_exec

name: redb
baseline: RocksDB and SQLite (also benchmarked against LMDB and fjall, with mixed results)

name: ccache
baseline: Uncached compilation (same compiler command run without ccache); the page does not involve Make/Ninja and does not name the compiler
one_liner: Compiler cache that skips re-running GCC/Clang/MSVC on unchanged source, reusing prior object output.

name: lanehash
baseline: xxHash (xxh3), rapidhash

name: MuJS
baseline: goja (Go JavaScript interpreter); also Boa (Rust) and Jint (.NET) JavaScript interpreters in the same table

name: fast_prng (cd-mcfarland modified ziggurat)

name: httpp

name: HOMCC

name: GPUJPEG

name: mph (Go, Hash-Displace-Compress / CHD)

name: cespare/xxhash (Go amd64/arm64 assembly)

name: ImageZero

name: sajson

name: ChainedFilter

name: ChakraCore

name: TRON (TRajectory Optimized NUFFT)
baseline: gpuNUFFT (GPU NUFFT gridding library), Fessler's Image Reconstruction Toolbox (IRT, MATLAB) and BART (the reproduction steps also build BART)
one_liner: CUDA NUFFT gridding/degridding hard-wired for 2D radial MRI trajectories; paper reports 6-30x over gpuNUFFT, BART and IRT.

name: JUring
baseline: java.nio.channels.FileChannel (Java NIO)
one_liner: Java FFM bindings to Linux io_uring (via liburing) for batched file reads/writes; beats FileChannel on small random reads.

name: Dlib (dnn module, CUDA/cuDNN deep learning API)
baseline: Caffe (GPU, cuDNN)
one_liner: dlib's dnn module: C++ type-defined CNN training and inference on cuDNN; 2016 author claim of about 1.6x Caffe's speed.

name: bolt
baseline: Eigen dense float matrix multiply (`out.noalias() = X * Q`, the repo's 'matmul' rows; README and slides call it BLAS) and the repo's own product quantization (PQ, OPQ) encoders; FAISS is not benchmarked
one_liner: AVX2 vector-quantization library that encodes float vectors into 4-bit codes and computes approximate distances and dot products far faster than PQ or exact float math.

name: Sprintz
baseline: Simple8b, FastPFor, SIMD-BP128 (also LZ4HC, Brotli, Blosc, FSE, LZO in the author's wider runs)
one_liner: Research codec for 8/16-bit multivariate integer time series; beats Simple8b, FastPFor and SIMD-BP128 on ratio at GB/s decode.

name: stepreduce-rs (Rust port of stepreduce)
baseline: stepreduce C++ original (uses libstdc++ std::regex) by Seth Hillbrand
one_liner: Rust port of Seth Hillbrand's C++ stepreduce STEP CAD deduplicator; 5.2x faster than the std::regex C++ version, which has since caught up.

name: long.js (64-bit integer library with a WebAssembly fast path)
baseline: the library's own floating-point-based JavaScript fallback for 64-bit multiply, divide and remainder
one_liner: Closure-derived int64/uint64 class for JavaScript; a tiny hand-written WebAssembly module beats its own float-based JS fallback on mul, div and rem.

name: AMGCL
baseline: PETSc (GAMG); Trilinos ML; CUSP
one_liner: Header-only C++ algebraic multigrid solver library; sets up AMG preconditioners faster than Trilinos ML and PETSc GAMG on shared memory.

name: TOMLDecoder
baseline: toml++
one_liner: Swift TOML 1.1 parser and Codable decoder. In its author's harness, its lazy parse ran about 5x faster than toml++.

name: FFTW++ (implicit dealiased convolutions on FFTW3)
baseline: FFTW 3 with explicit zero-padded convolutions (and FFTW's MPI transpose for the distributed code)
one_liner: C++ layer over FFTW3 whose implicitly/hybrid-dealiased convolutions beat explicit zero-padded FFT convolutions in 2D and 3D.

name: S6 (DeepMind CPython JIT)
baseline: CPython 3.7 interpreter
one_liner: DeepMind's archived decorator-driven JIT library for CPython 3.7; first-party 7-9.5x on Richards, 5x slower on unpack_sequence.

name: Heartbeat Scheduling (deepsea-inria/heartbeat)
baseline: Cilk Plus (PBBS implementations)
one_liner: Research prototype of Heartbeat Scheduling (PLDI 2018): amortizes task creation against Cilk Plus-style eager spawning without manual grain-size tuning.

name: Cornflakes
baseline: Protobuf, FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto via the pure-Rust crates protobuf 3.0.3 (rust-protobuf), flatbuffers 2.1.2 and capnp 0.13.6 (cf-kv/Cargo.toml); Redis handwritten serialization for Table 3
one_liner: Rust research serialization library and kernel-bypass UDP stack that sends large fields zero-copy via NIC scatter-gather, beating Protobuf/FlatBuffers/Cap'n Proto.

name: qajson4c
baseline: RapidJSON, nlohmann/json
one_liner: C99 JSON DOM parser building the whole tree in one caller-supplied buffer; claims lower parse memory than RapidJSON (unpublished).

name: delaunator-cpp
baseline: mapbox/delaunator (JavaScript original), in its own README and PR #8; the repo has no C++ baseline (bench/run.cpp times delaunator-cpp only). A third-party table in the Delaunay32 README compares it with Triangle 1.6, CDT 1.4.5 and Fade2D 2.17.3.
one_liner: Single-header C++14 port of mapbox/delaunator for 2D Delaunay; about 10% faster than JS at 1M points, roughly matches Triangle.

name: jrsonnet
baseline: google/jsonnet C++ reference implementation (v0.22.0-rc1); also go-jsonnet v0.22.0-rc1 and Sjsonnet 0.6.2
one_liner: Rust Jsonnet interpreter, CLI and libjsonnet-compatible library; 1.9x to thousands of times faster than C++ jsonnet.

name: benc
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Pure-Go raw binary serializer with optional schema codegen; hand-written benc code runs ~3.5x faster than protobuf-go on small structs.

name: dennwc/varint
baseline: Go encoding/binary.Uvarint
one_liner: Fully unrolled Go LEB128/protobuf varint decoder, roughly 1.3x-2.9x faster per call than encoding/binary.Uvarint on Go 1.17.3.

name: LibFResample
baseline: libsamplerate (Secret Rabbit Code 0.1.8)
one_liner: BSD-licensed C polyphase sinc resampler for 16-bit mono/stereo using SSE2/AltiVec; roughly 8-13x libsamplerate at comparable bandwidth.

name: tickdb (DerekNest)
baseline: Parquet (zstd-compressed)
one_liner: Rust tick-trade store: delta-of-delta/varint+zstd segments ~20% smaller than Parquet+zstd, but slower than DuckDB on ingest and all queries.

name: space-pruner
baseline: scalar despace loop (despacer.h despace) and Lemire's neontbl_despace in the same app
one_liner: Two table-free ARM NEON in-place whitespace strippers, built as alternatives to Lemire's scalar and lookup-table NEON despacers; no published timings.

name: yuv2rgb (descampsa)
baseline: FFmpeg libswscale 3.0.0 (MMX path)
one_liner: Two-file C99 SSE2 converter between planar YUV420 (also NV12/NV21) and RGB24 that roughly doubles old libswscale's speed.

name: Random123
one_liner: Header-only counter-based CPU/GPU RNG family (Philox, Threefry, ARS); only AES-NI variants clearly beat std::mt19937_64.

name: libjpeg-turbo-rs
baseline: libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 (decode) and 3.2.0 (encode)
one_liner: Pure-Rust port of libjpeg-turbo with AVX2/NEON kernels that decodes a few percent faster than C on x86_64 and encodes at about C speed.

name: dp::thread_pool (DeveloperPaul123/thread-pool)
baseline: BS::thread_pool (bshoshany/thread-pool), task_thread_pool, riften::Thiefpool
one_liner: Header-only C++20 thread pool with per-worker mutex queues and stealing; first-party bench shows ~7% over BS::thread_pool 3.5.

name: FastOpenCV (fastcv kernels)
baseline: OpenCV 4.14.0 cv::resize (INTER_CUBIC, INTER_AREA), cv::transform and cv::pow, built from source by the repo's scripts with IPP disabled (WITH_IPP=OFF in every variant) and TBB threading at the default thread count; libfastcv is compiled against the linux-dispatch install, so the cv:: column is most likely that build, not a distribution build.
one_liner: Threaded cv::Mat kernels that replace OpenCV 4.14 resize (cubic downscale, integer INTER_AREA), transform and general-exponent pow.

name: OTFFT (OK Ojisan's Template FFT)
baseline: FFTW
one_liner: MIT double-precision Stockham FFT library for x86 (SSE2/AVX/AVX2) whose upstream author claims it beats FFTW at 2^1 to 2^24.

name: CacheAdvance
baseline: SQLite
one_liner: Size-capped append-only Swift log file (optional ring-buffer eviction); appends far faster than per-row-committed SQLite inserts.

name: Palanteer
license: MIT (instrumentation libraries); AGPL-3.0-or-later (viewer and scripting module)
baseline: spdlog (logging) and NanoLog; profiler instrumentation cost
one_liner: Single-header C++11 tracing/logging instrumentation plus viewer; enqueues a log in ~19 ns versus 1250 ns measured for spdlog.

name: Badger (BadgerDB)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Pure-Go embedded LSM key-value store using WiscKey key-value separation; 3.7x lower random-read latency than RocksDB in Dgraph's 2017 test.

name: Ristretto
baseline: The groupcache LRU (golang/groupcache/lru behind a sync.Mutex). The charts label it 'groupcache'; it is presumably the suite's 'base-mutex' entry.
one_liner: Concurrent in-process Go cache with TinyLFU admission and cost-based eviction; ~3x a mutex-wrapped groupcache LRU's throughput in its own benchmarks.

name: go-mph (Go, Hash-Displace-Compress)
baseline: Go native map[K]V
one_liner: Go hash-and-displace minimal perfect hash for fixed string sets; author reports 25-50% faster index lookups than a Go map.

name: DGtal QuickHull
baseline: CGAL convex_hull_3 (Cartesian and Exact_predicates_inexact_constructions_kernel)
one_liner: Exact-integer QuickHull for convex hulls in any dimension, inside DGtal; authors claim over 2x faster than CGAL convex_hull_3.

name: Admiral
baseline: FFTW 3 (FFTW_MEASURE, single thread; version and build flags of the system fftw3 not stated in the admiral repo, while the author's separate fft_bench uses FFTW 3.3.11); also ducc0 (commit c4dda23)
one_liner: Compiled C++20 SIMD FFT library (any size, 1-D/N-D, c2c/r2c/DCT); the author's sweep has it 1.34-1.43x faster than single-thread FFTW_MEASURE.

name: simdrng
baseline: std::mt19937_64 and std::uniform_real_distribution; also scalar xoshiro256++
one_liner: C++20 xoshiro256++, ChaCha and Philox engines with xsimd SIMD bulk fill; beats std::mt19937_64 per call and in bulk.

name: Ravi
baseline: Lua 5.3 (the dialect it extends; LuaJIT is named as a different-goal alternative)
one_liner: Lua 5.3 dialect with optional static types and a MIR-based JIT; typed numeric loops ran 10-26x faster than Lua 5.3.2 (old LLVM backend).

name: FAST+FAIR (Failure-Atomic ShifT + Failure-Atomic In-place Rebalancing B+-Tree)
baseline: wB+-tree, FP-tree, WORT and SkipList (single-threaded); FP-tree, B-link tree and SkipList (concurrent)
one_liner: Crash-consistent persistent-memory B+-tree using failure-atomic in-place shifts; range scans 6-33% faster than FP-tree/wB+-tree (emulated PM).

name: zita-resampler
baseline: libsamplerate (Secret Rabbit Code), named in the library docs as the comparison
one_liner: Real-time-safe polyphase windowed-sinc audio resampler (fixed and variable ratio); claims to beat libsamplerate, with no published numbers.

name: Futhark
baseline: Hand-written OpenCL reference implementations from Rodinia 3.1 (CUDA for Myocyte on NVIDIA), Parboil 2.5 (MRI-Q) and FinPar (LocVolCalib, OptionPricing); the four Accelerate benchmarks (Crystal, Fluid, Mandelbrot, N-body) were compared against Accelerate 0.15.1 (a Haskell DSL with a CUDA backend), not C/C++.
one_liner: Purely functional data-parallel language compiled to OpenCL/CUDA/HIP/multicore C; PLDI 2017 compared it with hand-written Rodinia, Parboil and FinPar GPU code.

name: pocketfft-tuned (benchmark-driven PocketFFT fork)
baseline: FFTW3 FFTW_ESTIMATE, upstream PocketFFT (ref 32424d2) and KissFFT; the fork is slower than FFTW_MEASURE and KFR
one_liner: Header-only PocketFFT fork with AVX float 1-D codelets: 2.4x upstream, 1.35x FFTW_ESTIMATE on 1-D c2c; loses to FFTW_MEASURE.

name: Ultimate Express
baseline: Express.js (Node.js)
one_liner: Express 4 API re-implemented on uWebSockets.js; README shows 3-12x Express req/s, but Node 24 narrows most gaps.

name: Dino
license: GPL-2.0-or-later (DINO interpreter sources; COPYING is GPLv2) and LGPL-2.0-or-later (AMMUNITION library sources; COPYING.LIB is the Library GPL v2)
baseline: Python 3.4.x and Ruby 2.1.x (also PyPy 2.2.x, SpiderMonkey 1.8.x, Scala 2.10.x, OCaml 4.0.x)
one_liner: Research scripting language and VM in C (RTL bytecode, type-inferred specialization, GCC-based JIT); beats Python 3.4 and Ruby 2.1 interpreters.

name: Dioxus (web renderer)
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust UI framework whose web renderer runs a WebAssembly virtual DOM; about 1.43x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark.

name: DiaLSM
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Hash-sharded LSM built on RocksDB 8.3.2 that reroutes writes around stalled shards, cutting write stalls ~94%. Code not released.

name: Zest (generalized Ziggurat sampler: normal, gamma, Student t, etc.)
baseline: STL <random> distributions (std::normal_distribution and the other std distributions) and Boost.Random
one_liner: Header-only generalized Ziggurat sampler for gamma, Student t, F, Weibull and custom unimodal densities; 2.5-10x faster than STL distributions.

name: BinaryFuseFilter (.NET)
baseline: Bloom filter (BloomFilter.NetCore package)
one_liner: Managed C# binary fuse filter: about 9 bits/key at 0.39% FPP, queried ~21x faster than BloomFilter.NetCore.

name: lexer-exp (SIMD NEON lexer experiments, dist1ll)
baseline: logos (Rust lexer-generator crate, v0.13)
one_liner: Hand-rolled NEON SIMD lexer for a toy language; beats the Rust logos crate 20-35% on Apple M1.

name: distcc
baseline: local single-machine compilation (make with every compile run locally); also plain distcc for the pump-mode rows
one_liner: Compiler front end that farms C/C++ compile jobs out to networked servers; beats a local single-machine make on big parallel builds.

name: walkdir and ignore walkers (dkorunic/bench_walk shootout)
baseline: GNU find (C), system find invoked as 'find <root>'
one_liner: Criterion shootout of Rust directory walkers; walkdir edges out a spawned GNU find, parallel ignore wins 3.7x with 8 threads.

name: minifind (dkorunic, Rust parallel find(1) reimplementation)
baseline: GNU find (findutils, C)
one_liner: Parallel work-stealing Rust find(1) subset that lists a warm Linux kernel tree about 3.5x faster than GNU find.

name: DLR-FT wasm-interpreter
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift), Wasmer (Cranelift) startup
one_liner: no_std Rust in-place WebAssembly 2.0 interpreter for safety-critical use; starts modules ~150x faster than Wasmtime/Wasmer Cranelift.

name: utl::parallel (UTL ThreadPool)
baseline: std::async
one_liner: Header-only C++17 work-stealing thread pool with recursion-safe futures; beats std::async on small and recursive tasks.

name: utl::json (part of the UTL header-only library collection)
baseline: nlohmann::json (also PicoJSON; beats RapidJSON on serialization tasks only, loses to it on most parsing tasks)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 JSON library, 2-4x faster than nlohmann::json at parsing and serializing; RapidJSON still wins parsing.

name: XGBoost
baseline: scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier 0.15.2 and R gbm package (gradient-boosted trees training)
one_liner: Multithreaded gradient-boosted-tree library; trained 3-9x faster than R gbm and 120-375x faster than 2015 scikit-learn GBM.

name: odiff
baseline: ImageMagick compare (and pixelmatch)
one_liner: Zig (formerly OCaml) CLI and Node tool that diffs screenshots pixel by pixel with a YIQ threshold; README times it 4.8-7.6x faster than ImageMagick compare and pixelmatch.

name: zlob
baseline: Rust glob crate, globset+walkdir, walkdir and ignore crates; README also claims glibc glob() is 1.2-1.7x slower
one_liner: Zig glob(3)-compatible globbing and parallel file walker with C/Rust APIs; about 2-3x faster than Rust glob crate and walkdir.

name: FunctionalPlus (fplus::keep_if)
baseline: std::copy_if (and a hand-written for loop)
one_liner: Header-only functional helpers (keep_if, transform, fold, compose) over STL containers; matches std::copy_if speed, does not beat it.

name: doctest
baseline: Catch2 (Catch 2.3.0 single header catch.hpp)
one_liner: Single-header C++11 unit-testing framework whose header and asserts compile far faster than Catch2 v2's single header.

name: DoltLite
baseline: SQLite (stock SQLite built from the reference amalgamation by test/build_stock_reference.sh)
one_liner: SQLite fork with a prolly-tree storage engine that adds Git-style branch, merge and diff; 1.1-2.9x slower than SQLite, not faster.

name: httpbeast
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Minimal multi-threaded epoll/kqueue HTTP/1.1 server core for Nim; about 7% above actix-web at 256-512 connections on hello-world.

name: faster-minuter (wt_fbb fixed-block-boosting wavelet tree)
baseline: SDSL wavelet trees (e.g. Huffman-shaped and hybrid-bitvector wavelet trees inside SDSL FM-indexes)
one_liner: Single-header SDSL-compatible byte-alphabet wavelet tree (wt_fbb) using fixed-block compression boosting, aimed at faster, smaller FM-indexes than SDSL's.

name: goja
baseline: otto (pure-Go JavaScript interpreter)
one_liner: Pure-Go ECMAScript 5.1+ bytecode engine; about 9x faster than otto on fib(35), far slower than V8.

name: llm.mojo (Mojo port of llm.c, CPU)
baseline: llm.c train_gpt2.c (karpathy/llm.c, with and without OpenMP)
one_liner: Single-file Mojo port of llm.c's GPT-2 CPU training loop; about 1.17x faster per step than the May-2024 train_gpt2.c with OpenMP on one M2 MacBook Pro.

name: Rain (Rainbow hash)
