baseline: HighwayHash-128 and FarmHash-128.CM (128-bit hashes in the SMHasher3 results table); the repo names no baseline itself
one_liner: Small scalar multiply-rotate hash with 64/128/256-bit output; beats HighwayHash-128/256 and FarmHash-128 only on short-key latency.

name: CRYPTOGAMS (dot-asm/cryptogams, perlasm crypto kernels for x86_64, ARM, RISC-V, PPC, MIPS, s390x)
license: BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-or-later (CRYPTOGAMS licence text with GPL alternative)
language: Perl-generated assembly (x86_64, ARMv4/v8, RISC-V, PPC, MIPS, SPARC, s390x, IA64, webasm)
baseline: gcc 4.8 compiled C (integer 'IALU' column) for the same ChaCha20 and Poly1305 algorithm; for Poly1305 the footnote says the comparison is against __int128 C code and gains over clang are about 50%
one_liner: Andy Polyakov's perlasm generators for ChaCha20, Poly1305, Keccak, SHA, AES and X25519 on a dozen ISAs; integer paths 1.4-3x faster than gcc output.

name: Kestrel (ASP.NET Core HTTP server, HttpArena kestrel entry)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG); h2o (C), agensio, proxygen, userver and Drogon (C++) rows in the same suite
one_liner: ASP.NET Core's managed HTTP server; in HttpArena it beats nginx on pipelined and cleartext HTTP/2 but loses on plain HTTP/1.1, TLS and HTTP/3.

name: .NET runtime (CoreCLR RyuJIT)
baseline: LuaJIT 2.1, PyPy 7.3.x and Node.js (V8) on kostya brainfuck in JIT mode; OpenJDK HotSpot only beaten in plb2 NativeAOT mode
one_liner: The .NET runtime's RyuJIT tiered JIT runs kostya's brainfuck interpreters 2-7x faster than Node.js, LuaJIT and PyPy, though still behind HotSpot.

name: CompV
baseline: OpenCV (cv::resize bilinear; cvtColor CV_RGB2GRAY, CV_YUV2RGB_I420, CV_RGB2HSV)
one_liner: GPL C++ computer-vision library with hand-written x86/ARM assembly; first-party numbers show 3-11x over OpenCV colour conversion and bilinear resize.

name: rte_memcpy (DPDK): SSE/AVX2/AVX-512 memcpy for small, cache-resident copies
baseline: glibc memcpy()
one_liner: DPDK's header-inlined x86 SSE/AVX2/AVX-512 memcpy for small, cache-hot, non-overlapping packet-sized copies, pitched against glibc memcpy.

name: VDT (VectoriseD maTh)
baseline: <cmath> (libm)
one_liner: Header-only Padé-polynomial libm replacements for exp/log/trig/asin-acos-atan/isqrt, auto-vectorizable, 1.3-13x faster scalar.

name: tracing_malloc
baseline: Valgrind (memcheck default tool)
one_liner: Linux LD_PRELOAD malloc hook that records live allocations with stack traces; far lower overhead than Valgrind for leak hunting.

name: Scheduling (dpuyda)
baseline: Taskflow
one_liner: Header-only C++20 work-stealing thread pool and task-graph runner, under 600 lines, benchmarked faster than Taskflow on fine-grained tasks.

name: Dragonfly
baseline: Redis, Memcached
one_liner: Multi-threaded, shared-nothing in-memory store that speaks the Redis and Memcached protocols; beats single-process Redis once there are many cores.

name: Lightstorm
baseline: mruby VM executing the same program's precompiled bytecode (tests/benchmarks/bench.py pairs 'lightstorm <bench>' with 'mruby <bench>' built from mrbc bytecode linked to mruby_static); the README chart labels it only 'Baseline'
one_liner: Ahead-of-time compiler from mruby 3.0 bytecode to C via MLIR/EmitC; about 1.4x faster than the mruby VM on aobench.

name: AESRand
baseline: std::mt19937
one_liner: AES-NI hardware-accelerated PRNG streaming 256 bits per iteration, far outpacing std::mt19937 in raw throughput.

name: chili
baseline: Rayon (rayon::join)
one_liner: Rust port of Spice: heartbeat-scheduled fork-join join() with far lower per-join overhead than rayon::join on fine-grained recursion.

name: Flat-Map-RB-Tree (dro::FlatMap)
baseline: std::map
one_liner: Header-only flat red-black tree map/set in a vector; 1.4-1.9x faster than std::map at scale.

name: Drogon
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Async C++17/20 HTTP/1.1 web framework on an epoll reactor; ~1.8-2x Go net/http req/s on hello-world.

name: fast_rsync (Dropbox, Rust SIMD rsync algorithm)
baseline: librsync (C), legacy MD4 signatures, called through the goffrie/librsync-rs bindings (whole::signature_with_options, whole::delta, whole::patch). The README numbers (commit 'Update README.md with newer benchmarks', 2020-03-01; v0.1.1) used librsync-rs rev ab9c427, which builds mbrt/librsync aed9ab6, a pre-2.0.1 librsync 2.0.x snapshot whose NEWS still lists 2.0.1 as unreleased. That snapshot has search.c and no hashtable.c.
one_liner: Rust librsync-compatible signature, delta and patch library; SIMD multi-buffer MD4 makes signatures about 5.5x faster than librsync.

name: rust-brotli (Dropbox Rust port of Brotli)
baseline: google/brotli C reference implementation
one_liner: Safe, no_std-capable Rust port of Google's Brotli encoder and decoder; slower than the C reference, not faster.

name: sve-string-routines-benchmarks (Arm SVE strcpy, strncpy, strcmp, strncmp)
license: LGPL-3.0 (repository LICENSE and harness sources); the routine sources derived from Arm optimized-routines keep Arm's header 'SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' (checked in string/aarch64/new/strcpy-sve.S)
language: Assembly (AArch64 SVE) with a C harness
baseline: GNU libc 2.39 string routines (strcpy, strncpy, strcmp, strncmp, strlen, memcpy as selected on Graviton3E) and the Arm Optimized Routines 23.01 SVE versions
one_liner: Research SVE assembly for strcpy, strncpy, strcmp and strncmp that times 1.3-1.6x faster than glibc on Graviton3E, but drops page-fault safety.

name: dstogov/ir (IR framework and JIT behind PHP 8.4+ JIT)
baseline: gcc -O2 (compile time; the README also reports the generated code speed against it)
one_liner: Small C JIT back end (PHP 8.4+ JIT) that compiles about 40x faster than gcc -O2 for code about 4% slower.

name: VkFFT
baseline: NVIDIA cuFFT (CUDA 11.7) and AMD rocFFT (ROCm 5.2)
one_liner: Header-only, cross-vendor GPU FFT library; matches cuFFT on smooth lengths and is ~1.5-3x faster on prime/Bluestein lengths.

name: QuickPHF
baseline: phf (rust-phf) static compile-time hash maps
one_liner: Rust PTHash-based static maps/sets generated at build time; ~2x faster lookups and 10x+ faster generation than phf.

name: DTVM (ZetaEngine lazy-JIT Wasm VM)
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift); also Wasmer Singlepass, Cranelift and LLVM
one_liner: C++ deterministic Wasm/EVM JIT for smart contracts. Its lazy JIT reaches first invocation about 20x sooner than Wasmtime's eager compile.

name: pure-rand (fast-check PRNG library for JavaScript/TypeScript)
baseline: JavaScript native Math.random() (Xorshift128+ in Node 16.19.1) and the seedrandom, random-js, chance and faker Mersenne Twister libraries
one_liner: Seeded JavaScript/TypeScript PRNGs (xoroshiro128+, Mersenne Twister, LCG) with unbiased ranges; author's shuffle benchmark beats Math.random 1.4x.

name: DuckDB (CSV reader)
baseline: pandas read_csv
one_liner: In-process OLAP SQL engine that queries CSV files directly, beating pandas read_csv + groupby on large files.

name: DuckDB-Wasm
language: C++ (DuckDB) compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten, TypeScript API
baseline: Arquero (JavaScript dataframe library) and SQLite WASM; danfo also in the table
one_liner: DuckDB's columnar SQL engine compiled to WebAssembly. Analytical queries in the browser run several times to tens of times faster than Arquero or SQLite WASM.

name: merge-spmv (merge-based CsrMV)
baseline: Intel MKL CSR SpMV; NVIDIA cuSPARSE csrmv
one_liner: Merge-path load-balanced CSR SpMV (SC'16) for CPU and GPU; about 1.2x over MKL on average, wins big on skewed rows.

name: gdu
baseline: GNU du -hs and ncdu
one_liner: Parallel Go disk usage analyzer (TUI, CLI and web UI); scans about 6.5x faster than GNU du on a cold SSD.

name: flatcc
baseline: Google FlatBuffers (C++)
one_liner: FlatBuffers schema compiler and runtime for pure C. Wire-compatible with Google's flatc, and roughly as fast as its C++ code.

name: jz (dy/jz)
baseline: V8 (Node.js) running the same JavaScript, plus AssemblyScript
one_liner: Ahead-of-time compiler from a static JavaScript subset to WebAssembly; about 2.3x faster than V8 running the same numeric kernels.

name: watr
baseline: wabt (wat2wasm) and Binaryen (parseText plus emitBinary)
one_liner: Zero-dependency pure-JavaScript WAT-to-Wasm compiler; about 3.6x wabt.js and 6.6x binaryen.js on one small module, in-process.

name: Dr. Memory
baseline: Valgrind Memcheck
one_liner: DynamoRIO-based memory error checker for unmodified binaries; about 2x faster than Valgrind Memcheck on SPEC CPU2006 per its CGO 2011 paper.

name: CBQN (BQN array language) - CRLF-to-LF conversion versus plain C
language: BQN (implementation in C, SIMD kernels generated with Singeli)
baseline: Plain scalar C loop for the same line-ending conversion (crlf_to_lf), compiled with clang 15.0.7 -O3 -march=native
one_liner: C interpreter for the BQN array language whose SIMD primitives beat a plain C loop 5-11x on CRLF-to-LF filtering.

name: xxUTF
baseline: ICU4C (unorm2 NFD normalization on UTF-8 input; also compared for NFC, NFKD, NFKC and case folding per README)
one_liner: Allocation-free C library for Unicode NFD/NFC/NFKD/NFKC and case folding; ARM NEON NFD runs about 3-4.5x ICU4C on non-ASCII UTF-8.

name: MultiFloats.jl
baseline: MPFR (via Julia BigFloat)
one_liner: Julia double/triple/quad-Float64 expansion arithmetic (about 106-212 bits) claimed 30x faster than BigFloat (MPFR) at 30 digits.

name: MultiFloats.hpp (dzhang314/MultiprecisionBenchmarks)
baseline: MPFR (also GMP mpf, CLN, FLINT, Boost.Multiprecision, QD, CAMPARY, libquadmath in the same harness)
one_liner: Paper harness with an AVX-512 header of branch-free double- to quad-double add/multiply that outruns MPFR, QD and CAMPARY.

name: libzbitmap
baseline: lzfse (Apple LZBITMAP reference implementation, not open source)
one_liner: Clean-room C reimplementation of Apple's closed LZBITMAP codec; format compatibility only, self-described as much slower than Apple's.

name: SafeRE
baseline: java.util.regex (JDK)
one_liner: Linear-time, ReDoS-proof Java regex engine; drop-in java.util.regex replacement, RE2 port, 2.22x faster on real-world workloads.

name: c4x86 (JIT variant of c4 by EarlGray)
baseline: Lua (LuaDist lua build, July 2015, version not stated)
one_liner: 86-line x86-32 template JIT for the c4 C subset; about 9.9x faster than stock Lua on a 2015 fib(34) run.

name: Parquet Sort (Earnix)
baseline: DuckDB
one_liner: Java CLI that sorts a flat Parquet file by one column; 1.12-1.26x faster than DuckDB on TPC-H lineitem.

name: Pure SIMD (pure_simd)
baseline: scalar_shader, the same per-pixel shader written as a plain scalar C++ loop in the repo's benchmark directory
one_liner: Header-only C++17 vector template that unrolls element-wise operators at compile time for compiler auto-vectorization; beat a scalar shader loop 9.4x.

name: eBay TSV Utilities (D)
baseline: GNU awk 4.2.1, mawk 1.3.3, GNU cut 8.25 and GNU Datamash 1.3 (all C)
one_liner: D toolkit of single-purpose TSV tools (filter, select, join, summarize) that outruns awk, cut and datamash on multi-GB files.

name: libdeflate
baseline: zlib crc32()
one_liner: Whole-buffer DEFLATE/zlib/gzip C library: about 2.6x zlib's decompression speed and 3.3x its level-6 compression, plus faster CRC-32.

name: msgspec-serde
baseline: FlatBuffers (official Python API)
one_liner: Rust-backed Python FlatBuffers codegen producing msgspec Structs; ~19-22x faster encode, ~11-12x faster decode than official Python FlatBuffers.

name: qbc (Quick adaptive Binary Arithmetic Coder)
baseline: Quake 3 / ioquake3 adaptive Huffman Huff_Compress()/Huff_Decompress() (~50k memory)
one_liner: Tiny adaptive order-0 binary arithmetic coder for short strings, pitched as a replacement for Quake 3's adaptive Huffman Huff_ functions.

name: Eclipse Cyclone DDS
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: C implementation of OMG DDS brokerless pub/sub over UDP; one 2023 vendor-adjacent test measured ~37x Kafka's small-message rate.

name: iceoryx (iceperf)
baseline: POSIX message queue and Unix domain socket (SOCK_DGRAM)
one_liner: Zero-copy shared-memory publish/subscribe IPC for C++ and C; sub-microsecond same-host latency versus POSIX message queues and Unix sockets.

name: Eclipse Mosquitto
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: Lightweight C MQTT broker; one 2023 vendor study measured ~2.7x lower 64 B latency than Kafka, but lower message rate.

name: Eclipse OpenJ9
license: EPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only WITH OpenJDK-assembly-exception-1.0
baseline: HotSpot (AdoptOpenJDK 11.0.7)
one_liner: Alternative Java VM (ex-IBM J9) whose shared class cache plus dynamic AOT starts Java servers faster, with less RAM, than HotSpot.

name: Eclipse Vert.x (HttpArena vertx entry)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', quictls TLS); h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma (C) and Drogon, userver, proxygen, agensio, cutelyst (C++) rows in the same suite
one_liner: JVM event-loop HTTP toolkit on Netty; beats some C++ servers on HttpArena but trails nginx, h2o and mongoose on scored profiles.

name: Vert.x gRPC server (Java): grpc_bench unary echo vs C++ gRPC (cpp_grpc_mt)
baseline: gRPC C++ async server (cpp_grpc_mt in LesnyRumcajs/grpc_bench): the stock async greeter pattern with one completion queue per server thread, GRPC_SERVER_CPUS threads and a single pre-posted CallData per queue; main.cpp and the generated code are built with g++ 15.2.0 --std=c++20 -O3 -flto and linked with jemalloc against Debian-packaged libgrpc++, libgrpc and libprotobuf (versions and build flags not recorded). It was the fastest of the run's three C++ rows (cpp_grpc_mt, cpp_asio_grpc, cpp_grpc_st) at 1, 3 and 4 CPUs and within 0.4% of cpp_asio_grpc at 2 CPUs.
one_liner: Eclipse Vert.x's own gRPC server for the JVM; served unary grpc_bench echo 1.75x faster than the gRPC C++ async server in one 2026 run.

name: Zenoh
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: Rust pub/sub and query protocol that can run with or without a broker; in one 2023 study it moved 10-65x Kafka's bitrate.

name: shoco
baseline: smaz (short-string compressor); also gzip and xz command-line tools
one_liner: Tiny C entropy coder for short ASCII strings; first-party 2014 timings show about 2x smaz's speed on English words.

name: zigg (lightweight Ziggurat normal, exponential and uniform generators with a C/C++ interface)
baseline: R's built-in RNG (rnorm, rexp, runif; base R default Mersenne Twister with inversion for normals)
one_liner: Small GPL C++ header (KISS + Marsaglia-Tsang Ziggurat) for standard normal, exponential, uniform draws; 4.7-7.4x faster than base R.

name: hx (binary-to-hex-simd, NEON table lookup)
baseline: naive byte-by-byte hex encoding
one_liner: Hobby Rust crate that hex-encodes bytes with an AArch64 NEON tbl lookup in inline asm, ~7.9x its own scalar loop.

name: sha2-wasm
baseline: hash-wasm (WebAssembly SHA-2 compiled from heavily optimised C); native C built with gcc -O3 -march=native
one_liner: AssemblyScript SHA-256/SHA-512, HMAC and PBKDF2 compiled to a 13 KB wasm; claims 5-7% over hash-wasm under Bun.

name: Rasm
baseline: SjasmPlus (Z80 cross-assembler). The README only says 'the best alternatives' and names no competitor; SjasmPlus is named in a CPCWiki snippet that could not be opened.
one_liner: Single-file C Z80 cross-assembler (Amstrad CPC, ZX Spectrum) claiming tens of millions of instructions/s; SjasmPlus comparison unpublished.

name: rsjsonnet (Rust jsonnet)
baseline: go-jsonnet (v0.22.0-rc1 per the doc; nix pin b5ef4cd9c4e24f2f14a68ef3bda0ca3079e11e78); also C++ jsonnet (d33798d4) and sjsonnet 0.6.2 in the same tables
one_liner: Rust Jsonnet 0.22 interpreter and library crate; about 4.8x faster than go-jsonnet and about 36x faster than C++ jsonnet across a third-party suite.

name: minicoro
license: Unlicense OR MIT-0 (public domain or MIT No Attribution)
baseline: POSIX ucontext (swapcontext)
one_liner: Single-header C stackful asymmetric coroutines with a hand-written assembly switch, about 40x cheaper than ucontext on x86-64 Linux.

name: Bourbon (learned index for LSM-trees, OSDI'20 artifact)
baseline: WiscKey (the authors' LevelDB-derived LSM with key-value separation; no direct stock-LevelDB or RocksDB comparison)
one_liner: LevelDB/WiscKey-based LSM key-value store that swaps SSTable index search for per-file linear models; 1.23-1.78x faster lookups than WiscKey.

name: pbtools
baseline: Google Protocol Buffers C++ (libprotobuf 3.6.1) and protobuf-c
one_liner: Python-generated C11 proto3 encoder/decoder with arena workspaces; beat libprotobuf C++ and protobuf-c on small messages at -O2.

name: libseff
baseline: Tencent libco
one_liner: C library of shallow effect handlers on stackful coroutines; OOPSLA 2024 paper reports about 2x faster generators than Tencent libco.

name: libcuckoo (cuckoohash_map, efficient/libcuckoo)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only concurrent cuckoo hash map with per-bucket locks; beats std::unordered_map only under real multi-core contention.

name: MemC3
baseline: memcached
one_liner: NSDI'13 research fork of Memcached 1.4.13: optimistic cuckoo hashing plus CLOCK eviction; ~3x read-heavy throughput, incomplete protocol.

name: MICA
license: Apache-2.0 (license text embedded in README; no separate LICENSE file in the repo)
baseline: memcached
one_liner: Research in-memory key-value cache/store over DPDK UDP; 65-77 Mops on tiny items per 16-core server, far above Memcached.

name: SuRF (Succinct Range Filter)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Static trie-based range filter (SIGMOD'18); beats Bloom filters on range seeks in RocksDB, loses on point lookups.

name: SerialXML
baseline: Boost.Serialization, cereal
one_liner: C++26 reflection-based struct-to-XML writer; author measures ~9.6x lower latency than Boost.Serialization/cereal XML archives.

name: RustFFT
baseline: FFTW 3.3.8 (via the Rust fftw crate v0.8.0, built from source by fftw-src without any SIMD configure flag, FFTW_ESTIMATE plan created inside each timed call)
one_liner: Pure-Rust SIMD FFT for any length, including primes; beats a scalar, per-call-planned FFTW 3.3.8 at tiny and huge sizes.

name: PureBLAS.jl
baseline: OpenBLAS (Julia's bundled build) and AOCL-BLIS (AMD's BLIS fork); the repo's gate is max(OpenBLAS, AOCL)
one_liner: Pure-Julia BLAS 1-3 plus LAPACK that matches or beats single-threaded OpenBLAS and AOCL on AMD Zen3/4/5.

name: Manifold
baseline: CGAL Nef/PMP mesh booleans (and OpenSCAD's CGAL backend)
one_liner: Apache-2.0 C++ mesh-boolean kernel with guaranteed manifold output; 2.5-6.9x faster than CGAL corefinement on 1.3M-triangle spheres.

name: fastquadtree
baseline: Rtree (Python wrapper of libspatialindex R-tree) and Shapely STRtree (GEOS); also PyQtree and other Python quadtrees
one_liner: Rust-core Python quadtree for points and boxes; NumPy-return path about 35x faster than Rtree, 4.5x than Shapely STRtree.

name: ConvectionKernels (CVTT BC6H decoder)
baseline: bcdec (also AMD Compressonator cmp_core, DirectXTex, SwiftShader, Mesa in the same chart; BC6H unsigned decode only)
one_liner: MIT texture-compression kernels (BC1-7, ETC1/2) whose scalar BC6H decoder narrowly beat bcdec in aras-p's 2022 single-thread test.

name: sme-gemm
baseline: Apple Accelerate (cblas_sgemm, which may use AMX); also candle and burn
one_liner: Rust crate of hand-written Apple M4/M5 SME GEMM kernels; edges out Accelerate sgemm/dgemm at mid-to-large sizes.

name: eastl::vector (EASTL)
baseline: std::vector
one_liner: EA's from-scratch STL reimplementation for games; eastl::vector targets faster push_back/indexing than std::vector.

name: ElementaryUI (SwiftWasm)
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: SwiftUI-style browser UI framework in Swift compiled to WebAssembly; 1.14x faster than React 19 hooks overall, all from swap rows.

name: SFFT3 (3-D FFT built from FFTW 1-D transforms)
baseline: FFTW3 own 3-D routines (FFTW_PATIENT on the Ryzen table, FFTW_MEASURE on the i7 table)
one_liner: 500-line OpenMP 3-D real FFT over FFTW 1-D plans; 1.2-1.3x faster than FFTW 3-D plans on large float volumes.

name: scnlib
baseline: std::stringstream / sscanf
one_liner: Type-safe scanf/istream replacement; ~3-5x faster than std::stringstream and sscanf at parsing ints, floats, and words.

name: EloqKV
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Multi-threaded Redis-API distributed KV database with ACID transactions; vendor benchmark shows about 4.5-8.5x single-threaded Redis throughput.

name: GBF-NEON (Galois Bipartite Filter, Ribbon-filter variant)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Static uint64 filter using per-block GF(2) solves and NEON parity; ~2x faster negative queries than author's blocked Bloom.

name: Elysia (Bun)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Bun-first TypeScript web framework; ties actix-web on a hello-world GET because Bun serves that route natively.

name: Embassy (async Rust executor) vs FreeRTOS
baseline: FreeRTOS (C RTOS, used through the CMSIS-RTOS v2 wrapper in an STM32CubeIDE project) on an STM32F446ZE
one_liner: Async Rust embedded framework whose cooperative executor replaces an RTOS; claimed smaller than FreeRTOS, latency win unproven.

name: CARMI (Cache-Aware RMI)
baseline: STX B+Tree and ALEX; also beats RMI on the SOSD benchmark platform
one_liner: Header-only, updatable learned index (a cost-model-built RMI) for numeric keys that beats STX B+ Tree and ALEX on in-memory lookups.

name: Hoard
baseline: Solaris default allocator, Ptmalloc (glibc malloc backing operator new/delete)
one_liner: Drop-in multithreaded malloc replacement beating Solaris/Ptmalloc via per-processor heaps and bounded blowup.

name: loguru
baseline: glog (google/glog v0.6.0)
one_liner: Two-file synchronous C++ logger with printf-style LOG_F; 1.8x lower per-line cost than glog 0.6.0 single-threaded, mixed under contention.

name: NanoGEMM
baseline: OpenBLAS (through NumPy 2.2.x sgemm / matmul)
one_liner: Tiny AVX2/NEON float32 GEMM C kernel behind a Python extension; beats NumPy/OpenBLAS call latency for matrices up to ~64x64.

name: em_inflate
baseline: zlib (inflate 1.2.11)
one_liner: Single-file, one-call memory-to-memory inflate for zlib, gzip and raw deflate; 11-16% faster than zlib 1.2.11 with checksums on.

name: lz4ultra
baseline: lz4 (lz4 1.9.2 -12 high-compression encoder, same LZ4 format)
one_liner: Offline optimal-parse LZ4 encoder whose standard LZ4 output decodes 1.45-1.54x faster than lz4 -12 output on enwik9.

name: LZSA
baseline: LZ4_HC (lz4)
one_liner: Byte-aligned LZ formats with an optimal packer: better ratio than LZ4_HC, and decompression as fast as LZ4 on 8-bit CPUs.

name: Granian
baseline: Uvicorn (httptools and h11 protocols) running on uvloop
one_liner: Rust (hyper + tokio) HTTP server for Python ASGI/WSGI/RSGI apps, with higher single-worker throughput than Uvicorn and Gunicorn.

name: Kaname-Shiki (MemoryAllocator.KanameShiki)
baseline: malloc (MSVC CRT), mimalloc, tcmalloc, jemalloc
one_liner: Small (2600-line) thread-caching general-purpose allocator for 64-bit Windows/Linux that beats the MSVC CRT malloc on its own alloc/free stress tests.

name: quic-zig
baseline: quiche
one_liner: Pure-Zig QUIC/HTTP/3/WebTransport stack; ~3% faster than quiche on handshake rate in one harness, slower almost everywhere else.

name: routez
baseline: nginx 1.30.5 (C) and HAProxy 3.2.23 (C)
one_liner: nginx-style edge server in pure Zig (HTTP/1.1, TLS 1.3, HTTP/3, proxy); beats nginx on fixed, proxied and TLS keep-alive rows.

name: bitdp (compile-time derived bit-parallel alignment kernels)
baseline: edlib (C++), ksw2 extz2_sse (C) and parasail scan16/diag16 (C)
one_liner: Zig compile-time generator of bit-parallel linear-gap alignment kernels; batched mode outpaces edlib, ksw2 and parasail on DNA pairs.

name: z-fasta (Zig FASTA index, extract and stats tool)
baseline: samtools faidx 1.24 with HTSlib 1.24 (C); also measured: fastahack, SeqKit (Go), noodles and rust-bio (Rust), pyfaidx (Python).
one_liner: Zig CLI that indexes and extracts uncompressed FASTA; builds samtools-compatible .fai indexes 6-21x faster than samtools faidx.

name: zipir (Zig streaming DEFLATE-family compression library and CLI)
baseline: zlib-ng 2.3.3 (zlib and raw DEFLATE), ISA-L igzip, and bgzip with libdeflate 1.26 or zlib-ng (htslib 1.24)
one_liner: Pure-Zig streaming gzip/zlib/raw-DEFLATE/BGZF codec in fixed memory; decodes zlib and raw DEFLATE about 1.24x faster than zlib-ng.

name: vanilla (V HTTP server)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG); same suite rows for libreactorng, libioma, h2o, mongoose (C) and Drogon, agensio, userver (C++)
one_liner: V-language HTTP/1.1 and h2c server engine on raw io_uring/epoll; about 1.31x nginx on HttpArena baseline, level with libreactorng.

name: libev
baseline: libevent
one_liner: Small, embeddable C event loop with io, timer, signal, child and stat watchers; halves libevent 1.4's per-iteration cost when timers churn.

name: dietlibc (qsort and bsearch)
baseline: glibc qsort and bsearch
one_liner: dietlibc's in-place 3-way quicksort and binary search; a 2001 changelog claimed 2.3x and 6.1x fewer cycles than glibc.

name: Envoy Proxy
baseline: NGINX 1.22.1 and HAProxy 2.7.3 as L7 reverse proxies
one_liner: CNCF C++ L7 proxy for service meshes and edges; in third-party HTTP/1 runs it is slower than NGINX and HAProxy.

name: SuperFast Codecs (fre:ac multi-threaded codec drivers)
baseline: fre:ac's regular single-threaded codec drivers: libopus (Opus), FAAC and Core Audio AAC in the initial release; FDK-AAC, LAME and Speex drivers added later
one_liner: fre:ac encoder drivers that run several Opus/AAC/MP3/Speex encoder instances on overlapping chunks to use multiple cores for one output file.

name: Enzyme
baseline: Adept and Tapenade (and AD on unoptimized IR)
one_liner: LLVM/MLIR compiler plugin that generates gradients of optimized IR; matched or beat Tapenade and Adept in its NeurIPS 2020 study.

name: minisearch-wasm
baseline: MiniSearch 7.2.0 (JavaScript full-text search library)
one_liner: Rust/Wasm reimplementation of MiniSearch 7.2.0 behind the same API; about 2x faster search(), 3.3x addAll, 7.5x autoSuggest.

name: mistral.rs (Rust LLM inference engine, CUDA)
baseline: llama.cpp (GGUF Q8_0 and Q4_K_M, llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1, CUDA backend); report also compares vLLM BF16
one_liner: Rust LLM inference engine on Candle whose CUDA build out-runs llama.cpp's CUDA backend on Gemma 4 prefill and decode.

name: range-v3
baseline: the issue's 'handrolled' implementation, marked '# base' in the reporter's table (its code is not shown, so it is not known to be a plain loop); the 'algorithm' row is a further comparison whose code is not shown either
one_liner: Header-only C++14/17/20 ranges library (basis of std::ranges); one bug-report benchmark beat an unshown hand-rolled loop by 3-13%.

name: Clipper2-WASM (clipper2-wasm)
language: C++ (Clipper2) compiled to WebAssembly, JavaScript/TypeScript API
baseline: Clipper1 WASM (js-angusj-clipper)
one_liner: Emscripten/Embind build of Angus Johnson's Clipper2 2.0.1; boolean ops 1.15-1.69x faster than Clipper1 WASM (js-angusj-clipper).

name: Box2D (v3.2 development, main branch)
baseline: Box2D v3.1.1 (previous release of the same library)
one_liner: 2D rigid-body physics engine in C17; the unreleased v3.2 steps the same scenes about 2x faster than v3.1.1.

name: BeamAsm (Erlang/OTP JIT)
language: C++ (asmjit-based JIT inside the Erlang/OTP runtime)
baseline: BEAM emulator (interpreter) without JIT, OTP 23
one_liner: BeamAsm: Erlang/OTP's load-time AsmJit template JIT, about 1.5x the BEAM interpreter's estone score on Erlang-heavy code.

name: Simd (ermig1979)
baseline: OpenCV (cv::resize and colour conversion) and libyuv; no published comparison found
one_liner: MIT C/C++ library of hand-vectorized image kernels (conversion, resize, filters) for x86 and Arm; no published win over OpenCV or libyuv.

name: ngi (N-gram Indexed Regex Search)
baseline: ripgrep
one_liner: CLI that builds a trigram index of a codebase to pre-filter files before ripgrep does the actual regex match.

name: WXInlinePlayer
license: Anti-996 License 1.0 (draft; non-OSI); package.json says ISC
language: JavaScript with C/C++ FLV demuxer and H.264/H.265 decoders compiled by Emscripten to WebAssembly and asm.js
baseline: FFmpeg-based wasm/asm.js H.264/H.265 web players: WASMVideoPlayer and the Taobao (Shoutao) and Huajiao implementations
one_liner: Browser FLV player that soft-decodes H.264/H.265 in WebAssembly/asm.js; claims lower CPU than FFmpeg-based wasm players.

name: eRPC
baseline: NSDI'19 paper baselines: FaSST RPCs and raw RDMA reads/writes (measured; eRPC is comparable but slightly slower), IX (per-core RPC rate quoted from the IX paper), NetChain and ZabFPGA replication (their published numbers), and the Cell RDMA B-tree (published numbers). The paper never benchmarks kernel TCP/UDP socket RPC or HERD.
one_liner: Kernel-bypass C++ datacenter RPC library over DPDK UDP or InfiniBand, near FaSST/RDMA speed on lossy Ethernet.

name: faf
baseline: lithium (C++) and cinatra (C++) in the TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext leaderboard
one_liner: Minimal Linux epoll HTTP/1.1 server in unsafe Rust that tied lithium and cinatra (C++) on TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext.

name: t1ha (Fast Positive Hash)
baseline: xxHash32 (also xxHash64 and the Murmur2/Murmur3 family) in SMHasher speed tests
one_liner: Portable C hash family (t1ha0/1/2) beating xxHash/Murmur on bulk throughput; modest edge on tiny keys.

name: fernBuffer
baseline: MessagePack
one_liner: Prototype bit-packed JSON encoder (C API over a C++17 core) that beats MessagePack on size for string- and key-heavy JSON.

name: ujson4c
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: Small C decode-only JSON DOM (UltraJSON decoder plus arena allocator); 4-10% faster than RapidJSON on citm/twitter, slower on canada.

name: SHISHUA
baseline: xoshiro256+ (also RomuTrio, wyrand, ChaCha8)
one_liner: Non-cryptographic SIMD PRNG for bulk byte streams; about 6.7x xoshiro256+ throughput on AVX2 Intel per first-party numbers.

name: ESP-DSP
baseline: The library's own non-optimized ANSI C implementations of the same DSP functions (the 'ANSI Xtensa' and 'ANSI Risc-V' columns), built with the same toolchain at -O2 and -Os
one_liner: Espressif's official DSP component: hand-written Xtensa/RISC-V assembly kernels for ESP32, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-P4 beating its own ANSI C versions.

name: ESP-NN
baseline: The library's own ANSI C reference kernels (selectable with the 'ANSI C' option under idf.py menuconfig NN_OPTIMIZATIONS) for TensorFlow Lite Micro int8 operators
one_liner: Espressif's int8 NN kernels in Xtensa/RISC-V PIE SIMD assembly for TFLite Micro, 1.4x to 20x over its ANSI C reference kernels.

name: LERC (Limited Error Raster Compression)
baseline: zlib deflate level 9 (labelled 'LZW' in the benchmark document; called through compress2)
one_liner: Esri's raster codec with a per-pixel error bound for 8- to 64-bit integer and float tiles; encodes far faster than zlib level 9.

name: FakeLua
baseline: PUC Lua 5.4.7 (LuaJIT not compared)
one_liner: Embeddable Lua 5.4-subset runtime that compiles scripts to C (GCC/TCC) and runs numeric kernels 30-40x faster than PUC Lua 5.4.

name: metapool
baseline: std::allocator (via std::vector), std::pmr::unsynchronized_pool_resource
one_liner: Header-only, TLS pool allocator with compile-time size classes; up to 1380x faster reserve() than std::vector, 3.6x vs pmr::vector.

name: zune-entropy
baseline: FSE library (Huff0 Huffman and FSE tANS modes), Yann Collet's FiniteStateEntropy
one_liner: Rust order-0 Huffman and tANS block coders that out-decode FSE/Huff0 on enwik8 at slightly worse ratio.

name: zune-png (zune-image workspace)
baseline: libspng 0.6.3 through the Rust spng 0.1.0 binding (spng-sys 0.1.0, 2021) linked to bundled stock zlib via libz-sys (zlib-ng feature off); libpng is not measured
one_liner: Pure-Rust PNG/APNG decoder (zune-png) that decodes 1.5x-2.7x faster than an old libspng 0.6.3 build in the maintainer's criterion run.

name: MuseAir
license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the Rust crate (Cargo.toml, README); CC0-1.0 for the algorithm and the museair.cpp reference (README)
baseline: xxHash (XxHash64) and wyhash
one_liner: Portable wide-multiply Rust hash: about 1.9-2.2x XXH64 and 1.1-1.3x wyhash on bulk data; XXH3 is faster in SMHasher3.

name: COSMA
baseline: Intel MKL ScaLAPACK pdgemm (also Cray LibSci, Cray LibSci_acc, CARMA, CTF)
one_liner: Communication-optimal distributed (MPI) matrix multiply with a ScaLAPACK p?gemm drop-in; beats MKL ScaLAPACK and Cray LibSci pdgemm.

name: COSTA (communication-optimal distributed matrix redistribution and transpose; ScaLAPACK pxgemr2d/pxtran replacement)
baseline: Intel MKL ScaLAPACK v19.1 pdgemr2d (matrix redistribution between block-cyclic layouts)
one_liner: MPI library for redistributing and transposing distributed matrices; link-time replacement for ScaLAPACK pdgemr2d/pdtran, 2-21x faster than MKL's.

name: SpFFT (sparse-input 3D FFT)
baseline: FFTW / MKL and cuFFT / rocFFT dense 3D FFT (implied; no comparison is published; SpFFT itself calls these libraries for its 1D/2D sub-transforms)
one_liner: 3D FFT layer for sparse (spherical-cutoff) frequency data that skips empty columns before calling FFTW/MKL/cuFFT/rocFFT; no published speedup.

name: SPLA
baseline: Intel MKL ScaLAPACK pdgemm (also COSMA and Cray LibSci_acc)
one_liner: MPI(+CUDA/ROCm) library for tall-and-skinny distributed GEMM with stripe layouts; outscales MKL ScaLAPACK pzgemm and Cray LibSci_acc.

name: Tiled-MM
baseline: NVIDIA cublasXt (vanilla and manually tuned with 4000 tile size and pinned memory)
one_liner: Out-of-core GPU GEMM on host-memory matrices for CUDA/ROCm; 2-4.7x faster than default cublasXt, on par with tuned cublasXt at n>=12000.

name: UltraSIMD
baseline: the benchmark's own scalar reference loops: scalar_dot_product_no_autovec / scalar_dot_{f16,i8,bf16}_no_autovec for dot products (volatile per-element loads, noinline, optnone under Clang), plain inline scalar loops for L2, cosine, Hamming, Jaccard and SAXPY; the whole benchmark target is built with auto-vectorization disabled
one_liner: Small x86 AVX2/AVX-512 header of dot, L2, cosine, Hamming, Jaccard and SAXPY kernels; beats non-vectorized scalar loops, barely beats auto-vectorized ones.

name: Lycon
baseline: Pillow (PIL) 4.0.0 and scikit-image 0.12.3 via their Python APIs; OpenCV 3.2+ cv2 (whose code Lycon reuses) runs at parity
one_liner: Small OpenCV-derived resize and JPEG/PNG I/O extension for NumPy; beats Pillow 4.0 and scikit-image, ties OpenCV.

name: ETL static containers (etl::vector, etl::map, etl::unordered_map)
baseline: std::unordered_map (the only container with a timing harness); also std::vector and std::map
one_liner: Heap-free, fixed-capacity STL-style containers (vector, map, unordered_map) for embedded C++03+; no maintained speed claim against std.

name: ETL fixed-capacity strings and algorithms (etl::string, etl::algorithm)
baseline: std::string
one_liner: Heap-free fixed-capacity strings (etl::string<N>) and STL-style algorithms for embedded C++03+; no speed claim versus std::string or std::sort.

name: bpftime
baseline: Linux kernel uprobe/uretprobe (the in-kernel dynamic instrumentation path used by perf probe, bpftrace and bcc)
one_liner: Userspace eBPF runtime that runs unmodified libbpf/bpftrace uprobe programs with about 13-16x lower per-hit cost than kernel uprobes.

name: Windowed Cuckoo Filter (WindowFilter, implements 'Smaller and More Flexible Cuckoo Filters')
baseline: cuckoo filter, Bloom filter
one_liner: Safe-Rust (2,2) windowed cuckoo filter: 12.8 bits/key at 2^-10 FPR, 12% under Bloom, 7-25% under cuckoo; slower inserts.

name: cblt
baseline: nginx (Docker image nginx:latest per benchmark/nginx/Dockerfile)
one_liner: Small Rust (tokio) static file server and reverse proxy whose '10x faster than nginx' small-file claim does not survive a harness check.

name: Guillotine (evmts)
baseline: REVM (Rust EVM interpreter) and Geth EVM
one_liner: Early-alpha Zig EVM interpreter with tail-call threaded dispatch; first-party runs show it 1.05-1.48x faster than REVM, about level with evmone.

name: EvoTrees.jl (Julia gradient-boosted trees) vs XGBoost hist (C++, CPU and GPU)
baseline: XGBoost v3.1.2 (C++/CUDA, 'hist' algorithm) driven from Julia through XGBoost.jl
one_liner: Pure-Julia histogram gradient-boosted trees (CPU and GPU); edges out XGBoost hist only in narrow table rows.

name: Codon
baseline: CPython 3.10.7
one_liner: LLVM-based ahead-of-time compiler for a statically typed Python subset; 10-90x faster than CPython, mostly ahead of PyPy.

name: tinywasm
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift, Winch, Pulley), Wasmer (Cranelift, Singlepass) and WAMR fast-interpreter startup
one_liner: Small safe-Rust, no_std WebAssembly 3.0 interpreter whose eager compile+instantiate beats every JIT runtime's startup, not WAMR's execution.

name: Expr (expr-lang)
baseline: cel-go (also compared against goja, govaluate, otto, gval, starlark-go)
one_liner: Statically typed Go expression language compiled to bytecode; about 1.3x faster than cel-go on a small boolean rule.

name: toml-spanner
baseline: toml (toml-rs/toml, the de facto standard Rust TOML crate)
one_liner: Arena-backed, span-preserving Rust TOML 1.1 library; parses ~9x and parse+deserializes ~3x faster than the `toml` crate.

name: RapidXml
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Single-header in-situ C++ XML DOM parser from 2009; about 4x libxml2's DOM parse throughput on 10-100 MB inputs.

name: zpp::bits
baseline: JSON serialization (RapidJSON)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 binary serializer using compile-time aggregate reflection; no schema, no codegen, faster than JSON via RapidJSON in third-party benchmarks.

name: Hana Jit (LLVM-backed Python JIT, hanajit)
baseline: Numba 0.66 (and NumPy 2.x)
one_liner: Alpha llvmlite-based Python JIT: ties Numba on scalar loops, beats it on call overhead and fused NumPy expressions.

name: zimdjson
baseline: simdjson
one_liner: Zig port of simdjson with streaming and reflection decoding; its On-Demand parser beats simdjson on 3 of 5 author benchmarks.

name: elfmalloc (allocators-rs)
baseline: glibc ptmalloc2 (glibc 2.19) and jemalloc (dev build, August 2017); also llalloc and rpmalloc
one_liner: Rust research malloc (elfmalloc) with a C API, faster than glibc ptmalloc2 and often 2017 jemalloc on multithreaded benchmarks.

name: frawk
baseline: gawk 5.1 (Linux) / 5.0.1 (macOS) run with -b, and mawk 1.3.4; one ad-hoc task also against a CPython csv-module script and a Rust csv-crate program (Python version not stated); xsv 0.13.0 and tsv-utils 2.1.1 also compared
one_liner: JIT-compiled AWK dialect in Rust with SIMD CSV/TSV parsing; runs AWK scripts several times faster than gawk and mawk.

name: F-Stack
license: BSD-2-Clause for F-Stack's main code, per the LICENSE file (GitHub reports 'Other'/NOASSERTION). Bundled components: DPDK BSD-3-Clause (kernel modules GPL-2.0), FreeBSD stack BSD-4-Clause, Nginx BSD-2-Clause, Redis BSD-3-Clause, libplebnet/libuinet BSD-2-Clause, inih BSD-3-Clause, Microthread framework GPL-2.0.
baseline: epoll
one_liner: DPDK kernel-bypass framework with a ported FreeBSD TCP/IP stack and epoll/kqueue-style API; beats kernel-stack epoll Nginx on RPS/CPS.

name: Zipp (Rust JavaScript and Python VM)
baseline: QuickJS-NG v0.16.2 (maintained QuickJS fork) for the interpreter; Node.js, Bun and Deno for the JIT builds
one_liner: Rust JavaScript engine (plus experimental Python frontend) whose interpreter ran about 1.6x faster than QuickJS-NG on its own suite.

name: FastBinarySearch
baseline: std::lower_bound
one_liner: Header-only C++ library for O(1)/vectorized insertion-point search in sorted float arrays, beating std::lower_bound scalar and SIMD-batched.

name: VMT19937 (V-family and X-family vectorized Mersenne Twister)
baseline: std::mt19937 and std::mt19937_64 (STL-MT19937 / STL-MT19937-64 rows); also the original reference MT19937 / MT19937-64 / SFMT19937 and Intel MKL MT/SFMT
one_liner: Header-only SIMD Mersenne Twister (MT19937, MT19937-64, SFMT); bulk fills 3.7-4.9x std::mt19937_64 on AVX2/AVX-512, X-family bit-identical.

name: Buck2
baseline: Buck1 (Meta's original Buck build system)
one_liner: Meta's Rust rewrite of the Buck build system; up to 2x faster than Buck1 in Meta's internal monorepo usage.

name: CacheLib
baseline: Memcached
one_liner: Meta's in-process C++ caching engine with an optional SSD tier; the authors report up to 60% more throughput than Memcached.

name: fbfft / fbcunn (FFT-based convolution for Torch7)
baseline: NVIDIA cuDNN R2 (layer-wise table); cuDNN R4 appears in the full-network tables where fbfft is slower
one_liner: Archived Torch7 CUDA module set whose FFT spatial convolution ran about 4x faster than cuDNN R2 on large-kernel layers in 2015.

name: fbthrift
baseline: Protocol Buffers C++ (protobuf; version not stated), measured with SerializeToArray, SerializeAsString and SerializeToZeroCopyStream
one_liner: Meta's C++ Thrift serialization and RPC framework; its Binary/Compact protocols encode and decode about 2-3x faster than libprotobuf in Meta's own microbenchmark.

name: folly F14 (F14ValueMap)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: SIMD 14-way probing hash map (F14) in Facebook's Folly library; 2-4x faster build/find/churn, 16x faster iteration than std::unordered_map.

name: Hermes
baseline: JavaScriptCore as shipped in stock React Native (start-up, memory, binary size); QuickJS for the throughput charts in the repo's own blog. V8, the listed baseline, is not compared on any page opened (Kudo/react-native-js-benchmark compares JSC, V8 and Hermes, but its results are in Google Sheets that are blocked here).
one_liner: Meta's AOT-bytecode JavaScript engine for React Native; roughly halves app start-up versus JavaScriptCore by skipping parsing at launch.

name: HHVM
license: PHP-3.01 AND Zend-2.0 (core); MIT (Hack typechecker and Hack Standard Library)
baseline: PHP reference interpreter (Zend Engine), 2014-era version per the OOPSLA 2014 paper (version not seen); HPHPc as a second comparison
one_liner: Meta's JIT virtual machine for Hack; reported 1.6x over the 2014-era Zend PHP interpreter on real applications.

name: libPhenom
baseline: libevent
one_liner: Archived Facebook C eventing framework (epoll/kqueue/ports job scheduler); first-party gut check shows 1.07-1.39x libevent events/s.

name: MyRocks (RocksDB storage engine for MySQL)
baseline: InnoDB B-tree storage engine (MySQL / Percona Server 5.7)
one_liner: Meta's RocksDB (LSM-tree) storage engine for MySQL: ~4x smaller on disk, ~5x InnoDB's TPC-C tps when cache is tiny.

name: OpenZL
baseline: zstd
one_liner: Meta's graph-of-codecs compression framework: format-aware compressors for structured data plus a native LZ that decodes about 2.3x faster than zstd -1.

name: Pyrefly
baseline: mypy; Pyright
one_liner: Rust type checker and LSP for Python; faster than mypy and Pyright on cold, whole-project checks.

name: RocksDB Ribbon Filter
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: RocksDB's built-in Ribbon SST filter: same FP rate as its Bloom filter in about 30% less memory, at 3-4x CPU.

name: Zstandard (zstd)
baseline: zlib
one_liner: General-purpose lossless compressor beating zlib/deflate on speed and ratio, with tunable levels and negative fast modes.

name: fbcuda / fbfft (archived)
baseline: cuFFT (NVIDIA GPU FFT library)
one_liner: Archived Facebook CUDA headers whose fbfft kernels batch tiny power-of-two FFTs; authors claim ~1.5x over cuFFT at CNN sizes.

name: Cinder (Meta's CPython fork with method JIT)
baseline: CPython interpreter: the same Cinder build with the JIT disabled (the README calls it stock CPython; the paper did not run a separate stock CPython build)
one_liner: Meta's CPython fork with a method-at-a-time C++ JIT and Static Python; 1.5-3.8x over its own interpreter on four microbenchmarks.

name: dispenso
baseline: oneTBB (Intel Threading Building Blocks)
one_liner: Meta's work-stealing C++ thread pool and parallel-algorithms library, faster than oneTBB on small/medium parallel-for loops.

name: Fizz
baseline: OpenSSL (via folly's AsyncSSLSocket)
one_liner: Meta's C++ TLS 1.3 library built on folly; Meta reports ~10% more load-balancer throughput than its OpenSSL AsyncSSLSocket stack.

name: go-qfext (Facebook Quotient Filter for Go)
baseline: Bloom filter (bits-and-blooms/bloom v3 Go implementation)
one_liner: Pure-Go quotient filter that keeps full 64-bit hashes plus optional per-key integers; about 3.6x faster positive lookups than bits-and-blooms/bloom.

name: mvfst
baseline: HTTP/2 over TCP (Facebook's prior production transport stack)
one_liner: Meta's C++ IETF QUIC transport (client+server) under Proxygen HTTP/3; cut Facebook-app tail latency 20% vs HTTP/2-over-TCP.

name: Velox
baseline: Presto Java execution engine (stock Presto vs Prestissimo, i.e. Presto with Velox C++ workers)
one_liner: Meta's C++ vectorized execution-engine library; as Presto's C++ worker it ran 3TB TPC-H queries 2-9x faster than Presto Java.

name: BaSpaCho
baseline: CHOLMOD (SuiteSparse)
one_liner: Supernodal sparse Cholesky for block-structured SPD systems with CPU and batched-CUDA backends; factors faster than CHOLMOD on its synthetic tests.

name: DietGPU (GPU rANS codec)
baseline: nvCOMP ANS (NVIDIA proprietary GPU ANS codec); the README itself compares against nothing
one_liner: CUDA byte-wise rANS encoder/decoder at 250-410 GB/s on A100; open alternative to nvCOMP's proprietary ANS codec.

name: FAISS
baseline: Babenko et al. CVPR'16 inverted multi-index search on CPU (Deep1B); Wieschollek et al. CVPR'16 GPU product-quantization search (Bigann)
one_liner: Meta's C++ library for approximate nearest-neighbour search over dense vectors on CPU and GPU; beat the 2016 billion-scale ANN papers 4-5x.

name: Wav2Letter++
baseline: ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq (other end-to-end ASR training frameworks; the paper compares training time per batch against these)
one_liner: FAIR's all-C++ end-to-end speech-recognition training toolkit; its 2018 paper claims faster training than ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq.

name: Bonxai
baseline: Octomap (octree-based 3D occupancy map)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 sparse, unbounded VDB-style voxel grid; first-party preliminary numbers show 4.5-22x faster inserts and iteration than Octomap.

name: ctx (2D vector rasterizer and terminal by Oyvind Kolas)
license: LGPL-3.0-or-later (renderer, ctx.h); GPL-3.0-or-later (ctx terminal), per COPYING on the mirror's dev branch
baseline: Cairo (with pixman); Qt6 also compared; Blend2D is faster than ctx in the same tournament
one_liner: Portable C 2D vector rasterizer (HTML5-canvas-style API, one generated header) that wins many heats against cairo and Qt6 but loses most to Blend2D.

name: HP-SpMM-SDDMM (fast GPU SpMM for GNN graphs)
license: Apache-2.0 via per-file headers on the HP-SpMM sources (spmm/mm/spmm_kernel.cu, spmm/mm/spmm_common.cpp, include/spmm/mm/*, test/*.cpp). The repo has no LICENSE file. The bundled starml framework headers (e.g. include/starml/basic/matrix.h, allocator.h) and include/spmm/utils/timer_cuda.h carry no license. The integrated GE-SpMM baseline code is MIT upstream.
baseline: cuSPARSE 12.2 SpMM (CSR ALG2, CSR ALG3, CSR default, COO) and GE-SpMM
one_liner: FP32 GPU SpMM kernel for GNN graphs (IPDPS'23 HP-SpMM); tops cuSPARSE 12.2 and GE-SpMM on 17 graphs on an H800.

name: libsrt (srt_vector sort)
baseline: std::sort (GNU/Clang std::vector sort) and C qsort()
one_liner: C container/string library whose srt_vector sort uses counting sort for 8-bit elements, about 5x faster than libstdc++ std::sort.

name: TinyScaler
baseline: Pillow resize (bilinear) and OpenCV cv2.resize (area filter); scikit-image also timed
one_liner: Python/Cython float32 RGBA image downscaler with SSE C kernels; beats Pillow by skipping antialiasing, loses to OpenCV bilinear.

name: FABE13-HX
baseline: libm sin/cos/sincos (the implementation <cmath>'s std::sin/std::cos ultimately call into)
one_liner: SIMD sin/cos/sincos array kernel for C beating libm; rational Ψ-Hyperbasis approximation, no bit-exact IEEE guarantee.

name: Lily
baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (per javascript/duktape/duktape.h in the scriptorium repo), built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG; the same table lists PUC Lua at 1.341 s, where this engine is slower
one_liner: Statically typed embeddable C interpreter; about 4.8x faster than Duktape 1.2.2 on 2015 fib(34), slower than PUC Lua.

name: fastrace
baseline: tokio-tracing
one_liner: Rust timeline-tracing library (successor to minitrace) whose span creation costs 19-151x less than tokio-tracing in its own benchmark.

name: FASTBuild
baseline: the same build without FASTBuild's object cache, Unity/Blob builds or distributed compilation (implicit; no baseline tool is named)
one_liner: Full build system combining object caching, unity builds and distributed compilation; replaces make/MSBuild, not a wrapper.

name: Binary Fuse Filter demo (FastFilter/FilterPassword)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Demo CLI pair that builds an mmap-queried binary fuse filter over HaveIBeenPwned SHA1 prefixes, with a Bloom filter for comparison.

name: Xor Filter (xor_singleheader)
baseline: Bloom filter, cuckoo filter
one_liner: Header-only C99 xor and binary fuse filters: static membership filters with fewer bits/key and faster lookups than Bloom/cuckoo.

name: xorfilter (Go binary fuse / xor filter reference implementation)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Pure-Go binary fuse and xor filters: static membership filters at ~9 bits/key (0.39% FPR) vs ~11.5 for Bloom.

name: fast_float
baseline: std::stod/strtod
one_liner: Header-only C++ from_chars for float/double/int; 3-5x faster than glibc strtod, exact IEEE rounding.

name: fasthqc/hqc (vectorized sparse-dense multiplication + syndrome generation)
baseline: HQC NIST Round 2 optimized reference implementation (Aguilar-Melchior et al.); HQC is a KEM historically supported by liboqs
one_liner: AVX2 patch to the HQC Round-2 KEM's sparse-dense multiply and BCH syndrome step; 34-46% fewer cycles than the optimized reference.

name: fCWT
baseline: PyWavelets (pywt.cwt), MATLAB cwt, SciPy, ssqueezepy, CCWT, Rwave (C), Wavelib (C++) and Mathematica CWT implementations
one_liner: Single-precision Morlet continuous wavelet transform on FFTW, OpenMP and AVX; README times it 10-120x faster than other CWT libraries.

name: Lite³ (lite3)
baseline: FlatBuffers
one_liner: Schemaless, JSON-compatible zero-copy C format: a B-tree in one mutable buffer; author runs beat FlatBuffers and simdjson.

name: MiniVM
baseline: LuaJIT (interpreter-only luajit -joff, and with the JIT on); the 2022 README also compares Node.js and C (clang -Ofast); the current test harness also runs PUC Lua
one_liner: Small C register VM running a Lua subset; 2022 build beat luajit -joff on fib(35) but lost to LuaJIT's JIT.

name: Web49 (miniwasm interpreter)
baseline: wasm3 (the fastest WebAssembly interpreter incumbent; wasmtime, wasmer, WAMR and V8 are not in the published charts)
one_liner: Small C WebAssembly interpreter (miniwasm) plus wat/wasm tools; first-party charts show it 1.06-2.6x faster than wasm3 in 2023.

name: genedex
baseline: rust-bio FM-index (bio large, sampling 32); also fm-index crate and sview-fmindex
one_liner: Rust FM-index for DNA-sized texts; locates short reads in hg38 about 4.4x faster than rust-bio's FM-index with a third of its memory.

name: Cista++
baseline: cereal
one_liner: Header-only C++17 zero-copy serializer for native structs; beats cereal ~48x serializing and ~670x deserializing flat index-linked graphs.

name: stb_xml
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Single-header, zero-allocation XML tokenizer for C; beats libxml2's DOM parser on raw throughput.

name: Ferron
baseline: nginx (C); the HN threads also name Caddy, Apache httpd and HAProxy
one_liner: Rust web server and reverse proxy with automatic TLS and built-in tracing; markets nginx-class speed but publishes no numbers.

name: FEX (x86/x86-64 emulator for ARM64 with JIT)
baseline: QEMU user-mode (qemu-x86_64 and qemu-i386); Box64 is faster than FEX in the same tables
one_liner: Usermode x86 and x86-64 Linux emulator for ARM64 hosts with an IR-based JIT; about 1.6-2.4x QEMU user-mode in a 2022 test.

name: FFmpeg (libswscale and filters)
license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (optional parts make the build GPL-2.0-or-later when configured with --enable-gpl, per LICENSE.md); libswscale and vf_convolution.c are LGPL
baseline: ImageMagick 7.1.1 (magick, convert)
one_liner: FFmpeg's libswscale and libavfilter (scale, crop, convolution) run the vips-bench crop/resize/sharpen job about 2.1x faster than ImageMagick 7.

name: mako (fg-labs, Rust SAM/BAM sorter built on the fgumi sort engine)
baseline: samtools sort (C, htslib), template-coordinate order
one_liner: Rust SAM/BAM sorter packaging fgumi's external merge-sort engine; claims about 1.9x over samtools sort in template-coordinate order.

name: Efficient Compression Tool (ECT)
baseline: zopfli (and gzip -9); the published benchmark is gzip/deflate on enwik8, not PNG
one_liner: Command-line PNG/JPEG/gzip/ZIP optimizer whose modified-zopfli deflate matches zopfli -i30 output size about 15x faster.

name: Firebolt Core
baseline: DuckDB and ClickHouse via the ClickBench leaderboard (Firebolt wins vs DuckDB on hot runs; roughly ties ClickHouse hot and trails it cold and on Combined)
one_liner: Firebolt's free self-hosted distributed SQL engine (ClickHouse-derived runtime); beats DuckDB on ClickBench hot runs, roughly ties ClickHouse.

name: Firedancer fd_sha256 batch (AVX-512 / AVX2 / SHA-NI)
baseline: single-buffer SHA-256: Rust sha2 crate (serial, hardware-accelerated) in the only numeric comparison found; no OpenSSL comparison found
one_liner: Firedancer's 8- and 16-lane multi-buffer SHA-256 kernels in C; about 2x the Rust sha2 crate on AVX-512 x86.

name: FireDucks
baseline: pandas
one_liner: NEC's closed-source drop-in for pandas: lazy IR optimization plus multithreaded Arrow kernels; first-party TPC-H SF10 claims 141x.

name: firenio
baseline: lithium (C++) and cinatra (C++) in the TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext leaderboard
one_liner: Java NIO/epoll network framework whose stripped 'http-lite' TechEmpower entry ties lithium and cinatra (C++) on plaintext.

name: NativeMinuit.jl (pure-Julia port of C++ Minuit2)
baseline: C++ Minuit2 (ROOT's standalone Minuit2 built through CMake, default Release, C++17) running MIGRAD on the same objectives
one_liner: Pure-Julia port of CERN's Minuit2 minimizer (MIGRAD, HESSE, MINOS) whose low-level MIGRAD kernel beats C++ Minuit2 6.24.0 on microsecond toy fits.

name: fkYAML
baseline: yaml-cpp
one_liner: Header-only C++11 YAML 1.2 DOM parser/emitter that parses 7.3-7.7x faster than yaml-cpp in the project's benchmark.

name: fmm-gen (Generating Families of Practical Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms)
baseline: Conventional GEMM. The public harness (the test driver emitted by meta/misc_gen.py) times the generated Strassen-like routine against the project's own BLIS-style dgemm (bl_dgemm in common/dgemm/my_dgemm.c, built on the same AVX 8x4 micro-kernel) and prints the effective GFLOPS of both. MKL is linked (-DUSE_BLAS, -mkl=parallel) only for bl_dgemm_ref. Whether the IPDPS 2017 paper also compared against BLIS or MKL dgemm could not be checked.
one_liner: Python generator for Strassen-like DGEMM variants that fuse the extra additions into BLIS-style packing and micro-kernels; claims wins over conventional GEMM.

name: tblis-strassen (Strassen's Algorithm for Tensor Contraction)
baseline: TBLIS regular tensor-contraction routine (Strassen level L=0 in the same code); TBLIS is itself the state-of-the-art non-BLAS contraction library
one_liner: Research code on 2016-era TBLIS: tensor contractions via one- or two-level Strassen, up to 1.3x over regular TBLIS.

name: Kanzi (kanzi-cpp)
baseline: xz
one_liner: Multithreaded BWT/context-mixing/LZ compressor with nine presets; beats xz -9 on compress speed at similar or better ratio.

name: FlashInfer
baseline: vLLM 0.2.6 PageAttention kernels and FlashAttention 2.4.2 (kernel-level, 2024 launch blog); Triton-based compiler attention backends in LLM serving (MLSys 2025 paper)
one_liner: CUDA kernel library for LLM serving (paged/ragged attention, MLA, GEMM, MoE, sampling); beat vLLM 0.2.6 PageAttention and FlashAttention 2.4.2 kernels.

name: Flashlight
baseline: PyTorch 1.8 and TensorFlow 2.4
one_liner: C++-native deep learning framework from FAIR (wav2letter successor) that trains standard networks slightly faster than PyTorch 1.8 and TensorFlow 2.4.

name: FlashRT
baseline: NVIDIA TensorRT, torch.compile, PyTorch eager, OpenPI reference implementation (numbers copied from NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and Jetson AI Lab pages, not re-measured in one harness)
one_liner: Hand-built CUDA-graph inference pipelines for robot VLA models (Pi0/Pi0.5, GR00T) on Jetson Thor and RTX GPUs; beats TensorRT latency.

name: FINUFFT (with cuFINUFFT)
baseline: NFFT3 (Chemnitz NUFFT library, built on FFTW); docs also name CMCL NUFFT
one_liner: CPU (and CUDA) nonuniform FFT library, types 1-3 in 1-3 dimensions, several times faster than NFFT3 and CMCL NUFFT.

name: FLINT
baseline: GMP (Chudnovsky pi, mpz matrix multiplication)
one_liner: C number-theory library on top of GMP; FLINT 3 (with Arb) computes pi about 2x faster than GMP and does integer matmul far faster.

name: VBCSR
baseline: SciPy sparse (scipy.sparse CSR/BSR) matrix operations
one_liner: MPI-distributed variable-block CSR matrix library (C++ core, Python API); README claims about 4.2-4.5x over SciPy CSR.

name: ART Synchronized (Optimistic Lock Coupling / ROWEX for Adaptive Radix Tree)
baseline: Masstree (concurrent B-tree/trie hybrid key-value index) -- not one of the assignment's named baselines, recorded honestly as the incumbent the paper actually benchmarks against
one_liner: In-memory concurrent Adaptive Radix Tree (OLC and ROWEX variants); roughly 1.5-3x Masstree's throughput on 8-byte integer keys.

name: Pipy
baseline: nginx
one_liner: C++ programmable proxy scripted in PipyJS; the vendor's single-core hello-world test shows 1.4-2.6x nginx keep-alive throughput.

name: Fluent Bit
baseline: Fluentd and Logstash
one_liner: C telemetry agent that collects, parses and forwards logs, metrics and traces; about 8x Fluentd's regex-parsing throughput per core.

name: Fluvio
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: Rust distributed streaming broker with a Kafka-style topic/partition log and in-broker WASM transforms; vendor bench shows 1.4-1.56x Kafka producer throughput.

name: pgregory.net/rand (sfc64-based replacement for Go math/rand)
baseline: Go math/rand/v2 (PCG source and top-level functions), math/rand, golang.org/x/exp/rand
one_liner: Go package pgregory.net/rand: sfc64-based *Rand whose draw methods run about 1.5-3.3x faster than math/rand/v2's PCG-backed *Rand.

name: {fmt}
baseline: printf (sprintf)
one_liner: Type-safe C++ formatting library beating printf/iostreams; its Dragonbox-based float formatter is the speed driver here.

name: micro-http (foldright)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Tiny tokio HTTP/1.1 server and web framework; matches actix-web on hello-world throughput, ahead ~2% only at 512 connections.

name: lexy
baseline: PEGTL (taocpp/PEGTL)
one_liner: C++17 parser combinator DSL that beats PEGTL on JSON validation by avoiding implicit backtracking.

name: libmorton (Forceflow)
baseline: libmorton's shipped non-BMI default (LUT Shifted) and its other LUT methods, as measured in morton-nd's fork of the libmorton test harness
one_liner: Header-only C++ 2D/3D Morton (Z-order) encode/decode; its BMI2 pdep/pext path beats its own lookup-table and magic-bits code.

name: fastsafetensors
baseline: safetensors loader using mmap
one_liner: Python safetensors loader with a C++17 pybind11 core that replaces mmap with parallel pread/GDS reads into GPU memory.

name: bitsery
baseline: Boost.Serialization and cereal
one_liner: Header-only C++11 binary serializer; 7-10x faster than Boost.Serialization and 4.7-7.3x faster than cereal in its author's benchmark.

name: RadixHeap (radix_heap_rust)
baseline: Rust std::collections::BinaryHeap (with Reverse)
one_liner: Monotone bucket-based radix heap for Rust; ~1.7-2x faster than std BinaryHeap<Reverse<u32>> for large random u32 heapsort.

name: PPy (Pretty Python compiler with LLVM JIT and AOT backends)
baseline: PyPy 3.11.15 (warm); also Numba 0.67, Codon 0.19.6, Cython 3.3, mypyc, Nuitka and CPython 3.14.5
one_liner: Ahead-of-time and JIT LLVM compiler for annotated Python; 1.27x faster than warm PyPy on one Collatz kernel.

name: vvdec (VVdeC)
baseline: FFmpeg native VVC decoder (FFVVC); also VTM and OpenVVC per the lead, but no numbers against them on opened pages
one_liner: Fraunhofer's optimized H.266/VVC Main10 software decoder; claims to outrun FFmpeg's native VVC decoder, with no published ratio.

name: VVenC
baseline: VTM-19.2 (JVET VVC reference encoder) and HM-17.0 (HEVC reference encoder); x265 v3.5 is also plotted but only in figures
one_liner: Fraunhofer's open H.266/VVC encoder; with 8 threads it runs 19x to 2400x faster than the single-threaded VTM reference encoder.

name: cw (Rust wc replacement)
baseline: wc from FreeBSD base (C) and GNU coreutils 8.30 wc (gwc, C)
one_liner: Rust wc clone with SIMD line and UTF-8 character counting; 1.5-70x faster than FreeBSD 12 wc and GNU wc 8.30 in 2019.

name: rust-linereader
baseline: Rust std BufRead::read_until / read_line / lines
one_liner: Small Rust buffered reader returning borrowed line slices; beats std BufRead::read_until and lines() for byte-oriented line scanning.

name: FreeBSD in-kernel TLS (kTLS) with NIC TLS offload
baseline: OpenSSL (conventional userspace TLS via SSL_write()/sendfile())
one_liner: FreeBSD in-kernel TLS record encryption, optionally NIC-offloaded, keeping zero-copy sendfile for HTTPS; beats userspace OpenSSL SSL_write data paths.

name: clcache
baseline: uncached MSVC compile (cl.exe without a compiler cache)
one_liner: Python ccache-style object cache for MSVC cl.exe that skips recompiling unchanged translation units on repeat builds.

name: io_uring-echo-server (frevib)
baseline: epoll
one_liner: Single-threaded ~200-line C TCP echo server on liburing, benchmarked in 2020 against the same author's minimal epoll echo server.

name: friendly-pow (Friendly Captcha proof-of-work solver in AssemblyScript)
baseline: the library's own JavaScript fallback solver
one_liner: Friendly Captcha's BLAKE2b proof-of-work solver in AssemblyScript WASM, claimed an order of magnitude faster than its own JS fallback.

name: libgrapheme
baseline: libutf8proc (the only library the repo's benchmark/ programs compare against: grapheme cluster break and UTF-8 decode); the README also names ICU and GNU libunistring, but no benchmark against them exists
one_liner: Tiny freestanding C99 Unicode segmentation and case-mapping library; claims to beat libutf8proc, ICU and libunistring, with no published numbers.

name: Axiom (C++ tensor library)
baseline: Eigen3 element-wise Array ops (A.array().sin()/cos()/exp()/log() on float32 MatrixXf)
one_liner: Lazy-evaluated C++20 NumPy/PyTorch-style tensor library for CPU and Metal GPU; beats Eigen3 on some unary math ops, loses on others.

name: frozenca/BTree
baseline: std::set
one_liner: Header-only C++20 B-tree (BTreeSet/Map) with optional AVX-512 SIMD search, ~5x faster than std::set on int64 keys.

name: Cyber
baseline: Lua (PUC-Rio), LuaJIT and QuickJS (also Janet on the fiber test)
one_liner: Embeddable scripting language in Zig with a C API; its 0.3 VM beat Lua and LuaJIT's interpreter on call and fiber microbenchmarks.

name: fast-http
baseline: http-parser (joyent/http-parser)
one_liner: Pure Common Lisp HTTP/1.x request/response parser; on SBCL its README shows it 1.25x faster than joyent's C http-parser.

name: hexdump-rs (Rust hexdump -C replacement)
baseline: system hexdump -C (C; implementation and version not stated, likely util-linux or BSD hexdump)
one_liner: Single-file Rust re-implementation of hexdump -C only; about 40x faster than the system hexdump on non-repeating input.

name: swisseph-wasm
license: MIT for the wrapper (LICENSE, Cargo.toml, deno.json), but the WASM compiles in Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 C sources (vendor/swisseph submodule of aloistr/swisseph), which are dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 or Swiss Ephemeris Professional License (the README calls it 'GPL/Commercial')
language: Rust FFI over C (Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03) compiled to WebAssembly
baseline: astronomy-engine 2.1.19 (pure-JavaScript astronomy library; version pinned in deno.json and benches/browser_bench.html)
one_liner: Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 C compiled to WASM through a Rust wasm-bindgen shim; beats astronomy-engine on Moon positions only (1.44x).

name: CircleHash64f
baseline: XXH3 (xxHash)
one_liner: Pure-Go seeded 64-bit hash from Abseil's wyhash-style design; beats seeded XXH3 5-13% at 4-128 B, 1.4-1.8x at 192-256 B.

name: juFFTe
baseline: FFTW3
one_liner: Fortran FFTE rewrite with Spiral-generated RISC-V Vector kernels; its authors report beating FFTW3 on RVV 1.0 chips, but the FFTW comparison is weak.

name: GLM (glm::mat4 add and multiply)
baseline: Eigen (Matrix4f, 2011 snapshot eigen-eigen-13a11181fc5a); CML 1.0.2 also measured
one_liner: Header-only GLSL-style C++ vector/matrix library; beat a 2011 Eigen snapshot on 4x4 float math, but only on ARM phones.

name: Density (density-rs)
baseline: lz4 (also Snappy)
one_liner: Pure-Rust block compressor using 4-byte hashed dictionary units; compresses faster than LZ4 at matching ratios, decompresses slower.

name: Daslang (daScript)
baseline: Lua 5.5.1 and QuickJS 2026-06-04 (the same table also has LuaJIT 2.1 with -joff, Luau 0.736, Quirrel 4.29.1, Mono --interpreter)
one_liner: Statically typed game scripting language with tree interpreter, C++ AOT and LLVM JIT; interpreter outpaces Lua 5.5 and QuickJS.

name: Quirrel (Gaijin Entertainment Squirrel fork)
baseline: Squirrel 3.2 (original); also measured against Lua 5.5.1, LuaJIT 2.1 with -joff, Luau 0.735, QuickJS-ng 0.16.2
one_liner: Gaijin's stricter Squirrel fork: about 1.28x faster than Squirrel 3.2 on the same scripts, still slower than Lua 5.5.

name: Gambit Scheme
baseline: Guile 3.0.11 (guild compile -O3); Chez Scheme 10.3.0 also in the same suite (Gambit is slower than Chez on aggregate)
one_liner: Scheme-to-C compiler and runtime whose executables run about 2x faster than Guile 3.0.11 on the R7RS benchmark suite.

name: memcpy_fast (gamesun): Cortex-M4 word and doubleword memcpy
baseline: the toolchain's standard memcpy on Cortex-M4 (C library not stated)
one_liner: Plain-C Cortex-M4 memcpy with doubleword and unaligned-word loops; 1.3-5.3x faster than the toolchain memcpy on 10 KB copies.

name: falkhash
baseline: xxHash (xxh3), wyhash, CityHash
one_liner: One-function AES-NI 128-bit hash for x86-64; 1.4-2.5x XXH3 bulk throughput, but 3-4x slower on small keys.

name: avxbls-sig (AVX-512 BLS signatures on BLS12-381)
baseline: blst (supranational/blst x64 assembly: blst_sign_pk_in_g1/g2, hash_to_g1/g2, pairing aggregation)
one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA BLS12-381 BLS signature code (keygen, sign, aggregate, verify) layered on blst; paper claims at least 1.57x over blst.

name: inspector-gadget
baseline: Ropper (Python ROP gadget finder)
one_liner: Multi-architecture ROP gadget finder in Rust; much faster than the Python tool Ropper on large binaries.

name: GaspardPetit SIMD base64
baseline: base64 (aklomp/base64, the reference SIMD-accelerated C99 base64 codec)
one_liner: Small BSD-3 C/C++ Base64 codec with AVX2/NEON kernels; edges out aklomp/base64, simdutf and Turbo-Base64 at 32 KiB.

name: learn-cuda attention (hand-written SM120 flash attention)
language: CUDA C++ with inline PTX (PyTorch harness)
baseline: flash-attn (FlashAttention-2 package) and PyTorch F.sdpa FlashAttention backend; PyTorch F.sdpa cuDNN backend is NOT beaten
one_liner: Educational ~300-line CUDA C++ FlashAttention-2 forward kernel; 4-6% faster than flash-attn on one RTX 5090 shape, 3% slower than cuDNN.

name: bc and dc (Gavin Howard)
baseline: GNU bc 1.07.1
one_liner: POSIX bc/dc in C, plus the bcl library; its bignum math beats GNU bc 1.07.1, its interpreter loop does not.

name: video_reader-rs
baseline: OpenCV VideoCapture and decord
one_liner: Rust-built Python video reader over libavcodec for ML loading; its own table beats OpenCV VideoCapture and decord.

name: diStorm3
baseline: Capstone, Zydis, Intel XED, bddisasm, udis86, BeaEngine (x86/AMD64 disassembler libraries); no GNU as, NASM or MASM comparison
one_liner: Small table-driven x86/AMD64 decoder in C; decode+format runs 2.6-4.2x faster than Zydis, bddisasm, XED and Capstone in disas-bench.

name: tokio-websockets
baseline: mongoose (C, gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto, OpenSSL backend, epoll, one mg_mgr per core) and ringzero-ws (C, io_uring); proxygen (C++) rows in the same HttpArena suite
one_liner: Strict RFC 6455 WebSocket client/server crate for Tokio; ties or edges mongoose (C) on HttpArena small-message echo.

name: RE/flex
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Flex-style C++ lexer generator plus a multi-engine regex matcher library; DFA scanners far outrun std::regex, PCRE2, and Boost.Regex at tokenizing.

name: ugrep (with ugrep-indexer)
baseline: ripgrep
one_liner: ugrep-indexer builds Bloom-filter file indexes so ugrep's cold recursive search skips non-matching files, beating ripgrep.

name: math_intrinsics
baseline: C standard library scalar float math functions (acosf, asinf, atanf, cbrtf, cosf, sinf, expf, exp2f, logf, log2f); libc and compiler not stated
one_liner: Single C header of branchless AVX2 (8-lane) and NEON (4-lane) float32 sin, cos, exp, log, pow and more; libm comparison is not like-for-like.

name: volesti
baseline: VINCI 1.0.5 (exact polytope volume; package birkhoff for the Birkhoff polytopes) and Cousins and Vempala's Matlab volume implementation (reference [13] in the text; the Table 7 caption labels it [12], their SODA 2014 Gaussian-volume paper)
one_liner: Randomised C++ volume estimation and sampling for high-dimensional convex polytopes; orders of magnitude faster than exact VINCI above about 10 dimensions.

name: Canvas-Txt v5
baseline: canvas-hypertxt (standard measuring mode)
one_liner: Canvas 2D text-box layout for JavaScript that wraps text about 9-11x faster than canvas-hypertxt's measuring mode by caching word widths.

name: FastReader
baseline: std::ifstream
one_liner: Windows memory-mapped line reader using memchr; ~4x faster line iteration than std::ifstream::getline on a 9 KB file.

name: geo-index (packed immutable R-tree and k-d tree)
baseline: rstar (georust dynamic R-tree, bulk_load)
one_liner: Packed, immutable 2D R-tree and k-d tree crate (Rust port of flatbush/kdbush); builds about 2x faster than rstar bulk_load.

name: jpeg-nitro (nitrojpeg and nitropng parallel decoders)
baseline: libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 (TurboJPEG 3 API, SIMD, one thread) for JPEG; Wuffs (unpinned wuffs-unsupported-snapshot.c, decoding to BGRA) for PNG; libpng is not measured
one_liner: Parallel single-image baseline JPEG and 8-bit PNG decoders in C; one-thread speed equals libjpeg-turbo, all-core latency ~9x lower.

name: reflect-cpp
baseline: RapidJSON, nlohmann/json
one_liner: C++20 reflection serializer that reads JSON into structs through embedded yyjson; claims ~2x hand-written RapidJSON, ~10x nlohmann/json.

name: pgl (Pangolin plane geometry library)
baseline: CGAL 6.1.2 (Delaunay_triangulation_2, convex_hull_2, Kd_tree, AABB_tree, Arrangement_2, General_polygon_set_2, minkowski_sum_2; EPECK and EPICK kernels)
one_liner: Header-only, exact 2D geometry library (MIT) that beats CGAL on segment intersection, arrangements and unions, loses on Delaunay.

name: Timsort (gfx::timsort, cpp-TimSort)
baseline: std::sort and std::stable_sort (also std::inplace_merge for gfx::timmerge)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 TimSort and TimSort-merge; beats std::sort/std::stable_sort only on presorted, reversed or run-structured input.

name: Anti-Grain Geometry (AGG 2.6)
baseline: Skia (CPU pipeline) and Cairo 1.18.4
one_liner: Classic scalar C++ template 2D rasterizer; an independent bl_bench run puts it ~1.2x Skia and ~2.3x Cairo single-threaded.

name: BLASFEO
baseline: Intel MKL and OpenBLAS (level-3 BLAS and LAPACK routines on small matrices)
one_liner: C BLAS/LAPACK subset tuned for cache-resident small matrices; 2-3x faster than OpenBLAS/BLIS at sizes in the tens.

name: TurboRoutine
baseline: POSIX ucontext (swapcontext)
one_liner: Small x86-64 Linux C library for stackful coroutines with an assembly context switch; README claims about 70x faster round trips than swapcontext.

name: SimpleSIMD
baseline: naive scalar loop over int[] (Sum), BenchmarkDotNet 'Naive' row
one_liner: C# .NET 7 generic Vector<T> span helpers (Sum, Min/Max, Dot, elementwise); about 6x a naive int loop.

name: zip.js (@zip.js/zip.js WebAssembly zlib codec)
language: JavaScript with bundled WebAssembly zlib and AES codecs
baseline: zip.js's own pure-JavaScript zlib port, jszip (pako) and fflate; also native CompressionStream and node:zlib shown for reference
one_liner: ZIP library whose bundled WebAssembly zlib inflates about 2x faster than pako/jszip and its own JS port.

name: fast_zlib
baseline: zlib 1.2.11 (stock deflate, level 9)
one_liner: Drop-in replacement for zlib's longest_match() that makes level 6-9 deflate about 2.5-10x faster on the author's data, output still standard deflate.

name: addr2line (gimli-rs)
baseline: GNU binutils addr2line (also elfutils eu-addr2line and llvm-addr2line)
one_liner: Rust DWARF symbolication library plus addr2line-style CLI; first-party chart shows it beating binutils, elfutils and llvm-addr2line.

name: Ginkgo
baseline: NVIDIA AmgX; MAGMA batched dense; MA57; LAPACK dgbsv
one_liner: C++17 sparse linear algebra library with portable CUDA/HIP/SYCL/OpenMP kernels; beat AmgX AMG and MAGMA batched solves in DOE apps.

name: giotto-ph (giotto-ai)
baseline: Ripser v1.2 (Ripser/ripser by Ulrich Bauer); also compared with GPU Ripser++ according to the release notes
one_liner: Multithreaded lock-free Vietoris-Rips persistent homology (Python API, C++ backend) that outruns single-threaded Ripser v1.2 when given several cores.

name: Pool-allocator string (Dicanio STL/ATL/Pool string benchmark)
baseline: std::string
one_liner: Fixed-chunk pool allocator for bulk wide-char strings, beating ATL CStringW and std::wstring on creation.

name: geo-utils-cpp
baseline: Boost.Geometry 1.90 (spherical_equatorial strategy: bg::within and bg::area); also S2 Geometry 0.14.0 and GeographicLib 2.7
one_liner: Header-only C++17 port of Google Maps' spherical geometry utils; beats Boost.Geometry's spherical strategies on area and point-in-polygon.

name: tup
baseline: Make
one_liner: File-based build tool that beats Make's incremental-rebuild scanning via a persistent Linux-only file monitor and per-command sandboxing.

name: E9Patch
baseline: Dyninst
one_liner: Static x86_64 ELF binary rewriter that skips control-flow recovery; more robust and scalable than Dyninst-style rewriters, but not faster.

name: gkurt/quickjs (performance-optimised QuickJS-NG fork)
baseline: Upstream quickjs-ng master (QuickJS-NG, the maintained fork of Bellard's QuickJS)
one_liner: Personal QuickJS-NG fork with inline caches and interpreter fast paths; Octane 2022 to 2385 (+18%) against upstream quickjs-ng on CI.

name: jsColorEngine
baseline: Little CMS 2 (lcms2 2.18 native built with gcc at -O2 and -O3; lcms-wasm = LittleCMS 2.16 compiled to WebAssembly)
one_liner: Pure-JavaScript ICC colour engine with WebAssembly SIMD CLUT kernels; 3.1-3.6x faster than lcms-wasm on 8-bit LUT image transforms.

name: canvas-hypertxt
baseline: canvas-txt (JavaScript canvas multi-line text library)
one_liner: Zero-dependency JavaScript line breaker for HTML5 canvas text; up to 9.8x faster than canvas-txt 3.x (19x with HyperWrapping).

name: greenpack
baseline: Protocol Buffers (Go implementations: gogo/protobuf gogofaster, golang/protobuf, DeDiS/protobuf); FlatBuffers Go and Cap'n Proto Go are also in the table
one_liner: Go msgpack2 code generator with versioned, typed field names; ~15% faster writes than gogo/protobuf in author's 2017 benchmark.

name: sofia-ml
baseline: SVM-perf (SVM-perf-roc), SVM-light and SVM-struct-rank (Joachims' RankSVM solvers); for data parsing, Shalev-Shwartz's reference Pegasos and svm_perf
one_liner: Stochastic pairwise-descent linear SVM and ranking trainer for sparse data; about 160x faster than SVM-perf RankSVM on RCV1.

name: ZebraPack
baseline: Protocol Buffers (golang/protobuf, gogo/protobuf, DeDiS/protobuf), Cap'n Proto (glycerine/go-capnproto v1, zombiezen capnproto2), FlatBuffers
one_liner: Go code generator for a msgpack2 format with integer field keys; marshals ~1.3-4x faster than Go protobuf libraries

name: @gmod/inflate (wasm libdeflate batch inflate)
language: Rust (libdeflater compiled to WebAssembly) with TypeScript
baseline: pako 3.x inflateRaw (pure JavaScript inflate in V8), called once per block with a chunkSize hint. Both arms skip the 2-byte zlib header and leave adler32 unchecked.
one_liner: libdeflate compiled to WebAssembly for JS, inflating many raw-deflate blocks per call; about 2-3x faster than pako on BigWig blocks.

name: babl
baseline: Little CMS 2 (lcms2)
one_liner: GIMP/GEGL's C pixel-format and matrix+TRC colour-space converter. GIMP claims up to 10x over LCMS2; no published benchmark backs it, and an lcms2 test found babl slower.

name: libRSVG
baseline: resvg 0.8.0 (cairo, Qt, raqote and Skia backends) and QtSvg 5.12.3
one_liner: GNOME's Rust SVG renderer onto Cairo; beat resvg 0.8.0 on blur- and clip-heavy icons, lost on simple ones.

name: GNU gperf
baseline: std::unordered_map<std::string_view, int> (std::hash in the perfect_hashing harness; boost::hash in the qlibs/mph README nanobench tables)
one_liner: Build-time generator of perfect-hash C/C++ lookup code for fixed keyword sets; about 2-5x faster lookups than std::unordered_map in third-party tests.

name: GNU Guile
baseline: Lua 5.4.7 (PUC-Rio). The same table also lists LuaJIT 2.1.1, Janet 1.36.0 and Tcl 9.0.0.
one_liner: GNU's embeddable Scheme with a JIT; about 2x faster than PUC Lua 5.4.7 on a naive fib(47) shootout.

name: Nettle (assembly for x86_64, arm64, powerpc64, s390x)
language: C with assembly (arm, arm64, powerpc64, s390x, sparc64, x86, x86_64 directories)
baseline: Nettle's own previous code: the generic C implementations for the PowerPC64 AES, GCM and Chacha figures (Nettle had no PowerPC64 assembly before 3.7), and Nettle's earlier plain x86_64 assembly for the sha_ni SHA-1/SHA-256 figure (x86_64 SHA1 assembly since Nettle 2.0, SHA256 since 2.7)
one_liner: Nettle's runtime-dispatched assembly for AES, GCM, ChaCha and SHA, using CPU crypto instructions; beats Nettle's own table C up to 13x on POWER9.

name: go-fft
baseline: FFTW 3.3.11 (native C, FFTW_MEASURE, threads=1); also numpy.fft, scipy.fft (pocketfft) and gonum/dsp/fourier
one_liner: Pure-Go (no cgo) float64 FFT for any length; fastest pure-Go option, behind FFTW on most single-core 1-D sizes.

name: go-gfx (resample package)
baseline: Pillow 12.2.0 Image.resize (BICUBIC, LANCZOS, BOX)
one_liner: Pure-Go (CGO=0) RGBA resizer whose multicore Bicubic/Lanczos beat single-thread Pillow 12.2 1.7-4.9x; its serial Box loses.

name: go-images/images (RGB to HSV and box-blur kernels)
