baseline: scikit-image 0.26.0 (rgb2hsv, scipy.ndimage.uniform_filter); OpenCV 4.13.0 also measured and is faster
one_liner: Pure-Go (CGO=0) scikit-image-style image library; first-party table shows RGB to HSV and box blur 2-5x faster than float64 scikit-image, far slower than OpenCV.

name: go-simd/utf8
baseline: Go standard library unicode/utf8 package
one_liner: Pure-Go SIMD UTF-8 validator and rune counter, byte-identical to unicode/utf8, faster on non-ASCII text.

name: go-json
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Import-swap replacement for Go's encoding/json; unmarshalled typed structs ~2x faster than encoding/json in one third-party benchmark.

name: wasm2go
baseline: wazero (an equivalent wazero-driven build of the same wasm module)
one_liner: Ahead-of-time WebAssembly-to-Go translator; on its author's SQL engine it beats wazero on startup and call-heavy queries, ties on long scans.

name: hardware-rust-crypto
baseline: ring (BoringSSL-derived) and RustCrypto aes-gcm crate
one_liner: Hardware-only AES-256-GCM/GCM-SIV crate for Rust with compact, zeroized key state; faster than ring and RustCrypto on Apple M4.

name: gofiber/utils v2 simd package (AVX2 Memchr2, Memchr3, Memmem, IsASCII for Go)
baseline: Go standard library, per simd/bench_test.go: bytes.Contains (bytes.Index) for Memmem; bytes.ContainsAny(data, "zy") and bytes.ContainsAny(data, "zyx") for Memchr2 and Memchr3 (a per-byte ASCII-set loop, not a vectorised search); the package's own scalar loops (memchr2Generic, memchr3Generic) and SWAR fallbacks as second baselines. bytes.IndexByte is deliberately not wrapped because the Go runtime already vectorises it.
one_liner: Go package with AVX2 assembly multi-byte, class, ASCII and substring scans on []byte; beats bytes.ContainsAny, bytes.Index and its own SWAR loops above 64 bytes.

name: PsiTri (arbtrie)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: C++20 embedded transactional KV store (radix trie, node-level COW) with a RocksDB-API shim; 1.6-3x RocksDB on bank transfers.

name: psio / pSSZ (successor to fracpack)
baseline: Protobuf, Cap'n Proto, FlatBuffers, MessagePack
one_liner: C++23 reflection-driven, SSZ-derived binary format with zero-copy views; author benchmarks show faster encode/decode than libprotobuf, capnp, FlatBuffers, msgpack.

name: AlphaDev sort3-sort8 assembly programs (libc++ branchless sort3/4/5)
language: Python (RL pseudo-code) / C++ test harness with x86-64 assembly sort programs
baseline: libc++ std::sort with its previous __sort3/__sort4/__sort5 helpers
one_liner: RL-discovered x86-64 cmov sorting kernels for 3-8 ints; the branchless sort3/4/5 form now sits inside libc++ std::sort.

name: Sputnik (sparse GPU kernels for deep learning: SpMM and SDDMM)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpMM
one_liner: CUDA SpMM and SDDMM kernels tuned for the moderate sparsity of pruned neural networks; several times faster than cuSPARSE SpMM.

name: AFL (american fuzzy lop)
baseline: blind fuzzing (random mutation without coverage guidance)
one_liner: Original coverage-guided fuzzer: edge-coverage feedback plus a fork server; far more code reached than blind mutation fuzzing.

name: BoringSSL
baseline: OpenSSL 1.1.1-dev (pre-release 9 master, 2018)
one_liner: Google's OpenSSL fork, the TLS and crypto library of Chrome and Android; only weak, mixed evidence that it beats OpenSSL on RSA/ECDSA.

name: CityHash
baseline: MurmurHash2/MurmurHash3 (Murmur2, Murmur3F, Murmur3A) — widely-used non-cryptographic hash functions used in place of std::hash
one_liner: Non-cryptographic 64/128-bit string hash family beating Murmur2/Murmur3F, ~1.7-2.5x faster at 64 bytes.

name: google/double-conversion
baseline: std::ostringstream (iostreams); page's headline ratio is vs sprintf()
one_liner: Grisu3-based double<->string library extracted from V8; beats sprintf/ostringstream, covers both to_chars- and from_chars-like directions.

name: FarmHash
baseline: CityHash, xxHash (xxh3)
one_liner: Google's CityHash successor. Its SSE4.1 32-bit hash is 3.9x City32 and ~6% faster than XXH3 on large x86-64 inputs.

name: FlatBuffers
baseline: protoc
one_liner: Zero-copy binary serialization with schema-generated accessors; reads fields in place without unpacking, unlike protoc.

name: Gipfeli
baseline: zlib
one_liner: Archived Google LZ77 compressor with a light static entropy stage, claimed about 5x faster than zlib.

name: glog
baseline: Boost.Log 1.56 (trivial severity logger, text file sink)
one_liner: Google's synchronous C++ stream logger (LOG, CHECK, VLOG); about 4x faster than Boost.Log 1.56 file logging in 2014 tests.

name: Highway (vqsort)
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: SIMD-dispatched vectorized quicksort/quickselect for built-in key types; ~10x faster than LLVM std::sort on large arrays.

name: HighwayHash
baseline: SipHash
one_liner: SIMD-based keyed hash function; ~5x faster than SipHash at 1 KiB while keeping DoS-resistant strong-hash security claims.

name: J2CL WasmGC backend (Google Sheets calculation worker port)
baseline: The same Java code transpiled by J2CL to Closure-compiled JavaScript, running in V8 (Chrome)
one_liner: Google's Java transpiler with a WasmGC backend (J2Wasm); Sheets reports its calc worker about 2x faster than J2CL's JavaScript output.

name: jpegli
baseline: libjpeg-turbo
one_liner: Google's libjpeg62-compatible JPEG encoder/decoder tuned for quality per byte; not faster than libjpeg-turbo, and slower at decode.

name: LevelDB
baseline: SQLite3 3.7.6.3 (also Kyoto Cabinet 1.2.67 TreeDB)
one_liner: Google's embedded ordered key-value LSM store; 10-17x SQLite3's write and scan rates in its 2011 benchmark.

name: Marl
baseline: The repo's own std::thread plus std::mutex SingleQueue and MultiQueue executors (non_marl_bench.cpp); not oneTBB or a known library pool
one_liner: C++11 hybrid thread/fiber task scheduler from Google; tasks that block on marl primitives yield their worker instead of stalling it.

name: QUICHE (Google)
baseline: TCP+TLS (HTTPS over TCP, pre-QUIC production stack)
one_liner: Google's C++ QUIC/HTTP/3 stack behind Chrome; production A/B trials cut Search latency 8% (desktop) vs TLS/TCP.

name: Randen
baseline: std::mt19937_64 / pcg64_c32 (also Philox, ISAAC, ChaCha8)
one_liner: AES-based backtracking-resistant PRNG (C++11 URBG) at roughly std::mt19937_64 speed; reference code for absl::BitGen's engine.

name: RE2
baseline: PCRE
one_liner: Linear-time, non-backtracking C++ regex engine beating classic PCRE on untrusted input; loses to PCRE2 JIT and Hyperscan.

name: skcms
baseline: Little CMS (lcms2)
one_liner: Skia's small ICC colour-management library (parse profiles, SIMD pixel transforms); no published speed comparison against Little CMS.

name: Skia
baseline: ImageMagick 6.8.9-9
one_liner: Google's 2D graphics library; its 2016 convolution scaler (Skia 53) resized 4.2x to 9.7x faster than single-threaded ImageMagick 6.8.

name: Snappy
baseline: zlib (fastest mode, level 1)
one_liner: Google's byte-oriented LZ77 codec: about 5x faster compression and 3x faster decompression than zlib -1, with larger output.

name: Souper (LLVM IR superoptimizer)
baseline: stock LLVM optimisation pipeline output (clang -O2/-O3 without Souper)
one_liner: SMT-backed superoptimizer for LLVM IR that finds peephole rewrites stock LLVM misses; its published win is code size, not speed.

name: TCMalloc (google/tcmalloc)
baseline: glibc malloc
one_liner: Google's per-CPU-cache C/C++ allocator, positioned as a faster-at-scale alternative to glibc malloc, though unquantified in the repo.

name: Wuffs deflate/zlib/gzip decoder
baseline: zlib
one_liner: Memory-safe deflate, gzip and zlib decoder shipped as single-file C; 1.2x-1.9x faster than zlib 1.2.11 inflate on 10-100 KB inputs.

name: Fontations (skrifa / read-fonts)
baseline: HarfBuzz OT font backend (hb-ot font functions: cmap lookup, advances, extents, outline drawing)
one_liner: Google's memory-safe Rust OpenType stack (read-fonts, skrifa); mostly 1.1-1.6x slower than HarfBuzz's own OT font functions.

name: FluxMQ
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: Single-binary Rust broker that speaks the Kafka wire protocol; claims ~29% more producer msg/s than Kafka 3.9.

name: aw-backtrace
baseline: libgcc _Unwind_Backtrace and LLVM libunwind (stack unwinders used by profilers)
one_liner: Async-signal-safe, crash-free DWARF (.eh_frame) backtracer from the gperftools maintainers that unwinds faster than libgcc and LLVM libunwind.

name: gperftools TCMalloc
baseline: glibc 2.3 malloc (ptmalloc2)
one_liner: Thread-caching malloc replacement for glibc's ptmalloc2; per-thread free lists cut lock contention and per-call cost.

name: GnuPG (gpg)
baseline: Sequoia-PGP sq (sq encrypt)
one_liner: The reference OpenPGP command-line tool; in 2021 runs it streamed public-key encryption 1.3-2.7x faster than Sequoia's sq.

name: libgcrypt (assembly for x86, ARM, PowerPC)
license: LGPL-2.1 (library, COPYING.LIB); GPL-2.0 for helper programs and documentation (COPYING)
baseline: libgcrypt's own previous implementation of the same primitive, which differs per row: earlier assembly paths for several rows (VAES/AVX512 AES is measured against libgcrypt's VAES/AVX2 assembly; AES-NI XTS against earlier AES-NI code; SHA-NI SHA-1 against the previous SHA-1 path), generic C for others; NEWS does not say which
one_liner: GnuPG's crypto library with runtime-dispatched x86, ARM, PowerPC, s390x and RISC-V assembly; each new kernel beats libgcrypt's previous path.

name: gpu_fftw
baseline: FFTW3 (running on the Raspberry Pi CPU)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD shim that reroutes FFTW3 1-D power-of-two complex float FFTs to the original Raspberry Pi's VideoCore IV GPU.

name: spECK (lightweight-analysis GPU SpGEMM)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpGEMM
one_liner: CUDA SpGEMM (C = A*B in CSR) with adaptive hash/dense accumulators; PPoPP '20 reports wins over cuSPARSE and other GPU SpGEMM libraries.

name: apple-bottom
baseline: Apple Accelerate DGEMM on AMX (and OpenBLAS 6-thread in a Quantum ESPRESSO run)
one_liner: Double-float (FP32-pair) DGEMM/ZGEMM on Apple Silicon GPUs via Metal; about 1.1-1.2x Accelerate's AMX DGEMM for resident N>=2048 matrices.

name: python-diskcache
baseline: Memcached (pylibmc client) and Redis (redis.StrictRedis)
one_liner: Pure-Python, SQLite-backed persistent cache that runs in-process and beats localhost Memcached/Redis on read latency, not writes.

name: aquatic (aquatic_udp)
baseline: epoll (aquatic_udp's own mio backend, which uses epoll on Linux); also opentracker (C), which the bencher runs with 'listen.udp.workers N', so it uses N pthreads doing blocking recvfrom on one shared socket rather than its libowfat epoll event loop
one_liner: Rust open UDP BitTorrent tracker (BEP 15) whose io_uring backend out-serves its own epoll path and opentracker.

name: parallel-hashmap (phmap)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only, Abseil-derived flat/node hash maps and a btree; drop-in for std::unordered_map/map, ~3x faster inserts.

name: sparsepp (spp::sparse_hash_map, greg7mdp/sparsepp)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only open-addressing hash map/set beating std::unordered_map on memory and, per two independent suites, speed.

name: Parshred
baseline: pugixml
one_liner: C++20 SIMD XML parser with a flat 32-byte-node DOM; 1.6-3.3x pugixml's read-only parse throughput on synthetic XML.

name: pngenc
baseline: libpng 1.6 (with zlib)
one_liner: Small OpenMP-parallel C PNG encoder with stored, Huffman-only and RLE deflate paths; about 11x faster than libpng single-threaded in those modes.

name: Grok JPEG 2000 codec
baseline: OpenJPEG (JPEG 2000); also Kakadu (proprietary, via GDAL JP2KAK)
one_liner: AGPL C++23 JPEG 2000 (Part 1 and HTJ2K) codec. Its GDAL driver beats OpenJPEG on tiled, region and S3 reads.

name: GROMACS
baseline: NAMD 3.0 (3.0b5 multicore-CUDA build) and OpenMM 8.1
one_liner: GPU-resident molecular dynamics engine; on one 6N4O PME benchmark 1.04-2.40x NAMD 3.0b5 and 1.11-1.65x OpenMM 8.1 throughput.

name: grpc-dotnet (gRPC for .NET)
baseline: gRPC C++ (grpc/grpc) servers cpp_grpc_st, cpp_grpc_mt and cpp_asio_grpc in the grpc_bench suite
one_liner: Managed gRPC for ASP.NET Core; outran stock gRPC C++ async servers 1.48-1.67x on grpc_bench's 2026 unary test.

name: grpc-go
baseline: gRPC C++ (grpc/grpc) servers cpp_grpc_st, cpp_grpc_mt and cpp_asio_grpc in the grpc_bench suite
one_liner: Google's pure-Go gRPC; beat a stock gRPC C++ async server at 2-4 CPUs in one grpc_bench run, lost in another.

name: phashtable (gsauthof)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Tiny C/C++ two-level perfect hash index, built at startup, that flattens worst-case lookup latency versus std::unordered_map.

name: GStreamer (gst-vaapi VA-API pipelines)
baseline: FFmpeg (libavcodec through OpenCV's VideoCapture/VideoWriter FFmpeg backend, CPU software codecs)
one_liner: Plugin-based C media framework; its VA-API pipelines decoded and encoded on an Intel iGPU 1.2-10x faster than OpenCV's software FFmpeg backend.

name: C2 (cache-conscious succinct tries)
baseline: MARISA (marisa-trie), FST (SuRF), CoCo-trie
one_liner: Research re-implementations of FST, CoCo-trie and MARISA succinct tries; C2-FST and C2-MARISA beat the originals on lookup and size.

name: expr-cls (Go expression evaluator from typed closures)
baseline: expr-lang/expr and google/cel-go
one_liner: Experimental Go expression compiler that turns expr-lang/expr's AST into typed closure chains; ~19x faster evaluation than expr.Run on one formula.

name: galois (finite-field arithmetic with AssemblyScript WebAssembly acceleration)
baseline: JavaScript BigInt arithmetic (256-bit and 128-bit prime fields) in the same library on Node.js
one_liner: TypeScript prime-field library whose AssemblyScript WASM backend runs 128-bit vector field ops about 9x faster than its JS BigInt path.

name: GraphBLAST (GraphBLAS on the GPU)
baseline: SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS through LAGraph (CPU)
one_liner: CUDA implementation of the GraphBLAS API for graph algorithms; paper reports 43.51x geomean over multi-threaded SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS.

name: es-module-lexer
language: C compiled to WebAssembly (emcc) with a TypeScript/JavaScript wrapper
baseline: Acorn (fastest pure-JS parser, per the README) and the library's own CSP asm.js build of the same C lexer
one_liner: C lexer compiled to Wasm that returns ES module import/export records; 2-3x faster than its own asm.js build.

name: Supersnappy
baseline: Google Snappy (C++), called through its C API (snappy_compress, snappy_uncompress, snappy_validate_compressed_buffer) from a prebuilt libsnappy.dll loaded by the nimsnappy wrapper (version and build flags unknown; the wrapper says it tracks 1.1.3). Also Andi Kleen's snappy-c (C), compiled from source into the benchmark through the nimsnappyc wrapper's {.compile.} pragma. The pure-Nim status-im/nim-snappy is the fourth column.
one_liner: Pure-Nim raw Snappy codec; its 2022 README table beats snappy-c everywhere and a libsnappy build on text, loses three files.

name: Zippy (Nim deflate/zlib/gzip)
baseline: zlib via the nim-lang/zip wrapper (zlib version and build unstated; tests/bench.nim comments say the zlib path 'Requires zlib1.dll' and the README command uses a Windows-style path, so the README's 'zlib found on a fresh Linux install' may not describe the run shown)
one_liner: Pure-Nim deflate/zlib/gzip codec (plus zip and tar readers) that the author times as faster than zlib on small files.

name: ucg (UniversalCodeGrep)
baseline: GNU grep (egrep -R with --include filters)
one_liner: Ack-style recursive source-code grep using PCRE2 JIT and threaded traversal; about 3.7x faster than egrep -R on a kernel-tree search.

name: LA-vector
baseline: SDSL compressed bitvectors (sdsl::s18_vector, sdsl::rle_vector and other rank/select dictionaries compared in the paper repo)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 compressed sorted-integer container and rank/select dictionary built from piecewise linear approximations; competes with SDSL sd_vector-style dictionaries.

name: PGM-index (Piecewise Geometric Model index)
baseline: STX B+-tree (v0.9) and cache-efficient CSS-tree (authors' implementation), plus a 2-stage RMI (Recursive Model Index)
one_liner: Header-only learned index over sorted integer arrays that matches B+-tree lookup latency with an index orders of magnitude smaller.

name: aWsm
baseline: Wasmer; WAVM; Lucet; Node.js with Emscripten; wasm3 on microcontrollers
one_liner: Research ahead-of-time Wasm-to-LLVM compiler plus a tiny C runtime; its 2020 PolyBench/C slowdown over native C was 13.4%, against WAVM 28.1% and Wasmer 149.8%.

name: NMHASH (NMHASH32X)
baseline: xxHash64
one_liner: Header-only 32-bit seeded C hash built on 16-bit SIMD multiplies; about 2x XXH64 bulk throughput with AVX2, weak SMHasher3 quality.

name: H2O
baseline: nginx 1.7.9 (HTTP/1.1 local benchmark); nginx 1.9.10 in the later EC2 static-file chart
one_liner: C HTTP/1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 web server and reverse proxy; 2016 charts show more req/s per core than nginx 1.9.

name: picotls "fusion" AES-GCM engine
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: x86-64 AES-GCM engine inside picotls, tuned for short QUIC packets; ~1.3x OpenSSL 1.1.1g throughput at 1440-byte records.

name: base64-turbo (hacer-bark)
baseline: base64 (RFC 4648) codecs: Turbo-Base64 (C, the prior fastest known codec) and the Rust default `base64` crate 0.23 (its SIMD path on by default), plus base64-simd and base64-ng, all in the same harness
one_liner: 0BSD Rust base64 crate with AVX2/AVX-512 VBMI/NEON kernels; 2.7-6x the default base64 crate, roughly ties Turbo-Base64.

name: EverCrypt (HACL*) Curve25519 (Vale-optimized)
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Formally verified C/asm crypto library; its ADX X25519 took about 4% fewer cycles than OpenSSL's ADX assembly.

name: HALAC (High Availability Lossless Audio Compression)
baseline: FLAC 1.5.0 (flac CLI) at -8 and -5. The 0.5.4 notes also list WavPack 5.9.0 -h and HALAC 0.5.1. Monkey's Audio, WavPack and OptimFROG (versions not stated) appear only in the 0.4.8 notes for the 32-bit float set.
one_liner: Fast lossless audio codec, closed Windows binaries plus an early MIT source; encodes 2.2-4.4x faster than FLAC 1.5.0 at similar size.

name: HALIC (High Availability Lossless Image Compression)
language: unknown (binaries only; README says built with GCC and Clang)
baseline: libwebp lossless (Pillow 10.1.0, method 1) and PNG (Pillow 10.1.0, optimize=False)
one_liner: Closed-source lossless RGB/gray image codec (CLI binaries) that encodes about 15-32x faster than Pillow PNG and WebP lossless at smaller size.

name: Halide
baseline: Expert hand-tuned C++ (OpenMP + Intel IPP), ARM NEON intrinsics/assembly and CUDA implementations of the same image-processing pipelines used as baselines in the PLDI 2013 paper (local Laplacian filters, bilateral grid, camera pipe, etc.)
one_liner: C++-embedded DSL compiling image/array pipelines via LLVM; team's 2013 results beat expert C++, NEON and CUDA 1.1-4.4x.

name: fcvvdp
baseline: cvvdp reference implementation (gfxdisp/ColorVideoVDP, Python, multithreaded)
one_liner: C reimplementation of the CVVDP video-quality metric; first-party 1.28x (1 thread) and 3.22x (8 threads) faster than Python cvvdp.

name: wpd (WebP decoder)
baseline: libwebp at pinned revision 94d3c4a (decoder version 1.6.0), static libwebpdecoder plus libwebpdemux built through Meson's CMake subproject, single-threaded
one_liner: Rust and hand-written assembly WebP decoder with a C ABI; 1.04-1.76x faster than libwebp 1.6.0 on one thread.

name: CTRE (compile-time regular expressions)
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Header-only C++ template-metaprogramming regex engine for compile-time-known patterns, with large wall-clock wins over std::regex.

name: Nova-LSM
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: LevelDB-based LSM KV server split into RDMA-linked compute and storage parts; beats LevelDB/RocksDB under skewed access.

name: authia
baseline: jose (JavaScript JOSE library: WebCrypto on Cloudflare Workers, native Node.js crypto bindings on Node)
one_liner: Rust/Wasm Ed25519-only JWT verifier; first-party 1.5x lower latency than jose on Cloudflare Workers, 6-20x slower on Node.

name: zlog
baseline: syslog(3) with rsyslogd
one_liner: Pure-C, config-file-driven logging library (log4j-style categories and rules); claims about 1000x syslog(3) throughput, unmeasured in the repo.

name: harfbuzz
baseline: rustybuzz (Rust port of HarfBuzz); the guessed 'built-in text shaping' baseline has no published numbers
one_liner: The standard OpenType/AAT text shaping engine (C++11, no C++ standard library); 1.76x geomean faster than its Rust port rustybuzz.

name: ttf-parser
baseline: FreeType (FT_Load_Glyph with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, glyph outlining); stb_truetype also compared
one_liner: Safe, zero-allocation Rust font parser with a C API; extracts unscaled glyph outlines 1.3-5x faster than FreeType's FT_Load_Glyph path.

name: SNKV
baseline: SQLite
one_liner: C key-value API on SQLite's B-tree, pager and WAL minus the SQL layer; 1.6-2x SQLite in first-party KV microbenchmarks.

name: HashLink (Haxe virtual machine, Neko successor)
baseline: NekoVM (Haxe code compiled to the Neko target; also Haxe's Lua and Python targets, not stock Lua or CPython)
one_liner: Haxe's typed-bytecode VM with an x86-64 JIT and a C backend (HL/C); several times faster than the older NekoVM target.

name: hxcpp (Haxe C++ backend and runtime)
baseline: NekoVM and HashLink (HL/JIT) Haxe targets; also compared with Haxe's JVM/Java and JavaScript (Node) targets
one_liner: Runtime and build tool for Haxe's C++ target; native output beats the HashLink/JIT and Neko VM targets on CPU-bound benchmarks.

name: NekoVM
baseline: PUC Lua 5.3.1 (the Scriptorium repo vendors lua/lua-5.3.1; the table links LuaDist/lua; build flags not stated)
one_liner: Deprecated dynamically typed bytecode VM behind Haxe's Neko target; about 1.2x PUC Lua on one 2015 fib run, within noise.

name: berith (Ed25519 and X25519 in Rust WebAssembly)
language: Rust (ed25519-dalek and x25519-dalek compiled to WebAssembly with wasm-pack) with TypeScript
baseline: @noble/curves 0.7.0 (pure TypeScript/JavaScript Ed25519 in V8)
one_liner: Deprecated wasm-pack build of Rust ed25519-dalek/x25519-dalek for JS; 5.9-7.1x faster than @noble/curves 0.7 on keygen+sign+verify.

name: FlashFFTConv
baseline: PyTorch FFT convolution (torch.fft, backed by cuFFT)
one_liner: CUDA tensor-core FFT convolution for PyTorch; 1.3x to 7.9x faster than torch.fft (cuFFT) convolution on H100.

name: HipKittens (AMD) / ThunderKittens sibling
baseline: AITER (AMD hand-tuned assembly attention kernels); also Composable Kernel, PyTorch SDPA, Triton and hipBLASLt in other plots
one_liner: C++ tile-primitive kernel DSL for AMD Instinct GPUs; its GQA attention backward runs about 3x faster than AITER on MI355X.

name: ThunderKittens
baseline: cuBLAS GEMM and FlashAttention-3 / cuDNN attention
one_liner: Header-only CUDA tile DSL for writing GEMM/attention/SSM kernels that match cuBLAS and FA3 and beat FA3 backward.

name: ThunderMittens
language: C++ (Metal Shading Language) with Python/MLX bindings
baseline: MLX mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention and mx.matmul (Apple's MLX Metal kernels)
one_liner: Metal port of the ThunderKittens tile DSL for Apple GPUs; its bf16 GEMM is about 9% faster than MLX's mx.matmul.

name: avxbls
baseline: blst (non-vectorized x64 assembly BLS12-381 pairing)
one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA BLS12-381 optimal ate pairing built on blst; about 1.9x lower single-pairing latency than blst's x64 assembly.

name: ziggit (Zig git reimplementation)
baseline: git (C) CLI: status, log -20, branch -a, blame
one_liner: Pure-Zig git CLI and embeddable library; first-party numbers beat Apple git on tiny macOS commands, not large Linux repos.

name: vstat (SIMD descriptive statistics on EVE)
baseline: Boost.Accumulators 1.69, GNU Scientific Library 2.6, NumPy 1.19.4 and linasm statistics 1.13
one_liner: Header-only C++20 SIMD mean/variance/covariance/correlation on EVE; plots show 14-130x over GSL and Boost.Accumulators, near linasm.

name: dumac (Rust parallel du -sh for macOS)
baseline: macOS du -sh (BSD du, C); diskus is also compared
one_liner: macOS-only Rust du -sh clone: parallel getattrlistbulk walk, about 5.7x faster than BSD du on a warm synthetic tree.

name: Helidon SE (Nima WebServer)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native) for HTTP/2; Drogon, userver, hical (C++) for the other profiles, all in the HttpArena suite
one_liner: Java 27 microservice framework on the virtual-thread Níma WebServer; edges nginx on HttpArena's HTTP/2 hello-world profiles only.

name: Spellbook (Rust Hunspell-format spellchecker, rewrite of Nuspell)
baseline: Hunspell and Nuspell (C++), single-word check()
one_liner: Rust rewrite of Nuspell that checks Hunspell-format dictionaries; 1.5-8x faster single-word check() than Nuspell and Hunspell on en_US.

name: ZXC
baseline: LZ4 (fast, default, HC -9) and zstd -1
one_liner: Asymmetric LZ77 codec in C that decodes faster than LZ4, LZ4HC and zstd -1 at equal or smaller output.

name: bls-eth-wasm (herumi), benchmarked in ChainSafe/bls
language: C++ (mcl/bls) compiled to WebAssembly, JavaScript API
baseline: noble-bls12-381 (pure JavaScript); blst native bindings shown for reference
one_liner: herumi's mcl/bls C++ pairing code compiled to WebAssembly for Eth2 BLS12-381 signatures; 1.5-10.6x faster than pure-JS noble-bls12-381 0.7.

name: fmath (herumi)
baseline: std::logf, std::expf (<cmath>)
one_liner: SIMD array-mode log/exp for float buffers, 9-19x faster than std::logf/std::expf via AVX2/AVX-512.

name: NVthreads
baseline: Atlas (HP persistent-memory failure-atomic-section library) and Mnemosyne (word-level STM persistent memory); plain pthreads is faster than NVthreads
one_liner: pthreads replacement that makes lock-based C/C++ programs crash-consistent on NVM; beats Atlas and Mnemosyne, slower than pthreads.

name: RetroWrite
baseline: Valgrind Memcheck
one_liner: Static rewriter adding ASan and AFL coverage to Linux x86-64/aarch64 binaries without source; claims 3x faster than Valgrind memcheck.

name: vectorcmp (hexon)
baseline: pure-Go scalar loop that sets one bit per matching element (build tag purego), compiled by the Go gc compiler
one_liner: Go AVX2 assembly comparing one value against a column into a bitmask; 5-232x faster than its scalar Go loop.

name: ClangJIT (Clang with JIT extensions for C++ templates)
baseline: The same Eigen expression (m = Ones + 0.00005*(m + m*m)) compiled ahead of time with runtime-sized Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic> and float/double/long double dispatch, by the same Clang at -march=native -ffast-math -O3; the wiki also reports an AoT build specialized for one fixed size, which matches the JIT.
one_liner: Research Clang 9 fork adding [[clang::jit]]: templates instantiated at run time; beats dynamic-size Eigen, ties size-specialized AoT.

name: hglm ARM memcpy, memset, memzero and copy_page kernel patches (test-arm-kernel-memcpy)
license: Per-file headers: MIT/X11 (benchmark.c, memcpy_armv6v7.S, new_arm.S, Copyright 2013 Harm Hanemaaijer) and GPL-2.0-only (kernel-derived memset.S, memzero.S, copy_page.S, copy templates, user-copy variants and the *_orig.S baselines); asm.h, new_arm.h and kernel_defines*.h have no header; no repo-level LICENSE file
baseline: original Linux kernel ARM memcpy, memset, memzero and copy_page (the benchmark harness also runs libc memcpy/memset alongside)
one_liner: 2013 hand-tuned ARMv6/ARMv7 assembly for Linux kernel copy_page, memset, memzero and memcpy, with a userspace benchmark against the old kernel routines.

name: HiAE (libhiae)
baseline: OpenSSL AES-128-GCM / AES-256-GCM
one_liner: Portable C library for the HiAE AES-round AEAD; about 3.8x OpenSSL AES-128-GCM encryption throughput on Apple M5 Max.

name: Hickory DNS (formerly Trust-DNS)
baseline: BIND
one_liner: Memory-safe Rust DNS server, resolver and protocol crates; matches BIND 9.11 on single-query UDP latency, within noise.

name: gif_load
baseline: giflib 5.2.2 (also stb_image)
one_liner: Public-domain single-header C animated-GIF decoder; with the file cached it decodes 1.3-1.7x faster than giflib 5.2.2.

name: libco (higan-emu)
language: C (hand-assembled machine-code context switch per CPU)
baseline: POSIX ucontext context switch (libco's own ucontext.c backend), plus its setjmp/longjmp and Windows-fiber backends, each expressed as a multiple of an ordinary C function call; the README also contrasts kernel-scheduled preemptive threads
one_liner: C89 stackful coroutine library whose hand-assembled per-CPU switch costs a few function calls, against hundreds for POSIX ucontext.

name: Higgs (higgsjs/Higgs JavaScript JIT)
baseline: V8 (its baseline compiler; its optimizing Crankshaft compiler is faster than Higgs)
one_liner: Research JavaScript JIT in D using lazy basic block versioning; per paper snippets it beats V8's old non-optimizing compiler, not Crankshaft.

name: FastMath C++ Library (fast_math_cpp)
baseline: <cmath> single-precision (float) overloads (std::sinh, std::tanh, std::atanh, std::atan2, std::pow, std::acos, std::log10, std::tan, std::exp, std::log, etc.), backed by glibc libm (sinhf, tanhf, ...)
one_liner: Header-only float math library beating glibc's <cmath> on composed functions (sinh, tanh, atan2, integer pow), not raw trig or exp/log.

name: ikd-Tree (incremental k-d tree)
baseline: Boost.Geometry R*-tree, PCL octree and nanoflann dynamic k-d tree, each integrated into FAST-LIO2 (FAST-LIO2, IEEE T-RO 2022, Table III); also a static k-d tree rebuilt every scan (FAST-LIO, and the ikd-Tree preprint's PCL comparison)
one_liner: Incremental 3-D k-d tree for LiDAR SLAM maps: point/box updates without full rebuilds; per-scan time 1.03-2.1x below nanoflann and Boost R*-tree.

name: libaco
baseline: Tencent libco (coctx_swap)
one_liner: Small C asymmetric-coroutine library for x86/x86-64 whose hand-written switch routine runs about 1.7x faster than Tencent libco's coctx_swap.

name: sorug (WHATWG URL parser, Rust)
baseline: url crate (servo/rust-url)
one_liner: Safe-Rust WHATWG URL parser with a zero-copy fast path for canonical URLs; 3.4-4.1x faster than the url crate on ASCII.

name: Hoedown
baseline: cmark (CommonMark reference implementation)
one_liner: Callback-driven C Markdown-to-HTML library (Sundown fork); edged out cmark 0.21 s vs 0.29 s in cmark's own 2015-era benchmark.

name: uint256 (holiman)
baseline: Go math/big (big.Int)
one_liner: Allocation-free fixed 256-bit unsigned integer type for Go; 1.2-17x faster than math/big.Int on 256-bit arithmetic.

name: TiTanF
baseline: RustType and ab_glyph (long-standing, widely used pure-Rust glyph rasterizers); Fontdue, another pure-Rust rasterizer, also measured and faster at 10-160px; FreeType and HarfBuzz are not measured
one_liner: Zero-dependency no_std Rust TrueType rasterizer; 1.5-3.5x faster than RustType and ab_glyph, slower than Fontdue below 200px.

name: rapidhash (Rust port)
baseline: xxHash (XXH64, XXH3-64, via the Rust twox-hash 2.1.1 crate) and wyhash (Rust wyhash crate 0.6.0)
one_liner: Rust rapidhash (wyhash successor): portable 64-bit hasher, faster than XXH64/wyhash and faster than XXH3 up to about 4 KB inputs.

name: ReLAPACK
baseline: reference LAPACK, OpenBLAS LAPACK routines and Intel MKL LAPACK routines
one_liner: Recursive C replacements for LAPACK compute kernels (LU, Cholesky, LDL, trtri, Sylvester) that beat reference LAPACK's blocked versions.

name: TCCG / GETT (Tensor Contraction Code Generator)
language: Python (generator that emits vectorized C code)
baseline: TTGT (transpose-transpose-GEMM-transpose) tensor contraction built on Intel MKL sgemm/dgemm (the repo's default BLAS in config.cfg is MKL); TTGT is TCCG's own backend, not a third-party tensor library
one_liner: Python code generator for GETT tensor contractions; beats MKL-backed transpose-transpose-GEMM-transpose up to about 2x on bandwidth-bound cases.

name: orzo (Elias-Fano encoded L2 rank/select)
baseline: cs-poppy and pasta-flat
one_liner: Research rank/select index for plain bitvectors that Elias-Fano-packs L2 counts, cutting index space below pasta-flat and cs-poppy.

name: MANS (Multi-byte ANS compressor)
baseline: FSE-ANS (Finite State Entropy) on CPU; nvCOMP Huffman on GPU; 16-bit Huffman for ratio
one_liner: ANS pipeline for 16/32-bit integer arrays on CPU, CUDA and HIP; reports 1.92x/2.04x faster than FSE on CPU.

name: Smolscale
baseline: libswscale (FFmpeg), Pixman, stb_image_resize, GDK-Pixbuf, SDL_gfx and Skia (as wired into the project's own benchmark harness)
one_liner: Embeddable C bilinear/box RGBA scaler (SWAR, AVX2, row-batch threading); no published speed ratio against Pixman, libswscale or stb.

name: HSE (Heterogeneous-memory Storage Engine)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Micron's embedded C key-value engine for NVMe SSDs; its own YCSB run shows about 8x RocksDB's load throughput.

name: encoding_rs
baseline: ICU
one_liner: Rust implementation of the WHATWG Encoding Standard; beats ICU at UTF-8/UTF-16/legacy transcoding on Web-shaped text.

name: crc32c (htot)
license: BSD-3-Clause (crc32c/LICENSE, MIT copyright, with Intel slicing-by-8 under the same terms; the README says BSD 2-clause). crc32intelc.cc and crc32adler.cc are under the Zlib license, and crc_iscsi_v_pcl.asm is Intel BSD-3-Clause. GitHub's license API detects none.
baseline: CRC32 (CRC-32C/Castagnoli; SlicingBy8 software baseline is representative of the algorithm used by most CRC32 library implementations)
one_liner: C++ port of Intel's 3-way crc32q+pclmulqdq CRC-32C kernel that also runs on 32-bit x86; ~11x faster than slicing-by-8.

name: hpp-proto
baseline: Protobuf (Google's C++ libprotobuf)
one_liner: Wire-compatible C++23 Protobuf implementation; non-owning mode decodes and builds+serializes 1.5-1.9x faster than libprotobuf arenas.

name: LuaAOT (lua-aot-5.4)
baseline: Lua 5.4.3 interpreter (the stock interpreter the fork is based on)
one_liner: Patched Lua 5.4.3 plus a bytecode-to-C compiler (luaot); compiled modules ran 1.2x to 2.6x faster than the stock interpreter.

name: commp-wasm (@hugomrdias/commp-wasm)
baseline: @web3-storage/data-segment (original JavaScript CommP implementation)
one_liner: Rust-to-WASM Filecoin CommP (piece commitment) hasher; 11-34x the throughput of @web3-storage/data-segment in Node and browsers.

name: nativewebp
baseline: Go standard library image/png encoder at png.BestCompression
one_liner: Pure-Go lossless WebP (VP8L) encoder; README shows it 1.2-2.3x faster than Go's image/png at BestCompression with 14-26% smaller files.

name: nexus
baseline: Taskflow, BS::thread_pool
one_liner: Header-only C++26 work-stealing thread pool with about 3x to 7x lower scheduling overhead than Taskflow and BS::thread_pool on tiny tasks.

name: Hydra Columnar (Postgres columnar extension)
license: AGPL-3.0 (the columnar engine in columnar/, per README and columnar/LICENSE) + Apache-2.0 (the rest of the repo; GitHub reports Apache-2.0 from the root LICENSE)
baseline: PostgreSQL (native heap/row storage)
one_liner: Postgres table-access-method extension (Citus Columnar fork) adding compressed columnar storage, parallel scans, vectorized filters; ~23x vs heap on ClickBench.

name: hyper
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Rust's low-level HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 library under axum and warp; raw hyper roughly ties actix-web on minimal GET /.

name: tonic (Rust gRPC)
baseline: gRPC C++ (grpc/grpc) servers cpp_grpc_st, cpp_grpc_mt and cpp_asio_grpc in the grpc_bench suite
one_liner: Rust async gRPC (tokio, hyper, prost) that out-served the stock C++ gRPC async servers in grpc_bench's small unary echo test.

name: Wisp
baseline: NATS
one_liner: Experimental Rust server speaking the NATS Core client protocol; about 3.7-4.4x nats-server throughput on 1,000-subscriber loopback fan-out.

name: quantette
baseline: libimagequant (imagequant crate 4.4.1, the engine behind pngquant); also color_quant 1.1.0 (NeuQuant) and exoquant 0.2.0
one_liner: Rust palette quantizer (Wu and Oklab k-means); author's 4-thread runs show 3-14x faster than libimagequant on large opaque photos.

name: yy_itoa (itoa_yy.c in ibireme/c_numconv_benchmark)
baseline: fmt::format_to(buf, FMT_COMPILE("{}"), val) from fmtlib (the baseline the repo's own itoa report uses); the repo does not time std::to_chars, fmt::format_int or sprintf
one_liner: yy_itoa: a 200-byte-table ANSI C integer-to-decimal routine (yyjson's) that formats u32/u64/i32/i64 about 1.7-2.5x faster than fmt's compiled format_to.

name: yyjson
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: ANSI C JSON DOM library beating RapidJSON via single-file design, in-situ parsing, and low-allocation strategy.

name: itlib small and flat containers (itlib::flat_map, itlib::small_vector, itlib::static_vector)
baseline: std::map
one_liner: Single-header C++11 flat_map/flat_set (sorted vector) plus small_vector and static_vector; claims to beat std::map for small sizes, unmeasured.

name: icecream (icecc)
baseline: local single-machine compilation (make without icecream)
one_liner: SUSE's distcc-derived distributed C/C++ compiler with a central scheduler; beats single-machine make when several networked machines are free.

name: iced (iced-x86)
baseline: Capstone, Zydis, Intel XED, bddisasm, diStorm, udis86, BeaEngine (x86/x64 disassembler libraries); no GNU as, NASM or MASM assembler comparison
one_liner: Rust x86/x64 decoder, formatter, encoder and assembler; decodes 4-7x faster than Zydis, XED and bddisasm in disas-bench.

name: heFFTe (Highly Efficient FFT for Exascale)
baseline: Distributed 3-D FFT libraries fftMPI, SWFFT, AccFFT and P3DFFT (FFTW-MPI-class); FFTW is heFFTe's own CPU backend
one_liner: MPI-distributed 2-D/3-D FFT layer over FFTW, MKL, cuFFT and rocFFT; on GPUs about 2x fftMPI and SWFFT, at parity on CPU.

name: Coost co/log
baseline: glog (single thread) and spdlog (1-8 threads)
one_liner: Asynchronous double-buffered logger inside the coost C++17 base library; first-party numbers claim it beats glog and synchronous spdlog.

name: Coost co/json
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: JSON DOM module of the coost C++ base library; first-party numbers claim 1.4-3.6x faster parse/stringify than RapidJSON 1.1.0.

name: Coost fastring and fastream
baseline: snprintf and std::ostringstream (fastream); std::string (fastring, benchmark code only, no published numbers)
one_liner: coost v3's fastream (append-only text buffer) and fastring (heap string), claimed 10-30x faster than snprintf with no published harness.

name: RE# (Resharp)
baseline: Rust regex
one_liner: Automata-based .NET/F# regex engine beating Rust's regex crate on rebar benchmarks; adds intersection, complement, lookarounds.

name: pflua (pflang packet-filter compiler on LuaJIT) vs libpcap BPF interpreter and Linux kernel BPF JITs
baseline: libpcap's user-space BPF interpreter (pcap_offline_filter in the Debian system libpcap, version and build flags not stated) running bytecode from pcap_compile with libpcap's optimizer on; also the 2011 Linux kernel BPF JIT and the 2014 Linux eBPF JIT (C, built with gcc -O3 as user-space shared objects in pflua-bench), whose filters run as JIT-emitted machine code
one_liner: LuaJIT library that compiles tcpdump (pflang) filter expressions to Lua; 1.3-7.1x libpcap's BPF interpreter in its authors' benchmarks.

name: Ferrous
baseline: Valkey 8.0.4
one_liner: AI-written Rust Redis/RESP2 server; self-reported 0-8% over Valkey 8.0.4 on single commands, ~2x slower pipelined SET.

name: libJSON (IgnacioPomar)
baseline: nlohmann/json
one_liner: Learning-project C++17 JSON DOM (shared_ptr nodes) that parses and walks 1.25-1.42x faster than nlohmann/json in its author's benchmark.

name: igraph
baseline: NetworkX 2.4 (pure Python); SNAP 5.0.0 as a second row
one_liner: C network-analysis library with Python/R/Mathematica bindings; 5-49x faster than pure-Python NetworkX on loading, PageRank, k-core, SCC.

name: md4w
language: Zig and C (md4c) compiled to WebAssembly, JavaScript API
baseline: markdown-it (pure JavaScript); markdown-wasm (another WASM md4c wrapper) also in the benchmark
one_liner: md4c Markdown parser plus a Zig HTML writer compiled to WebAssembly; renders 2.7-11.6x faster than markdown-it in JavaScript runtimes.

name: orjson
baseline: Python json (stdlib)
one_liner: CPython JSON extension in Rust (yyjson-backed parser) that serializes ~11-14x and parses ~2-6x faster than stdlib json.

name: ik_llama.cpp
baseline: llama.cpp (mainline ggml CPU kernels)
one_liner: llama.cpp fork with rewritten CPU quantized-matmul kernels; 1.1-7x faster CPU prompt processing than mainline on the same GGUF.

name: GeoToolbox KdBoxTree
baseline: Boost.Geometry 1.90 R*-tree (also GEOS 3.14.1 STR-tree, nanoflann 1.10.1, tidwall rtree.c)
one_liner: Static C++17 k-d tree that indexes boxes as well as points; out-queries Boost.Geometry's R*-tree on bulk-loaded data.

name: lexindex
baseline: XCDAT 15 (C++ compressed double-array trie dictionary) and MARISA (marisa-trie 0.2.6)
one_liner: Rust crate of immutable string-to-id dictionaries; front-coded DictIndex comes in smaller than MARISA and XCDAT on the author's 13 corpora.

name: libbsc
baseline: xz (xz 5.8.4); also bzip2 1.0.8
one_liner: Block-sorting (BWT/ST + LZP + QLFC) compressor library that reaches xz -5 ratios with 5x faster single-thread compression.

name: fdeflate
baseline: zlib-rs and zlib-ng (zlib-compatible deflate/inflate); also compared with miniz_oxide and libdeflate on the plot
one_liner: Safe-Rust zlib/deflate codec tuned for PNG data; decoder claimed on par with zlib-ng and zlib-rs, encoder still preliminary.

name: image-png (Rust png crate)
baseline: libpng 1.6.37 (Debian Bullseye)
one_liner: Pure-safe-Rust PNG/APNG decoder and encoder that decodes faster than libpng on most images; Chromium's default PNG decoder.

name: mexce
baseline: native compiler-generated C++ code for the same expressions (statically compiled)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 JIT that compiles run-time math formula strings to x86/x86-64 code, roughly matching statically compiled C++.

name: mozjpeg-rs
baseline: mozjpeg (C encoder, libjpeg-turbo fork with trellis quantization)
one_liner: Safe-Rust port of the mozjpeg JPEG encoder; its trellis mode timed 6% faster than C mozjpeg on one synthetic image.

name: rav1d-safe
license: AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Imazen-Commercial (Cargo.toml, LICENSE-AGPL3, LICENSE-COMMERCIAL); code inherited from dav1d/rav1d is BSD-2-Clause (COPYING)
baseline: upstream memorysafety/rav1d commit d3d1cd6 (package 1.1.0) built with default-features=false (bitdepth_8, bitdepth_16 only), i.e. with its hand-written assembly disabled; not dav1d and not rav1d's default assembly build, both of which are faster
one_liner: Memory-safe Rust AV1 decoder (rav1d fork); faster only than upstream rav1d with its assembly disabled, slower than dav1d.

name: zenjpeg
baseline: libjpeg-turbo (mozjpeg-sys 2.2 with nasm_simd, C+NASM)
one_liner: Safe pure-Rust JPEG encoder/decoder; progressive decode 1.35x libjpeg-turbo, baseline about 6% slower single-threaded.

name: zenquant (imazen)
baseline: libimagequant (imagequant crate 4, presets s1 d50, s1 d100, s4 d100); also quantette 0.5 k-means, quantizr, color_quant
one_liner: Pure-Rust 256-colour palette quantizer in OKLab with perceptual masking; smaller PNG/GIF than libimagequant, not faster.

name: PCG (pcg-cpp)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 PCG-family RNG beating std::mt19937/std::mt19937_64 raw-generation throughput by ~2.6-4x.

name: uberlog
baseline: synchronous write-per-message file logging (a 'naive logging system' that issues one OS write call per message)
one_liner: Two-process C++ logger: callers format into a shared-memory ring that a child process drains, avoiding one write() per message.

name: batmobile (CUDA kernels for equivariant GNNs)
baseline: e3nn (PyTorch library for E(3)-equivariant neural networks; generic implementation)
one_liner: Hand-unrolled FP32 CUDA kernels for L_max=3 spherical harmonics and Clebsch-Gordan tensor products, timed against generic e3nn.

name: Infinity
baseline: Elasticsearch 8.13.4 (full-text and dense vector search); Qdrant 1.9.2 also measured
one_liner: C++ AI-native search database for RAG; vendor run shows 10x Elasticsearch's full-text QPS on 33M Wikipedia documents.

name: sparse_dot_topn
baseline: SciPy sparse CSR matrix multiplication (scipy.sparse A.dot(B), SciPy 1.12.0)
one_liner: Python package with a C++17 OpenMP kernel for sparse A*B that keeps only the top-n values per row; multithreaded, so it beats single-threaded SciPy.

name: Lizard
baseline: zlib
one_liner: LZ4-derived C codec (formerly LZ5) with optional Huffman; decompresses 4-5x faster than zlib -9 at similar ratio.

name: InkWasm (inkeliz/go_inkwasm)
language: Go (wasm target) with generated JavaScript and assembly
baseline: Go standard library syscall/js
one_liner: Go js/wasm binding generator and runtime replacing syscall/js calls; about 2x faster on DOM and localStorage micro-benchmarks.

name: Karmem
baseline: FlatBuffers
one_liner: Zero-copy, schema-compiled binary format for Go/TinyGo and WASM; own benchmark: 5-18x faster than FlatBuffers' Go implementation.

name: inkooboo/thread-pool-cpp
baseline: boost::asio thread pool
one_liner: Header-only C++11 thread pool with per-worker Vyukov MPMC queues; reposts jobs about 20x faster than an asio io_service pool.

name: IKV (Inlined Key-Value Store)
baseline: Redis (AWS ElastiCache, Redis Cluster)
one_liner: Embedded, eventually consistent Rust key-value store for ML features that serves reads in-process instead of calling a remote Redis.

name: pleat (Pleated Ribbon Filter, Rust)
license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Cargo.toml and README; LICENSE plus LICENSE-APACHE present; GitHub detector reports MIT)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Rust ribbon-filter crate: about 7.6 bits/key at 0.8% FPR, less than Bloom, with cache-local 'pleated' construction.

name: Intel Cryptography Primitives Library
baseline: OpenSSL SHA-2/SHA-3 (implied incumbent only; no published comparison against it)
one_liner: Intel's C crypto-primitives library (ex-IPP Crypto) with SHA-NI/AVX2/AVX-512 SHA-1/2/3 kernels; claimed but unbenchmarked alternative to OpenSSL.

name: Fast UI Draw (FastUIDraw)
baseline: Skia (OpenGL backend), Cairo (CPU renderer and OpenGL backend), Qt
one_liner: Intel's archived GPU-only C++ canvas (OpenGL/GLES); author's clip-heavy demo ran about 5-8x Skia GL's frame rate in 2016.

name: Hyperscan
baseline: PCRE2
one_liner: SIMD multi-pattern regex matching library beating PCRE2 6.9-183x on large network-security rulesets.

name: Intel(R) Multi-Buffer Crypto for IPsec (intel-ipsec-mb)
baseline: OpenSSL (AES-256-CBC+HMAC-SHA-256 throughput) and FreeBSD OpenCrypto Framework (OCF) default kernel crypto (AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 VPN throughput)
one_liner: Intel's x86-64 assembly packet-crypto library; batches many packets per SIMD pass; beat OpenSSL AES-CBC+HMAC-SHA-256 once.

name: ISA-L (igzip)
baseline: zlib
one_liner: Intel's assembly-tuned deflate/gzip/zlib codec (igzip): about 4.8x zlib -1 compression speed and 2.3x its decompression speed.

name: Intel ISA-L Crypto (multi-buffer SHA)
baseline: The best-known single-buffer SHA-256 of 2012. The whitepaper cites Intel's own 'Fast SHA-256 Implementations on Intel Architecture Processors' (Guilford, Yap, Gopal, May 2012; ref [4]). OpenSSL is not named.
one_liner: Intel's SIMD multi-buffer SHA/MD5/SM3 hashing library; beats single-buffer SHA-256 throughput when many independent buffers are in flight.

name: Intel oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler (icpx)
license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception (intel/llvm LICENSE.TXT, the open-source base); the benchmarked icpx 2025.3.3 binary and its SVML/libimf runtimes came from the proprietary intel/oneapi-basekit image
baseline: GCC 13.3.0 and Clang 18.1.8
one_liner: Intel's LLVM-based C++ compiler (icpx); under relaxed FP it ran a math-heavy pipeline 1.5-1.8x faster than GCC/Clang.

name: Intel Neural Speed / LLM Runtime
baseline: ggml-based (llama.cpp) INT4
one_liner: Archived Intel llama.cpp-style CPU LLM runtime with low-bit weight-only GEMM kernels; ~1.2-1.4x faster INT4 next-token latency than ggml on Xeon.

name: Intel Parallel STL
baseline: std::accumulate (serial, libstdc++ 12)
one_liner: Intel's C++17 parallel algorithms (now oneDPL; libstdc++'s <execution>): std::reduce(par) on oneTBB beats serial std::accumulate ~98x.

name: Intel QPL (IAA hardware deflate path)
baseline: zlib-ng and zstd software compression (Intel RocksDB guide); Snappy and CPU deflate execution in DuckDB (ADMS 2025 paper)
one_liner: Intel's C library that offloads Deflate (4 KB window) to the IAA accelerator on Sapphire Rapids Xeons, beating Snappy, zstd and zlib-ng in database pipelines.

name: Intel XED (x86 encoder decoder)
baseline: Capstone (decode+format); Zydis and bddisasm (decode only)
one_liner: Intel's own x86/x86-64 decoder and encoder in C; decodes faster than full-mode Zydis, roughly ties or trails Capstone once formatting is included.

name: metajson (iod::metajson)
baseline: nlohmann/json, RapidJSON
one_liner: Header-only C++17 JSON codec for structs with compile-time-known shape; README claims up to 9x nlohmann/json, 2x RapidJSON.

name: iohttpparser (stateful-strict/lenient profiles)
baseline: llhttp
one_liner: Pull-based C23 HTTP/1.1 parser with strict framing checks; beats llhttp on header-heavy messages, not on tiny requests.

name: bcdec
baseline: DirectXTex BCn decoders (also Compressonator and bc7enc_rdo decoders)
one_liner: Single-header C BC1-BC7 block decoder; 1.3-11x DirectXTex's single-thread throughput in aras-p's 2022 decoder comparison.

name: Quarry
baseline: Protocol Buffers (C++, including Arena allocation)
one_liner: Schema compiler emitting no-heap C99, C++20 and Python BRF codecs; its C decoder beats Protobuf C++ on large/nested payloads.

name: LZMA (7-Zip LZMA SDK)
baseline: bzip2 1.0.8
one_liner: Igor Pavlov's public-domain LZMA/LZMA2 codec behind 7-Zip: 11% smaller than bzip2 -9, 2.2x faster decoding, 5x slower compression.

name: picoquic-DPDK (Tyunyayev kernel-bypass fork)
baseline: picoquic
one_liner: Research fork of picoquic that swaps kernel UDP sockets for DPDK; about 3x picoquic single-connection goodput on 100 GbE.

name: IPS⁴o (In-place Parallel Super Scalar Samplesort)
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: In-place parallel/sequential comparison sort beating std::sort via cache-efficient block-based samplesort partitioning.

name: evmone
baseline: go-ethereum (geth) built-in EVM interpreter
one_liner: C++20 Ethereum Virtual Machine interpreter behind the EVMC API; about 3.5x faster than go-ethereum's EVM in evm-bench.

name: v8malloc
baseline: glibc malloc, jemalloc, tcmalloc, mimalloc
one_liner: Early-stage Linux malloc replacement (LD_PRELOAD) claiming parity or small wins over glibc, tcmalloc, jemalloc and mimalloc on microbenchmarks.

name: libfiber (iqiyi)
baseline: libco (Tencent)
one_liner: C stackful coroutine runtime with libc network hooks; first-party echo-server chart shows about 1.6-1.7x libco's QPS.

name: cfilter (Cuckoo Filter implementation in Go)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Unmaintained pure-Go cuckoo filter (Fan et al. 2014) offering deletion as a Bloom-filter alternative; speed claims unmeasured, known item-loss bugs.

name: succinct-bitvec-cpp (FastBitVec / RRRBitVec)
baseline: SDSL rank_support_v and select_support_mcl
one_liner: Small header-only rank/select bit vectors (FastBitVec, RRRBitVec) tuned on Apple Silicon; edges SDSL rank_support_v/select_support_mcl at 1M bits.

name: iOverlay (Rust polygon boolean overlay engine)
baseline: Clipper2 (C++ polygon clipping library, v1.4.0); also Boost.Geometry (Boost 1.86.0)
one_liner: Rust 2D polygon boolean engine (union/intersect/difference/xor, offsetting) that outscales Clipper2 on very large, intersection-heavy inputs.

name: ISPC (Intel SPMD Program Compiler)
baseline: reference serial C++ implementations of the examples/ workloads (gcc 4.2.1 on OS X 10.7.2; MSVC 2010 on Windows Server 2008 for the 40-core table)
one_liner: LLVM-based compiler for an SPMD C dialect that runs kernels on CPU SIMD lanes; 3-7x one-core speedups over serial C++ in Intel's examples.

name: Marlin (FP16xINT4 LLM matmul kernel)
baseline: FP16 PyTorch matmul (calls CUTLASS) and other 4-bit kernels: torch-nightly, exllamav2, AWQ, bitsandbytes
one_liner: FP16 x INT4 weight-only GEMM for Ampere/Ada GPUs; near-ideal 3.9x over FP16 torch.matmul up to batch 16-32.

name: ITensors.jl (Julia) vs C++ ITensor v3.1.6 in ITensorBenchmarks.jl
baseline: C++ ITensor v3.1.6 (github.com/ITensor/ITensor), same tensor-network algorithms, Intel MKL BLAS/LAPACK on both sides
one_liner: Julia tensor-network library (DMRG, TRG, CTMRG) that matches or beats C++ ITensor v3 at large bond dimension on MKL.

name: libhv
baseline: libevent, libuv
one_liner: Cross-platform C event-loop library with built-in HTTP/WebSocket/MQTT; ~1.4-1.6x libevent/libuv echo throughput, ties libev/asio.

name: PGM Extra (pgm-extra-rs)
baseline: std::collections::BTreeSet / BTreeMap (Rust)
one_liner: Pure-Rust PGM learned index with BTreeSet/BTreeMap-style Set and Map; beats BTreeSet on u64 lookups, loses to binary search.

name: DeLZSA (ivagorRetrocomp)
baseline: LZSA reference decompressor (emmanuel-marty/lzsa)
one_liner: Intel 8080 and PDP-11 assembly decompressors for the LZSA1/LZSA2 formats; code no longer publicly reachable, no speed figures.

name: cbk (Compact Batch Kernels)
baseline: Intel MKL compact kernels (mkl_dgeqrf_compact, mkl_dpotrf_compact, mkl_dtrsm_compact pipeline) and per-matrix LAPACKE (LAPACKE_dgels, LAPACKE_dposv, LAPACKE_dgeqrf)
one_liner: Batched QR, Cholesky and unpivoted LDL^T solves for thousands of small matrices in interleaved layout; beats per-matrix LAPACKE and matches or beats MKL compact.

name: QuickJS-AOT (ivankra/quickjs-aot)
baseline: QuickJS interpreter ('base' column: commit b226856 of ivankra/quickjs, a bellard/quickjs fork)
one_liner: QuickJS fork whose qjsc -A compiles a script's bytecode to C ahead of time; about 1.36-1.43x the stock QuickJS interpreter on V8 suites.

name: loudness (iver56)
baseline: pyebur128 (Cython wrapper of libebur128), pyloudnorm, torchaudio, pyloudness
one_liner: Python wheel over a C++20 BS.1770 meter (Nomono's libloudness) that computes integrated LUFS about 1.7x faster than pyebur128/libebur128.

name: radix-heap (pair_radix_heap)
baseline: std::priority_queue
one_liner: Header-only C++ monotone radix heap: 1.2-1.7x faster than std::priority_queue on Dijkstra shortest-path workloads.

name: yaxpeax-x86
baseline: Capstone, Zydis, Intel XED, bddisasm, diStorm (x86/x64 disassembler libraries); no GNU as, NASM or MASM comparison
one_liner: Rust x86/x86-64 instruction decoder and formatter; in current disas-bench runs it decodes 5-9x faster than XED and Zydis.

name: NanoLog (Iyengar111)
license: MIT (full text in NanoLog.hpp and NanoLog.cpp, Copyright 2016 Karthik Iyengar)
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Small asynchronous C++11 stream-style logger; lower median caller latency than spdlog async, far behind Quill/fmtlog/PlatformLab NanoLog.

name: LinqFaster
baseline: System.Linq (LINQ to Objects) Min, Sum and OrderBy on int arrays under .NET Framework 4.x (CLR 4.0.30319.42000, 64-bit RyuJIT)
one_liner: Eager LINQ-style C# extension methods, with optional SIMD and parallel variants, for arrays, Span and List; beat .NET Framework LINQ 4-55x in 2017.

name: Verstable
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Single-header C hash table beating std::unordered_map on lookups, erasures, and iteration; insertion only average.

name: as-str
baseline: AssemblyScript standard library String methods (native String ops compiled by asc, run in V8 15.1.42)
one_liner: Zero-copy UTF-16/UTF-8 string views for AssemblyScript with SIMD/SWAR search; beats stdlib String on search and ASCII case folding.

name: json-as
baseline: JavaScript built-in JSON.parse / JSON.stringify in V8 (also fast-json-parse and assemblyscript-json)
one_liner: Schema-compiled JSON (de)serializer for AssemblyScript; on real payloads about 1-1.7x V8's JSON on 1-5 kB inputs, 3-6x on tiny ones.

name: TinyVM (tvm)
baseline: Lua (LuaDist lua build, July 2015, version not stated)
one_liner: About 1,200-line C virtual machine for an x86-style assembly language; a hand-written fib(34) ran about 1.7x faster than PUC Lua in 2015.

name: CO2
baseline: Boost.Coroutine2
one_liner: Header-only C++14 macro emulation of N4286 stackless coroutines; resume costs about 6 ns versus 82 ns for Boost.Coroutine2.

name: libxml2-wasm
language: C (libxml2) compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten; TypeScript wrapper
baseline: libxmljs2 0.32.x (native N-API binding of libxml2) and the pure-JavaScript XML parsers @rgrove/parse-xml, fast-xml-parser and xmldoc
one_liner: libxml2 compiled to WebAssembly with a TypeScript DOM API; parses XML faster than pure-JS parsers, roughly level with native libxmljs2.

name: postcard
baseline: Protobuf (prost 0.14.4; Google's protobuf 4.36.1-release crate also on the page), FlatBuffers (flatbuffers 25.12.19), Cap'n Proto (capnp 0.27.0), MessagePack (rmp-serde 1.3.1); all are the Rust crates for those formats, not the C++ libraries
one_liner: no_std serde binary format for Rust; serializes ~2x faster than prost/flatbuffers, ~3.6x faster than rmp-serde on log records.

name: FastAD
baseline: Adept, Stan Math, ADOL-C, CppAD, Sacado (C++ AD libraries)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 expression-template AD library; author reports 2-10x over Adept and 2-19x over Stan Math gradients.

name: AquaHash
baseline: xxHash (xxhash64)
one_liner: Single-header AES-NI 128-bit hash: about 4x XXH64 bulk throughput in SMHasher3, but fails 55/250 quality tests.

name: MetroHash
baseline: CityHash (City64/City128/City128crc)
one_liner: 2015 family of machine-generated 64/128-bit non-cryptographic hashes pitched as a faster CityHash; now outpaced by XXH3 and wyhash.

name: magic-trace
baseline: perf -g (and perf sampling flame graphs)
one_liner: Intel PT tracer recording every function call at about 40 ns resolution, with 2-10% overhead, below perf -g call-graph sampling.

name: Janet
baseline: CPython
one_liner: Embeddable Lisp-family scripting language in one C99 file; roughly CPython speed, ahead only on interpreter-bound object and float code.

name: jank persistent_string
baseline: std::string
one_liner: jank's built-in immutable string (jtl::immutable_string, backing persistent_string); claims to tie or beat std::string and folly::fbstring.

name: Janos95/kdtree
baseline: nanoflann
one_liner: Tiny 2020 Magnum/Corrade 3D kd-tree with 1-NN only; build ~15% faster than nanoflann, query claim invalidated by a pruning bug.

name: Vettel
baseline: Redis
one_liner: A ~300-line C CLI key-value store on one flat text file; its README times it slightly faster than redis-cli.

name: CodeJeNN (Keras-to-C++ inference header generator)
baseline: Keras eager-mode inference (TensorFlow backend for the MLP case, PyTorch backend for the CNN case)
one_liner: Python tool that turns a trained Keras MLP/CNN into one dependency-free C++ header; snippet-reported 2-25x over Keras eager on one core.

name: hop
baseline: unzip and tar (reading individual files)
one_liner: Uncompressed, read-only archive format and CLI in Zig with an indexed footer, for pulling single files faster than tar or unzip.

name: Blink
baseline: qemu-x86_64 (user-mode x86-64-linux emulation)
one_liner: 221 kB user-mode x86-64-linux emulator with a splicing JIT; claims up to 2x over qemu-x86_64 on some workloads.

name: Cosmopolitan Libc (pthread_mutex_t)
baseline: glibc pthread_mutex_t (also musl pthread_mutex_t)
one_liner: Portable libc whose pthread_mutex_t (Google nsync underneath) beat glibc 2.7x and musl 9.6x on a contended 30-thread lock test.

name: json.cpp
baseline: nlohmann::json (nlohmann::ordered_json)
one_liner: Lean C++11 JSON parser/serializer beating nlohmann::json 2-3x on parse/round-trip latency and compile time.

name: wallClockProfiler
baseline: Valgrind callgrind
one_liner: Single-file C++ 'poor man's profiler' that drives GDB to sample wall-clock stacks, with far less slowdown than callgrind.

name: Nino
baseline: MessagePack (MessagePack-CSharp, NuGet package 'MessagePack'); MemoryPack also compared
one_liner: C# source-generated binary serializer for .NET and Unity; beats MessagePack-CSharp and edges MemoryPack on its own microbenchmarks.

name: NonIntegerSRC (Holters-Parker resampler)
baseline: libsamplerate (SRC_SINC_FASTEST)
one_liner: SSE Holters-Parker IIR resampler, timed 17-40x faster than libsamplerate SINC_FASTEST at far lower, unmatched quality.

name: RTNeural
baseline: libtorch, ONNX Runtime 1.15.1, TensorFlow Lite 2.14.0
one_liner: Real-time-safe C++ inference for small Dense/GRU/LSTM/Conv nets; per-sample calls run 2x-190x faster than ONNX Runtime/libtorch/TFLite.

name: java-fast/quad-search
baseline: java.util.Arrays.binarySearch
one_liner: Java port of Lemire's SIMD Quad search: quaternary narrowing plus a Vector API block scan, 5-29% lower mean latency than Arrays.binarySearch on int arrays.

name: PicoTree
baseline: nanoflann v1.7.1 (also OpenCV FLANN 4.11.0, SciPy KDTree, scikit-learn KDTree, pykdtree)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 kd-tree for exact and approximate kNN, radius and box search; builds faster than nanoflann and OpenCV FLANN.

name: libcoro
baseline: cppcoro (Boost.Cobalt for the channel row)
one_liner: C++20 coroutine library with epoll/kqueue TCP, UDP, TLS and DNS; edges cppcoro on single-threaded socket ping-pong.

name: Nail (NailDNS demo server)
baseline: BIND
one_liner: 295-line C authoritative DNS demo built on the Nail parser generator; ~2.9x BIND 9.9.5 qps in a 2014 loopback test.

name: HalftimeHash
baseline: xxHash (xxh128)
one_liner: Keyed almost-universal C++ hash for long strings; ~1.3-1.4x xxh128 on 256 KiB inputs with AVX-512.

name: TinyBVH
baseline: Intel Embree (also madmann91/bvh)
one_liner: Header-only C++ BVH builder and ray tracer; author's benchmark shows faster SAH builds and single-ray traversal than Embree.

name: CavalierContours
baseline: Clipper (ClipperLib polygon offsetting, Angus Johnson, original Clipper)
one_liner: Header-only C++ offsetting and booleans for 2D polylines with exact arcs; up to 16-85x faster than Clipper1 offsets when arcs stay exact.

name: jc_voronoi
baseline: Boost.Polygon voronoi_diagram (Boost 1.92.0); also jc_voronoi 0.9.0, and in older README prose Fastjet/Fortune C, O'Sullivan C++, voronoi++
one_liner: Single-header C99 Fortune-sweep 2D Voronoi/Delaunay generator, 1.4-3.7x faster than Boost.Polygon voronoi on random points.

name: jeaiii/itoa
baseline: sprintf (C standard library, MSVC CRT) and MSVC _itoa/_ui64toa in the README's release charts; {fmt} in the godbolt table. No std::to_chars comparison exists.
one_liner: Header-only branchless integer-to-ASCII conversion, ~7-9x faster than sprintf/MSVC _itoa, ~1.6-1.8x vs {fmt}.

name: libsodium (BLAKE2b)
baseline: OpenSSL BLAKE2b (EVP_blake2b512)
one_liner: libsodium's crypto_generichash BLAKE2b: ~1.2-2.7x OpenSSL EVP BLAKE2b-512 on 64 B-1 KB inputs, roughly even from 4 KB.

name: parasail
baseline: SSW (Complete-Striped-Smith-Waterman-Library, C, SSE2 striped Smith-Waterman); the same page also times Opal, SWIPE and ssearch36
one_liner: C99 SIMD library of local, global and semi-global pairwise sequence alignment kernels; beats SSW on protein database search.

name: jemalloc
baseline: phkmalloc (FreeBSD libc malloc, the incumbent jemalloc replaced)
one_liner: General-purpose malloc(3) with per-thread arenas and decay-based purging; beats FreeBSD's phkmalloc under concurrency.

name: Polylidar3D
baseline: CGAL 2D Alpha Shapes (also PostGIS ST_ConcaveHull 2.5.2 and Spatialite ST_ConcaveHull, which the README treats as GEOS-based)
one_liner: C++ concave-polygon (with holes) extraction from 2D points and 3D data; about 4.8x faster than CGAL 2D alpha shapes.

name: httpserver.h
baseline: NGINX 1.14.0 (worker_processes 1)
one_liner: Single-header C library for embedding a non-blocking HTTP/1.1 server; the author's 2019 ab hello-world run beat a one-worker nginx 1.14 by about 1.7x.

name: Klein
baseline: GLM (glm::quat multiplication; glm::dualquat converted with mat3x4_cast and applied to a glm::vec4), with RTM (Realtime Math) as a second reference
one_liner: Header-only SSE library for 3D projective geometric algebra; its llvm-mca listings show about half GLM's estimated cycles for quaternion and dual-quaternion work.

name: Clustered Elias-Fano Indexes (CPEF)
baseline: Partitioned Elias-Fano (PEF) and Binary Interpolative Coding (BIC) inverted index compression
one_liner: Research inverted-index codec that encodes clusters of posting lists against a shared reference list; smaller than partitioned Elias-Fano.

name: LPHash
baseline: BBHash (also PTHash)
one_liner: Locality-preserving MPHF for DNA k-mer sets: 0.53-0.87 bits/k-mer at k=63, versus 3.06-3.71 for BBHash and 2.04-2.76 for PTHash.

name: mutable_rank_select
baseline: Fenwick-tree based rank/select over mutable bitmaps (Marchini and Vigna, now part of sux)
one_liner: SIMD b-ary Segment-Tree index for rank/select/flip on mutable bitmaps; paper reports it beats Marchini-Vigna compact Fenwick trees.

name: opt_vbyte
baseline: Plain unpartitioned VByte (varint)
one_liner: Research code that partitions posting lists into VByte and bitmap blocks, cutting VByte index space 30-47% at equal query speed.

name: PTHash
baseline: BBHash
one_liner: Header-only C++17 minimal perfect hash library (PTHash/PHOBIC) with 3.1-4.6x faster lookups than BBHash at ~3 bits/key.

name: Sliced Indexes (s_indexes)
baseline: Partitioned Elias-Fano (ds2i-style PEF); Roaring also compared
one_liner: Universe-sliced compressed integer sets (bitmaps/posting lists) with SIMD intersection; 5-10x faster AND than Partitioned Elias-Fano.

name: SSHash
baseline: Pufferfish (and dBG-FM, BLight k-mer dictionaries)
one_liner: Compressed static DNA k-mer dictionary: ~5x smaller than Pufferfish, 1.6-2.4x faster streaming lookups, but slower random lookups.

name: wasm-perf (Emscripten Wasm SIMD intrinsics vs JavaScript matrix multiply)
baseline: JavaScript (mul_mats.js) running in Node.js v16.16.0 (V8)
one_liner: Blog demo: 64x64 int32 matrix multiply in C compiled to Wasm SIMD128 by Emscripten, timed against a plain JavaScript loop.

name: JerryScript
baseline: Duktape
one_liner: C99 JavaScript engine for microcontrollers that trades speed for footprint; uses less memory than Duktape but runs about 2x slower.

name: Kotlin/Wasm (JetBrains kotlin-wasm-benchmarks)
baseline: Kotlin/JS output (JavaScript) running in V8
one_liner: Kotlin's WasmGC compiler backend; JetBrains' 2023 charts show 1.25-2.5x faster than Kotlin/JS output on most macro benchmarks.

name: EVE (Expressive Vector Engine)
baseline: scalar C++ / compiler auto-vectorization (no baseline stated; successor of Boost.SIMD)
one_liner: C++20 SIMD wrapper (eve::wide) with a large vectorised math library and SIMD STL-style algorithms; successor of Boost.SIMD, no published speedups.

name: banzai
baseline: bzip2 reference implementation (C); lbzip2 and pbzip2 not compared
one_liner: Pure-Rust bzip2 encoder using linear-time SA-IS for the BWT; bounds bzip2's worst case but is slower on average.

name: SIMD-math-prims (vectorizable approximate sin, cos, log, exp)
baseline: libm sinf, cosf, logf, expf (scalar single-precision functions)
one_liner: One MIT header of polynomial sin/cos/exp/log approximations that compilers auto-vectorise; 21-36x over scalar libm floats, about 1e-5 error.

name: ENG25519 (Curve25519_AVX512IFMA)
baseline: OpenSSL 1.1.1 X25519 (x86-64 assembly, crypto/ec/asm/x25519-x86_64.pl) and Ed25519 (C implementation, crypto/ec/curve25519.c), extracted from OpenSSL_1_1_1-stable and compiled into the paper's benchmark harness; the TLS-level experiments use OpenSSL 1.1.1q
one_liner: AVX-512IFMA X25519/Ed25519 code plus an OpenSSL 1.1.1 ENGINE; beats OpenSSL's x86-64 Curve25519 code 3.3-12x on throughput.

name: PQRV (Keccak, Kyber, Dilithium on RV{32,64}IM{B}{V})
baseline: pq-crystals reference C for Kyber (ref, commit 441c051) and Dilithium (ref, commit f1f8085) and PQClean fips202.c for Keccak (commit 05df469), compiled with the XuanTie GCC 10.4.0 at -O3 on the same core
one_liner: RISC-V assembly Keccak, Kyber and Dilithium for RV32/RV64 with B and V; 2-5x fewer cycles than pq-crystals reference C.

name: VecFalcon (Vectorized Falcon-Sign)
license: MIT (root LICENSE). The C-FN-DSA-derived opt/ and ref/ directories carry the Unlicense. opt/fft_neon.c is Apache-2.0 (derived from GMUCERG Falcon_NEON).
baseline: C-FN-DSA (Thomas Pornin's FN-DSA/Falcon implementation, github.com/pornin/c-fn-dsa at commit 96e3b92), SHAKE256X4 variant
one_liner: Falcon/FN-DSA signing with a batched SIMD Gaussian BaseSampler and RISC-V FFT; sign_core runs 1.13-1.59x faster than C-FN-DSA.

name: LIPP (Updatable Learned Index with Precise Positions)
baseline: STX B+Tree; also beats Adaptive Radix Tree (ART), ALEX, PGM-index, BwTree, and a 2-level RMI ("Learned Index")
one_liner: Header-only, single-threaded learned index for numeric keys; beats STX B+Tree, ART and ALEX on point-lookup and insert throughput.

name: chyaml
baseline: rapidyaml
one_liner: C++20 YAML 1.2.2 parser/emitter whose 8-byte event tape builds about 2x faster than rapidyaml's arena tree on config-shaped YAML.

name: jianrong7/http-parser (Go zero-alloc parser)
baseline: net/http (Go standard library, http.ReadRequest)
one_liner: Tiny zero-allocation Go HTTP/1.x request parser that records byte offsets; ~5-10x faster than net/http.ReadRequest, with far less validation.

name: MPSFT (Matrix Pencil Sparse Fourier Transform)
baseline: FFTW (FFTW_ESTIMATE and FFTW_MEASURE plans)
one_liner: Research sparse Fourier transform (C++11) that recovers S dominant modes of a huge noisy spectrum faster than a full FFTW transform.

name: blz4
baseline: lz4 (lz4 -12 -l, legacy format)
one_liner: Experimental LZ4 legacy-format encoder using BriefLZ's optimal parser; output matches lz4 -12 or is a few bytes smaller, at much lower speed.

name: BriefLZ
baseline: zlib (zlib 1.2.11 in the README table, zlib 1.3.2 in lzbench 2.4)
one_liner: Tiny C LZ77 compressor with gamma-coded lengths/offsets; at -6 it matches zlib -9's ratio with about 2x faster compression.

name: kb_text_shape
baseline: HarfBuzz
one_liner: Single-header C library for Unicode segmentation and OpenType shaping; claimed faster than HarfBuzz, measured 2-160x slower independently.

name: NonuniformFFTs.jl (Julia NUFFT, CPU and GPU) vs FINUFFT and cuFINUFFT
baseline: FINUFFT v2.4.1 (C++, CPU) and cuFINUFFT (CUDA C++, GPU), both compiled locally and called through FINUFFT.jl v3.4.0
one_liner: Julia NUFFT library for CPU, CUDA and AMD GPUs; its shared-memory GPU spreading beats cuFINUFFT on dense 3D type-1 transforms.

name: CapelliniSpTRSV (thread-level synchronization-free GPU sparse triangular solve)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpTRSV (CUSPARSE_SOLVE_POLICY_NO_LEVEL / USE_LEVEL) and the SyncFree SpTRSV of bhSPARSE
one_liner: GPU sparse lower-triangular solve (CSR) using one thread per row; ICPP '20 reports 4.00x over cuSPARSE csrsv2.

name: Dragonbox
baseline: std::to_chars
one_liner: Shortest round-trip double/float-to-decimal conversion, faster than std::to_chars.

name: rans_static (rANS_static4x16, r32x16b_avx2 SIMD rANS experiments)
baseline: rANS_static4c (4-way interleaved scalar rANS, the CRAM variant) and arith_static (unrolled static arithmetic coder), both in the same repo
one_liner: James Bonfield's 2014-2018 static rANS experiments; the 32-way AVX2 decoder runs about 4x faster than the CRAM rANS_static4c codec.

name: camellia-simd-aesni
baseline: Camellia reference implementation (NTT camellia-BSD-1.2.0 camellia.c, table-based scalar C, built at -O2 in the same harness)
one_liner: Byte-sliced Camellia kernels computing S-boxes with AES-NI/VAES/GFNI; 3-19x faster than NTT's table-based reference C.

name: TinyTIFF
baseline: libTIFF (libtiff 3.8.2 and 4.6.0)
one_liner: Small C library that appends fixed-size uncompressed frames to a multi-page TIFF with less per-frame overhead than libTIFF.

name: HPS (High Performance Serialization)
baseline: Boost.Serialization
one_liner: Header-only C++11 serializer for STL/user types; faster and smaller than Boost.Serialization, no schema needed.

name: Julia vs C++11 random-walk Monte Carlo (jlapeyre/ranwalk-Julia-vs-Cxx)
baseline: C++11 std::mt19937 with std::bernoulli_distribution(0.5), compiled with c++ -std=c++11 -O3 (Debian gcc 4.9.1)
one_liner: 2014 toy random-walk benchmark: Julia 0.3's dSFMT-backed randbool() beats libstdc++ mt19937 plus bernoulli_distribution(0.5) about 3x.

name: nanoflann
baseline: Boost.Geometry 1.90 R*-tree (point k-nearest and range queries)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 k-d tree for exact point kNN/radius search; about 2.4x faster point kNN than Boost.Geometry's R*-tree.

name: Yomm2
baseline: C++ virtual member function call (closed dispatch via vtable)
one_liner: Archived C++17 open multi-methods library; plain dispatch is slower than virtual calls, and its 5x virtual_ptr win is a cache-layout artifact.

name: absurd-sql
language: JavaScript backend for SQLite compiled to WebAssembly (sql.js)
baseline: IndexedDB used directly in the browser
one_liner: IndexedDB-backed block storage for sql.js (SQLite in WebAssembly); its own browser benchmark shows it beating one-row-per-record IndexedDB.

name: libxlsxwriter
baseline: Python XlsxWriter (the same author's pure-Python XLSX writer, the incumbent for this task)
one_liner: ANSI C write-only XLSX library; same API family as Python XlsxWriter, about 4.4x faster than it on a 200k-cell sheet.

name: ruopus
baseline: libopus 1.6.1 (SIMD-enabled C)
one_liner: Pure-Rust Opus encoder and decoder: SILK/hybrid decode 1.4-1.8x faster than libopus 1.6.1; encode at parity at matched complexity.

name: Easy::jit
baseline: the same kernel compiled ahead of time (non-specialised) with clang
one_liner: Clang plugin plus runtime that re-optimises a C++ function at run time with some arguments fixed as constants; beats the generic AOT build.

name: jnettlet/cortex_a72_memcpy (Cortex-A72 tuned AArch64 memcpy/memset)
baseline: glibc memcpy (the 'memcpy' row) and Arm Optimized Routines memcpy (__memcpy_aarch64, __memcpy_aarch64_simd)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD AArch64 memcpy/memmove/memset from Arm optimized-routines, re-tuned for Cortex-A72; ties glibc except small aligned copies.

name: jdz_allocator
baseline: C malloc (glibc via Zig c_allocator), Zig GeneralPurposeAllocator, rpmalloc Zig port, zimalloc
one_liner: rpmalloc-style span allocator for Zig; claims parity with the rpmalloc Zig port and lower memory, no shown win over malloc.

name: meow_fft
baseline: KissFFT
one_liner: Single-header C99 float FFT (0BSD), scalar radix-8 mixed-radix, 1.1-1.5x faster than KissFFT on power-of-two sizes.

name: Miller 6 (mlr, Go rewrite of C Miller 5)
baseline: Miller 5.10.3, the earlier C implementation of the same tool (charts label it mlr-5.10.3); the docs explicitly decline to compare with awk, sort or cut
one_liner: Go rewrite of Miller, the header-keyed CSV/JSON record tool; beats its C predecessor 5.10.3 on CSV and multi-verb chains.

name: gemm (johnnyw3, AVX/AMX kernels)
baseline: OpenBLAS or Intel MKL, whichever was faster on each machine (OpenBLAS built with BUILD_BFLOAT16=1 for AMX)
one_liner: Hand-written AVX2/AVX-512/AMX square GEMM kernels; 3-4% faster than OpenBLAS/MKL only on Granite Rapids AMX (bf16).

name: gpu-compute (SGEMM for Blackwell)
baseline: cuBLAS cublasSgemm with CUBLAS_PEDANTIC_MATH (true FP32) on an RTX 5080
one_liner: Hand-written CUDA SGEMM kernels that beat pedantic-FP32 cuBLAS only on tiny square matrices (N<=256) on an RTX 5080.

name: Randompack
baseline: C++ std <random> (std::mt19937_64 + std::uniform_real_distribution / std::normal_distribution), NumPy, Base-R, Julia, oneMKL
one_liner: C11 bulk random-variate library (xoshiro/PCG/Philox/ChaCha, 20+ distributions); ~10-15x faster than C++ <random> for U(0,1)/N(0,1) fills.

name: simd-radix-sort (SIMD MSB radix sort with separate key and payload streams)
baseline: std::sort (STLSort in the thesis); thesis also compares Intel IPP Radix Sort, Bramas AVX-512 quicksort, Blacher AVX2 quicksort and Moeller's SIMD radix sort
one_liner: AVX-512 in-place binary MSB radix sort for any arithmetic key plus payload arrays; about 2.7-4.1x std::sort on random keys.

name: RSHash
baseline: SSHash
one_liner: Static compressed k-mer dictionary that swaps SSHash's MPHF for rank/select bitvectors; 1.4x faster streaming lookups than current SSHash.

name: xmloxide
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Pure-Rust libxml2 reimplementation: parsing at libxml2 parity, self-reported 1.5-2.4x faster serialization and 1.1-2.7x faster XPath.

name: Jooby (Java)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Java/Kotlin web framework on Netty (or Jetty/Undertow/Vert.x); ties actix-web on the-benchmarker's empty GET / test.

name: json_struct
baseline: nlohmann/json v3.11.3
one_liner: Single-header C++11 JSON-to-struct binder; about 2.6x faster roundtrip than nlohmann/json on a third-party M1 benchmark.

name: Kore
baseline: nginx (with the echo module)
one_liner: Sandboxed C (or Python/Lua) web application server; outran an OpenResty nginx echo setup 1.5x in a 2015 unequal hello-world test.

name: diamond-types
language: Rust (npm packages diamond-types-node and diamond-types-web via WebAssembly)
baseline: Automerge v0.5.9 (Rust) and Yjs v13.6.10 (JavaScript on Node.js v22.2.0), per the EuroSys 2025 Eg-walker paper; also the authors' own reference CRDT (Yrs, the Rust port of Yjs, was run but omitted from the paper)
one_liner: Rust Eg-walker text CRDT (wasm npm builds) merging editing histories 22-404x faster than Automerge and mostly faster than Yjs.

name: jumprope (Rust rope)
license: ISC (LICENSE.txt and README); Cargo.toml declares ISC OR Apache-2.0
baseline: librope (C skip-list rope by the same author)
one_liner: Rust rope (skip list of gap-buffer leaves) that replays real editing traces about 2.4-2.7x faster than the author's C librope.

name: librope
baseline: flat contiguous string (a hand-written Rust String insert/delete by Unicode character offset, labelled 'Raw string'); the README itself says 'straight C strings' but gives no numbers for that
one_liner: Two-file C99 skip-list UTF-8 rope with O(log n) insert/delete at character offsets; beats flat strings on large documents.

name: vkvg
baseline: Cairo (GL ES3 backend) and Skia (Vulkan backend)
one_liner: Cairo-style 2D vector library in C on Vulkan; the author's chart shows it beating Cairo's GL ES3 backend on lines, circles and stars.

name: JPHP
baseline: PHP 5.6, PHP 7.0 and PHP 7.4 (Zend engine)
one_liner: PHP 7.1+ compiled to JVM bytecode; claims 2.5x over PHP 5.6 and 1.1x over 7.0, but is 13% slower than 7.4.

name: memtrail
license: MIT (permission headers in memtrail.cpp, memtrail.h and the memtrail script, Copyright 2011-2019 Jose Fonseca; no LICENSE file)
baseline: Valgrind Memcheck and Massif
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD heap profiler and leak finder for Linux; claims much lower overhead than Valgrind Massif or Memcheck, unmeasured.

name: raqote
baseline: Cairo (image surface; 1.18.4 on the M1 Pro run, 1.18.2 on the Windows x86 run); not faster than Skia once the broken rotated tests are excluded
one_liner: Small pure-Rust CPU 2D rasterizer built on Skia-style 4x4 supersampling. Its path fills beat Cairo's image surface on an M1 Pro; overall it does not beat Skia.

name: Jolt Physics
baseline: Bullet Physics (via Ammo.js, the Emscripten build of Bullet)
