one_liner: Multicore C++ rigid-body physics and collision library; as single-threaded wasm it beats Ammo.js (Bullet) once bodies sleep, not while they collide.

name: JRuby
baseline: CRuby (MRI) 2.7.7p221
one_liner: Ruby on the JVM; with invokedynamic it beat CRuby 2.7.7 on 9 of 13 single-threaded shootout programs once warm.

name: autoscale_cuckoo_filter
baseline: cuckoo filter: sile's scalable_cuckoo_filter crate v0.5.1 (the upstream it was forked from, labelled 'cuckoo_filter' in the table) and the axiomhq cuckoofilter crate v0.5 with FarmHasher (~6M crates.io downloads)
one_liner: Rust auto-growing cuckoo filter, a retuned copy of sile/scalable_cuckoo_filter; 4-5.6x faster positive lookups than it and cuckoofilter.

name: json-c
baseline: Jansson v2.7 (same suite also: nlohmann/json v2.0.3, JsonCpp 1.0.0, cJSON 1.5.0)
one_liner: Long-standing reference-counted C JSON DOM; in a 2016 independent run it stringified a parsed canada.json 4x faster than Jansson, losing elsewhere.

name: jsoniter (json-iterator/go)
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Pure-Go encoding/json replacement with cached per-type codecs; ~1.8x faster typed-struct Unmarshal than encoding/json. Archived.

name: jtkukunas/zlib (Intel zlib fork)
baseline: zlib (stock deflate)
one_liner: Archived Intel fork of zlib with SSE4.2 hashing and new quick/medium deflate strategies; about 1.8x stock zlib at mid levels.

name: JUCE software renderer (juce_graphics)
baseline: Skia (CPU pipeline) and Cairo 1.18.4
one_liner: JUCE's CPU path rasterizer (EdgeTable + SWAR pixel blending); about 1.7x Skia and 2.9x Cairo single-threaded on M1 Pro.

name: TupleMarkup (TML)
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Tiny C parser for TML, a bracket-based nested-list markup format; author claims ~5x libxml2's parse speed on equivalent data.

name: Spice
baseline: Rayon (cross-language comparison)
one_liner: Zig fork/join library using heartbeat scheduling; sub-nanosecond fork/join overhead versus Rayon's ~15 ns per join.

name: GeometryOps.jl
baseline: GEOS (through GeoPandas/Shapely in Python and the 'geos' package in R)
one_liner: Pure-Julia 2D/spherical geometry ops; beats GEOS-through-GeoPandas/R on simple point tasks, but trails GEOS called directly.

name: VoronoiDelaunay.jl
baseline: CGAL 4.4 2D Delaunay triangulation
one_liner: Julia package for incremental 2D Delaunay/Voronoi tessellation; its author's 2014 benchmark had it about 20% faster than CGAL 4.4.

name: Julia
language: Julia (C/C++ runtime on LLVM; embeddable from C/C++ through libjulia)
baseline: LuaJIT 2.1, PyPy 3 (7.3.x), Node.js (V8) and OpenJDK HotSpot, on the same CPU-bound algorithms
one_liner: Dynamic language JIT-compiled through LLVM per concrete argument types; beats LuaJIT, PyPy and Node on loop-heavy CPU code.

name: LowRankApprox.jl (Julia randomized interpolative decomposition) vs SciPy/Fortran ID
baseline: SciPy interpolative decomposition (scipy.linalg.interpolative via PyMatrixID), which at the README's time wrapped the Fortran77 ID library; SciPy 1.15.0 ported that code to Cython. The README also names MATLAB. Neither is a C or C++ -O3 baseline.
one_liner: Julia package of randomized, early-terminating low-rank factorizations (ID, pivoted QR, SVD, CUR); README times an ID about 3.5x faster than SciPy's Fortran ID.

name: Octavian.jl
baseline: OpenBLAS and Intel MKL (also BLIS)
one_liner: Pure-Julia multithreaded GEMM built on LoopVectorization; median 1816 GFLOPS at 1000^3 vs OpenBLAS 1254 and MKL 1348.

name: RecursiveFactorization.jl
baseline: OpenBLAS (Julia LUFactorization default) and Intel MKL (MKLLUFactorization)
one_liner: Pure-Julia recursive LU (Toledo's algorithm) that beats OpenBLAS and often MKL getrf on dense matrices up to about 500x500.

name: Bessels.jl
baseline: SpecialFunctions.jl wrappers: openlibm (C, FreeBSD msun) j0/y0/j1/y1/jn/yn for integer-order and order-0 and 1 calls, AMOS zbes* routines (Fortran, via openspecfun) for non-integer order, so only the order-0 and order-1 rows have a C baseline
one_liner: Pure-Julia Bessel, Hankel and Airy functions for real arguments; README claims 2.3-10x over SpecialFunctions.jl (openlibm/AMOS).

name: DoubleFloats.jl
baseline: MPFR (via Julia BigFloat at 128-bit precision, 'Big128')
one_liner: Julia double-double floats (Double64, about 106-bit significand) running 6-25x faster than 128-bit BigFloat/MPFR on vector and matrix kernels.

name: FFTA.jl (pure Julia FFT) vs FFTW.jl on small static vectors
baseline: FFTW (C library) through FFTW.jl fft(x)
one_liner: Generic pure-Julia FFT for any element type; its only speed claim over FFTW is a 2021 one-shot N=64 snippet that no longer reproduces.

name: triehash
baseline: gperf
one_liner: Order-preserving minimal perfect hash generator emitting nested C switches for fixed string sets; 1.85-5x gperf's throughput in author's benchmark.

name: LoopVectorization.jl
baseline: Intel MKL dgemm (single-threaded, via Julia LinearAlgebra.mul!)
one_liner: Julia @turbo macro that SIMD-vectorizes plain loops; its triple-loop gemm edges single-threaded MKL on small matrices.

name: TriangularSolve.jl
baseline: Intel MKL (libmkl_rt.so loaded through MKL.jl; MKL version not stated) triangular solve called through Julia LinearAlgebra: rdiv!(copyto!(C, A), UpperTriangular(B)) and the 3-argument ldiv!(C, LowerTriangular(B), A) on the Intel run. The M1 run prints no BLAS configuration or versioninfo, so its BLAS is not named.
one_liner: Pure-Julia SIMD triangular solves (trsm-style) that beat MKL by 9-11% single-threaded at N=100 in a 2021 README run.

name: VectorizedRNG.jl (SIMD Xoshiro256++ for Julia)
baseline: Julia Base default RNG of the time (dSFMT-based MersenneTwister, a SIMD-oriented Mersenne Twister variant)
one_liner: Julia SIMD xoshiro-style RNG with vectorized Box-Muller; about 2x Julia's old dSFMT MersenneTwister for randn! (1.5-3.4x for rand!).

name: SymbolicUtils.jl / Symbolics.jl (Julia symbolic engine) vs SymEngine (C++): SciMLBenchmarks SymEngineComparison
baseline: SymEngine v0.12.0 (C++ symbolic library, via SymEngine.jl v0.13.2 and SymEngine_jll)
one_liner: Pure-Julia symbolic term-rewriting engine (core of Symbolics.jl). It beats SymEngine (C++) only on IR-cached search and substitution and on JIT-compiled evaluation.

name: xxhash-wasm
language: WebAssembly with JavaScript wrapper (implementation of xxHash 32-bit and 64-bit)
baseline: xxhashjs (pure JavaScript xxHash, uses cuint for 64-bit math); also Node built-in crypto md5 and sha1 (different, cryptographic algorithms)
one_liner: Hand-written WebAssembly XXH32/XXH64 for browsers and Node, tens to hundreds of times faster than pure-JS xxhashjs.

name: lo (just-js)
baseline: Node.js (V8)
one_liner: Small V8-based JavaScript runtime with C++ bindings; scores 1.09-1.41x Node 26 on the v8-v7 suite.

name: blazehttp
baseline: valyala/fasthttp
one_liner: Go HTTP/1.1+HTTP/2 server/client with zero-copy header parser; ~11-14% more HTTP/1.1 req/s than fasthttp (author's wrk runs).

name: swerver
baseline: nginx (openresty/openresty:alpine Docker image, unpinned tag; tuned nginx.conf with worker_processes auto, reuseport, 'return 200' for /health and content_by_lua for /echo)
one_liner: Zig HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server and gateway on io_uring; edges an -O3 nginx on HttpArena plaintext and TLS, loses badly on HTTP/3.

name: sax-wasm
baseline: sax-js and saxes (JavaScript streaming XML parsers)
one_liner: Rust/WebAssembly streaming SAX parser for XML, HTML, JSX and Angular templates with positions; claims to beat saxes and sax-js, but only measured with no events subscribed.

name: dhi (Zig SIMD WASM Zod 4 replacement)
language: Zig (compiled to SIMD WebAssembly, plus an N-API addon and a Python C extension)
baseline: Zod 4 (TypeScript/JavaScript schema validation)
one_liner: Zod 4 API clone in plain TypeScript with code-generated validators; 1.6-7.8x faster than Zod 4 on reused schemas.

name: nanoregex
baseline: Python re (CPython built-in re module)
one_liner: Pure-Zig regex engine beating Python's re module on 6 of 7 README benchmark patterns.

name: argminmax
baseline: scalar Rust argmin+argmax loop (the repo's own scalar_* benchmark rows)
one_liner: Rust crate: argmin and argmax indices in one SIMD pass, 2.4-21x faster than its own scalar loop.

name: bilinear_filter_simd
baseline: plain scalar C++ bilinear filter in the same repo ('No SIMD')
one_liner: Demo SSE4, AVX2 and AVX-512 bilinear sampler for packed 24-bit BGR images; 1.2-2.3x over its own scalar loop.

name: tiny-skia-cpp
baseline: Rust tiny-skia (linebender/tiny-skia, a Skia subset)
one_liner: C++20 port of Rust tiny-skia (Skia-subset CPU rasterizer) with AVX2/NEON backends; first-party 1.2-1.9x faster than the Rust original.

name: cpp-lazy
baseline: std::ranges / std::views (libstdc++ 13): filter, chunk, chunk_by, lazy_split, stride, slide, zip, cartesian_product, repeat, take, join
one_liner: Header-only C++11 lazy-iterator library; first-party 32-element benchmarks show filter 3.6x and chunks 2.6x faster than std::views.

name: FPC (Fast Prefix Coder)
baseline: zlib Huffman (zlibh) and FSE Huff0 (fsehuf) as packaged in TurboBench
one_liner: Single-file ISC C Huffman (prefix) coder decoding silesia.tar about 1.25x faster than FSE's Huff0 and 3.7x faster than zlib's Huffman.

name: Zynum
baseline: OpenBLAS 0.3.34 (also Apple Accelerate)
one_liner: Zig BLAS 1-3 with CBLAS/Fortran ABI and SME kernels; about 2x OpenBLAS GEMM on Apple M5, roughly even with Accelerate.

name: kalcutter/bitshuffle
baseline: kiyo-masui/bitshuffle reference implementation (bshuf_trans_bit_elem / bshuf_untrans_bit_elem)
one_liner: C99 rewrite of the Bitshuffle bit-transpose filter with SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512/GFNI kernels; claims 1.3x-10x over classic bitshuffle.

name: poplar-trie
baseline: std::unordered_map (also tsl::robin_map, tsl::htrie_map, google::dense_hash_map, cedar, libart, JudySL)
one_liner: Header-only dynamic path-decomposed trie string map; about 5.4x less memory than std::unordered_map, but 3-4x slower.

name: sucds
baseline: vers-vecs RsVec and succinctly BitVec (Rust crates), not SDSL
one_liner: Safe pure-Rust succinct structures (Rank9Sel, DArray, Elias-Fano, wavelet matrix); select1 1.3-7.8x faster than vers-vecs on ARM64.

name: xcdat
baseline: marisa-trie (LOUDS nested patricia trie, s-yata/marisa-trie); also compared against tx LOUDS trie, fst, pdt
one_liner: Header-only C++17 compressed double-array trie dictionary; about 2x faster key-to-ID lookup than marisa-trie, at about 1.1-2x its size.

name: lodepng-turbo
baseline: libpng
one_liner: 2019 lodepng hack with libdeflate inflate and SSE2 PNG unfiltering; claims 2x libpng decode, unmeasured, and HEAD has decode bugs.

name: Hyperbolic Caching
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Research Redis 3.0 fork plus simulator whose cost-aware 'hits over time-in-cache' eviction beats Redis's sampled LRU on miss rate.

name: Partitioned Learned Bloom Filter (PLBF)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Python solver for Partitioned Learned Bloom Filter parameters; the resulting design uses less space than Bloom, sandwiched LBF, Ada-BF.

name: khttp
baseline: Drogon 1.9.13 (C++, trantor event loop; the-benchmarker cpp/drogon, cmake release build); also agoo-c 0.7 (C) in the same table
one_liner: Synchronous Rust HTTP/1.1 micro-framework (memchr and libc only) with an epoll dispatcher; 1.12-1.22x Drogon on the-benchmarker's trivial routes.

name: http.zig (httpz)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Zig HTTP/1.1 server library on epoll/kqueue; ties actix-web on hello-world req/s, leading ~5% only at 512 connections.

name: llm.c (GPT-2/GPT-3 training in C/CUDA)
baseline: PyTorch Nightly (parallel reference implementation train_gpt2.py)
one_liner: GPT-2/GPT-3 pretraining in plain C/CUDA with hand-written fused kernels; about 7% faster than PyTorch nightly on one A100.

name: kd3
baseline: nanoflann (header-only C++ kd-tree)
one_liner: AGPL header-only C++23 static kd-tree for low-dimensional points (3D default); median 3.7x faster builds and 1.9x faster k-NN than nanoflann.

name: Contour-Coherent Hausdorff Distance
baseline: Boost.Geometry discrete_hausdorff_distance
one_liner: Header-only exact discrete Hausdorff distance for ordered 2D contours; 245x faster than Boost.Geometry on similar silhouettes (author's run).

name: atJIT (autotuning JIT on Easy::jit)
baseline: untuned default configuration of the same code as labelled 'Default' on the author's slide (optimisation level not stated, so not shown to be clang -O3 ahead-of-time or Easy::jit)
one_liner: Research JIT for C++ that specialises a function at runtime and autotunes LLVM knobs online; up to 1.48x over its own default on matmul.

name: picoev
baseline: libevent
one_liner: Tiny C event loop (~1k lines; epoll/kqueue/select) that beat 2009-era libevent ~2x on libev's bench.c.

name: PicoJSON
baseline: nlohmann/json
one_liner: Single-header C++03-compatible JSON DOM on std::map/std::vector; stringified 1.09x faster than nlohmann/json 2.0.3 in a 2016 run, parses 1.9x slower.

name: heaptrack
baseline: Valgrind Massif
one_liner: Linux heap profiler using LD_PRELOAD and libunwind; much lower time and memory overhead than Valgrind massif (no published numbers).

name: faster-enhancer.c
baseline: ONNX Runtime fp32 graph of the same FastEnhancer-Medium weights
one_liner: Dependency-free C int8 runtime for the FastEnhancer-Medium speech denoiser; paper reports 3.3x lower RTF than fp32 ONNX Runtime on M2.

name: thhp (Totemo-Hayai HTTP Parser)
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: Small zero-copy Rust HTTP/1.x parser; beats picohttpparser only on short requests (1.14-1.29x), ties or loses on realistic ones.

name: kelindar/simd
baseline: generic pure-Go implementation inside the same package
one_liner: Go package of clang auto-vectorised Sum/Min/Max and element-wise Add/Sub/Mul/Div kernels, 2-80x over scalar Go loops.

name: rbloom
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Rust (PyO3) Bloom filter for Python with a set-like API; beats other PyPI Bloom packages on insert+lookup wall time.

name: VROOM (vectorized RNS modular multiplication, BoringSSL fork)
baseline: BoringSSL BN_mod_mul_montgomery / BN modular exponentiation and RSA (same binary, multiplication backend swapped), OpenSSL at commit 7a53925 including its AVX-512 IFMA almost-Montgomery routines ossl_rsaz_amm52x{20,30,40} (separate harness kevin-he-01/vroom-openssl), FLINT 3.2.1 (GMP-based mpn_mod_mul / fmpz_mod_mul), and Arkworks (Rust, modmul only)
one_liner: Research BoringSSL fork that swaps Montgomery multiplication for AVX-512 IFMA residue-number-system arithmetic to speed up RSA modexp.

name: opencodecs
baseline: imagecodecs (Python wrappers over libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, OpenJPEG, libjxl and others) and tifffile for TIFF reading
one_liner: Python imaging-codec package over libdeflate, libspng, libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG and libjxl, with its own TIFF LZW decoder about 2x faster than imagecodecs'.

name: CAFS (cache-aware frequency sort)
baseline: vqsort (Google Highway), std::sort, pdqsort, IPS4o, ska_sort
one_liner: Header-only AVX2 hash-count sort for integer vectors with few distinct values; beats pdqsort, IPS4o and vqsort while K stays far below N.

name: Keystone
baseline: LLVM as a whole (the full LLVM build whose MC layer Keystone was stripped down from; the page mentions llvm-mc but does not measure it specifically)
one_liner: Embeddable multi-architecture assembler library cut down from LLVM 3.9's MC layer; claims over 10x smaller footprint than full LLVM.

name: KFR
baseline: FFTW
one_liner: C++20 SIMD DSP framework whose any-length FFT tracks or beats FFTW in vendor and LIGO/KAGRA benchmarks; GPL or paid license.

name: Parson
baseline: JsonCpp (also json-c)
one_liner: Two-file C89 JSON DOM with dot-path access; parsed 1.85x faster than JsonCpp 1.0.0 in a 2016 run, mostly on number-heavy canada.json.

name: KNLMeansCL
baseline: HandBrake NLMeans (CPU non-local means filter); not FFmpeg nlmeans or nlmeans_opencl
one_liner: OpenCL non-local means denoiser plugin for AviSynth(+) and VapourSynth; one user anecdote shows it about 2.5-3x faster than HandBrake's CPU NLMeans.

name: Luava
baseline: LuaJ 3.0.1 (the widely used Java Lua implementation); PUC Lua and LuaJIT are not benchmarked
one_liner: Pure-Java Lua 5.4 engine with a tiered Lua-to-JVM-bytecode JIT; 1.2x to 19x faster than the LuaJ 3.0.1 interpreter.

name: detria
baseline: CDT (artem-ogre/CDT) and poly2tri; Triangle (CMU) is also in the comparison but is faster on random point sets
one_liner: Single-header C++17 constrained Delaunay triangulator with exact predicates; about 1.5-3x faster than CDT on polygon outlines, close to Triangle.

name: newLISP Neo
baseline: CPython 3.14.4 and CPython 3.12.3 (also original newLISP 10.7.6 tree-walker, the project it derives from)
one_liner: newLISP 10.7.6 rebuilt with a computed-goto bytecode VM, tail calls and a nursery GC; beats CPython 3.14 on fib(30).

name: libpopcnt
baseline: scalar POPCNT loop (unrolled __builtin_popcountll, the std::popcount-style baseline) and the lookup-8 table algorithm; for the 4.2 claim, the library's own earlier scalar POPCNT or Harley-Seal paths
one_liner: Single-header C/C++ array popcount with runtime CPU dispatch (AVX512 VPOPCNTDQ, AVX2, NEON, SVE); beats a scalar POPCNT loop on mid-size and large buffers.

name: TurboKV
baseline: fjall (the page's like-for-like peer); redb shown only as architectural context
one_liner: Async (Tokio) Rust LSM key-value store whose unsynced-WAL mode acknowledges single-caller writes 2-4x faster than fjall 2.11.

name: refreshed-astc-encoder
license: ARM End User Licence Agreement for the Mali ASTC Specification and Software Codec, version 1.3 (license.txt): non-OSI, use limited to the 'Authorised Purpose' of ASTC compression tools, no right to develop hardware; not Apache-2.0
baseline: Mali GPU Texture Compression Tool astcenc binary (32-bit) and ARM astc-encoder official repo build (64-bit, 2015 era)
one_liner: 2016 fork of ARM's 2015 astcenc 1.x CLI that reuses scratch buffers per thread; 1.2x-2.2x faster on one image, superseded.

name: G3log
baseline: Boost.Log (asynchronous_sink with text_ostream_backend, auto_flush off) in the Quill logger_benchmarks latency tables; also std::fstream with std::flush after every line and Boost.Log in the reckless doc/performance.md Disk I/O scenario (g3log is not faster than stdio fprintf+fflush there)
one_liner: Public-domain asynchronous C++ logger with crash-safe flush; ~3x lower call-site latency than Boost.Log, 3-4x slower than spdlog.

name: Oniguruma
baseline: PCRE2 (pcre2_match interpreter; pcre2_jit_match and pcre2_dfa_match also measured); secondary baseline C++ std::regex
one_liner: Ruby-style backtracking regex library in C; beats std::regex on every shared pattern and interpreted PCRE2 on some, not PCRE2-JIT.

name: klauspost/compress fse and huff0 packages (Go tANS and Huffman)
baseline: Huffman (Go deflate Huffman coding stage)
one_liner: Pure-Go deflate/gzip/zlib/zip, zstd and S2 packages; deflate about 2x Go stdlib, S2 beats Go Snappy.

name: klauspost/crc32 (2025 AVX-512 revival)
baseline: CRC32 (Go standard library hash/crc32, IEEE polynomial - the same checksum family zlib's crc32() implements)
one_liner: Fork of Go's hash/crc32 adding an AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ path that roughly doubles IEEE CRC32 throughput on inputs of 1 KB and up.

name: klauspost/reedsolomon (Go AVX2/AVX512/GFNI/NEON/SVE assembly)
baseline: the library's own pure-Go Galois-field code path (generic Go compiler output)
one_liner: Go Reed-Solomon erasure coder with generated SSSE3/AVX2/AVX-512/GFNI, NEON/SVE and ppc64le kernels; 5-19x its own pure-Go path.

name: zttp
baseline: llhttp (via MagicStack/httptools 0.8.0, the Python binding over llhttp)
one_liner: Sans-IO HTTP/1.1 (plus HTTP/2, HTTP/3) parser for Python with a Zig core; out-parses httptools/llhttp on 13 of 14 microbenchmarks.

name: Orion Proxy
baseline: Envoy Proxy (C++)
one_liner: Rust L4/L7 proxy configured through Envoy's xDS and bootstrap protobufs; first-party wrk charts show 2.3-6x Envoy's HTTP req/s.

name: aes-armcortexm (Schwabe and Stoffelen, Cortex-M3/M4 AES assembly)
baseline: RIOT OS default C AES implementation (third-party forum report); the SAC 2016 paper compares against unnamed prior Cortex-M AES implementations; the repo README names no baseline
one_liner: Hand-scheduled Thumb-2 AES-128/192/256 (T-table CTR, bitsliced and masked) for Cortex-M3/M4; about 33 cycles/byte AES-128-CTR.

name: ZoneTree
baseline: RocksDB, SQLite
one_liner: Pure-C# LSM-tree ordered key-value engine for .NET; beats RocksDB (via RocksDbSharp) and SQLite on its own indexed profile-store benchmark.

name: count-db
baseline: LevelDB
one_liner: Java embedded store for 64-bit-keyed counters; first-party bigram test: ~82x LevelDB write, ~12x read throughput.

name: Masstree
license: MIT plus two clauses taken from the W3C license (no use of the copyright holders' names in publicity without prior written permission; title to copyright stays with the holders). It is a custom text, not a verbatim OSI/SPDX license; GitHub reports NOASSERTION.
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Concurrent in-memory trie of B+-trees with ordered range scans; authors measured 1.5-3.7x Redis 2.4 throughput on 16 cores.

name: fast_gicp (FastGICP / FastVGICP / FastVGICPCuda)
baseline: PCL pcl::GeneralizedIterativeClosestPoint (GICP); also PCL NormalDistributionsTransform (NDT)
one_liner: PCL-compatible multithreaded GICP and voxelized GICP (CPU and CUDA); about 6-9x faster than PCL GICP on 8 cores.

name: small_gicp
baseline: PCL pcl::VoxelGrid (voxel downsampling) and pcl::GICP / fast_gicp::GICP (registration)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 point-cloud registration (ICP/GICP/VGICP) and voxel downsampling; beats PCL VoxelGrid, PCL GICP and fast_gicp.

name: cry-wasm (Ruby methods compiled to WebAssembly through Crystal)
baseline: CRuby (pure Ruby interpreter) running the same function
one_liner: Experimental Ruby gem that compiles type-annotated Ruby methods to Crystal, then Wasm; about 11-14x CRuby on recursive fib(40).

name: Kokkos
baseline: OpenMP (hand-written OpenMP variant of the same particle-in-cell plasma code)
one_liner: Performance-portability programming model (Views plus parallel dispatch); a Kokkos PIC port beat its OpenMP variant 1.4-1.6x on Xeon.

name: Kokkos Kernels SpGEMM (KKSPGEMM / KKMEM)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpGEMM (CUDA 8.0.44) on P100; Intel MKL sparse-sparse multiply (MKL-INS, MKL7, MKL8 variants; intel-18.0.128) on Knights Landing
one_liner: Portable Kokkos SpGEMM (hash-accumulator KKSPGEMM) that beat CUDA 8 cuSPARSE and MKL 18 sparse multiply in 2018 tests.

name: Effort (bucketMul approximate matrix multiplication for LLM inference on Apple Silicon)
baseline: Apple MPS default matrix-vector multiplication (benchmark.swift prints 'Default Apple MPS implementation (comparable to llama.cpp)'); the project page also plots a llama.cpp tokens/s line
one_liner: Swift/Metal LLM engine whose approximate bucketMul matrix-vector product trades quality for speed against Apple MPS on Apple Silicon.

name: FastAlloc
baseline: glibc malloc, jemalloc 5.3.0, mimalloc 2.1.7
one_liner: Thread-caching slab allocator (C++17) that beats glibc malloc on small mixed-size alloc/free pairs and returns memory aggressively.

name: xor-filter (Java, komiya-atsushi)
baseline: Bloom filter (Guava com.google.common.hash.BloomFilter)
one_liner: Small Java xor filter (8/16-bit) built on Guava Funnels; about 2x faster Long-key queries than Guava BloomFilter at equal FPR.

name: komrad36/CRC ("Golden" hardware-accelerated CRC32)
baseline: The author's own C++/asm reimplementations of bitwise (naive) and slicing-by-1..16 tabular CRC-32C, plus a single-stream SSE4.2 _mm_crc32_u64 loop. zlib is never mentioned or tested.
one_liner: x86-64 CRC-32C in one function: three interleaved SSE4.2 crc32 streams recombined with PCLMULQDQ, ~2.9x a single-stream crc32 loop.

name: CUDARGB2Y
baseline: OpenCV cv::cvtColor(image, out, CV_BGR2GRAY) on a host cv::Mat (CPU), as called in main.cpp; OpenCV version and build (SIMD, threading backend) unstated, though the CV_BGR2GRAY and CV_WINDOW_NORMAL C-API constants point to OpenCV 2.x/3.x
one_liner: 20-line CUDA kernel converting packed BGR8 already on the GPU to 8-bit gray; claims 5-30x over OpenCV's CPU cvtColor.

name: FastArrayOps
baseline: unspecified 'best compiler output' scalar loops (the README headline also says 'compiler or STL', but no std::find / std::min_element / std::max_element baseline code or compiler is identified)
one_liner: Hand-written AVX2 assembly for find, contains, min/max and argmin/argmax over plain arrays; claims to beat scalar compiler loops.

name: FastDivide (komrad36)
baseline: hardware 64-bit unsigned div instruction (what a runtime a / b and a % b compile to on x86-64)
one_liner: Branch-free 64-bit unsigned divide and modulo via a Newton-Raphson reciprocal; claims about 30% faster than hardware div on Intel.

name: FastDivide128 (komrad36)
baseline: compiler-rt __udivti3, __umodti3 and __udivmodti4 (unsigned 128-bit division as lowered by Clang)
one_liner: Unsigned 128-bit Div/Mod/DivMod for x86-64 with BMI2; author says about 2x faster than compiler-rt's __udivmodti4.

name: FastThreadPool (komrad36)
baseline: None named by the author; std::async, boost::asio::thread_pool and BS::thread_pool are the natural incumbents (inferred by the search agent, never compared)
one_liner: 183-line header: an unbounded MPMC work queue of plain function pointers with spin-bit locking; no benchmark against any thread pool.

name: KFAST
baseline: Edward Rosten's reference FAST-9 C code (fast9_detect / fast9_detect_nonmax in the repo's Rosten folder) and OpenCV's cv::FAST, both timed in main.cpp
one_liner: Single-header AVX2, multithreaded FAST-9 corner detector matching Rosten's output; 5.1x faster than single-threaded OpenCV cv::FAST (2016).

name: KLERP / KNERP
baseline: OpenCV resize (bilinear and nearest-neighbor interpolation)
one_liner: Header-only AVX2 bilinear and nearest-neighbour resize for 8-bit grayscale; author claims 25-100% faster than OpenCV cv::resize.

name: Leftpack (komrad36)
baseline: naive scalar left-pack loop (branchy, 'super naive') and branchless naive scalar loop, both listed in the README
one_liner: Single-header AVX2+BMI2 left-pack (compress) of one 32-byte register; author claims 1.6-5.3x over a branchless scalar loop.

name: RGB2Y
baseline: OpenCV cv::cvtColor (CV_BGR2GRAY)
one_liner: Header-only AVX2 BGR-to-grayscale for 8-bit images; README claims roughly 3x faster than OpenCV cv::cvtColor.

name: huniq (Rust sort | uniq replacement)
baseline: GNU `sort -u` (uniq mode) and `sort | uniq -c` (count mode), awk (`!visited[$0]++` / associative count), GNU datamash (`-s groupby`), and the author's earlier C++ huniq version 1 (SoftwearDevelopment/huniq: std::getline on std::cin, tsl::sparse_set of 128-bit MetroHash128 values, tsl::sparse_map<std::string,size_t> for counts).
one_liner: Rust command-line filter that drops duplicate lines with a hash set, replacing sort -u and sort | uniq -c when order does not matter.

name: pngquant / libimagequant
baseline: ImageMagick's built-in colour quantization (an old ImageMagick 6-era version, not stated); no pngnq, Pillow quantize or other baseline numbers were found in the repo
one_liner: Lossy PNG palette quantizer (CLI plus libimagequant library); author claims its fast setting is 2.5-6x ImageMagick's quantizer.

name: kornia-rs (Image.resize and imgproc kernels, kornia-py)
baseline: OpenCV 4.13.0 cv2.resize (INTER_LINEAR, INTER_CUBIC, INTER_LANCZOS4) and cv2.cvtColor; Pillow 12.2.0 Image.resize (LANCZOS)
one_liner: Rust/Python (PyO3) vision library whose NEON u8 resize and colour kernels beat OpenCV bilinear resize on aarch64 Jetson.

name: bytehound
baseline: heaptrack and Valgrind massif/DHAT
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD heap profiler for Linux recording every allocation with full backtraces, positioned as a cheaper heaptrack/massif alternative.

name: html5-parser
baseline: html5lib (pure-Python HTML5 parser); also BeautifulSoup with html5lib and lxml (libxml2) backends
one_liner: C extension pairing a gumbo-derived HTML5 tokenizer with a direct-to-libxml2 tree build; far faster than pure-Python html5lib.

name: BTreePlus
license: MIT for the Community Edition NuGet package (binary only) and the demo/docs repo; the engine source is not published; the Pro/Enterprise Edition is proprietary (private NuGet feed plus license token)
baseline: SQLite
one_liner: Binary-only fixed-width B+Tree index for .NET; vendor claims 4.4-7x faster bulk inserts than SQLite (paid Pro build).

name: ImGui SIMD ImStrlen/ImMemchr (PR #8421, Kraionix/ImGuiMemchrBench)
baseline: C runtime strlen and memchr (labelled CSTD; ImMemchrCSTD is a plain memchr call). The bench repo is a Visual Studio 2022 project (v143 toolset, Release|x64, static CRT /MT), so CSTD is the MSVC CRT implementation, not glibc
one_liner: Unmerged Dear ImGui PR: SSE/AVX2 strlen and memchr with software prefetch, 1.4-1.55x over MSVC CRT on large buffers.

name: musl
baseline: glibc (atoi, strtok/strtok_r, bsearch, strrchr, sprintf)
one_liner: Small MIT Linux libc; in one zig-built run its atoi (2.3x) and sprintf %f (1.2x) beat glibc, strtod loses 4.3x.

name: fast-containers (SIMD/hugepage B+Tree)
baseline: std::map
one_liner: Header-only C++23 B+tree with SIMD search and hugepage allocators, 2-5x faster than std::map on large trees.

name: xoroshiro128starstar (AssemblyScript WebAssembly seeded PRNG)
baseline: Math.random (V8) and the seedrandom npm package
one_liner: 262-byte AssemblyScript WebAssembly xoroshiro128** giving a seeded Math.random replacement for Node; about 10% faster than 2018 V8 Math.random.

name: constexpr-phf (Kronuz/phf)
baseline: std::unordered_map, std::set, if-ladder, switch (binary search), gperf
one_liner: Header-only C++17 constexpr minimal perfect hash for fixed integer key sets; lookups ~2.5x faster than std::unordered_map in author benchmarks.

name: cpp-btree (Kronuz)
baseline: std::map, std::set, std::multimap, std::multiset
one_liner: Header-only B-tree replacement for std::map/set/multimap/multiset with C++17 try_emplace API and lower per-element memory.

name: libsimdxml
baseline: pugixml
one_liner: C++23 port of Rust simdxml: SIMD structural XML indexer with XPath 1.0, claiming 1.04-1.24x pugixml parse throughput.

name: bzip3
baseline: xz
one_liner: BWT plus context-mixing compressor (bzip2 successor) that compresses text 3-4x faster than xz -9 at slightly smaller size.

name: parallel-disk-usage (pdu)
baseline: GNU du (also dust, dua, ncdu, gdu)
one_liner: Rust disk-usage analyzer (pdu) that walks directories in parallel with rayon; about 2.2x faster than GNU du warm-cache.

name: emhash (ktprime/emhash: emhash5/6/7/8 + emilib)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only open-addressing C++ hash table family; emhash7 beats std::unordered_map on insert/find/erase/iterate at 10M elements.

name: QPALM
baseline: OSQP
one_liner: Sparse C solver for convex and nonconvex quadratic programs; lower runtime geometric mean than OSQP on Maros-Meszaros, but less reliable.

name: LuaBridge3
baseline: Sol3 (sol2) and vanilla LuaBridge (C++ Lua binding overhead over the plain Lua C API)
one_liner: C++17 Lua binding (LuaBridge fork) with per-call overhead near sol2's; faster on Lua-to-C++ calls, slower on C++-side table access.

name: MPL / FastParse (kurotakazuki/mpl)
baseline: nom (also benchmarked against pest, peg, winnow, chumsky, serde_json)

name: SuperMalloc

name: LibJS (Ladybird browser JavaScript engine)
baseline: Duktape 2.99.99 on Ubuntu and macOS (QuickJS 2026.06.04 is faster than LibJS in the same suite)

name: Ladybug
baseline: Neo4j Community 2025.12.1 (Cypher over Bolt, Python driver)
one_liner: Embedded columnar Cypher graph database (the continuation of Kuzu), about 2x lower geomean read-query latency than a server Neo4j.

name: voracious_radix_sort
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Rust MSD/LSD radix-sort crate for primitive types and custom structs, several times faster than Rust's own sort on large arrays.

name: dusty
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C) and Drogon (C++) in the HttpArena suite; Hical (C++) and h2o (C) rows alongside
one_liner: Zig HTTP/1.1 server and client framework on the zio coroutine runtime; ties nginx and beats Drogon in HttpArena.

name: citor
baseline: oneTBB, Taskflow, OpenMP, dispenso, libfork, TooManyCooks

name: Larq Compute Engine
language: C++ (hand-written kernels with inline assembly and intrinsics) with Python converter
baseline: dabnn (its own published Bi-RealNet time on Pixel 1, cross-report, not a same-run measurement); the MLSys 2021 LCE paper (not opened) reportedly compares binary convolutions against full-precision TensorFlow Lite convolutions
one_liner: TensorFlow Lite custom ops for binarized neural networks on 64-bit ARM; reports lower Bi-RealNet latency than dabnn on a Pixel 1.

name: SimpleSignal
baseline: Boost.Signals2 (single-thread build) and libsigc++
one_liner: 223-line CC0 header of single-threaded C++11 signals; beats Boost.Signals2 (st) and libsigc++ in a community MSVC shootout.

name: Yac (PHP shared-memory object cache)
baseline: Memcached

name: TRE

name: FAFO (parallel EVM transaction scheduler on revm)
baseline: state-of-the-art sharded execution (paper's cost baseline); no sequential revm or pevm comparison found
one_liner: Pre-block transaction scheduler on revm and QMDB claiming 1.1M Merkleized ETH transfers/s on 96 cores; no sequential baseline.

name: AutoZig
baseline: JavaScript image filter in the browser; also Rust compiled to WASM ('Rust Native' row)
one_liner: Rust-to-Zig FFI generator whose WASM demo links a Zig SIMD128 image filter into a Rust module; claims 4.75x over JavaScript.

name: lazypoline (hybrid SUD plus binary-rewriting syscall interposer)

one_liner: x86-64 Linux syscall interposer: traps each syscall site once via Syscall User Dispatch, then rewrites it zpoline-style; exhaustive, near-zpoline steady state.

name: Truncated batch SIMD AVX512 Montgomery multiplication
baseline: GMP 6.2.0 (also OpenSSL 3.2.1)
one_liner: Research C code doing 8 Montgomery multiplications or modexps at once with AVX512-IFMA; ~4-5x GMP/OpenSSL throughput.

name: Cheerp
baseline: Emscripten (C/C++ to WebAssembly)
one_liner: LLVM/Clang-based C++ to WebAssembly and JavaScript compiler; vendor claims slightly smaller output than Emscripten at roughly equal speed.

name: RadixSpline

name: RMI (Recursive Model Index, reference implementation)
baseline: B-tree (STX B-Tree)
one_liner: Rust generator emitting a C++ two-stage learned index for static sorted arrays; beats STX B+Tree latency and size.

name: uWrap

name: TinyXML2

name: RVVM
baseline: QEMU TCG

name: libyuv

name: constmap
baseline: Go builtin map[string]uint64
one_liner: Immutable Go string-to-uint64 map built on binary fuse filters; up to 5.3x faster lookups than map[string]uint64 at 1M keys.

name: cpp_batched_random
baseline: std::shuffle
one_liner: Header-only drop-in std::shuffle replacement that batches multiple Fisher-Yates draws from one 64-bit random word.

name: despacer
baseline: scalar despace loop (branching) in the same repo; also faster_despace and despace64 scalar variants

name: dictionary (AVX2/AVX-512 fused bit-unpack plus dictionary decode)
baseline: Scalar binary-unpack-then-lookup dictionary decoder (scalarcodec) in the same repo; not a named external incumbent

name: fast_double_parser
baseline: std::stod (strtod)

name: fastbase64 (lemire)
baseline: base64 (glibc/Linux base64 utility and Google Chrome's base64 implementation)

name: fastconstmap
baseline: CPython dict
one_liner: Immutable string-to-uint64 map for Python, C11 core, built on binary fuse filters; beats CPython dict lookups and memory.

name: fastmod
baseline: Clang-generated code for 32-bit x % d and x / d with a compile-time-known divisor, and the hardware 32-bit division instruction
one_liner: Header-only C/C++ 32-bit remainder, division and divisibility by a reused divisor (LKK direct remainder); about 3x faster than hardware div.

name: FastPFor (SIMD-FastPFOR, SIMD-BP128)
baseline: Simple-8b and VByte (varint); also scalar FastPFOR/SimplePFOR
one_liner: C++11 library of SIMD integer codecs (SIMD-FastPFOR, SIMD-BP128) decoding 32-bit integer arrays 2-3x faster than Simple-8b and VByte.

name: fastrand (PCG32 and xorshift128+ with nearly-divisionless bounded integers for Python)
baseline: CPython random.randint (Mersenne Twister)
one_liner: Tiny CPython C extension: PCG32/xorshift128+ bounded integers about 9x faster per call than random.randint.

name: FastShuffleExperiments (nearly divisionless bounded random integers)
baseline: std::shuffle (same underlying PRNG), plus OpenBSD-style and Java-style bounded-integer generation
one_liner: Benchmark and reference code for Lemire's nearly divisionless bounded random integers; Fisher-Yates shuffles about 8-10x faster than std::shuffle.

name: fastvalidate-utf-8
baseline: scalar C UTF-8 validator (validate_utf8 in benchmarks/benchmark.c, copied in part from Guava, with an ASCII fast path)
one_liner: Header-only C99 SSE/AVX2 UTF-8 validator (2018) that validates at 0.45-0.7 cycles/byte versus about 11 for a branchy scalar loop.

name: JavaFastPFOR
baseline: VariableByte (the varint scheme included in the same library) and Kamikaze PForDelta
one_liner: Java integer-array codecs (FastPFOR, binary packing, OptPFD, Simple9) that decode 2.7x-4x faster than VariableByte and Kamikaze PForDelta.

name: MaskedVByte
baseline: scalar VByte / varint (FP_VByte, PC_Vbyte)
one_liner: SIMD decoder for standard 32-bit VByte/varint streams; about 1.7-2.2x faster decode than scalar VByte in third-party tables.

name: simdcomp
baseline: Simple-8b, VByte (FP_Vbyte)

name: SIMDCompressionAndIntersection
baseline: FastPFor (scalar) / varint-G8IU / VByte
one_liner: C++ research library of SIMD codecs (S4-BP128, SIMD-FastPFOR) for sorted uint32 lists, plus SIMD sorted-list intersection.

name: simdpcg
baseline: PCG32 (scalar reference by O'Neill)
one_liner: Vectorized PCG32 (pcg32 XSH-RR) in AVX2 and AVX-512 C intrinsics; 1.8x to 3.7x faster than scalar PCG32 at filling arrays.

name: simdsearch (Needle-Hammer)
baseline: memmem (platform libc; the headline figure is on an Apple M-series core)
one_liner: Header-only SIMD substring search with a linear-time worst-case fallback; ~30x libc memmem on Apple M-series.

name: Stream VByte (streamvbyte)
baseline: varint-G8IU, Masked VByte and VByte (varint)
one_liner: Small C99 library for byte-oriented uint32 compression (SIMD Group Varint variant) that decodes faster than VByte, MaskedVByte and varint-G8IU.

name: testingRNG (aesctr, lehmer64 winners)
baseline: mersennetwister (reference Nishimura/Matsumoto MT19937 C code adapted in source/mersennetwister.h, not std::mt19937), C library rand(), pcg32, pcg64, xoroshiro128+

name: validateutf8-experiments (lookup UTF-8 validation, Keiser and Lemire)

one_liner: Research harness for the Keiser-Lemire 'lookup' SIMD UTF-8 validator, about 4-6x faster than the best scalar validator it tests.

name: LJSON

name: Leptos
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust/Wasm fine-grained-reactive web UI framework; about 1.46x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark, slower than vanilla JS.

name: libleptris
baseline: libxml2

name: yeptris
baseline: libyaml

name: BoofCV
baseline: OpenCV (opencv-python 4.5.1.48 pip wheel, CPU)

name: cppcoro
baseline: concurrencpp (also HPX and libcoro thread-pool runtimes)
one_liner: C++ coroutine library whose work-stealing static_thread_pool runs fork-join tasks 20-86x faster than concurrencpp or HPX.

name: lexbor
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Standards-compliant C99 HTML5/CSS/DOM/URL engine; beats libxml2-based bindings on HTML parsing and CSS selector throughput.

name: MyHTML

one_liner: Pure C99 HTML5 parser using a thread-pool tokenizer/tree-builder; beats Gumbo and html5ever on parse throughput.

name: LFI (Lightweight Fault Isolation)

name: PNG XL (PXL)
license: libpng-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause (files under ffmpeg/ are FFmpeg patch material under LGPL-2.1-or-later)
baseline: libpng (decode into raw RGBA pixels)
one_liner: Lossless PNG-replacement format (.pxl) and C library: PNG row filters plus zstd, decoding about 2x faster than libpng.

name: minimp3
baseline: keyj's minimp3 (Martin J. Fiedler's fixed-point single-file MP3 decoder, https://keyj.emphy.de/minimp3/)
one_liner: CC0 single-header float MP1/MP2/MP3 decoder with SSE2/NEON paths; ISO-conformant and 2.0-6.4x fewer cycles per file than keyj's minimp3.

name: Liftbridge
baseline: NATS JetStream
one_liner: Go server adding Kafka-style partitioned, replicated logs on top of NATS; self-reports ~1.1x NATS JetStream publish throughput on one node.

name: Lightpanda
baseline: Headless Google Chrome 143 (Chromium, C++) driven over CDP
one_liner: Zig headless browser (V8 JS, no rendering) for CDP automation; vendor crawl 9.7x faster, 16x less memory than headless Chrome.

name: cudaFoam (cudaPCG: GPU PCG pressure-solver plugin for OpenFOAM)
baseline: OpenFOAM 12 CPU GAMG and CPU PCG-DIC (single rank)
one_liner: OpenFOAM 12 plugin running the pressure-equation PCG on an NVIDIA GPU; edges CPU GAMG, 5.6x over CPU PCG-DIC.

name: Recoil (parallel rANS decoding)
baseline: single-thread interleaved rANS, conventional fixed-partition parallel rANS, and the multians GPU ANS decoder (not zstd/lz4/zlib/brotli/xz)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 rANS library that splits one interleaved stream for parallel decode on AVX2/AVX-512 CPUs and CUDA GPUs.

name: Armeria gRPC server (Java): grpc_bench unary echo vs C++ gRPC (cpp_grpc_mt)
baseline: gRPC C++ async server (cpp_grpc_mt in LesnyRumcajs/grpc_bench): the stock async greeter pattern with one completion queue per server thread, GRPC_SERVER_CPUS threads and a single pre-posted CallData per queue; main.cpp and the generated code are built with g++ 15.2.0 --std=c++20 -O3 -flto and linked with jemalloc against Debian-packaged libgrpc++, libgrpc and libprotobuf (versions and build flags not recorded). It was the fastest of the run's three C++ rows (cpp_grpc_mt, cpp_asio_grpc, cpp_grpc_st) at 1, 3 and 4 CPUs and within 0.4% of cpp_asio_grpc at 2 CPUs.
one_liner: JVM microservice framework (Netty-based) whose gRPC server out-served the stock gRPC C++ async server at 2-4 CPUs in one grpc_bench run.

name: Parley
baseline: cosmic-text 0.19.0 (pop-os/cosmic-text), the established Rust rich-text shaping and layout library (bevy_text, iced, COSMIC); both shape with HarfRust, but different versions: cosmic-text 0.19.0 pulls harfrust 0.5.2 while parley 0.11.1 pulls harfrust 0.12.0 (flui spike Cargo.lock). Not a C/C++ incumbent such as HarfBuzz with FreeType or Pango.
one_liner: Pure-Rust rich-text layout (fallback, bidi, shaping, line breaking); 2.4-9x faster than cosmic-text on paragraph-per-layout workloads.

name: resvg
baseline: librsvg (2.45.5 in the resvg 0.8.0 README charts; 2.50 in the MediaWiki snippet) and QtSvg 5.12.3; Inkscape 1.0 and Batik only in the snippet-only MediaWiki table
one_liner: Pure-Rust static-SVG renderer with a C API; benchmarks faster than librsvg on icon sets, much slower on clip-path-heavy files.

name: tiny-skia
baseline: Cairo (and raqote); slower than Skia
one_liner: Pure-Rust port of Skia's CPU raster pipeline; about 1.7-2.3x faster than cairo on x86 overall, slower on solid rect fills.

name: Vello CPU (sparse strips renderer)
baseline: Skia (CPU pipeline) and Cairo; also Rust tiny-skia, raqote, AGG, JUCE
one_liner: Rust CPU 2D vector renderer (sparse strips, SIMD, optional threads); about 2.4x Skia and 4x Cairo raster speed on M1.

name: wasm-fun (hand-written WebAssembly text algorithms)
baseline: LingDong-/skeleton-tracing's C++ version compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten (wasm/compile.sh: emcc -O3 --closure 1, WebIDL glue, SINGLE_FILE=1, ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1) and its vanilla JavaScript implementation
one_liner: Hand-written WebAssembly text (WAT) image and utility algorithms; claims skeleton tracing beats an Emscripten build and vanilla JS.

name: Liger-Kernel
baseline: Hugging Face Transformers default PyTorch eager modeling code (RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU, cross-entropy, fused linear cross-entropy)
one_liner: Triton kernels that monkey-patch Hugging Face LLMs for training; mainly cut memory, with roughly 15-40% end-to-end throughput gains over eager PyTorch.

name: linkerd2-proxy (Rust) vs Envoy as service-mesh sidecars
baseline: Envoy (C++), as the Istio sidecar proxy
one_liner: Rust sidecar micro-proxy of the Linkerd mesh; vendor benchmarks show 6-9x less per-proxy memory than Istio's Envoy.

name: zsv (zsv+lib)
baseline: DuckDB CSV reader and Python Polars read_csv (also benchmarked against BurntSushi/xsv, qsv, and xan)
one_liner: SIMD C CSV parser/CLI beating DuckDB and Polars on read throughput, with a slow correct fallback for nonstandard quoting.

name: ls-hpack (LiteSpeed HPACK)
baseline: nghttp2 (HPACK); the numeric benchmark covers only nghttp2's HPACK Huffman encoder (nghttp2_hd_huffman.c at revision 0e1d0400d86a)
one_liner: LiteSpeed's C HPACK (RFC 7541) codec with 64K-entry two-byte Huffman tables; beat a 2016 nghttp2 Huffman encoder 2.4-5.8x.

name: ls-qpack
baseline: nghttp3 (QPACK encoder compression ratio); nghttp2/nginx Huffman coder (shared HPACK/QPACK Huffman alphabet)
one_liner: LiteSpeed's C QPACK (RFC 9204) codec. On one 2019 trace, its history-gated indexing out-compressed nghttp3 1.3-2.2x.

name: LSQUIC (LiteSpeed QUIC)
baseline: quiche
one_liner: LiteSpeed's C QUIC + HTTP/3 client/server library; LSQUIC-to-LSQUIC bulk downloads beat quiche-to-quiche 1.2-1.5x at 10 Gbit/s.

name: ccv (BBF face detector)
baseline: OpenCV default frontal face detector (Haar cascade, default settings; OpenCV version not stated)
one_liner: Brightness Binary Feature frontal face detector in the C library ccv; about 3x faster than OpenCV's 2.x-era Haar detector, now self-deprecated.

name: HXT parallel 3D Delaunay (in Gmsh)
baseline: CGAL 3D Delaunay triangulation (CGAL 4.12)
one_liner: Gmsh's HXT module: OpenMP-parallel 3D Delaunay tetrahedralization in C, about 3x faster serially than CGAL, TetGen and Geogram.

name: clangd-tidy
baseline: clang-tidy
one_liner: CLI wrapper around clangd that reports clang-tidy diagnostics much faster than standalone clang-tidy.

name: UMap
baseline: mmap (Linux system mmap service)
one_liner: LLNL user-space mmap replacement built on userfaultfd; beats Linux mmap for large-page, out-of-core reads with tuned paging.

name: YAJL
baseline: json-c 0.12.1 (also JsonCpp 1.0.0 and Jansson v2.7 in the same suite)
one_liner: Tiny ISC-licensed C streaming (SAX) JSON parser and generator; its DOM layer parsed 1.3x faster than json-c in nativejson-benchmark.

name: AddressSanitizer (LLVM compiler-rt)
baseline: Valgrind Memcheck
one_liner: Compiler-instrumented memory-error detector in Clang/GCC; about 2x slowdown where Valgrind Memcheck costs about 20x.

name: LMDB
baseline: RocksDB (rust-rocksdb 0.22.0 with LZ4, 4 GiB LRU block cache, bloom filters, OptimisticTransactionDB snapshot reads); SQLite (rusqlite 0.37 bundled, default settings, BLOB PRIMARY KEY table) is also in the table, but its adapter re-prepared every SQL statement per operation (see caveats)
one_liner: Memory-mapped copy-on-write B+tree key-value store in C; 4.6-8.8x faster reads than RocksDB in redb's harness.

name: upack (μpack)
baseline: Rust bitpacking crate (port of simdcomp); also compared in README prose to StreamVByte
one_liner: Rust SIMD bitpacking of 128-integer u32/u16 blocks; beats the bitpacking crate's BitPacker4x on x86, loses on ARM.

name: rscrypto
baseline: Fastest external Rust implementation per case. SHA-256/384/512: RustCrypto sha2, aws-lc-rs (AWS-LC) and ring. SHA3-224/256/384/512: RustCrypto sha3. BLAKE2: RustCrypto blake2, plus dryoc for BLAKE2b.
one_liner: Zero-dependency Rust crypto crate whose SIMD/asm SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE2 and AEADs beat RustCrypto, ring and aws-lc-rs in its benchmarks.

name: picohttpparser-rs
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: Safe-Rust, ABI-identical rewrite of picohttpparser; beats scalar -O2 C only on header-heavy requests, loses on six of eight workloads.

name: quickjs-jit (Longbridge JIT-enabled QuickJS-NG distribution)
language: Rust (with the vendored QuickJS-NG C engine)
baseline: QuickJS-NG interpreter (same runtime with the JIT detached); Bun 1.4.0 (JavaScriptCore) also measured as the external target
one_liner: Tiered Cranelift JIT bolted onto a patched QuickJS-NG via rquickjs; 20-50x the interpreter on scalar kernels, still slower than Bun everywhere.

name: fRPC (frpc-go)
baseline: gRPC
one_liner: Go proto3 RPC generator that swaps gRPC's HTTP/2 and Protobuf for 8-byte-header TCP framing and Polyglot encoding.

name: SmallFunction (LoopPerfect/smallfunction)
baseline: std::function
one_liner: Header-only, fixed-capacity alternative to std::function that placement-news the callable into an inline stack buffer instead of the heap.

name: OpSparse (optimized GPU SpGEMM framework)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpGEMM, nsparse and spECK
one_liner: Research CUDA hash-based SpGEMM (C = A*B, CSR, FP64) for V100; paper reports 7.35x average over cuSPARSE.

name: BuRR (Ribbon Filter)
baseline: Bloom filter, xor filter
one_liner: Static bumped-ribbon retrieval/filter library: 0.06-1.4% space overhead against Xor's 23% and Bloom's 44%+, with slower sequential queries.

name: wrs (lorenzhs/wrs, parallel weighted random sampling and alias tables, ESA 2019)
baseline: GNU Scientific Library (GSL) alias table implementation
one_liner: Research C++17 library of sequential and parallel alias tables and weighted samplers; reported 3-4x faster queries than GSL's gsl_ran_discrete.

name: Loro
language: Rust compiled to WebAssembly with JavaScript bindings
baseline: Yjs 13.6.11 (pure-JS CRDT library); the same table also lists ywasm 0.9.3 and Automerge 2.1.10 (both wasm)
one_liner: Rust CRDT library compiled to WebAssembly; replays a real 260k-op editing trace about 1.85x faster than Yjs 13.6.

name: PlayRho
baseline: Box2D 2.4.1
one_liner: C++17 2-D rigid-body physics engine derived from Box2D 2.3.2; first-party microbenchmarks show 1.2-4.9x faster steps than Box2D 2.4.1, with losses.

name: rustybuzz-wasm
license: unclear: Cargo.toml declares 'MIT/Apache-2.0' (left from the wasm-pack template, authors 'Your Name <you@example.com>'), but the LICENSE file only says 'the liecense goes here'
language: Rust (compiled to WebAssembly, driven from NodeJS)
baseline: harfbuzzjs (HarfBuzz compiled to WebAssembly, driven from NodeJS); also the HarfBuzz command-line tools spawned per line, opentype.js and fontkit
one_liner: Abandoned wasm-bindgen wrapper around rustybuzz 0.4 for Node.js; claims about 1.5x harfbuzzjs 0.1.5 on Latin text shaping.

name: LovyanGFX
baseline: Adafruit_GFX (Adafruit-GFX-Library) with the Adafruit_ILI9341 driver; TFT_eSPI is roughly equal in the same table
one_liner: Embedded display driver and drawing library for ESP32-class MCUs; 1.3x to 4.6x faster than Adafruit_GFX on an ILI9341 at 40 MHz SPI.

name: lowzag
baseline: libjpeg-turbo (progressive coefficient array memory); also ROM TJpgDec for decode time on ESP32
one_liner: Progressive-JPEG decoder in C99 that decodes at 1/2-1/8 scale in a fraction of libjpeg-turbo's coefficient memory.

name: rans-tricks
license: Public domain (dedication in README: 'All of this is public domain, do whatever you want with it'; no LICENSE file)
baseline: standard 4-way interleaved rANS (rans_byte style); FSE
one_liner: Branchless 16-bit-renormalizing variant of ryg's rans_byte.h; README reports about 1.5-1.7x over standard 4-way interleaved rANS.

name: Lwan
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: C HTTP/1.1 server and embeddable library; topped TechEmpower Round 10 JSON at ~5.8x Go net/http's throughput.

name: RadixMap (radix-map)
baseline: std::map
one_liner: Header-only PATRICIA/radix-tree map beating std::map on insert/contains for string and numeric keys.

name: http.c3l
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: Sans-IO streaming HTTP/1.1 request parser in C3; ties picohttpparser with callbacks, ~13% faster only when extracting nothing.

name: Spire
baseline: HAProxy 2.7.3 (C) and Envoy 1.22.8 (C++) reverse proxies; nginx 1.23.3 in the same table is faster than Spire
one_liner: Rust (Tokio/Hyper) reverse proxy and gateway; HAProxy and Envoy wins come from an unequal harness; nginx beats it.

name: LuaJIT Remake (Deegen)
baseline: PUC-Rio Lua 5.1 interpreter (also compared against the LuaJIT 2.1 interpreter)
one_liner: Research Lua 5.1 VM whose interpreter is generated by Deegen; about 1.3x LuaJIT's interpreter and 2.8x PUC Lua 5.1.

name: LuaJIT
baseline: Lua 5.4.7 (PUC-Rio reference interpreter, per the README environment table)
one_liner: Tracing JIT compiler and assembler-written interpreter for Lua 5.1; runs Lua code several times faster than PUC-Rio Lua 5.4.

name: Luau
baseline: PUC Lua 5.x interpreter (Lua 5.1 to 5.4)
one_liner: Roblox's sandboxed, gradually typed Lua 5.1 derivative whose interpreter runs about 1.2-1.5x PUC Lua 5.5 in independent tests.

name: calaminejs (calamine spreadsheet reader in WebAssembly)
language: Rust (calamine compiled to WebAssembly with wasm-pack) with TypeScript
baseline: SheetJS xlsx 0.18.5 (pure JavaScript spreadsheet parser in V8)
one_liner: Unofficial WebAssembly binding of the Rust calamine reader for xlsx/xls/xlsb/ods; about 4-5x faster than SheetJS 0.18.5 on large sheets.

name: Lucebox Megakernel (single-launch CUDA forward pass for Qwen 3.5-0.8B)
baseline: llama.cpp (BF16, CUDA backend) and PyTorch + HuggingFace Transformers (BF16)
one_liner: Model-specific CUDA decode megakernel for Qwen 3.5-0.8B at batch 1; 1.55x llama.cpp BF16 decode on an RTX 3090.

name: lumen (Rust JavaScript engine with ARM64 template JIT)
baseline: QuickJS (bellard, version 2026.06.04 in the CI table); V8 and JavaScriptCore are NOT beaten
one_liner: Std-only Rust JavaScript engine with an ARM64 template JIT; about 2.2x QuickJS on V8-v7 on Apple Silicon, slower on x86-64.

name: lucid-url
baseline: ada-url (C++ Ada)
one_liner: Dependency-free, safe-Rust WHATWG URL parser with Ada's API; faster than ada::url, slower than ada::url_aggregator and can_parse.

name: indexset
baseline: std::collections::BTreeMap / BTreeSet (Rust)
one_liner: Rust two-level B-tree (sorted Vec leaves) with positional indexing; beats std BTreeMap/BTreeSet on scans and Mutex-wrapped std under contention.

name: mpack
baseline: msgpack-c (msgpack C 1.3.0 and msgpack C++ 1.3.0)
one_liner: Embeddable C MessagePack codec; beat msgpack-c 1.1-3x in its author's 2016 suite; independent 2026 run: encode only.

name: LLFree
baseline: Linux kernel buddy page-frame allocator
one_liner: Lock- and log-free page-frame allocator in C; up to 88% (4 KiB) and 98% (2 MiB) lower concurrent allocation time than Linux's buddy allocator.

name: simdjson_nodejs
language: JavaScript (Node.js native addon binding to C++ simdjson)
baseline: V8 JSON.parse (Node.js built-in)
one_liner: Node.js N-API binding to C++ simdjson 0.9; lazyParse beats JSON.parse up to 2.3x by never building JS objects.

name: lukechampine/blake3 (Go BLAKE3 with avo-generated AVX-512 and AVX2 assembly)
baseline: The same package's pure-Go implementation (Go compiler output)
one_liner: Go BLAKE3 package with avo-generated AVX-512/AVX2 assembly; about 4-8x its own pure-Go path on 64 KiB inputs.

name: fastxor (lukechampine)
baseline: naive byte-wise Go for loop and a word-wise (uint64) Go loop, compiled by the Go gc compiler
one_liner: Go package that xors byte slices with AVX2/SSE2 assembly; about 5x a word-wise Go loop, 40x a byte loop.

name: frand (lukechampine/frand, Go userspace CSPRNG)
baseline: Go crypto/rand (and math/rand in parallel benchmarks)
one_liner: Go userspace CSPRNG: a sync.Pool of crypto/rand-seeded ChaCha8 generators, far faster than crypto/rand for bulk and parallel reads.

name: hpla-rs (Rust faer-based CSR SpMV and Lanczos exp(-A)b) against Eigen, PETSc, oneMKL and PSBLAS
license: MIT declared in the Cargo.toml license field only; the repo has no LICENSE file
baseline: Eigen CSR and CSC sparse matrix-vector product (C++); also PETSc CSR (C), Intel oneMKL inspector-executor CSR and CSC (C) and PSBLAS (C++/Fortran), single core
one_liner: Benchmark repo: Rust faer CSR SpMV and Lanczos exp(-A)b beat Eigen on one core but lose to oneMKL and PETSc.

name: Pika Parser (reference implementation)
baseline: ANTLR4 (also benchmarked against Parboiled2)
one_liner: Reference implementation of pika parsing: a bottom-up, right-to-left PEG algorithm that beats ANTLR4 on simple grammars but loses on Java.

name: WrenJIT
baseline: LuaJIT 2.1 with JIT on (docs/index.html report names LuaJIT 2.1.1785763465; build flags not stated); the report also shows a LuaJIT -joff column
one_liner: Tracing JIT for the Wren scripting language on SLJIT; beats LuaJIT on a few microkernels but loses on 9 of 10 Benchmarks Game ports.

name: LUME Kiwi (@lume/kiwi, TypeScript Cassowary constraint solver)
baseline: Cassowary.js (slightlyoff/cassowary.js), the JavaScript Cassowary implementation
one_liner: TypeScript Cassowary linear-constraint solver for UI layout; 10x faster setup, 2.3x faster re-solve than Cassowary.js.

name: Go goroutines vs Intel TBB on a task-graph dynamic program (Comparison-Go-CppTBB)
baseline: Intel oneTBB (2017 Update 3) C++ task scheduler, MSVC v14 build, on the same static optimal binary search tree task graph
one_liner: 2017 study: Go goroutines vs Intel TBB tasks on tiled optimal-BST dynamic programming; Go won only at N=4096, by 1.003-1.15x.

name: LodePNG
baseline: libpng 1.6.37 (with zlib 1.2.11, as shipped with Debian Bullseye)
one_liner: Two-file, dependency-free PNG encoder/decoder; decodes small PNGs about 1.1x faster than libpng+zlib 1.2.11, larger ones slower.

name: chacha20poly1305-simd
baseline: OpenSSL EVP_chacha20_poly1305 (ChaCha20-Poly1305)
one_liner: Pure-Rust (X)ChaCha20-Poly1305 with hand-written AVX-512/AVX2/SSE2/NEON kernels; beats RustCrypto everywhere, OpenSSL mainly on small messages.

name: zdu
baseline: dust and pdu (disk usage tools built on parallel stat/readdir)
one_liner: Parallel Rust disk-usage CLI with a dust-style tree chart; 2.7-10x faster than dust, mixed against pdu.

name: PrimJS
baseline: QuickJS (commit 6e2e68)
one_liner: ByteDance's QuickJS fork for Lynx with an arm64 template interpreter and tracing GC; claims 1.29x QuickJS on Octane.

name: hunt (hunt-rs)
baseline: GNU find (C)
one_liner: Multithreaded Rust file-name finder (CLI); the author's warm-cache README runs show it 5.5-12x faster than GNU find.

name: pXart
baseline: std::mt19937 (libstdc++, GCC 9.2.0); also Boost.Random mt19937
one_liner: Header-only C++17 SSE/AVX2 MT19937, Xoroshiro128+ and MSWS; AVX2 MT19937 matches std::mt19937 output and generates it about 8x faster.

name: LZ4
baseline: zlib
one_liner: In-memory block/frame compressor beating zlib deflate on speed, trading compression ratio for GB/s decode.

name: LZFSE (Apple reference implementation)
baseline: zlib (zlib 1.3.2)
one_liner: Apple's LZ77 + finite-state-entropy codec in plain C99; zlib -6 ratio at about 3.4x the compress and 2.3x the decompress speed.

name: file_io_benchmark (Windows unbuffered multi-threaded loading)
baseline: fread / memory-mapped file reads
one_liner: Windows benchmark showing multi-threaded FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING reads reach 11.3 GB/s on NVMe versus fread and memory mapping.

name: FastString
baseline: std::string
one_liner: Fixed-capacity, stack-allocated, constexpr string class that avoids the heap allocation std::string needs past SSO.

name: mem++ (memplusplus)
baseline: jemalloc, mimalloc, rpmalloc, ptmalloc2/3 (glibc malloc), gcpp
one_liner: Experimental single-threaded C++ arena allocator with GC smart pointers and heap compaction; beats jemalloc in its own charts, not glibc malloc.

name: libzahl
baseline: GMP (also TomsFastMath and LibTomMath)
one_liner: Small ISC-licensed C bignum library that beats GMP on cheap integer operations (assign, sign, compare, add/sub) but loses on multiply.

name: Mach
baseline: unspecified C# HTTP server (probably ASP.NET Core; the repo file is only labelled 'csharp', server code not included)
one_liner: C++20 web framework with ASP.NET Core-style minimal APIs on Boost.Beast; mixed against an unnamed C# server, slower than Drogon.

name: libchaos (KISS, Xoroshiro128Plus, Xorshf96 and other PRNGs)
baseline: std::mt19937 and std::mt19937_64 (also std::minstd_rand, ranlux24/48, knuth_b)
one_liner: Abandoned C++11 grab-bag of small PRNGs (xorshift128+, xorshift1024*, KISS, xorshf96) about 2.6x faster per call than std::mt19937.

name: Kobold
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust/Wasm UI framework with compile-time DOM templates; in js-framework-benchmark, non-keyed, near vanilla-JS speed and 0.53x keyed React's time.

name: logos
baseline: hand-written lexer
one_liner: Rust proc-macro lexer generator: compiles token/regex rules into one DFA with jump tables, aiming to beat hand-written lexers.

name: goja-perf
baseline: Upstream dop251/goja at merge base 8f1c069 (pure-Go JavaScript interpreter); V8 comparison suite exists but publishes no numbers
one_liner: API-compatible fork of the pure-Go goja JavaScript engine with quickening, loop traces and cheaper Go/JS calls; beats upstream goja.

name: LibC-String-Optimisations (XEOS x86 and x86-64 string functions)
license: XEOS Software License 1.0 (custom BSD-style licence with an advertising clause and a clause forbidding combination or linking with GPL/LGPL software; not OSI-approved)
baseline: OS X 10.9 libc strlen, memset, memchr, memcpy, strcat (the README notes it is also heavily optimised); not glibc or musl
one_liner: Hand-written SSE2/SWAR x86 and x86-64 assembly strlen, memchr, memcpy, memset, strcat for Mach-O; mostly 1-15% over OS X 10.9 libc.

name: lzvolt
language: Rust (hand-written assembly decoders; C header and cdylib/staticlib callable from C++)
baseline: LZ4 (liblz4 decode and pack)
one_liner: LZ77 codec for small cache/record values whose hand-written per-CPU decoders read 14-83% faster than liblz4.

name: pigz
baseline: gzip
one_liner: Multithreaded gzip/zlib/zip compressor by zlib's co-author; beats single-threaded GNU gzip on multicore machines.

name: madmann91/bvh
baseline: nanort and Fast-BVH (Embree 3.13 also compared and is faster)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 binary BVH builder and ray traverser; its chart shows it faster than nanort and Fast-BVH, but slower than Embree.

name: uvloop
baseline: CPython asyncio default event loop (pure-Python SelectorEventLoop, epoll-backed on Linux)
one_liner: Cython/libuv replacement for CPython's default asyncio event loop; 2-4x echo throughput in its own 2016 benchmark.

name: hmp3 (Helix MP3 encoder revival)
license: RPSL-1.0 (Helix encoder sources in hmp3/); MIT (other files)
baseline: LAME (MP3 encoder); no baseline comparison in the repository
one_liner: Maintained build of RealNetworks' Helix MP3 encoder, reputed (not measured here) to encode several times faster than LAME.

name: easyjson
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Go codegen tool producing reflection-free struct JSON marshalers; README (2016) shows ~2.8x marshal, ~5.7x unmarshal vs encoding/json.

name: Stitch (makepad)
baseline: WAMR fast interpreter and Wasmtime Pulley (execution); Wasmtime Cranelift (startup)
one_liner: Rust Wasm interpreter using tail-call threaded code; about 1.1x faster than WAMR fast-interp in wasmi-benchmarks (bug-fixed fork measured).

name: M4RI (dense GF(2) linear algebra: Method of the Four Russians, Strassen-Winograd, PLE elimination)
baseline: Magma 2.14 (2.14-14 on the Core 2 Duo, 2.14-13 on the Opteron, per search snippets), the proprietary computer algebra system's asymptotically fast GF(2) matrix multiplication; GAP 4.4 also appears in the tables. None of the listed baselines (OpenBLAS, Intel MKL, Eigen, BLIS) apply because they do not operate on bit-packed GF(2) matrices.
one_liner: C library for dense matrix arithmetic over GF(2); 2008 paper shows 1.4-1.5x faster multiplication than Magma on Core 2.

name: BLight
baseline: Pufferfish
one_liner: Minimizer-partitioned, MPHF-based exact k-mer dictionary; indexes human k=31 at 22.3 bits/k-mer versus Pufferfish's 55.6.

name: sparsam
baseline: GTSAM 4.2.1 (PyPI wheel driven through its Python bindings) on 2D pose graphs; Ceres 2.2 on BAL bundle adjustment
one_liner: From-scratch C++20 SLAM/pose-graph backend whose own block-sparse Cholesky beats GTSAM 4.2 on M3500, not Ceres on BA.

name: sroar
baseline: CRoaring (C): not compared; the README compares against RoaringBitmap/roaring (Go, roaring64 v0.6.1)
one_liner: Go Roaring bitmaps stored as one byte slice, no marshalling; beats Go roaring64 v0.6.1 FastOr, not 32-bit Go roaring.

name: zroar (Zig serialized Roaring bitmaps)
baseline: CRoaring 5.0.0 (roaring64 API, portable and frozen serialization)
one_liner: Zig 64-bit Roaring bitmap whose in-memory buffer is its serialized form; 2.2x faster than CRoaring roaring64 on warm operations.

name: Manticore Search
baseline: Elasticsearch
one_liner: SQL/HTTP full-text and analytics search database, C++ core, positioned as a faster Elasticsearch alternative.

name: Bigloo Scheme
license: GPL-2.0-or-later (compiler and tools) AND LGPL-2.0-or-later (run-time system and libraries, 'GNU Library General Public License' per the repo LICENSE file)
baseline: Guile 3.0.11 (guild compile -O3); Chez Scheme 10.3.0 also in the same suite (Bigloo is slower than Chez on aggregate)
one_liner: Optimizing Scheme-to-C (and JVM) compiler; about 1.6x faster than Guile 3.0.11 on the ecraven R7RS suite, slower than Chez.

name: earcut.hpp
baseline: earcut.js, the original JavaScript implementation (~445 ms for the same set in its README); test/bench.cpp also times libtess2 v1.0.2 on 9 small fixtures but publishes no results; CGAL and libtess2 are called 'slower and larger' in the README without numbers.
one_liner: Header-only C++ ear-slicing polygon triangulator (port of Mapbox earcut.js); about 1.6x faster than the JS original on tile polygons.

name: NNPACK (Winograd/FFT convolution)
baseline: XNNPACK (convolution_bench, 2020 version)
one_liner: C99 CPU convolution primitives using Winograd and FFT tiles for stride-1 layers; fp32, AVX2/FMA3 or NEON.

name: marcelcases/simd (std::experimental::simd kernels)
baseline: scalar C++ version of each kernel built with compiler auto-vectorization disabled (-fno-tree-vectorize)
one_liner: Seven teaching kernels written with libstdc++ std::experimental::simd, timed against de-vectorized scalar loops on x86-64, AArch64 and RVV.

name: Gigatoken
baseline: HuggingFace tokenizers (and OpenAI tiktoken)
one_liner: SIMD/cache-optimized BPE tokenizer with a Python API, roughly 7x-1300x faster encoding than HF tokenizers.

name: PIVCO-Huffman (pivco-huffman)
baseline: huf0 (zstd's Huffman decoder from FiniteStateEntropy, X1 single-symbol and X2 double-symbol variants) and an in-tree traditional 4-stream table Huffman decoder; Oodle Huffman (oo-huff) is wired into bench/bench_fair.c only when an Oodle SDK is linked and does not appear in the BENCHMARKS.md tables
one_liner: Block-SIMD Huffman decoder (pivoted coding) that decodes 2-6x faster than zstd's huf0 on most byte distributions.

name: coros-fibers
baseline: none named (ABI-compliant coroutine switch; libco-style)
one_liner: Small x86-64 Linux stackful coroutine switch (libcoro-style assembly) plus a priority fiber scheduler; no baseline compared.

name: mrcache
baseline: Redis (also memcached)
one_liner: Single-threaded io_uring key-value cache server in C; README claims 7x Redis and 46x memcached GET throughput at 16 B.

name: mrloop
baseline: unnamed epoll-based echo server (README row 'epoll'; neither libuv nor libev is named)
one_liner: Tiny single-threaded C event loop on io_uring; README echo test shows 1.51x an unnamed epoll server.

name: SparseDNN
baseline: LIBXSMM, Intel MKL/OpenBLAS dense, OpenVINO
one_liner: Python code generator emitting per-weight-matrix x86 assembly SpMM kernels for pruned networks; beats LIBXSMM sparse and dense BLAS above ~70% sparsity.

name: d3_geo_voronoi_rs (rust_d3_geo_voronoi)
baseline: d3-geo-voronoi (the original JavaScript library, github.com/Fil/d3-geo-voronoi), run on an equivalent benchmark web page
one_liner: Rust port of d3-geo-voronoi (spherical Delaunay/Voronoi); its wasm canvas demo draws frames about 1.95x faster than the JS original.

name: simd-rand (SIMD Xoshiro256+ / Xoshiro256++ and frand generators for Rust)
baseline: Scalar Xoshiro256+ (benchmark label 'rand/Xoshiro256+', from the rand crate ecosystem)
one_liner: Rust crate of 4- and 8-lane SIMD Xoshiro256+/++, frand and biski64 generators; about 4.5x scalar rand_xoshiro Xoshiro256+ on AVX-512.

name: nanobench::Rng (RomuDuoJr)
one_liner: nanobench's built-in RomuDuoJr generator: a drop-in <random>-style 64-bit PRNG, ~1.3-3.9x faster than std::mt19937_64.

name: robin_hood::unordered_map
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only, single-file open-addressing hash map/set beating std::unordered_map on speed and memory.

name: ankerl::svector (martinus/svector)
baseline: std::vector
one_liner: Single-header C++17 small vector packing 7 inline bytes into an 8-byte object; avoids std::vector's heap allocation for tiny sequences.

name: ankerl::unordered_dense
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Vector-backed hash map beating std::unordered_map on build, iteration, and string-key workloads, with weaker reference stability.

name: PFFFT (marton78 fork)
license: FFTPACK/NCAR (UCAR) BSD-style license (no SPDX id; terms equivalent to BSD-3-Clause)
baseline: KissFFT
one_liner: Small BSD-licensed SIMD 1D FFT (float/double) plus fast convolution, about 5x faster than KissFFT, about half FFTW's speed.

name: optimization-detective (SWAR memcasecmp, common suffix and whitespace patches for Abseil)
baseline: Abseil absl::strings_internal::memcasecmp, FindLongestCommonSuffix and RemoveExtraAsciiWhitespace (verbatim upstream code from abseil-cpp@7e706921, byte-at-a-time loops)
one_liner: Three patch-sized rewrites of Abseil string helpers (SWAR memcasecmp, word-at-a-time common suffix, clean-input fast path), 1.3-6.9x over Abseil's byte loops.

name: toml++
baseline: toml11 v4.2.0 (also cpptoml, tomlc99 in the same matrix)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 TOML 1.0 parser and serializer; parses 18x to 430x faster than toml11 v4.2.0 in a third-party matrix.

name: Gaius.jl (Julia multi-threaded divide-and-conquer BLAS-like matmul)
baseline: OpenBLAS gemm (C and assembly) with 6 threads (BLAS.set_num_threads(6)); for integer matrices Julia's generic matmul, since OpenBLAS has no integer matmul
one_liner: Pure-Julia recursive multithreaded matmul that beat 6-thread OpenBLAS on small and medium matrices in a 2020 run.

name: matbech/zlib (optimized zlib 1.2.11 fork, MSVC)
baseline: zlib (original 1.2.11)
one_liner: Archived Windows/MSVC zlib fork with SIMD hashing, CRC and match patches; about 1.3-1.9x zlib 1.2.11 level-6 compression.

name: simd-lexing
baseline: flex (lexer generator)
one_liner: Single-header AVX2 C99 lexer with no tables, ~3-6x faster than flex on tokenizing GCC source.

name: ATLAS
baseline: Netlib reference BLAS (Debian blas 1.2.20110419, lapack 3.5.0)
one_liner: Self-tuning C BLAS with part of LAPACK that times its own kernels on the build machine; about 6-8x faster than Netlib reference BLAS.

name: Apogee (Lua 5.5 VM in pure Go with amd64/arm64 JIT)
baseline: C Lua 5.5 (PUC-Rio; Lua 5.4.9 on the Apple M1 run) and Shopify/go-lua
one_liner: Pure-Go Lua 5.5 VM with an amd64/arm64 method JIT; 0.57x C Lua 5.5's time on 17 standard benchmarks, about 3x behind LuaJIT.

name: Lithium (HTTP server / web framework)
baseline: actix-web (best TechEmpower actix implementation in Round 20, actix-core; also actix-pg). H2O is a secondary comparison from the author's own statement.
one_liner: Header-only C++ HTTP server and async SQL toolkit on fibers; beat actix-web on TechEmpower DB tests only in Round 20.

name: Prolua
baseline: Lua 5.4.8 (reference C interpreter)
one_liner: Lua 5.4 reimplemented in Zig: roughly at parity with PUC Lua 5.4.8, faster on sort and numeric loops, slower on strings.

name: Fucina (Zig tensor runtime and LLM inference engine)
baseline: llama.cpp CPU backend (ggml kernels, llama-bench with -ngl 0), same GGUF file and thread count
one_liner: Pure-Zig CPU tensor/autograd runtime and GGUF LLM engine; outruns llama.cpp's CPU backend on most dense Qwen3 prefill shapes.

name: nam-zig
baseline: NeuralAmpModelerCore (C++) at -O3: no timing comparison found in the README or repo
one_liner: Zig port of Neural Amp Modeler (play, train, export .nam) on Fucina; no timing against NeuralAmpModelerCore C++.

name: Sirius64
baseline: xoshiro256++, xoshiro256**, PCG64 (RXS-M-XS and DXSM), xoroshiro128++, RomuTrio
one_liner: Six-line 64-bit-state PRNG, a SplitMix64-style Weyl counter with a stronger output mix; ~1.25x faster than xoshiro256++.

name: quad-wavelet-tree (C++ QWT)
baseline: SDSL wavelet trees/matrices
one_liner: Header-only C++20 4-ary (quad) wavelet matrix with about 2x lower access/rank/select latency than SDSL wavelet trees.

name: epeg
license: MIT-enna (Enlightenment MIT variant: COPYING requires publicly documented acknowledgment when the source is not published; COPYING-PLAIN is a non-binding plain-English note). Not OSI-approved.
baseline: ImageMagick convert -resize 150x150> (plain resize mode); ImageMagick's own -thumbnail mode with the jpeg:size hint is faster than epeg in the same table
one_liner: Small C library and CLI for JPEG-to-JPEG thumbnails via libjpeg scaled decode; beats plain 'convert -resize', loses to ImageMagick -thumbnail and libvips.

name: LitMath
baseline: naive scalar loop over System.Math.Exp and System.Math.Log (NaiveExpDouble, NaiveLogDouble); an older README table also compared Intel MKL via MKL.NET Vml.Exp
one_liner: C#/.NET AVX2 and AVX-512 array math (Exp, Ln, Sin, Erf, normal CDF, Sqrt), 5-7x over a scalar System.Math loop.

name: TBLIS (Tensor-Based Library Instantiation Software)
baseline: BLAS-based tensor contraction (TTGT: transpose plus GEMM). In the independent tblis-rs benchmark this is NumPy einsum backed by Intel MKL, alongside PyTorch (CPU).
one_liner: Native tensor-contraction library on BLIS kernels; beats transpose-plus-GEMM (NumPy/MKL einsum) on strided and permuted contractions.

name: tinymt-wasm-typescript-benchmark (minimal AssemblyScript TinyMT32)
baseline: TypeScript TinyMT32 running in V8 (Node 24.18.0) and C++ TinyMT32 compiled with Emscripten and embind
one_liner: Benchmark repo: hand-scalarised AssemblyScript TinyMT32 beats a TypeScript port 1.25-1.42x on ints and Emscripten C++ slightly.

name: reckless
baseline: std::fstream, fprintf (stdio)
one_liner: Asynchronous C++ logging library, drastically lower caller-side latency than std::fstream/fprintf and other async loggers.

name: IntrinsicML (hand-vectorized SIMD microkernels for ML)
baseline: plain triple-loop scalar C++ reference (GCC -O3 -ffast-math); also OpenBLAS sgemm single thread (where it is slower)
one_liner: Teaching-grade AVX2/AVX-512 SGEMM and activation kernels; beats a strided scalar triple loop, reaches 4-60% of single-thread OpenBLAS.

name: plf::bitset (plf_bitsets)
license: Computing For Good License v1.01 (non-OSI; zlib-style terms plus ethical field-of-use restrictions 4a-4e)
baseline: std::bitset
one_liner: Header-only bitset beating std::bitset at ranged set/reset, shifts, and bit search, minus from-string constructors.

name: plf::colony (plf::hive)
baseline: std::vector, std::deque, std::list
one_liner: Unordered container beating std::vector/deque/list on erase-heavy workloads via O(1) erase that never invalidates other iterators.

name: Indiesort (plf::indiesort)
baseline: std::sort (also std::list::sort)
one_liner: Indirect sort wrapper: sorts indices or pointers, then permutes once; beats std::sort on structs over ~152 bytes.

name: plf::list
baseline: std::list
one_liner: Node-clustering drop-in replacement for std::list; faster insertion, erasure, sort, and much faster clear/destruction.

name: plf::stack
baseline: std::stack (default std::deque backing container)
one_liner: Header-only LIFO container on chained, never-relocated memory blocks; author reports it beats std::stack over std::deque.

name: ztls
baseline: OpenSSL libssl 3.6.3; rustls 0.23.4x
one_liner: Sans-I/O TLS 1.3 state machine in Zig; lower per-record latency than OpenSSL libssl (1.04-3.6x) and rustls on AES-GCM.

name: djvu-rs (Rust DjVu codec) vs DjVuLibre
baseline: DjVuLibre 3.5.29 (C++): ddjvu rendering and the c44 / cjb2 encoders
one_liner: Pure-Rust, MIT DjVu reader, renderer and encoder; first-party runs show faster rendering and c44/cjb2-style encoding than DjVuLibre 3.5.29.

name: Spinel
baseline: CRuby 4.0.4 (MRI interpreter) and CRuby 4.0.4 with --yjit
one_liner: Ahead-of-time Ruby-subset-to-C compiler by Matz; README geomean 8.5x faster than CRuby 4.0.4 with YJIT.

name: atomic_queue
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Header-only lock-free MPMC/SPSC ring-buffer queues beating std::mutex-guarded queues by 4-10x in latency and throughput.

name: as-string-sink
baseline: JavaScript string concatenation (String += in V8, which uses ropes) and naive String += in AssemblyScript
one_liner: Growable UTF-16 string builder for AssemblyScript; replaces quadratic String += and beats V8 rope concat about 4x.

name: wasm-i128-div-bench (reciprocal 128-bit division for the Wasm wide-arithmetic proposal)
baseline: Rust u128/i128 division operators lowering to compiler-builtins __udivti3/__umodti3 (compiler-rt libcall) on wasm32
one_liner: Rust research benchmark: Moeller-Granlund reciprocal 128-bit division vs __udivti3, native and Wasm wide-arithmetic; wins mainly with hoisted divisors.

name: BtrBlocks
baseline: Apache Parquet (generated/read via the Apache Arrow C++ library) and Apache ORC
one_liner: C++ columnar compression library: sampled cascades of lightweight encodings; authors measured 2.6-3.8x faster decompression than Parquet.

name: StrangeQ
baseline: RabbitMQ
one_liner: Single-node Go AMQP 0.9.1 broker speaking RabbitMQ's wire protocol; author measures 1.1-4.5x RabbitMQ 4.3's durable, confirmed throughput.

name: pybase64
baseline: base64 (Python standard library base64 module)
one_liner: Python base64 module replacement backed by the SIMD libbase64 codec; roughly 6.6x faster encode than the stdlib.

name: otter
baseline: hashicorp/golang-lru
one_liner: Caffeine-style concurrent Go cache (adaptive W-TinyLFU): 10-34x hashicorp/golang-lru throughput at 25-100% reads; slower on pure writes.

name: emugemm-cdna
baseline: rocBLAS native FP32 sgemm on AMD MI250 (per-shape tuned solutions)
one_liner: FP32 GEMM emulated with bf16 matrix-core products on AMD MI250; 1.20-1.22x over per-shape-tuned rocBLAS sgemm at a lower accuracy tier.

name: asm-dom
baseline: snabbdom 0.7.0 (JavaScript virtual DOM library, in-browser; version pinned in benchmarks/package.json)
one_liner: C++ port of the snabbdom virtual DOM compiled to WebAssembly; wins pure-diff rows against snabbdom, loses where DOM writes cross into JavaScript.

name: Silverfir-nano
baseline: WAMR fast interpreter (execution) and Wasmtime Cranelift (startup)
one_liner: Rust no_std Wasm 3.0 runtime with interpreter and on-device JIT; interpreter about 1.9x WAMR fast-interp on wasmi-benchmarks.
