name: Mbed TLS
baseline: OpenSSL 3.6.0 EVP one-shot AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305
one_liner: Small-footprint C TLS library and PSA Crypto reference implementation; edges OpenSSL EVP only on 64-byte one-shot AEAD calls.

name: rasusa (Rust read and alignment subsampler)
baseline: seqtk sample (C) for random read subsampling; filtlong (C++) for target-bases selection
one_liner: Rust CLI that randomly subsamples reads to a target coverage, base count or read count; it matches seqtk sample -2 on speed and is far faster than filtlong, which does a different job.

name: simd-adler32
baseline: adler/adler2 crates (scalar Rust Adler-32; adler2 is the maintained successor used by miniz_oxide) and adler32 crate, plus wuffs std/adler32 built with gcc
one_liner: Pure-Rust Adler-32 with runtime-dispatched SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2 (AVX-512 on nightly) and NEON kernels; 17-23x the adler32 crate on x86.

name: vb64 (Rust std::simd Base64 codec)
baseline: base64 (marshallpierce/rust-base64 crate)
one_liner: Nightly-only std::simd Base64 codec that decodes 2-2.5x faster than the base64 crate on AVX2. It no longer builds.

name: ioxide
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C) and h2o (C) in the HttpArena suite; also libreactorng and libioma (C, io_uring), mongoose (C) and agensio (C++)
one_liner: Shared-nothing io_uring runtime for .NET; a hand-written HTTP/1.1 handler on it outruns nginx 1.25x on HttpArena baseline-4096.

name: simd-csv (Rust crate)
baseline: csv crate (docs.rs/csv, i.e. BurntSushi/rust-csv, the de facto standard Rust CSV library)
one_liner: SIMD-accelerated Rust CSV reader/writer family beating the csv crate on throughput, gains data-dependent.

name: xan
baseline: BurntSushi/xsv and Python Polars/DuckDB CSV readers (independent comparison; xan itself targets csvkit-style CSV toolkits)
one_liner: CLI CSV toolkit with a SIMD parser and built-in expression language; faster single-threaded select than xsv, Polars, DuckDB.

name: meet1214/thread-pool
baseline: std::async
one_liner: Header-only C++17 fixed-size thread pool with typed futures and exception propagation, beats std::async by reusing worker threads.

name: csvql
baseline: DuckDB
one_liner: Zig CLI and MCP server that runs read-only SQL on raw CSV files, about 3x faster than DuckDB's raw-CSV path.

name: fmtlog
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Asynchronous fmt-syntax C++ logger with about 6 ns caller-side latency per call, versus 150-400 ns for synchronous spdlog.

name: Str (MengRao/str)
baseline: std::string, std::to_string/stoi
one_liner: Fixed-capacity char-array type with SIMD-accelerated equality, compare, and fixed-width integer/string conversion, beating std::string and stoi/to_string in author benchmarks.

name: TCPSHM
baseline: ZeroMQ
one_liner: Header-only C++11 framework for crash-recoverable point-to-point messaging over TCP or shared memory; claims ~4.8x lower RTT than ZeroMQ.

name: SSW (Complete-Striped-Smith-Waterman-Library)
baseline: ordinary (non-SIMD) Smith-Waterman local alignment
one_liner: SSE2 striped Smith-Waterman C library (Farrar method) returning score, positions and CIGAR; claims ~50x over scalar SW.

name: awkrs (Rust AWK)
baseline: mawk 1.3.4 and GNU gawk 5.4.0 (C); BSD awk on macOS also timed
one_liner: AWK implementation in Rust with a fused bytecode VM; its single-rule fast paths run 2-5x faster than mawk on 1M-line files.

name: stryke (strykelang): Perl 5 compatible interpreter with bytecode VM and Cranelift JIT
baseline: LuaJIT 2.1.1774896198 (also perl 5.42.2, Python 3.14.4, Ruby 4.0.2, Julia 1.12.6, Raku)
one_liner: Rust Perl 5 interpreter with bytecode VM and Cranelift JIT; beats perl 5 on tiny scripts, LuaJIT only on three gamed rows.

name: dSFMT (MersenneTwister-Lab)
baseline: MT19937 (NumPy's reference-derived mt19937 implementation, as exposed by randomgen)
one_liner: Double-precision SIMD Mersenne Twister in C that emits IEEE 754 doubles directly; about 1.6x MT19937 for bulk uniform doubles.

name: SFMT (SIMD-oriented Fast Mersenne Twister)
baseline: MT19937-64 reference implementation (mt19937-64.c from the MT homepage; same algorithm as std::mt19937_64)
one_liner: Saito and Matsumoto's 128-bit SIMD variant of the Mersenne Twister; about 2.3-2.8x faster than MT19937-64 for bulk 64-bit output.

name: MeshLib
license: Proprietary non-commercial/educational license (AMV Consulting, LLC); commercial license sold separately
baseline: CGAL (also Manifold, libigl, MCut and 5 others)
one_liner: Source-available C++ mesh-processing SDK whose triangle-mesh booleans run tens of times faster than CGAL's exact booleans.

name: jieba-rs (Rust Chinese word segmentation)
baseline: cppjieba (C++ port of jieba Chinese word segmentation)
one_liner: Rust port of the jieba Chinese word segmenter; claimed faster than cppjieba, about 2.2x faster than nodejieba through Node bindings.

name: MeTA
license: MIT OR NCSA (repo carries LICENSE.mit and LICENSE.ncsa, both copyright 2016 Sean Massung and Chase Geigle; neither file states how they combine; both OSI-approved)
baseline: Lucene (indexing); Indri; LIBLINEAR (classification)
one_liner: C++ text retrieval and analysis toolkit; its ACL 2016 demo paper reports faster indexing than Lucene and Indri and faster linear classification than LIBLINEAR.

name: xxYUV
baseline: libyuv (version not stated) and Apple Accelerate
one_liner: Small MIT C++ BT.709 RGB/YUV 4:2:0 converter (SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2/NEON) whose README claims to beat libyuv and Accelerate.

name: mpFFT (multiprecision FFT on MPFR)
baseline: Mathematica 11.1 FFT with SetPrecision, and MATLAB 2019a with the Advanpix Multiprecision Toolbox (mp.Digits)
one_liner: Research-grade MPFR-based split-radix FFT in C that runs faster than Mathematica and MATLAB/Advanpix multiprecision FFTs.

name: sb_lower_bound (Fastest Branchless Binary Search)
baseline: std::lower_bound
one_liner: Branchless drop-in-shaped replacement for std::lower_bound that relies on clang emitting cmov instead of a branch.

name: opuspp
baseline: libopus 1.6.1 decoder (opus_decode_float), built with identical compiler and flags
one_liner: Header-only C++23 port of the libopus 1.6.1 decoder for one CELT stream type, bit-exact and 1.27-1.48x faster.

name: Malachite
baseline: GNU GMP (mpz, via the Rust rug 1.30.0 crate)
one_liner: Pure-Rust port of GMP/FLINT integer algorithms; beats GMP (via rug) on sub-64-bit values and string parsing, not on large operands.

name: zld
baseline: Apple ld (ld64)
one_liner: Drop-in fork of Apple's ld64 that speeds up incremental Xcode debug linking; archived, maintainer now recommends lld instead.

name: rv8
baseline: QEMU (RISC-V user-mode emulation)
one_liner: RISC-V to x86-64 user-mode JIT binary translator; its 2017 paper shows about 1.8x faster than QEMU riscv64 user mode.

name: Speedy.js
baseline: Plain JavaScript in V8 (Chrome 58) and SpiderMonkey (Firefox 53); Emscripten-compiled C++ shown alongside
one_liner: Experimental 2017 compiler from a typed TypeScript subset to WebAssembly via LLVM; up to about 4x over 2017-era browser JS.

name: FastBoxBlur
baseline: OpenCV cv::blur (box filter)
one_liner: Header-only C++ sliding-sum box blur with reflect-101 borders; claims 2-3x over OpenCV cv::blur on huge kernels.

name: LibGaussianBlur (FFT Gaussian blur, from Blur_algorithms)
baseline: OpenCV cv::GaussianBlur
one_liner: C++20 FFT (pffft) separable Gaussian blur for 8-bit RGB/RGBA; 9-20x faster than cv::GaussianBlur at very large sigma.

name: MicroPython
baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (per javascript/duktape/duktape.h in the scriptorium repo), built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG; the same table lists PUC Lua at 1.341 s, where this engine is slower
one_liner: Lean Python 3 implementation for microcontrollers and embedding; about 3.4x faster than Duktape 1.2.2 on 2015 fib(34), slower than PUC Lua.

name: ALEX (Adaptive Learned indEX)
baseline: STX B+Tree (std::map-like ordered index); also beats Adaptive Radix Tree (ART), a 2-stage RMI ("Learned Index"), and a Model-enhanced B+Tree
one_liner: Header-only C++ learned ordered index for numeric keys; beats STX B+Tree up to 4x on in-memory lookups and inserts.

name: BitBLAS
language: Python (TVM/TileLang code generation) with CUDA kernels
baseline: cuBLAS (W_FP16 A_FP16 GEMV/GEMM); also CUTLASS, bitsandbytes, FasterTransformer, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM and Marlin
one_liner: Auto-tuned mixed-precision GPU GEMV/GEMM (FP16/INT8 activations x INT4/INT2/INT1/NF4/FP4/FP8 weights) that beats FP16 cuBLAS by moving fewer bytes.

name: BitNet (bitnet.cpp)
baseline: llama.cpp FP16 inference
one_liner: llama.cpp-based CPU inference engine with ternary-weight kernels; 1.4-6.2x faster than llama.cpp FP16 on BitNet b1.58 models.

name: Microsoft Bond (Compact Binary v1)
baseline: FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto
one_liner: Discontinued Microsoft schema-based serializer whose Compact Binary wire format is smaller than FlatBuffers and unpacked Cap'n Proto.

name: CNTK
baseline: TensorFlow (tensorflow-gpu 1.2.1 as a Keras 2.0.6 backend)
one_liner: Microsoft's archived C++ deep-learning toolkit; as a 2017 Keras backend it trained LSTMs about 2.6-3.3x faster than TensorFlow 1.2.

name: Demikernel
baseline: Linux kernel sockets networking path
one_liner: Rust kernel-bypass library OS with a zero-copy, queue-based socket API over DPDK; 4-5x lower echo RTT than Linux sockets.

name: F2 (FASTER v2)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Microsoft's two-tier hash-and-log KV store for skewed, larger-than-memory point workloads; its paper reports ~11.8x RocksDB throughput at 10% memory.

name: FourQlib (SchnorrQ / FourQ curve arithmetic)
baseline: NIST P-256 (Gueron-Krasnov fast implementation, the code later merged into OpenSSL as nistz256)
one_liner: Microsoft Research C library for FourQ ECDH and SchnorrQ signatures; up to 5.6x faster scalar multiplication than fast P-256 code.

name: Garnet
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Multi-threaded Redis-protocol (RESP) cache-store in C# from Microsoft Research; up to ~100x Valkey/Redis throughput on many-core servers.

name: Machnet
baseline: Linux kernel TCP/IP stack (sockperf with Nagle disabled for microbenchmarks; kernel-TCP builds of a FASTER KV server and of Hashicorp Raft's transport)
one_liner: DPDK kernel-bypass messaging sidecar for cloud VMs; 2.6x lower median and 7.4x lower p99.9 RTT than Linux TCP.

name: mimalloc
baseline: jemalloc
one_liner: General-purpose malloc drop-in replacement using sharded per-thread free lists; beats jemalloc/tcmalloc on multi-threaded workloads.

name: ONNX Runtime (transformers GPU inference, BERT and GPT-2)
baseline: PyTorch 1.5.1 eager fp32 (GPT-2 rows) and TorchScript fp32 at batch 1 (BERT rows); PyTorch fp16 never measured
one_liner: Microsoft's ONNX inference runtime; its fused transformer graphs ran BERT/GPT-2 1.2-5.7x faster than TorchScript 1.5.1 on V100.

name: Regorus
baseline: OPA (Open Policy Agent, Go) opa eval
one_liner: Rust Rego interpreter (OPA's policy language), embeddable from C/C++; about 10x faster than an opa eval CLI run on one ACI policy.

name: snmalloc
baseline: glibc malloc
one_liner: Header-only C++ allocator using lock-free message-passing frees, beating glibc malloc on cross-thread and batch-deallocation workloads.

name: Vectorized std::search and std::find in the MSVC STL (SSE4.2/AVX2 runtime dispatch)
baseline: MSVC STL's own scalar std::search before vectorization (the same PR also times C strstr as an unchanged control)
one_liner: MSVC STL's built-in SIMD std::search and string::find (SSE4.2, AVX2, NEON), 2-12x faster than its former scalar loop.

name: T-MAC
baseline: llama.cpp low-bit dequantization kernels (Q2_K, Q4_0)
one_liner: Lookup-table CPU kernels for 1-4-bit LLM weights; 2-6x faster token generation than llama.cpp Q2_K/Q4_0 at low thread counts.

name: sntrup (Streamlined NTRU Prime, pure Rust)
baseline: liboqs 0.13.0 via oqs-sys 0.11.0 (sntrup761: AVX2 SUPERCOP-derived backend on x86_64, portable C on aarch64) and PQClean sntrup761 clean C via pqcrypto-ntruprime 0.1.6 (avx2 feature off)
one_liner: Pure-Rust Streamlined NTRU Prime KEM: ties liboqs AVX2 on Zen 5 and beats liboqs portable C on Apple M2 1.2-2.7x.

name: RSLAB (pure-Rust sparse LDL^T, LU and KLU solver)
baseline: Intel MKL PARDISO
one_liner: Pure-Rust sparse LDL^T/LU/KLU direct solver; solve phase 2.3-3.3x faster than MKL PARDISO, factorization usually slower.

name: milo Grisu2 (header-only, via miloyip/dtoa-benchmark)
baseline: std::ostringstream (iostreams); page's headline ratio is vs sprintf()
one_liner: Header-only Grisu2 double-to-string routine; fastest entry in its author's own benchmark, beating std::ostringstream and sprintf().

name: SSE2 itoa (Muła algorithm, via miloyip/itoa-benchmark)
baseline: sprintf (C stdio); std::ostringstream/std::to_string also tested but disabled by default with no numbers published on this page
one_liner: SSE2-vectorized itoa for uint32/int32/uint64/int64 in Milo Yip's benchmark repo; 25.51x faster than sprintf on 9-10 digit values.

name: normaldist-benchmark (Ziggurat and AVX/SSE2 Box-Muller)
license: MIT (src/ziggurat.cpp is Jochen Voss's GPL-2.0-or-later code)
baseline: std::normal_distribution with std::minstd_rand (the 'cpp11random' row)
one_liner: 2015 benchmark of normal-sample generators; Ziggurat and AVX Box-Muller run 2.8-8x faster than std::normal_distribution with minstd_rand.

name: Rasterizer (mindbrix)
license: Custom 'personal use zlib license' (LICENSE.txt): zlib terms, but permission is granted only for personal use, and commercial use needs a licence from the author. Not OSI-approved.
baseline: unnamed CPU path rasterization ('the CPU'); the README names no CPU renderer. HN thread snippets (seen through search only) say the author used CoreGraphics as the quality reference and called performance against Vello 'very competitive', with no numbers.
one_liner: Metal GPU 2D vector renderer (paths, strokes, gradients, clips, SVG/PDF) for macOS and iOS; claims 'up to 60x faster than the CPU', unmeasured.

name: blake2b-simd (Minio)
baseline: The package's own pure-Go BLAKE2b fallback (compress_generic.go, derived from dchest/blake2b), labelled 'go.txt' in the benchcmp output. Also compared against Go stdlib crypto/md5, crypto/sha1, crypto/sha256 and crypto/sha512.
one_liner: Archived Go BLAKE2b with AVX2/AVX/SSSE3 assembly, about 4x its pure-Go fallback and faster than 2016-era Go SHA-256/SHA-512.

name: c2goasm
baseline: cgo (calling the same C function through Go's C foreign-function interface)
one_liner: Converts clang-generated amd64 assembly into Go assembly so Go calls C SIMD kernels without cgo's per-call cost.

name: minio/md5-simd (AVX2/AVX-512 multi-lane MD5 in Go assembly)
license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE); files derived from Go's crypto/md5 are under BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE.Golang, Copyright 2009 The Go Authors)
baseline: Go standard library crypto/md5
one_liner: Go package computing 8 (AVX2) or 16 (AVX-512) independent MD5 streams per core; 3-8x crypto/md5 aggregate throughput.

name: MinLZ
baseline: LZ4 (also compared with Snappy, S2 and gzip)
one_liner: Go LZ77 compressor (new byte-aligned format, Snappy/S2 successor) that compresses faster and smaller than LZ4's fastest mode.

name: sha256-simd (minio)
baseline: Go crypto/sha256 (stdlib)
one_liner: Go SHA-256 using SHA-NI, ARMv8 SHA2 and 16-lane AVX-512; once beat crypto/sha256, now only its multi-buffer mode might.

name: simdjson-go
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Go port of simdjson's SIMD parser for AVX2 amd64; builds a navigable tape 2.3-16.5x faster than encoding/json's interface{} decode.

name: Minotaur
baseline: clang/LLVM -O3 without the Minotaur pass (per search snippets of the paper)
one_liner: LLVM IR superoptimizer pass that synthesizes cheaper SIMD/scalar code; 1-7% faster than clang -O3 on GMP, libYUV, SPEC.

name: fiat-crypto (generated Curve25519 field arithmetic in BoringSSL)
language: Coq (generates C, Rust, Go, Java, Zig, Bedrock2, x86-64 asm)
baseline: BoringSSL's previous curve25519 code: hand-written x86_64 x25519 assembly (884086e) and the earlier C field arithmetic on master (b2c312d)
one_liner: Coq-proved generator of finite-field arithmetic in C, Rust, Go and Zig; matches hand-written Curve25519 field code in BoringSSL, not faster.

name: libxev (HttpArena baseline server)
baseline: libreactorng (C, io_uring) and h2o (C) in the HttpArena suite; also nginx 1.31.4 (C) and Drogon (C++)
one_liner: Zig proactor event loop (io_uring, epoll, kqueue, WASI) with a C API; its HttpArena server ties libreactorng and beats h2o, nginx, Drogon.

name: TreeLine
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Update-in-place key-value store for NVMe SSDs with record caching and page grouping; beats RocksDB on read-heavy, skewed, scan YCSB.

name: libmdbx
baseline: LMDB
one_liner: LMDB fork: embedded memory-mapped ACID B+tree KV store; author reports 10-30% faster in-tmpfs CRUD than LMDB.

name: fast-base64 (mitschabaude)
baseline: The package's own pure-JS port (fast-base64/js), which the README says is 'the fastest existing JS implementation', plus native atob()/btoa() through its own fast-base64/nano wrapper
one_liner: Hand-written WebAssembly SIMD base64 codec for JS (browser/Node/Deno); beats pure-JS base64 loops, not native Buffer.

name: watsign
baseline: tweetnacl-js (Ed25519 sign/verify)
one_liner: WebAssembly port of TweetNaCl Ed25519 sign/verify for browsers, Node and Deno; ~4-6x faster than tweetnacl-js warmed up.

name: MD4C
baseline: cmark
one_liner: SAX-style CommonMark parser in C, no AST, beats cmark on speed and memory when you don't need a DOM.

name: rpmalloc
baseline: crt (system glibc malloc on Ubuntu 16.10, backing operator new/delete); charts also include tcmalloc, ptmalloc3, jemalloc, lockfree-malloc, scalloc, lockless
one_liner: Lock-free, per-thread-caching malloc replacement for C/C++, drop-in via LD_PRELOAD or override, faster than glibc/tcmalloc/jemalloc under threaded churn.

name: vldb26-iouring (io_uring for DBMSs artifact)
baseline: io_uring default configuration, epoll, pread/libaio style I/O in a DBMS
one_liner: VLDB'26 artifact measuring which io_uring settings speed up DBMS buffer managers and network shuffles compared with default io_uring and epoll.

name: superfasthash (SuperFastHash in JavaScript and AssemblyScript WebAssembly)
baseline: JavaScript implementation of SuperFastHash in the same module (and Node.js native crypto MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, RIPEMD-160)
one_liner: Paul Hsieh's SuperFastHash as a tiny npm module in JS and AssemblyScript Wasm; Wasm about 1.2x the JS port on Node.

name: libalgebra
baseline: naive scalar code with auto-vectorization disabled (__attribute__((optimize("no-tree-vectorize")))): popcount_scalar_naive_nosimd and intersect/union/diff_scalar_naive_nosimd, which count bits with an 8-bit lookup table (STORM_popcnt_lookup8bit), not the POPCNT instruction
one_liner: Header-only x86 C library: SIMD popcount, positional popcount and AND/OR/XOR bitmap cardinalities, with CPUID dispatch.

name: positional-popcount
baseline: pospopcnt_u16_scalar_naive (portable scalar C, auto-vectorized by GCC) and pospopcnt_u16_scalar_naive_nosimd
one_liner: C99 SIMD kernels counting set bits per bit position over 16-bit arrays; up to 16x faster than GCC-vectorized scalar code.

name: Swift-BigInt (BInt)
baseline: mini-gmp (GMP's portable minimal subset without assembly kernels); the README says full GMP was not counted because it needs to be installed and is not portable
one_liner: Pure-Swift arbitrary-precision integers (BInt) and fractions (BDouble), claimed about 2x faster than mini-gmp, not full GMP.

name: regexr (Rust regex engine with x86-64/ARM64 JIT)
baseline: regex crate (Rust); PCRE2 with JIT as the second comparison
one_liner: Pure-Rust regex engine with lookarounds, backreferences and an x86-64/AArch64 JIT; claims up to 4x over the regex crate.

name: mlpack
baseline: scikit-learn (sklearn); the same tables also compare Shogun Toolkit, MATLAB, Weka and mlpy
one_liner: Header-only C++17 machine learning library (Armadillo-based) whose tree-based k-NN and k-means beat 2012-era scikit-learn, Shogun, MATLAB and Weka.

name: Little-CMS fast_float plugin
license: GPL-3.0-or-later for the fast_float plugin (plugins/fast_float source headers say 'version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version'; COPYING.GPL3 in that directory; the plugin PDF says a paid alternative licence is available from the author). The lcms2 core in the same repo is MIT.
baseline: Little CMS 2 (lcms2) stock transforms
one_liner: GPL-3.0 add-on for Little CMS 2 that swaps stock transforms for precomputed-table, SSE2 and 15-bit kernels; about 7x on one Lab-to-RGB float case.

name: GPU scanline path rendering (Li, Hou, Zhou 2016)
baseline: state-of-the-art GPU path renderers (exact baselines not confirmed from an opened source)
one_liner: Research code for the SIGGRAPH Asia 2016 CUDA and OpenGL scanline path renderer; the abstract claims about 2.5x over prior GPU path renderers.

name: XS JavaScript engine (Moddable SDK)
license: XS engine sources (xs/sources) are LGPL-3.0-or-later and incorporate Apache-2.0 code from Kinoma/Marvell; SDK build tools GPL-3.0, examples CC-BY-4.0, some fonts OFL-1.1 (licenses/readme.md); a commercial licence is also offered
baseline: Duktape 2.3.0
one_liner: XS, Moddable's ROM-friendly C JavaScript engine for microcontrollers; beat Duktape 2.3.0 by about 1.6x on bench-v8 in 2019, not in 2026 CI.

name: Modin
baseline: pandas
one_liner: Parallel, partitioned pandas API on Ray, Dask or MPI; wins over pandas on heavy single ops, loses on small ones.

name: Hob3l
baseline: OpenSCAD with CGAL rendering (CGAL Nef polyhedron 3D CSG) converting SCAD/CSG to STL
one_liner: C command-line tool that turns SCAD/CSG models into layered STL for 3D printing, 50-350x faster than OpenSCAD's CGAL render.

name: cat-dog-asm-cnn
baseline: Equivalent NumPy-based CNN (and PyTorch, which it does not beat)
one_liner: Educational cat/dog CNN, training and inference, hand-written in NASM AVX-512; claims ~10x over an unpublished NumPy CNN, slower than PyTorch.

name: liburlparser (abspath fast-path vs ada)
baseline: ada-url/ada (ada::url_aggregator)
one_liner: C++17 RFC 3986-style URL splitter with Public Suffix List domain extraction; its own parse+accessor loop runs ~1.25x ahead of ada.

name: sasso
baseline: dart-sass 1.104.1 (the 138-stylesheet table does not name the dart-sass form; bench/three_way.md compares the dart2js JS CLI that npx sass runs, the native-VM CLI, sass-embedded and the sass JS library in-process, at dart-sass 1.100.0/1.101.0)
one_liner: Pure-Rust SCSS/Sass compiler matching dart-sass 1.104.1 output; ships native CLI, crate, C ABI and npm (wasm plus N-API) builds.

name: sparkdown (@momiji-rs/sparkdown, WebAssembly build)
language: Rust (wasm32 with simd128 and bulk-memory) with JavaScript wrapper
baseline: remark-parse (mdast-util-from-markdown, JavaScript) and the native pulldown-cmark crate
one_liner: Zero-dependency Rust CommonMark parser shipped as SIMD WebAssembly; replaces remark-parse and beats JS markdown renderers in Node.

name: libbson
baseline: cJSON (also jansson, json-c and parson as JSON serializers; cross-format comparison)
one_liner: MongoDB's C library for building and iterating BSON; in one third-party C shootout it round-trips faster than cJSON on 4 of 5 payloads.

name: The Platinum Searcher (pt, Go code search)
baseline: The Silver Searcher (ag, written in C: ggreer/the_silver_searcher has src/main.c) and ack (Perl); versions of all three tools not stated.
one_liner: pt: an ack/ag-style recursive code searcher in Go. A single 2015 first-party run put it 8% ahead of C ag on one literal search.

name: fontdue
baseline: FreeType 2 (glyph rasterization, via freetype-rs); also rusttype 0.9.2 and ab_glyph 0.2.3 for rasterization, glyph_brush_layout 0.2.0 for layout
one_liner: Pure-Rust, no_std TrueType/OpenType glyph rasterizer and simple layout; first-party plots show 2.3x-11x lower per-glyph latency than FreeType.

name: fancy-memset (fm): SSE2 and AVX2 memset in x86-64 assembly
license: BSD-2-Clause (headers in each memset .S file, Copyright 2021 Elijah Stone, commit ee040ef; no root LICENSE file; vendored competitor files keep their own Intel BSD and CDDL terms)
language: x86-64 assembly (GNU as) with a C benchmark harness
baseline: glibc memset (the harness's 'sys' row calls the system libc memset; glibc version not stated); the harness also times FreeBSD, Bionic and Solaris memset, a naive rep stos and a naive -O3 loop
one_liner: Three tiny x86-64 assembly memsets (GPR, SSE2, AVX2) after Microsoft's 2021 CRT design; claims 10-370% over glibc memset.

name: MoonBit
baseline: Plain JavaScript in Node v22.0.0 (V8): an idiomatic Array flatMap/filter/map/reduce chain and the same chain on JS Iterator Helpers, plus the json5 npm library's parse; vendor snippets also compare wasm output against Rust and Go compiled to WebAssembly
one_liner: Standard library of MoonBit, a Wasm/JS/native-targeting language; vendor benchmark shows its JS output 7.7-7.9x faster than idiomatic JS.

name: cpy
baseline: CPython 3.12 (the README names 'python3' as CPython 3.12)
one_liner: Tree-walking interpreter for a Python subset in portable C; claims 1.2x-50x over CPython 3.12 with no published benchmark scripts.

name: Arduino_GFX (GFX Library for Arduino)
baseline: Adafruit_GFX (Adafruit-GFX-Library) with the Adafruit_ILI9341 driver
one_liner: Arduino display library for about 40 panel controllers and many buses; 1.2x-5.2x faster than Adafruit_GFX on an ESP32 SPI ILI9341.

name: FlashKDA
baseline: flash-linear-attention (fla) Triton chunk_kda kernel, and fla chunk_gated_delta_rule (GDN) as a second reference
one_liner: CUTLASS CUDA forward kernel for Kimi Delta Attention; 1.7-3.3x lower latency than flash-linear-attention's Triton chunk_kda on H20/GB200.

name: binlog
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Asynchronous C++ logger writing structured binary logs; about 15x lower p50 call-site latency than async spdlog in Quill's harness.

name: Delaunay32
baseline: Triangle 1.6 (also CDT 1.4.5, delaunator-cpp c1521f6 and Fade2D 2.17.3; CGAL not compared)
one_liner: Parallel exact-integer 2D (constrained) Delaunay triangulator for int32 points; about 4.4x faster than Triangle single-threaded on 1M points.

name: MoroJS engine (@morojs/engine)
language: C++ (Node.js native addon via raw V8 bindings)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: C++ HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket server addon for Node.js, the engine under MoroJS; beat actix-web 1.11-1.14x on a hello-world shootout.

name: cvGPUSpeedup (OpenCV-style wrapper on the Fused Kernel Library)
baseline: OpenCV-CUDA calls launched as separate kernels on one stream (per crop cv::cuda::GpuMat::convertTo and cv::cuda::resize INTER_LINEAR, then cv::cuda::multiply, cvtColor RGB2BGR, subtract, divide and split), against one fused cvGS::executeOperations kernel
one_liner: Header-only CUDA C++20 wrapper that fuses chains of OpenCV-CUDA-style preprocessing calls into one kernel; first-party 38x over OpenCV-CUDA.

name: vergesort
baseline: std::sort, std::stable_sort
one_liner: Presortedness-detecting merge layer over pdqsort; beats std::sort/std::stable_sort when input has long sorted runs.

name: Flatbush
baseline: RBush (dynamic JavaScript R-tree; counts as an R-tree baseline)
one_liner: Static packed Hilbert R-tree for 2D boxes in JavaScript, stored in one ArrayBuffer; billed as faster and leaner than RBush.

name: KDBush
baseline: RBush (JavaScript R-tree)
one_liner: JavaScript static 2D point index (flat kd-tree in one ArrayBuffer); its author says it indexes points 5-8x faster than RBush.

name: RBush
baseline: imbcmdth RTree (older JavaScript R-tree library)
one_liner: JavaScript 2D R-tree for rectangles and points with bulk loading; beats the older imbcmdth RTree JavaScript library.

name: SpiderMonkey (Mozilla)
baseline: QuickJS 2026-06-04 (also Duktape 2.99.99 on Ubuntu and macOS, 2.7.0 on Windows)
one_liner: Mozilla's Firefox JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, embeddable through the C++ JSAPI; its JIT tiers score about 16x QuickJS on v8-v7.

name: llamafile tinyBLAS CPU matmul kernels
baseline: llama.cpp CPU matmul (prior kernels); Intel MKL sgemm
one_liner: tinyBLAS: register-tiled CPU GEMM kernels from llamafile; 1.3-5x faster LLM prompt eval than March-2024 llama.cpp, upstreamed since.

name: Clubcard
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Rust exact-membership filter (partitioned two-level Ribbon cascade) that replaced Firefox CRLite's Bloom filter cascade at under half the size.

name: mozjpeg
baseline: libjpeg-turbo
one_liner: libjpeg-turbo fork that trades much slower JPEG encoding for smaller files; it is not faster than libjpeg-turbo at anything.

name: sccache
baseline: uncached compile (no compiler cache)
one_liner: Compiler-cache wrapper for C, C++, CUDA and Rust with local or cloud storage; skips recompiling unchanged units.

name: source-map (mozilla/source-map, Rust/WebAssembly mappings parser)
language: JavaScript with Rust compiled to WebAssembly (wasm-mappings)
baseline: source-map 0.6 pure-JavaScript source map parser (the same library before the Rust/wasm rewrite of the mappings parser)
one_liner: Mozilla's source-map library with its mappings parser in Rust compiled to WebAssembly; beats the library's own 0.6 JavaScript parser.

name: xenium
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Header-only lock-free MPMC queue templates (Michael-Scott, Ramalhete, Vyukov) beating std::mutex latency 2.5-5.7x.

name: efuse_filter (Erlang NIF, Binary Fuse Filter)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Erlang/Elixir NIF wrapping FastFilter's C binary fuse8 filter; static membership filter beating BEAM Bloom libraries on lookup latency.

name: exor_filter (Erlang NIF, Xor Filter)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Erlang/Elixir C NIF for static xor8/xor16 filters; 2.6-10x faster lookups than BEAM Bloom libraries in the author's benchmark.

name: Constantine (inline x86-64 assembly field arithmetic)
language: Nim (C, Rust and Go bindings; x86-64 inline assembly emitted by Nim macros)
baseline: the same big-integer / finite-field code compiled without assembly (CTT_ASM=0) by GCC and Clang
one_liner: Constant-time pairing-curve cryptography in Nim whose macro-generated x86-64 MULX/ADCX/ADOX inline assembly beats its own compiler-built field arithmetic.

name: Laser (GEMM)
baseline: OpenBLAS
one_liner: Nim BLAS-style GEMM with strided and int32/int64 support; roughly at parity with OpenBLAS, not reliably faster.

name: Weave
baseline: Intel TBB, GCC OpenMP, Cilk
one_liner: Nim task- and data-parallel runtime that uses message-passing work-requesting; claims 3-10x less scheduling overhead than TBB and GCC OpenMP.

name: Tachyon.JSON v6
license: Proprietary (TACHYON PROPRIETARY SOURCE LICENSE v1.0; LICENSE file allows free personal/commercial use but forbids redistribution of source, sub-licensing, and modifying the ASM/SIMD kernels)
baseline: nlohmann::json (also compared against simdjson and Glaze)
one_liner: Single-header AVX2 JSON parser under a proprietary license; benchmarks nlohmann/simdjson but times only its structural-bitmask build, not full parsing.

name: PocketFFT (C++ branch)
baseline: KissFFT
one_liner: Header-only C++11 FFT (multi-D, any length, DCT/DST) behind NumPy and SciPy; about 4.5x faster than KissFFT on 3D transforms.

name: better_bitset
baseline: std::bitset
one_liner: Header-only C++20 bitset adding fast first_one/first_zero bit-scan that std::bitset lacks above 64 bits.

name: mrpt-serialization
baseline: Boost.Serialization binary archive (GTSAM's gtsam::serializeToBinaryStream / deserializeFromBinaryStream)
one_liner: MRPT's portable, versioned binary archive (CArchive); via the gtsam2mrpt_serial bridge it serializes GTSAM factor graphs about 2x faster than Boost.

name: mruby
baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (the copy vendored in scriptorium's javascript/duktape; PUC Lua at 1.341 s in the same table is faster than mruby)
one_liner: Embeddable lightweight Ruby VM in C; ran a 2015 recursive-fib test 4.5x faster than Duktape 1.2.2, 1.6x slower than PUC Lua.

name: mojo-regex (Mojo regular expression library)
baseline: CPython 3.12 re module (C implementation) and the Rust regex crate
one_liner: Pure-Mojo regex library with a re-like API and hybrid DFA/lazy-DFA/NFA engines; first-party micro-benchmarks claim wins over CPython re and Rust regex.

name: Zig wasm32-wasi build in msf/wasmplay
baseline: C++ compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten (em++ -O2), run on the same WASM runtime; also Go (GOOS=wasip1) wasm
one_liner: Zig-vs-C++-vs-Go benchmark repo: Zig ReleaseFast wasm32-wasi edges Emscripten -O2 C++ on one integer matmul loop.

name: msgspec
baseline: msgpack (msgpack-python reference implementation)
one_liner: Python C-extension MessagePack/JSON codec with typed Struct decoding; ~2-2.6x faster round-trip than msgpack-python.

name: SuperLAME
baseline: LAME (stock single-threaded libmp3lame 3.101 beta)
one_liner: Multithreaded MP3 encoder CLI that runs many LAME r6531 instances on chunks; beats single-threaded LAME on wall time, not per core.

name: curve25519 (mehdi sotoodeh / "Mehdi")
baseline: OpenSSL 1.1.1 EVP_PKEY API: EVP_PKEY_ED25519 (CreateKeyPair, SignMessage via EVP_DigestSign) and EVP_PKEY_X25519 (CalculatePublicKey, CreateSharedKey via EVP_PKEY_derive)
one_liner: C/x86-64-asm X25519 and Ed25519 library; precomputed fixed-base tables give 2.8x faster Ed25519 keygen than OpenSSL 1.1.1.

name: bstring
baseline: C standard library char* string functions (strcpy, strcat, strchr, strstr, strcspn, memmove)
one_liner: Maintained fork of Paul Hsieh's Bstrlib: length-prefixed, auto-growing C strings that avoid strcat-style rescans of char* code.

name: OpenRAND (Philox, Threefry, Squares, Tyche counter-based generators)
baseline: std::mt19937 (libstdc++) on CPU and NVIDIA cuRAND on GPU
one_liner: Header-only C++17 counter-based RNGs (Philox, Threefry, Squares, Tyche) for CPU and CUDA/HIP; beats stateful cuRAND in a Brownian dynamics run and std::mt19937 on short streams.

name: libcdada
baseline: libstdc++ std::set, std::map and std::list (native C++ code on the same libstdc++)
one_liner: Pure C API (list, set, map, queue, stack, string, bitmap) wrapping libstdc++ containers; matches libstdc++ at best, never beats it.

name: mTCP
baseline: epoll (Linux kernel TCP/IP stack)
one_liner: User-level, per-core TCP stack over DPDK/PSIO/netmap with an epoll-like API; beats Linux kernel sockets+epoll on short connections.

name: @mtcute/wasm (mtcute)
license: MIT; the tgcrypto-derived AES code in packages/wasm/lib/crypto is LGPL-3.0 (COPYING.lesser, per the package README)
baseline: pako (pure JS zlib) and Node.js built-in zlib for deflate/gunzip; @cryptography/aes (pure JS) for AES-IGE/CTR
one_liner: WebAssembly blob from the mtcute Telegram library: libdeflate gzip, tgcrypto AES-IGE/CTR and SHA hashes, beating pure-JS equivalents.

name: Essentia.js
language: C++ (Essentia) compiled to WebAssembly with a JavaScript API
baseline: Meyda (pure-JS audio feature extraction) and native Essentia; the paper benchmarks against both
one_liner: Essentia's C++ audio-analysis library compiled to WebAssembly with a JS/TypeScript API; papers benchmark it against Meyda, results unread.

name: contour-wasm
baseline: MarchingSquares.js isoBands (pure JavaScript, used internally by turf-isobands)
one_liner: Rust port of MarchingSquares.js isobands, plus isolines, compiled to WebAssembly; README shows 1.3-2x faster than the JS original.

name: Coros
baseline: Intel oneTBB and OpenMP task runtimes (GCC libgomp, LLVM libomp); libfork is not in the graphs
one_liner: Header-only C++23 coroutine fork-join task library with a work-stealing pool; roughly ties oneTBB, beats OpenMP tasks.

name: mtrebi/memory-allocators (free list allocator; linear, stack and pool allocators)
baseline: malloc/free (libc; the benchmark's CAllocator wraps malloc and free)
one_liner: Teaching-grade C++ linear, stack, pool and first-fit free-list allocators; README claims the free list runs about 3x faster than malloc.

name: Ripserer.jl (Julia persistent homology) vs Ripser and Cubical Ripser (C++)
baseline: Ripser (C++, master commit 286d369) and Cubical Ripser (C++, commits 6edb9c5 for 2D and a063dac for 3D)
one_liner: Pure-Julia reimplementation of the Ripser persistent-homology algorithm; matches C++ Ripser on thresholded Rips, beats it only on very sparse inputs.

name: haclog
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Plain C async printf-style logger; producer-side calls about 3.5x faster than spdlog when buffers are not full.

name: DAXFS
baseline: tmpfs (kernel in-memory file system, POSIX read/write)
one_liner: Linux kernel filesystem on DAX memory with lock-free CAS overlay; authors report up to 2.68x tmpfs random-write throughput.

name: bilrost
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Rust derive-based, protobuf-like binary encoding (a rewritten prost fork) that encodes and decodes faster than prost.

name: pqm4
baseline: pqm4 'clean' implementations (PQClean portable C) built with the same arm-none-eabi-gcc flags, but with the same hand-written assembly Keccak-f1600 (common/keccakf1600.S) linked in by mk/crypto.mk, so the baseline is portable C plus assembly hashing
one_liner: Cortex-M4F assembly-optimized ML-KEM and ML-DSA (plus other PQC schemes) that run 1.25-2.1x faster than PQClean clean C.

name: mus-go
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Go serialization primitives for the tagless MUS binary format; ~3x faster than protobuf-go on small structs, ~6x in unsafe mode.

name: BLARE (Blazingly Fast Regular Expression)
baseline: RE2
one_liner: Research framework that decomposes regexes into reordered sub-matches via a bandit-picked plan, layered on RE2/PCRE2/Boost/ICU.

name: mutable (WebAssembly/V8 query compiler)
baseline: HyPer (LLVM-based query compilation)
one_liner: Saarland research main-memory DBMS that JIT-compiles SQL to WebAssembly run by embedded V8; claims HyPer-level TPC-H speed.

name: Rapidgzip
license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (repo page lists both; per-file split not checked)
baseline: GNU gzip (single-threaded deflate decoder); also compared with pigz, igzip (ISA-L), bgzip and pzstd
one_liner: Parallel decompressor and random-access reader for ordinary gzip files; 7-20x faster than GNU gzip on 12 cores.

name: Generalized Elias-Fano (GEF)
baseline: ALP, LeCo, DAC (random-access integer compressors); also compared with Xz and Brotli
one_liner: Elias-Fano-style compressed integer arrays for unsorted sequences, with O(1) random access; claims smaller than ALP, LeCo and DAC.

name: RGC (Recursive Group Coding)
baseline: static 8-bit arithmetic coder (AC); TurboRC rcc2senc() range coder also listed
one_liner: Tiny MIT C entropy coder (Recursive Group Coding) that compresses large-alphabet data better than static AC, claiming about 2x its speed.

name: MySQL
license: GPL-2.0-only (with Oracle's additional linking permission; libmysqlclient also under the Universal FOSS Exception 1.0)
baseline: PostgreSQL 14.5 (sysbench, PostgreSQL run on a different, larger machine)
one_liner: Oracle's client-server SQL database (InnoDB). It edges PostgreSQL only on sysbench oltp_read_write in one cross-machine, durability-off comparison.

name: Qfplib-M0-full (Cortex-M0 floating-point library)
baseline: The GCC toolchain's floating-point library on ARMv6-M ('GCC library' in the README): libgcc soft-float for add/sub/mul/div, and presumably the toolchain's C math library (such as newlib libm) for sqrt, sin, cos, tan, atan2, exp and ln; version and flags not stated
one_liner: Hand-written ARMv6-M assembly float/double library for Cortex-M0, 1.3-14x fewer cycles than GCC's soft-float and math routines.

name: rt_memcpy_cm
language: Assembly (ARM Cortex-M, GCC/IAR/Keil sources) with a C interface
baseline: RT-Thread's C rt_memcpy and the Keil C library memcpy
one_liner: Silicon Labs uC/LIB Cortex-M3/4/7 assembly memcpy packaged as RT-Thread's rt_memcpy; beats RT-Thread's C copy, ties Keil memcpy.

name: ChibiHash
baseline: xxHash (xxhash64), CityHash (city64)
one_liner: 82-line public-domain C header 64-bit hash; about 1.5x XXH64 bulk throughput and a third fewer cycles on short keys.

name: imgdiff (n7olkachev)
baseline: odiff v1 (2020); PR #5 re-measured against odiff v2
one_liner: Multi-threaded Go pixel-diff CLI and package with pixelmatch-style YIQ threshold; README says 3-4.5x faster than 2020 odiff, but odiff v2 matched it.

name: nadavrot/memset_benchmark (AVX2 assembly memset and memcpy)
language: Assembly (x86-64 AVX2, AT&T .S) with C/C++ harness
baseline: glibc memset and memcpy (with and without PLT indirection, 'libc@plt' and 'libc'), also musl and folly (memcpy chart)
one_liner: Small-size-tuned AVX2 x86-64 assembly memset and memcpy that beat glibc, Folly and musl on 0-511 byte calls.

name: libQD3 (double-double, triple-double, quad-double, extended-double)
baseline: MPFR (the MPLAPACK manual's Rgemm numbers for upstream QD against MPFR and GMP at their 512-bit default); libQD3's own docs/qd.tex also carries the original QD paper's per-operation timing table against Bailey's MPFUN
one_liner: Maintained fork of the Hida-Li-Bailey QD library adding triple-double and binary80/binary32 expansions; fixed 106-212-bit floats, much cheaper than MPFR.

name: MPLAPACK (multiple-precision BLAS/LAPACK with double-double, quad-double and CUDA backends)
baseline: GMP (mpf) and MPFR backends of the same library, at their default 512-bit precision
one_liner: Full BLAS/LAPACK in C++ at binary80/128, double-double, quad-double, GMP and MPFR; the dd/qd backends far outrun its 512-bit GMP/MPFR backends.

name: NanoMsg
baseline: ZeroMQ
one_liner: C library of brokerless messaging patterns (PUB/SUB, REQ/REP, etc.) with lower small-message latency than ZeroMQ on one host.

name: NNG (nanomsg-next-generation)
baseline: NanoMsg
one_liner: Maintained C rewrite of nanomsg (Scalability Protocols). It beats nanomsg's pub/sub throughput only for very large messages.

name: jpeg-rusturbo
baseline: Rust image crate 0.25: its own built-in scalar JPEG encoder (4:2:0 only) and its zune-jpeg-backed decoder. libjpeg-turbo is never measured.
one_liner: Pure-Rust SIMD JPEG encoder and decoder with libjpeg-turbo-derived kernels; encodes about 5x faster than the image crate's encoder.

name: SpaceWasm (NASA JPL)
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift), Wasmer (Cranelift) startup
one_liner: NASA JPL's no_std Wasm 1.0 interpreter for flight software; compiles plus instantiates modules about 60x faster than Wasmtime or Wasmer Cranelift.

name: NATS JetStream
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: CNCF Go messaging server whose built-in JetStream persistence showed ~14x lower median latency than Kafka at light load.

name: supercop.wasm
language: C (orlp/ed25519 compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten, JavaScript wrapper)
baseline: @noble/curves 0.7.0 (pure JavaScript ed25519) and node:crypto ed25519 (native OpenSSL) in the third-party berith benchmark; tweetnacl-js and a native SUPERCOP build are not measured
one_liner: orlp/ed25519 compiled to a size-optimized WebAssembly module; about 10x faster than pure-JS @noble/curves 0.7.0 for Ed25519.

name: allox (Rust general-purpose allocator)
baseline: glibc malloc (the 'system' column of the Linux table), mimalloc and snmalloc, each driven through a Rust GlobalAlloc wrapper; Rust-native talc and dlmalloc are also compared
one_liner: Pure-Rust thread-caching global allocator; author's harness shows 1.9-3.5x the best C allocator on mixed-size churn, parity elsewhere.

name: ncruces/wasm2go (Wasm to Go compiler)
baseline: wazero v1.10.1 (go-marisa's wazero-based bindings at commit 37cde21, Wasm blob built with -msimd128; wazero execution mode not stated on the page)
one_liner: Ahead-of-time Wasm-to-Go source translator; cgo-free, runtime-free alternative to embedding wazero, faster on most trie queries.

name: Zserio
baseline: protoc
one_liner: Own-IDL C++/Java/Python serialization framework; bit-packed decode 1.2x-2.6x faster than protoc.

name: Magic Enum
baseline: conjure_enum (fix8mt/conjure_enum), another macro-free C++ enum-reflection library
one_liner: Macro-free C++17 enum reflection (enum to string, string to enum, iteration); compiles faster than conjure_enum at scale.

name: LLFIO
baseline: POSIX read/write (physical device latency used as reference)
one_liner: Low-level, zero-copy, race-free C++17 file and memory-map i/o library; no head-to-head numbers against POSIX read/write.

name: Breeze
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Go web framework on the gnet event loop; about 2.5x Go net/http on hello-world HTTP/1.1 throughput.

name: LZMAT
one_liner: Abandoned 2008 nibble-packed LZ77 codec; decompresses about 1.2x faster than zlib at zlib -1 ratio, compresses 3x slower.

name: LZO (lzo1x)
baseline: zlib (level 1, fastest mode)
one_liner: LZO1X-1: byte-aligned LZ77 block codec; 5.6x faster compression, 1.9x faster decompression than zlib -1, 30% larger output.

name: LightningXML
baseline: pugixml, RapidXML, libxml2
one_liner: Header-only C++20 pull deserializer binding XML straight into structs; beats pugixml, RapidXML and libxml2 on every author benchmark.

name: neon-ntt (hand-written Armv8-A Neon assembly NTTs for Dilithium, Kyber and Saber)
baseline: Dilithium reference C implementation (pq-crystals ref code compiled with gcc 10.3.0 -O3 on Cortex-A72 and Apple clang 12.0.5 -O3 on Apple M1); for Kyber and Saber the baseline is the previous Neon implementation by Nguyen and Gaj (re-benchmarked in SUPERCOP)
one_liner: Hand-written Armv8-A Neon assembly NTTs for Kyber, Dilithium and Saber; about 4-6x faster than reference-C Dilithium NTTs.

name: s1vm
baseline: wasmi (paritytech/wasmi as it stood in April 2021, version not stated); also compared with WASM3, which it loses to
one_liner: Proof-of-concept safe-Rust WebAssembly interpreter that compiles functions to nested closures; beat 2021-era wasmi 2.6x on fib, lost to wasm3.

name: tac (neosmart, SIMD-accelerated Rust rewrite of GNU tac)
baseline: GNU Coreutils tac (C)
one_liner: Rust tac that reverses a file's lines using mmap and an AVX2 newline scan; claims 2.55x over GNU tac.

name: MaxAs
baseline: cuBLAS sgemm (NVIDIA's library kernels, compiled by NVIDIA's toolchain)
one_liner: Perl assembler for NVIDIA Maxwell SASS; its hand-scheduled SGEMM beat cuBLAS's Maxwell kernels by about 4-25%.

name: Nervana neon (GPU convolution kernels)
baseline: cuDNN R4 (fp16 and fp32, via Torch bindings)
one_liner: Archived Python deep learning framework whose hand-assembled Maxwell GPU convolution kernels beat cuDNN R4 by 1.2-2x on 2016 ConvNet benchmarks.

name: Netty
baseline: nginx (echo module) and Crow (C++) in the same table
one_liner: Java asynchronous network framework; a 2015 Netty 3 hello-world server out-ran a 4-worker nginx echo setup and Crow.

name: Nelux (NeLux)
language: C++ (Python package with PyTorch tensor output)
baseline: FFmpeg CLI piped decode (ffmpeg-rgb24 subprocess; ffmpeg-nvdec subprocess for the GPU path); torchcodec also compared
one_liner: FFmpeg-backed Python video reader returning PyTorch tensors; parallel RGB conversion outruns torchcodec and ffmpeg-CLI rgb24 pipes.

name: nilo
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG), h2o (C, clang Release -march=native), agensio and proxygen (C++), Drogon and userver (C++) rows in the same suite
one_liner: Zig web framework on zio fibers; beats nginx on HttpArena h2/h2c, TLS-JSON and pipelined rows, loses on plain HTTP/1.1.

name: nghttp2 (nghttpx HTTP/2 proxy)
baseline: Apache Traffic Server (ATS) as HTTP/2 terminating reverse proxy
one_liner: C HTTP/2 framing library (curl's HTTP/2 backend) plus nghttpx, an HTTP/3/2/1.1 TLS-terminating reverse proxy; weak evidence against ATS.

name: NGINX
baseline: Apache httpd (Apache2, version and MPM not stated on the benchmark page)
one_liner: Event-driven C web server and reverse proxy; served a small static page at 1.9-3.2x Apache httpd's request rate.

name: njs (nginx JavaScript)
baseline: Duktape 2.99.99 (unreleased master, built by ahaoboy/duktape-build with Duktape's development Makefile, which uses -Os -fomit-frame-pointer -g) on ubuntu/macos-arm64; QuickJS 2026.06.04 is faster than njs in this suite
one_liner: nginx's built-in JavaScript engine (ES5.1 plus an ES6+ subset) for request scripting; about 1.5x Duktape on v8-v7, behind QuickJS.

name: DSL-JSON (Java, HotSpot) vs nlohmann/json, json-c and Boost.PropertyTree in kostya/benchmarks JSON
baseline: nlohmann/json (C++), json-c (C library called from a C++ driver) and Boost.PropertyTree (C++) as built by kostya/benchmarks; DSL-JSON does NOT beat RapidJSON (all variants incl. SAX Precise), Boost.JSON, simdjson, yyjson, yajl, gason or DAW JSON Link in the same table
one_liner: Java JSON databinding library with compile-time generated converters; about 2x nlohmann/json and json-c in kostya's JSON test, far behind fast C/C++ parsers.

name: ngtcp2
baseline: quiche
one_liner: Pure-C IETF QUIC transport library (RFC 9000); in one loopback harness, 1.5-2.1x quiche's bulk-transfer throughput.

name: Pfim
baseline: FreeImage (via FreeImage-dotnet-core 4.3.6 with a bundled FreeImage.dll), DevIL (via DevILSharp 0.2.4) and ImageMagick (via Magick.NET-Q16-AnyCPU 7.12.0), all native C/C++ libraries driven from .NET, plus managed Targa decoders TargaImage 1.0, ImageFormats 1.0, StbSharp 0.7.2.38 and TgaSharpLib 1.0
one_liner: Managed .NET decoder for Targa and DDS (BC1-BC7) images; beats FreeImage, DevIL and Magick.NET called from C#.

name: rapidhash
baseline: xxh3 (xxHash3) — not literally std::hash, but the widely-used fast non-cryptographic hash function developers use in place of std::hash
one_liner: Header-only, wyhash-derived 64-bit hash beating xxh3 on latency and throughput on most CPUs; ties or loses on AMD Ryzen.

name: Asmc
baseline: MASM (Microsoft Macro Assembler 6.15 and 10.0), also compared with JWasm and UASM
one_liner: Self-hosted MASM-syntax x86/x64 assembler descended from JWasm; forum timings put it about 1.5x faster than Microsoft's ML.

name: ctbignum
baseline: GMP (mpn/mpz)
one_liner: Header-only constexpr C++20 fixed-width big integers and Z/qZ arithmetic; beats GMP mpn_mul at 2-4 limbs.

name: Sep
baseline: CsvHelper (the most widely used .NET CSV parsing library)
one_liner: Zero-allocation, SIMD-vectorized .NET CSV/TSV parser built to beat CsvHelper on throughput.

name: QOIR
baseline: libpng (Debian Bullseye build); also libwebp lossless
one_liner: Single-header C codec for a new lossless image format; encodes about 30x and decodes about 4.9x faster than libpng.

name: fpconv (night-shift)
baseline: std::ostringstream (iostreams); page's headline ratio is vs sprintf()
one_liner: Tiny Grisu2 C library converting doubles to shortest round-trip strings, ~10x faster than std::ostringstream.

name: fulmine.js
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Drop-in Express 5 replacement on uWebSockets.js; hello-world suite run: ~5x Express, 1.25x actix-web req/s.

name: Jsonifier
baseline: simdjson
one_liner: Header-only C++20 JSON library that binds to registered structs; 1.1-1.8x simdjson ondemand read throughput on most whole documents.

name: trigno_simd_cpp (SIMD trigonometric approximations, Goyal & Arora)
baseline: <cmath> std::sin, std::cos, std::tan
one_liner: Piecewise rational sin/cos/tan approximation using AVX2 FMA plus a fast inverse-sqrt hack; beats scalar libm sin/cos/tan.

name: hparse
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: Zig SIMD HTTP/1.x parser modeled on picohttpparser; about 1.14x faster than a gcc -O3 picohttpparser build on x86-64.

name: icey (HTTP server module)
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Single-threaded libuv + llhttp HTTP/1.1 server inside a C++20 media toolkit; 34% more keep-alive req/s than Go net/http on one vCPU.

name: Ninja
baseline: GNU Make (CMake Unix Makefiles generator backend)
one_liner: Minimal C++ build executor fed by generated build.ninja files; much faster no-op and incremental builds than CMake-generated Makefiles.

name: fast_matmul (NinjadenMu; didactic BLIS-style SGEMM for Apple M4)
baseline: OpenBLAS as called through NumPy (float32 A @ B in scripts/openblas.py)
one_liner: Seven-step NEON SGEMM tutorial for Apple M4; single-thread ties NumPy/OpenBLAS, OpenMP version about 1.5x ahead.

name: MuBLIS
baseline: OpenBLAS (single-threaded, built for Apple Silicon)
one_liner: Small BLIS-style C framework for real L3 BLAS with NEON/AVX2 kernels; matches single-threaded OpenBLAS on Apple M4.

name: nim-regex (nitely/regex)
baseline: PCRE2
one_liner: Pure-Nim linear-time regex engine (PCRE-like syntax, no backtracking) beating PCRE2 on find-all throughput.

name: wut-server
baseline: nginx (C; own build with all optimization options, LTO, static OpenSSL, ngx_headers_more; 1 worker, 1024 worker connections, HTTP/2, TLS 1.3 only)
one_liner: Single-purpose Rust HTTPS server that returns the caller's IP; one first-party wrk run beat a one-worker nginx 1.49x.

name: YAS (Yet Another Serialization)
baseline: Boost.Serialization and cereal
one_liner: Header-only C++11 serializer with a Boost.Serialization-style API; its binary archive ran 3.5-7.2x faster than Boost.Serialization and cereal.

name: SpLLT (task-based sparse Cholesky)
baseline: HSL_MA87 (HSL parallel sparse Cholesky)
one_liner: Task-based supernodal sparse Cholesky (Fortran) on OpenMP, StarPU or PaRSEC; papers report parity with HSL_MA87, not a speedup.

name: SyLVER (NLAFET)
baseline: SPRAL SSIDS / HSL MA87 / PARDISO (no comparison found in the repo)
one_liner: Research StarPU task-based sparse Cholesky/LDL^T solver built on SPRAL SSIDS kernels; no published speedup in the repo.

name: Roto
baseline: Lua 5.5 (via mlua) and QuickJS (via rquickjs)
one_liner: Statically typed, Cranelift-JIT-compiled scripting language for Rust hosts; about 1.3x faster than Lua 5.5 (mlua) on a Rust-object sort benchmark.

name: simdzone
baseline: Knot DNS libzscanner (zscanner) 3.3.4, and NSD 4.9's previous zonec zone parser
one_liner: SIMD DNS zone-file (presentation format) parser in C; about 4x Knot DNS's zscanner on the .se zone.

name: Unbound
baseline: BIND
one_liner: NLnet Labs' validating, recursive, caching DNS resolver in C; the developer's 2008 changelog puts cache-hit throughput at ~3.4x BIND's.

name: lockfreelog
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Tiny header-only C++20 SPSC ring-buffer logger; about 5.3x spdlog async throughput to /dev/null on an Apple M3.

name: go-simdcsv
baseline: encoding/csv (Go standard library CSV parser)
one_liner: AVX-512 SIMD CSV parser for Go; drop-in encoding/csv replacement, faster only on unquoted data.

name: hist-rs (hist, Rust unique-line counter)
baseline: Plain 'sort | uniq -c | sort -n' as found on PATH (the README calls it coreutils; on macOS the default sort and uniq are the BSD-derived system tools unless GNU coreutils shadows them; implementation and versions not stated), in the default locale and with LC_ALL=C; also uutils coreutils sort/uniq with --parallel 1 and an awk pipeline (awk implementation not stated; README links the gawk manual).
one_liner: Hash-counting Rust replacement for 'sort | uniq -c | sort -n'; 5.3x faster than the LC_ALL=C pipeline (first-party).

name: Ubique (nalgebra compiled to WebAssembly)
language: Rust (nalgebra compiled to WebAssembly) with TypeScript on Deno
baseline: math.js (JavaScript numerical library)
one_liner: MATLAB-style TypeScript math library with nalgebra-in-WebAssembly kernels; first-party runs show 4.6-26x faster than math.js.

name: cjs-module-lexer (C lexer compiled to WebAssembly)
language: C compiled to WebAssembly (wasi-sdk and Binaryen), with a JavaScript build
baseline: the same lexer's pure JavaScript build (lexer.js) running in V8/Node.js
one_liner: C CommonJS export lexer compiled to Wasm; beat its own pure-JS build in 2020 Node, near parity on Node 24.

name: llhttp
baseline: http_parser (nodejs/http-parser, the parser llhttp replaced in Node.js)
one_liner: Node.js's HTTP/1.x parser: a C state machine generated by llparse that replaced http_parser; README claims 2.56x its parsing bandwidth.

name: merve (nodejs CommonJS export lexer)
baseline: cjs-module-lexer (the JS/WebAssembly lexer previously bundled in Node.js core)
one_liner: C++20 lexer that finds CommonJS named exports for Node's ESM import(); replaced cjs-module-lexer, making cold CJS imports about 21% faster.

name: SHA-Intrinsics (noloader)
baseline: portable C SHA-256 (the repo's own sha256.c reference) and OpenSSL SHA-256: neither is measured in the README
one_liner: Public-domain SHA-1/SHA-256 block functions on Intel SHA-NI and ARMv8 crypto intrinsics, plus POWER8 SHA-256/512; no measured baseline.

name: numpy-minmax
baseline: NumPy np.amin followed by np.amax
one_liner: Single-pass AVX/AVX-512 min and max for float32 and int16 NumPy arrays, replacing separate np.amin and np.amax passes.

name: Copapy
language: Python (tracing compiler) with C runner and stencils
baseline: NumPy 2.3.5 (also a pure-Python case in tests/benchmark.py)
one_liner: Python-traced copy-and-patch compiler for small realtime numeric graphs; beats NumPy 2.3.5 per-call overhead by 1.7-3.9x.

name: Paserati
baseline: goja (dop251/goja, pure-Go JavaScript engine) and QuickJS ports usable from Go: QJS (fastschema/qjs, QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly) and ModerncQuickJS (ccgo-translated QuickJS) in the third-party shootout; the README's own hyperfine table uses a 'qjs' QuickJS runner binary of unstated origin. Neither native QuickJS nor V8 is measured.
one_liner: Pure-Go TypeScript/JavaScript bytecode interpreter, about 1.2-1.7x faster than goja on V8 v7; native QuickJS is about 3x faster.

name: libnabo
baseline: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor library, exact-search kd-tree); tests/knnbench.cpp benchmarks ANN (stack and priority search) when ANN is installed. A FLANN code path exists but is switched off in knnbench.cpp ('currently disable FLANN', #undef HAVE_FLANN).
one_liner: Eigen-based C++ kd-tree for exact (or epsilon-approximate) k-NN in low dimensions; the README claims 5-20% faster than ANN.

name: nanoserde
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Zero-dependency Rust derive serializer whose schemaless binary format encodes ~3.8x and decodes ~1.6x faster than prost on logs.

name: aron
baseline: macOS as (Apple's system assembler, not GNU as)
one_liner: Incomplete Rust x86-64 Intel-syntax assembler emitting Mach-O; a startup-bound hello-world test ran 12.9x faster than macOS as.

name: stb_sprintf (nothings/stb)
baseline: sprintf/snprintf (C runtime, MSVC/GCC CRT)
one_liner: Single-header, public-domain sprintf/snprintf replacement claiming 4-35x faster formatting than MSVC 2008's CRT.

name: fast-alloc
baseline: malloc/free and new/delete
one_liner: Small C++20 pool, stack and free-list arenas for game code; beats new/delete and malloc only on fixed-size or frame-scoped patterns.

name: msf_gif
license: Dual: MIT or Unlicense-style public-domain dedication (text at the bottom of msf_gif.h)
language: C (single header, compiles as C99 or C++98)
baseline: gif.h (Charlie Tangora's single-header encoder, named gif_h in the timings file) and jo_gif
one_liner: Single-header C animated-GIF encoder with SSE2 frame quantization; first-party timings 5x to 30x faster than gif.h and jo_gif.

name: FastAndFourier (FAF, JIT-compiled DSP/FFT library)
baseline: KissFFT (and FFTW3 FFTW_ESTIMATE/FFTW_MEASURE, which beat it); also NotoriousFFT
one_liner: C11 DSP library (FFT, DCT/DST, DWT, CWT, STFT) with IR interpreter plus runtime gcc JIT; beats KissFFT only at some sizes.

name: Notorious-FFT
baseline: minfft (aimukhin/minfft, small power-of-two FFT library; not one of the listed incumbents)
one_liner: Header-only C FFT with an FFTW-shaped API and minfft-style split-radix core; 8-13% faster than minfft on ARM, far behind FFTW.

name: exec-rs
baseline: Tokio
one_liner: Rust port of C++ P2300 senders/receivers with a mio event loop; its single-threaded echo server beats Tokio 10-26% (self-reported).

name: 3star-rankselect (3* rank/select)
baseline: SDSL (sd_vector, mcl select), sux (rank9sel, simple_select), pasta flat rank/select, Poppy (benchmark script options)
one_liner: Research rank/select bit vector with worst-case constant-time select at about 0.8 percent space overhead, far below SDSL, sux and pasta.

name: ntex
baseline: Drogon (C++) in the HttpArena baseline profile; lithium and cinatra (C++) in the TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext leaderboard
one_liner: Rust framework for HTTP/1, HTTP/2, WebSocket and TLS services; in HttpArena it edges Drogon on keep-alive requests but loses on connection churn.

name: ArceKV (ElasticLSM + Arce)
license: GPL-2.0 (GitHub-detected; repo is a modified RocksDB tree that ships both LICENSE.Apache and LICENSE.leveldb, matching RocksDB's dual Apache-2.0/GPL-2.0 licensing)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: RocksDB fork whose workload-driven compaction and write-stall policy (Arce) beats RocksDB leveling when read/write mixes shift.

name: Walrus (embedded log/WAL storage engine)
baseline: Kafka
one_liner: Embeddable Rust per-topic write-ahead log engine; ~8% more unsynced writes/s than a local single-broker Kafka, tied when fsync'd.

name: kiwi (nucleic, C++ Cassowary solver)
baseline: original Cassowary C++ solver (cassowary-0.60 assumed; the README does not give a version)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 Cassowary linear-constraint solver for UI layout, claimed 10-500x faster than the original Cassowary C++ solver.

name: base64-simd (Nugine/simd)
baseline: GNU coreutils base64 (/usr/bin/base64, C), via the uutils coreutils base64 command that adopted base64-simd
one_liner: Rust SIMD base64 (plus hex, base32, UUID) crate; made uutils base64 1.56x faster than GNU coreutils base64 end to end.

name: Nuitka
baseline: CPython 2.7 (Debian build) running pystone
one_liner: Python-to-C compiler that runs unmodified CPython 2.6-3.14 code; about 3.4x CPython 2.7 on pystone, far less on typical code.

name: ALBUS
baseline: Intel MKL SpMV (oneAPI 2021); also CSR5 and merge-based SpMV
one_liner: Research OpenMP+AVX2 double-precision CSR SpMV kernel with nonzero-balanced thread split; paper reports beating MKL, CSR5 and Merge.

name: Numba
baseline: CPython 3.12 (interpreted Python; the dev-branch workflow sets python-version 3.12 via actions/setup-python, so the version is stated, not inferred; tables for 3.10, 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14 use the PyPI Pyccel 2.2.3 run)
one_liner: LLVM-based JIT for numeric Python: @njit-compiled NumPy loops run 1.4x to 450x faster than CPython 3.12 in pyccel-benchmarks.

name: NumPy numpy.random Generator (PCG64, PCG64DXSM, SFC64 bit generators)
baseline: MT19937 (legacy RandomState and MT19937 under Generator)
one_liner: NumPy's Generator API with PCG64/PCG64DXSM/SFC64 bit generators and ziggurat samplers; about 1.6-2.5x faster than legacy MT19937 RandomState.

name: x86-simd-sort (numpy/x86-simd-sort)
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: AVX-512/AVX2 SIMD quicksort/select library beating std::sort on primitive arrays and key-derived struct sorts (object_qsort).

name: Lua-CSharp
baseline: NLua (C# binding to native Lua) and MoonSharp (Lua interpreter in C#)
one_liner: Pure C# Lua 5.2 interpreter for .NET and Unity with low-overhead C# interop; beats NLua and MoonSharp on host-call loops.

name: Thrust (thrust::sort)
license: Apache-2.0 (Thrust, with portions under BSL-1.0 and a FreeBSD-derived licence); CUB, which supplies thrust::sort's CUDA radix sort, is BSD-3-Clause; libcu++ is Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Header-only CUDA algorithms library; thrust::sort's GPU radix sort beat single-threaded std::sort 80-320x on large int arrays.

name: cuEquivariance
language: Python (frontends; CUDA kernels ship as separate pip packages)
baseline: e3nn (PyTorch equivariant tensor products for MACE, NequIP and similar models)
one_liner: NVIDIA's CUDA kernels for equivariant tensor products (MACE, NequIP, Allegro); an independent study puts MACE inference about 3x faster than e3nn.

name: CUTLASS
baseline: cuBLAS (cublasSgemm, run through the CUDA samples' matrixMulCUBLAS)
one_liner: NVIDIA's header-only CUDA C++ templates (CuTe) and Python DSLs for building GEMM/conv kernels; matches cuBLAS at best, wins on fusion and flexibility.

name: FasterTransformer
baseline: TensorFlow XLA (FP16) and PyTorch TorchScript (FP16) for the BERT encoder; TensorFlow and PyTorch decoder and beam-search implementations for translation decoding
one_liner: NVIDIA's discontinued CUDA C++ transformer inference library; beats TensorFlow XLA and TorchScript FP16 BERT on T4, mostly via INT8.

name: MatX
baseline: handwritten CUDA kernels + cuFFT (FFT pipeline); also CuPy 14.1.1 eager and NumPy 2.5.1 + SciPy 1.18.0 (Black-Scholes)
one_liner: NumPy-style C++20 GPU array library whose JIT fusion of a cuFFT pipeline ran 1.61x faster than handwritten CUDA + cuFFT.

name: NCCL
license: Apache-2.0 for most of the project; some parts keep a BSD-3-Clause license (LICENSE.txt)
baseline: Gloo CPU allreduce_ring (gloo/benchmark/main.cc CPU benchmark, run with -s 2), compared against NCCL on GPUs
one_liner: NVIDIA's GPU collective-communication library (all-reduce, all-gather, send/recv); far faster than Gloo for large GPU all-reduces, slower for small ones.

name: PhysX
baseline: Bullet Physics
one_liner: NVIDIA's frozen 2018 PhysX 3.4 rigid-body and scene-query SDK; one forum user timed PhysX capsule sweeps 6-19x faster than Bullet's.

name: CGBN (Cooperative Groups Big Numbers)
baseline: GMP 6.1.2 (OpenMP, 20-core Xeon)
one_liner: NVIDIA's header-only CUDA library for fixed-size unsigned big integers; a V100 out-throughputs 20-core OpenMP GMP 4-77x on batches.

name: tiny-cuda-nn
baseline: TensorFlow v2.5.0 with XLA (which uses cuDNN/cuBLAS)
one_liner: CUDA framework whose fully fused small-MLP kernels train and infer 2x-10x faster than TensorFlow 2.5 XLA (RTX 3090).

name: NOVA (linux-nova)
baseline: ext4-DAX, xfs-DAX, PMFS, Ext4-data, Btrfs (kernel file systems on NVM)
one_liner: Research Linux kernel file system for persistent memory; per-inode logs beat ext4-DAX, xfs-DAX, PMFS and btrfs on write-heavy workloads.

name: keccak-batch
baseline: keccak-asm (assembly Keccak-256 backend behind Alloy's asm-keccak feature) and tiny-keccak scalar implementation
one_liner: Rust crate that hashes 2/4/8 equal-length inputs at once with SIMD Keccak-256; ~5.5x per hash over keccak-asm (README).

name: msdfgl
baseline: msdfgen (Chlumsky's CPU multi-channel signed distance field generator, single-threaded and OpenMP builds); incumbent for MSDF font atlas generation, not one of HarfBuzz or FreeType
one_liner: OpenGL shader port of Chlumsky's MSDF glyph generator; first-party chart shows 60x-132x faster than single-threaded msdfgen on one laptop.

name: Unsigned Bigint (fixed-width ADX/BMI2 big integer)
baseline: Boost.Multiprecision (backend and version not stated)
one_liner: Fixed-width unsigned big integer for MSVC x64 with MASM MULX/ADX kernels; beats Boost.Multiprecision on add/sub/mul/modexp, loses on division.

name: curve25519-voi
baseline: Go standard library crypto/ed25519 and golang.org/x/crypto/curve25519 (X25519) for single operations; ed25519consensus (hdevalence) for batch verification, since stdlib has no batch verify; Cloudflare CIRCL also benchmarked
one_liner: Go Ed25519/X25519/sr25519 library ported from curve25519-dalek; ~1.9x faster signing, ~1.7x faster verification than Go 1.17 crypto/ed25519.

name: Oat++
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Zero-dependency C++ web framework (REST, DTO/JSON, Swagger, WebSocket) whose default server beat Go net/http ~1.5x on hello-world.

name: HyperJet (hyper-dual number automatic differentiation)
baseline: Eigen AutoDiffScalar (nested), autodiff (dual2nd) and ceres::Jet
one_liner: Header-only C++23 hyper-dual numbers giving value, gradient and dense Hessian in one pass; 1.2-3.3x faster than Eigen AutoDiffScalar/autodiff.

name: Objeck
baseline: LuaJIT 2.1 (tracing JIT); the same table also lists Java 21 (OpenJDK 21.0.12 HotSpot, tiered JIT), CPython 3.12.3 and Ruby 3.2.3
one_liner: Objeck: object-oriented language with a C++ VM and AMD64/ARM64 method JIT; beats CPython and Ruby, LuaJIT only on binarytrees.

name: tinyrand (obsidiandynamics/tinyrand, Rust no_std PRNGs)
baseline: Rust rand crate (ChaCha12 StdRng) and the fastrand crate (Wyrand)
one_liner: Dependency-free no_std Rust crate with Wyrand, Xorshift and SplitMix-style PRNGs; README shows about 2x fastrand and 6x rand's ChaCha12.

name: blake2b_simd / blake2s_simd
baseline: OpenSSL SHA-512 / OpenSSL SHA-1 (also compared to libsodium BLAKE2b)
one_liner: Rust BLAKE2b/2s/2bp/2sp crates with AVX2/SSE4.1 kernels; its BLAKE2b hashes about 1.8x faster than OpenSSL SHA-512 in its own benchmark.

name: wasm_of_ocaml (OCaml to WebAssembly GC compiler in ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)
baseline: js_of_ocaml (OCaml bytecode to JavaScript) output running in Node.js / V8
one_liner: OCaml-bytecode-to-WebAssembly-GC compiler in the js_of_ocaml repo; preliminary 2023 runs: 10-20% faster than js_of_ocaml's JavaScript.

name: octobuild
baseline: stock Unreal Build Tool / Unreal Automation Tool build without octobuild (README 'Without octobuild' column)
one_liner: Rust compiler cache for Unreal Engine that impersonates IncrediBuild's xgConsole to speed up re-compiles vs. no cache.

name: ODE (Open Dynamics Engine)
baseline: Bullet Physics (through Gazebo-classic's Bullet plugin); the same benchmark also runs DART and Simbody
one_liner: Long-lived C/C++ rigid-body dynamics engine with joints and built-in collision; Gazebo's fork ran slightly faster than Bullet in OSRF benchmarks.

name: tiny-ml-runtime
baseline: PyTorch 2.x (Python, batch size 1)
one_liner: Educational pure-C MLP inference loop; beats per-call Python PyTorch only on tiny nets, loses 5x on MNIST.

name: Quill
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Asynchronous C++17 logger whose LOG_INFO call site costs single-digit nanoseconds, about 45x below async spdlog at p50.

name: hashtree
baseline: OpenSSL SHA-256
one_liner: Batched SHA-256 of many fixed 64-byte inputs for Merkle trees; ~4.7x OpenSSL's per-message SHA256() on AVX2.

name: gxhash
baseline: xxHash (XXH3)
one_liner: AES-round Rust hash: about 1.5-2.35x XXH3's bulk throughput in SMHasher suites, but slower than XXH3 on keys under 32 bytes.

name: ohkami (nio backend)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Rust HTTP/1.1 web framework whose nio thread-per-core build out-served actix-web by ~11% on an empty-route benchmark.

name: Agoo-C
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Small C HTTP/1.1 and GraphQL server library built on Ruby Agoo's C core; ~2.1x Go net/http at 256+ connections.

name: corvus
baseline: scalar vendor libm called through std::cos/std::sin/std::exp/std::lgamma (UCRT on Windows, Apple libSystem on macOS); also compared against corvus's own element-at-a-time calls
one_liner: Accuracy-first SIMD double-precision erf/lgamma/incomplete gamma-beta and sin/cos/exp batch kernels; sin/cos 3.2-5.6x faster than scalar vendor libm.

name: libstats
baseline: scalar loops over std::exp, std::log, std::erf and std::cos (platform libm); corvus v1.0.1 SIMD kernels on M1 as a second baseline
one_liner: C++20 statistical-distributions library with runtime-dispatched SSE2/AVX/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON exp, log, erf and cos kernels that beat scalar libm loops.

name: Proteus (programmable runtime specialization and JIT layer on LLVM for C++, CUDA and HIP)
baseline: Ahead-of-time compiled CUDA/HIP/C++ kernels (typical AoT compilation of the same application)
one_liner: LLVM-based JIT layer that respecialises existing C++, CUDA and HIP kernels on runtime values; beats AOT builds of the same code on GPUs.

name: evtx (Rust Windows Event Log parser and evtx_dump)
baseline: libevtx evtxexport (C, libyal), built from source by the repo's benchmark script
one_liner: Rust Windows .evtx parser and evtx_dump CLI; 8.8x faster than libyal's C evtxexport on one thread (same run).

name: needletail (Rust FASTA/FASTQ parser)
baseline: kseq.h from klib (C FASTA/FASTQ parser)
one_liner: Rust zero-copy FASTA/FASTQ parser; 1.75x faster than C kseq.h on plain 4-line FASTQ in lh3's 2020 biofast run.

name: OneFlow
baseline: NVIDIA NGC 20.03 containers (MXNet 1.6.0, TensorFlow 1.15.2, PyTorch 1.5.0a0) running NVIDIA DeepLearningExamples, plus stock PyTorch 1.6.0, TensorFlow 2.3.0, MXNet 1.6.0 (gluon-cv/gluon-nlp), PaddlePaddle 1.8.3 and MindSpore official model scripts
one_liner: Distributed deep learning training framework (C++/CUDA core, PyTorch-like Python API); vendor DLPerf shows 1.1-1.5x NGC PyTorch/MXNet on 32 V100s.

name: sigilbuzz
baseline: rustybuzz 0.20 (archived Rust port of HarfBuzz) only; HarfBuzz itself and FreeType are never measured, and the sigilbuzz-capi hb_* C library is never benchmarked against libharfbuzz
one_liner: Pure-Rust, no_std HarfBuzz-API text shaper with an hb_* C library; faster than rustybuzz on Latin/Hebrew only, slower on complex scripts.

name: OpenCilk (opencilk-project)
baseline: Intel oneTBB, OpenMP and the Intel Cilk Plus runtime, each reached by OpenCilk's own compiler lowering the same Cilk programs to that runtime (the PMAM 2023 program, seen as a search snippet, says OpenCilk was extended to support Cilk Plus, OpenMP and oneTBB with fewer than 2000 new lines each; the abstract itself says only 'the other runtimes')
one_liner: LLVM/Clang fork compiling Cilk fork-join C/C++ onto a work-stealing runtime; paper reports beating oneTBB, OpenMP and Cilk Plus runtimes.

name: go-sieve
baseline: hashicorp/golang-lru (LRU and ARC)
one_liner: Fixed-capacity generic Go SIEVE cache whose mutex-free Get path out-scales hashicorp/golang-lru LRU/ARC under concurrent reads.

name: OpenCV
baseline: ImageMagick (6.9 via the Wand binding, single-threaded, in pillow-perf; magick and convert 7.1.1 in the libvips Speed-and-memory-use table)
one_liner: Computer-vision library whose cv::resize upscaling and cv::GaussianBlur ran 3-17x faster than ImageMagick 6.9, single-threaded.

name: riscv-sbt (OpenISA RISC-V static binary translator)
baseline: QEMU (user-mode RISC-V dynamic binary translation) and rv8
one_liner: Research static RV32-to-x86/ARM binary translator built on LLVM; translated MiBench runs near native, far ahead of QEMU and rv8.

name: CTranslate2
baseline: PyTorch 1.13.1 (OpenNMT-py, Hugging Face Transformers), TensorFlow 2.11.0 (OpenNMT-tf), Marian 1.11.0, FasterTransformer 5.3 (GPU)
one_liner: C++ inference runtime for converted Transformer models; about 2.4-3.6x the CPU throughput of PyTorch-based translation.

name: PowPow
baseline: Drogon 1.9.13 (C++, trantor event loop; the-benchmarker cpp/drogon, cmake release build); also agoo-c 0.7 (C) in the same table
one_liner: Nim event-loop library with a built-in HTTP/1.1 server that out-served Drogon by 1.34-1.39x in one the-benchmarker snapshot.

name: lua-resty-core (LuaJIT FFI API for ngx_lua) vs the ngx_lua built-in Lua C API
baseline: the Lua C API implementation of the ngx.* and ngx.shared.* functions in lua-nginx-module (ngx_lua, C)
one_liner: LuaJIT-FFI reimplementation of ngx_lua's ngx.* API that lets calling Lua code stay JIT-compiled; claimed faster than the Lua C API, never measured.

name: libpostal
baseline: Deepparse (GRAAL-Research neural address parser; fastText, fastText-light, BPEmb and attention variants, GPU and CPU)
one_liner: C library that parses and normalizes street addresses worldwide with a CRF; about 10-65x faster per address than Deepparse's neural parser.

name: OpenVINO (CPU inference runtime)
baseline: TensorFlow Lite with the XNNPACK delegate (XNNPACK)
one_liner: Intel's open-source inference runtime; on x86 CPUs it ran ResNet-50 about 2x faster than TFLite+XNNPACK, but did not win on MobileNet V2.

name: OpenVVC
baseline: VTM reference decoder and Fraunhofer VVdeC
one_liner: INSA Rennes' lightweight C decoder for H.266/VVC; matches Fraunhofer VVdeC's speed in an independent study while using about half the memory.

name: Graal compiler (GraalVM JIT)
baseline: HotSpot C2 JIT (OpenJDK HotSpot VM, JDK 25)
one_liner: Java-written optimizing JIT that replaces HotSpot's C2; 16% lower time-per-op geomean than C2 on a third-party JMH compiler suite.

name: Graal.js (GraalJS)
baseline: Node.js (V8)
one_liner: Oracle's JavaScript and Node.js engine in Java on Truffle/Graal; beat Node.js 6 on 2016 peak benchmarks, loses to current V8.

name: GraalPy
baseline: CPython (first-party: CPython 3.12.8; independent suite: CPython 3.10.7); PyPy3 7.3.11 also in the independent suite, where GraalPy mostly loses
one_liner: Python 3.13 runtime on GraalVM Truffle; JIT-compiled pure Python runs many times faster than CPython, but mostly behind PyPy.

name: TruffleRuby
baseline: CRuby 4.0.6 (MRI interpreter), also CRuby with --jit (YJIT)
one_liner: Ruby 4.0 implementation on GraalVM/Truffle with a partial-evaluation JIT; peak-throughput wins over CRuby and YJIT on CPU-bound pure-Ruby code.

name: Discount
baseline: Markdown.pl
one_liner: C Markdown-to-HTML library and CLI implementing original Markdown.pl syntax; converts orders of magnitude faster than Markdown.pl.

name: simstr
baseline: std::string and std::string_view idioms: concatenation, std::to_string, std::format hex formatting, find, replace and split code written with the C++ standard library
one_liner: C++20 string types and expression-template concatenation that build strings with one allocation; 1.5-5x faster than naive std::string idioms.

name: LAMG+ (lean algebraic multigrid for graph Laplacians)
baseline: PETSc GAMG; the same study also runs hypre BoomerAMG, pyAMG, CMG and approximate Cholesky (Laplacians.jl approxchol_lap)
one_liner: Julia algebraic multigrid solver for graph-Laplacian systems; 6.6-13.6x faster than PETSc GAMG on social, web and optimization graphs.

name: crypto-js-wasm (@originjs/crypto-js-wasm)
language: WebAssembly (source language not confirmed; repo has a rust directory)
baseline: crypto-js (JavaScript)
one_liner: crypto-js API with the hash and cipher block functions ported to Rust/WebAssembly; big wins only for SHA-512/384 and SHA-3.

name: foldhash
baseline: SipHash-1-3 (Rust std::collections::HashMap's default hasher)
one_liner: Seeded folded-multiply Rust hasher for in-memory HashMaps; about 4.6x lower geometric-mean time per op than SipHash-1-3.

name: pdqsort
baseline: std::sort, std::stable_sort
one_liner: Header-only C++ drop-in std::sort replacement: pattern-defeating quicksort with branchless partitioning and a guaranteed O(n log n) worst case.

name: CUDA-L2
baseline: NVIDIA cuBLAS (also cuBLASLt heuristic, cuBLASLt AutoTuning, torch.matmul)
one_liner: 1,000 per-shape fp16 GEMM CUDA kernels found by LLM-guided reinforcement learning; on average 7-12% faster than autotuned cuBLASLt on A100/3090/H100 (offline mode).

name: ds2i (Partitioned Elias-Fano and OptPFor indexes)
baseline: OptPFD (OptPFor), Interpolative coding, Varint-G8IU, SIMD-BP128 era codecs
one_liner: Research C++ library of compressed posting-list encodings (partitioned Elias-Fano, OptPFD, Varint-G8IU, Interpolative, QMX) for inverted-index query experiments.

name: emphf
baseline: CMPH
one_liner: Hypergraph-peeling (MWHC) minimal perfect hash builder that constructs 5-63x faster than CMPH's CHD, using ~0.5 more bits/key.

name: Bun (Bun.serve)
license: MIT for Bun's own code, per LICENSE.md (GitHub reports NOASSERTION). Bun statically links JavaScriptCore/WebKit (LGPL-2) and tinycc (LGPL-2.1), plus permissive libraries such as BoringSSL, a uWebSockets fork and uSockets (Apache-2.0), mimalloc (MIT) and zstd (BSD OR GPL-2.0).
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Bun's built-in JavaScript HTTP server (Bun.serve); 2.0-2.2x Go net/http throughput on a 3-route hello-world API, 4 cores.

name: libcopp
baseline: Tencent libco
