one_liner: Cross-platform stackful coroutine library (with C++20 coroutine helpers) that switches up to about 1.65x faster than Tencent libco at 30,000 coroutines.

name: Oxlint (oxc-project/oxc)
baseline: ESLint
one_liner: Rust-based JavaScript/TypeScript linter and toolchain that replaces ESLint with 50-100x faster linting.

name: Clarabel.rs (Rust interior-point conic and QP solver) vs ECOS in qpbenchmark Maros-Meszaros
baseline: ECOS 2.0.14 (C interior-point conic solver, also homogeneous self-dual embedding based)
one_liner: Rust interior-point solver for LP, QP, SOCP, SDP and exponential/power-cone problems; roughly ties ECOS on speed, solves far more QPs.

name: oxipng
baseline: OptiPNG
one_liner: Multithreaded Rust lossless PNG/APNG optimizer; 2.2x (default) to 5x (-o4) faster than OptiPNG 0.7.7 wall-clock on one test image.

name: oxtra
baseline: QEMU 4.1.0 (x86-64 binary translation)
one_liner: Student-built x86-64 to RISC-V user-mode binary translator; up to 2.6x faster than QEMU 4.1.0 on tiny inputs, slower on larger ones.

name: uGO
baseline: Tengo, go-lua, GopherLua and goja (Go-embedded scripting engines); native Lua is faster than uGO in the same table
one_liner: Pure-Go bytecode scripting VM for embedding in Go programs; ran fib(35) about 10% faster than Tengo and 1.5x faster than go-lua.

name: QLIC (Quick Lossless Image Codec)
baseline: JPEG XL lossless via stock cjxl (-d 0 -e 9 --num_threads=0) and WebP lossless via stock cwebp (-lossless -exact -z 6), per benchmark/run-large-matrix.ps1; the page also lists JPEG XL efforts 1-8, WebP presets 1-9 and an OxiPNG level 6 row. No PNG or QOI decoder is a baseline
one_liner: Lossless image codec reaching JPEG XL effort-9 file sizes at about one-ninth of cjxl's single-thread encode time.

name: M*LIB (m-dict hash map, DICT_DEF2)
baseline: std::unordered_map (GNU libstdc++ STL; also std::vector, std::set, std::string in the same suite)
one_liner: Header-only C99/C11 generic container library whose DICT_DEF2 hash map ran 12.6x faster than libstdc++ std::unordered_map in its author's harness.

name: LRSTAR (DFA lexer generator)
baseline: flex
one_liner: A grammar-driven DFA-table lexer generator for C++, claiming 2x flex's throughput at similar table size.

name: KeplerAs and SGEMM assembly (PPoPP 2017 artifact)
license: No repository-wide licence. KeplerAs/LICENSE is MIT (Copyright 2014 Scott Gray, 2015~2016 Xiuxia Zhang); the SGEMM .sass kernels carry 'Copyright 2015~2017 Xiuxia Zhang ... All rights reserved' lines (commit 'Added licence information', 2017-05-24), and one kernel file carries an Apache-2.0 header.
language: SASS assembly kernels plus an assembler (implementation language not confirmed; README says KeplerAs is based on MaxAs)
baseline: NVIDIA cuBLAS 7.0 SGEMM (and cuDNN v4.0 for the convolution kernel), i.e. NVIDIA's library kernels built by NVIDIA's own toolchain
one_liner: Kepler (sm_35) SASS assembler plus hand-scheduled SGEMM kernels that beat cuBLAS 7.0 by up to 1.15x on a Tesla K20m.

name: couring
baseline: single-threaded blocking file reads
one_liner: Single-file C++20 teaching demo comparing blocking reads, a thread pool, raw io_uring and io_uring coroutines for loading OBJ files.

name: FlyCV
baseline: OpenCV (per-operator average speedup; operator list is in image charts, not text)
one_liner: ARM NEON-tuned C++ image library (colour conversion, resize, warps) with an OpenCV-like API; first-party phone demos beat OpenCV 1.16-2.19x.

name: Pallene
baseline: PUC-Rio Lua 5.4 interpreter (the Lua 5.4 bundled with Pallene in 2020); LuaJIT and C in the same post
one_liner: Typed Lua dialect compiled ahead of time to C Lua modules; about 12x faster than Lua 5.4 on an integer n-queens loop.

name: zmph (Zig Minimal Perfect Hash Map)
baseline: Zig std.StringHashMap and std.StaticStringMap
one_liner: Pure-Zig minimal perfect hash map for fixed string key sets; about 1.7x faster average lookups than std.StringHashMap.

name: gnet
baseline: Go standard library net package (runtime netpoller over epoll)
one_liner: Pure-Go epoll/kqueue multi-reactor TCP/UDP framework; 1.4-1.95x Go net's packet rate on streaming 1KB echo.

name: libfyaml
baseline: yaml-cpp
one_liner: Full-spec YAML 1.2/JSON parser and emitter in C, with 3.0-3.6x yaml-cpp's parse throughput in fkYAML's benchmark.

name: PAPAGENO (PArallel PArser GENeratOr)
baseline: GNU Bison + GNU Flex (sequential LALR(1) parser/lexer)
one_liner: Bison-style generator that emits pthreads-parallel operator-precedence parsers, up to 5.5x faster than Flex+Bison on ARM.

name: Parabix (bitstream UTF-16 validation kernel)
baseline: simdutf
one_liner: Bitstream-parallel text-processing framework whose LLVM-JIT'd SIMD kernel beat a simdutf CLI wrapper on UTF-16 validation.

name: revmc (revm AOT/JIT compiler)
baseline: revm interpreter
one_liner: LLVM-based JIT/AOT compiler that turns EVM bytecode into native code for revm; beats the revm interpreter, modestly on real blocks.

name: ParGeo (parallel 3D convex hull and kd-tree library)
baseline: CGAL (3D convex hull) and Qhull
one_liner: Multicore C++17 computational-geometry library (3D convex hull, kd-tree, spatial graphs) that outruns sequential CGAL and Qhull hulls through parallelism.

name: PolkaVM
baseline: Wasmtime (cranelift); the same table also lists Wasmtime winch, Wasmer singlepass, Wasm3, Wasmi, wazero, CKB VM and Solana RBPF
one_liner: Sandboxed RISC-V (RV32EM/RV64EM) VM with a single-pass x86-64 recompiler: compiles 170-470x faster than Wasmtime Cranelift, executes near Wasmtime speed.

name: colfer
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Schema-compiled binary format with generated C11, Go, Java and JavaScript code; beats protobuf-go and protobuf C++ 2-3x on small records.

name: OpenEquivariance
language: Python/C++ (JIT-generated CUDA, HIP and SYCL kernels)
baseline: e3nn (torch.compile max-autotune with CUDA graphs in the harness); also compared with NVIDIA cuEquivariance and FlashTP
one_liner: JIT GPU kernel generator for e3nn-style Clebsch-Gordan tensor products and fused graph convolutions; claims up to 10x over e3nn.

name: ParAMD (parallel approximate minimum degree ordering)
baseline: SuiteSparse AMD (single-threaded approximate minimum degree fill-reducing ordering)
one_liner: OpenMP parallel approximate minimum degree ordering, 2.9-8.5x faster than sequential SuiteSparse AMD on 64 cores.

name: pasta::bit_vector
baseline: cs-poppy (Zhou, Andersen & Kaminsky, SEA'13 compact rank/select bit-vector structure)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 rank/select bit vector: 8% faster rank, 16.5% faster select than cs-poppy.

name: ayafileio
baseline: aiofiles (thread-pool async file I/O)
one_liner: Python async file I/O with a C++ native core on io_uring, IOCP and Dispatch I/O; beats thread-pool aiofiles on small cached reads.

name: Ultra-Sort (SIMD sorting DSL for AVX2 and AVX-512)
baseline: std::sort (also std::stable_sort, ips4o::sort, pdqsort)
one_liner: 2018 course-project AVX-512/AVX2 bitonic merge sort for power-of-two numeric arrays; 7.7x std::sort on 1M 32-bit ints in its own report.

name: rust-dominator
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust/Wasm DOM library driven by futures-signals, no virtual DOM; about 1.47x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark.

name: LeMac (pauldreik C++20 port)
baseline: SHA-1 (OpenSSL EVP)
one_liner: C++20 library and lemacsum CLI for LeMac, an AES-round MAC measured at ~27x OpenSSL SHA-1 bulk throughput on Zen 4.

name: awasm-noble
baseline: @noble/hashes (pure-JavaScript hashes), measured for BLAKE3
one_liner: WASM-SIMD (optionally multi-threaded) hashes and ciphers from Paul Miller; BLAKE3 about 8-19x single-threaded throughput of @noble/hashes in reported runs.

name: BitSerializer
baseline: nlohmann::json (nlohmann::json::to_msgpack / from_msgpack, DOM-based MsgPack path)
one_liner: C++17 multi-format struct serializer whose built-in MsgPack archive saves about 33x and loads about 22x faster than nlohmann::json's MsgPack path.

name: Falcon audio codec
baseline: libopus 1.6.1 (float and fixed point), opusfile 0.12, libvorbis 1.3.7, Tremor (decoders)
one_liner: New MIT-licensed MDCT audio codec in Rust, with a C API, whose decoder runs about 1.5x faster than libopus at equal file size.

name: PCRE2
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Mature C library for Perl-compatible regex matching; 4-12x faster than libstdc++'s std::regex on find-and-count benchmarks.

name: Symphonia
baseline: FFmpeg libavcodec native decoders (FLAC, ALAC, MP1, MP2, MP3, AAC-LC, Vorbis, ADPCM), single-threaded, built as the static 'ffbench' example from a pdeljanov/FFmpeg fork
one_liner: Pure, safe-Rust audio demuxing and decoding library; beats single-threaded libavcodec on FLAC, ALAC, MP1/MP2, high-bitrate MP3.

name: MatrixKV
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: RocksDB 5.18 fork that moves L0 into Optane persistent memory with fine-grained column compaction; 3.6x NVM-assisted RocksDB random-write throughput.

name: SGCL
baseline: malloc via std::unique_ptr / std::shared_ptr (macOS libmalloc nano zone); also Go and Java ZGC collectors
one_liner: Header-only C++20 concurrent garbage collector whose allocation path beats malloc-backed unique_ptr/shared_ptr for small objects on macOS.

name: zurand
baseline: dqrng (R package) and base R runif()/rnorm() (Mersenne Twister); randompack x256++simd (SIMD xoshiro256++) is the closest competitor
one_liner: Stateless key-based R RNG package with C core; xoshiro256++ fills ~2.3x dqrng, ~8x runif(), thread-count-independent output.

name: Pelikan / Segcache
baseline: Memcached
one_liner: Rust cache-server framework whose pelikan-segcache speaks memcached's text protocol over Segcache, a TTL-segmented store with 5-byte-per-item metadata.

name: go-toml v2
baseline: BurntSushi/toml (the most widely used Go TOML library)
one_liner: Pure-Go TOML 1.1 library with an encoding/json-style API; project benchmarks show 2.4-6.4x faster than BurntSushi/toml.

name: Fero
license: MIT (declared in the README's License section, 'MIT License © Pedram Emrouznejad', and in package.json as 'pemrouz.mit-license.org'; no LICENSE file, so GitHub reports no SPDX id)
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: Experimental Node.js library for sharded, replicated in-memory state services; claims sub-millisecond round-trip acks versus Kafka's quoted 2 ms.

name: TokuDB / PerconaFT Fractal Tree Index
license: GPL-2.0 and AGPL-3.0 per README (GitHub reports AGPL-3.0); locktree and omt portions also Apache-2.0; separate PATENTS file
baseline: MongoDB's default B-tree index (MMAPv1 storage engine)
one_liner: Fractal Tree (Bε-tree) transactional key-value library behind TokuDB/TokuMX; beat MongoDB 2.2's B-tree indexes on out-of-RAM inserts.

name: svgo.mbt (@rivus/svgo)
baseline: svgo 4.1.0 (JavaScript, Node 24)
one_liner: svgo's 34-plugin preset-default rewritten in MoonBit as a 188 KB wasm-gc module; 1.7-4.8x faster than svgo 4.1.0 in Node.

name: cperl
baseline: perl5 releases 5.6.2 to 5.30.0 on the same machine (PerlBench); the README names 'perl5' and 5.14
one_liner: Diverged Perl 5 fork with types, faster signatures and FNV1a hashing; about 6% faster than perl 5.30.0 on PerlBench.

name: Life (perlin-network)
baseline: wasmi (paritytech/wasmi, 2018 version) and wagon (go-interpreter/wagon)
one_liner: Pure-Go WebAssembly MVP interpreter with gas metering; 2018 runs beat the then-current wasmi and wagon by about 2x.

name: Perry
baseline: Node.js v25.8.0 (V8); Bun 1.3.12 and Java OpenJDK 21.0.7 (HotSpot) appear in the same table
one_liner: Ahead-of-time TypeScript-to-native compiler (SWC + LLVM); beats Node/V8 on some numeric and JSON micro-benchmarks, loses others.

name: ProtoCache
benchmark_url: https://github.com/PeterRK/protocache (README.md benchmark tables; code in test/benchmark)
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Zero-copy flat binary format for Protobuf schemas; reads messages in place ~20x faster than Protobuf parse-and-traverse.

name: W1Hash
baseline: wyhash
one_liner: A wyhash-derived 64-bit non-cryptographic hash, tuned to spend fewer cycles on 1-16 byte keys than wyhash v4.2.

name: libfixmath
baseline: software single-precision float arithmetic (add, sub, mul, div) as compiled by avr-gcc for ATmega128 (avr-libc/libgcc soft-float; toolchain version unstated)
one_liner: Q16.16 fixed-point math library in C for FPU-less targets; on 8-bit AVR, add/sub beat soft-float about 2x, mul/div lose.

name: csv-zero (Zig SIMD CSV field iterator)
baseline: zsv (C library, built from src/c/zsv with 'cc -O3 main.c -lzsv'; labelled 'zsc (c)' in the result CSV) and lazycsv (C++ header library, g++ -O3 -march=native); Rust simd-csv and csv also measured
one_liner: Zig zero-allocation SIMD CSV field iterator; counts fields 1.4-2.6x faster than zsv (C) and 1.1-2.9x faster than lazycsv (C++) in its author's harness.

name: libpg_query
baseline: sqlparser-rs (Rust SQL parser, sqlparser crate 0.52, MySQL dialect rows)
one_liner: PostgreSQL's own Bison parser as a standalone C library; raw parse about 5-7x faster than sqlparser-rs in a rival's harness.

name: @phi-ag/argon2
baseline: hash-wasm Argon2 and libsodium.js Argon2 (both WebAssembly builds)
one_liner: Argon2 password hashing as a 48 KB npm package with a WebAssembly SIMD build; 1.4-2.1x faster than hash-wasm and libsodium.js.

name: trees (balanced and left-balanced kd-trees)
baseline: nanoflann (parallel construction and querying)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 kd-trees (balanced and stackless left-balanced) for parallel kNN; builds faster than nanoflann, queries sometimes slower.

name: metal-flash-attention
baseline: Dao-AILab FlashAttention-2 (A100) and FlashAttention-3 (H100), compared by utilization percentage, not wall time
one_liner: Swift/Metal port of FlashAttention for Apple GPUs; claims higher ALU utilization than FlashAttention-2/3 on NVIDIA, not wall-clock wins.

name: libMetalFloat64 (philipturner/metal-float64; emulated FP64 on Apple GPUs)
baseline: Native hardware FP64 on the Apple Silicon CPU (NEON) in the README table, and OpenCL FP64 in the precision table; the listed baselines GMP and MPFR are not compared
one_liner: Archived plan for emulated FP64 on Apple GPUs in Metal; no arithmetic is implemented, only theoretical peaks versus CPU FP64.

name: cardigan
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native) in the HttpArena suite; h2o, mongoose (C) and Drogon (C++) rows in the same table
one_liner: Experimental Java 26 HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server on raw io_uring; out-runs nginx's custom C module on HttpArena's plaintext profiles.

name: QOA (Quite OK Audio)
baseline: Opus (libopus); also MP3 encoding
one_liner: Single-header C codec for fixed 3.2-bit/sample lossy audio; author's run encodes 12x and decodes 7x faster than ffmpeg Opus.

name: QOI (Quite OK Image format)
baseline: libpng
one_liner: Reference C header for the QOI lossless RGB/RGBA format: about 27x faster encode and 3.4x faster decode than libpng, with files about 17% larger.

name: Typr.js
baseline: opentype.js (the widely used JavaScript OpenType font parser, a recognisable incumbent in JavaScript); HarfBuzz and FreeType are not measured
one_liner: Small browser JavaScript font parser (TTF/OTF/TTC/WOFF) that claims 2x-5x faster parsing than opentype.js, largely by parsing less up front.

name: PHP JIT (php-src opcache JIT)
baseline: PHP 8.2.3 without JIT (also compared in the same suite against LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3 and PyPy3 7.3.11)
one_liner: PHP's built-in opcache JIT: 2-9.5x faster than the plain PHP 8.2 interpreter on numeric benchmarks-game kernels.

name: sefer-alloc (SeferAlloc, Rust allocator with large-segment cache)
baseline: mimalloc (C, via the Rust mimalloc 0.1 crate as GlobalAlloc) and the Windows System allocator
one_liner: Pure-Rust global allocator whose committed large-segment cache makes same-size 4-64 MiB alloc/free 12-33x cheaper than mimalloc.

name: phuslu/log
baseline: zap, zerolog, log/slog
one_liner: Zero-allocation structured JSON logger for Go, faster than zerolog, zap and log/slog in its own benchmarks.

name: SIMD_TriangleAABB (SIMD triangle-box overlap test)
baseline: Moeller's scalar triangle-box overlap code ('old code', and the 'new, faster code' variant) from Tomas Akenine-Moeller's page
one_liner: SSE version of Akenine-Moeller's triangle-vs-AABB SAT overlap test; about 2x on full tests, 20x with an added early exit.

name: pugz
baseline: GNU gunzip (gzip); libdeflate also compared in the paper
one_liner: Research prototype that decompresses one gzip stream of ASCII text on many threads; beats single-threaded GNU gunzip and libdeflate.

name: Xin26x
baseline: x265 (--preset fast, single thread, build dated 2020-12-25)
one_liner: Low-delay HEVC/VVC encoder framework in C; README shows 2.4-4.7x x265 fast fps single-threaded, HEVC core binary-only.

name: pikkr
baseline: serde_json
one_liner: Rust implementation of the Mison speculative JSON field extractor; pulls named fields 2-4x faster than serde_json in its benchmark.

name: sul::dynamic_bitset
baseline: std::vector<bool>
one_liner: Header-only C++17/20 dynamic bitset beating std::vector<bool> on word-level shift/count operations in third-party benchmarks.

name: as-proto
baseline: protobuf.js (reflect and static) and google-protobuf in Node.js/V8; also JSON string/buffer
one_liner: Protobuf codec generated as AssemblyScript classes inside WebAssembly; encodes about 2.2x faster than protobuf.js but decodes slower.

name: rproxy
baseline: nginx as a reverse proxy (version and config not stated); HAProxy 2.8.5 (vendored build) as a second row
one_liner: Rust io_uring HTTP/1.1 filtering reverse proxy; first-party 1.24x nginx-as-proxy throughput on a 2-byte keep-alive response.

name: PISA (Performant Indexes and Search for Academia)
baseline: Lucene 10.4.0 (also Lucene 10.4.0 with BP doc reordering, and Tantivy 0.26) in the independent search-benchmark-game; the original codec baseline (StreamVByte / SIMD-BP128 inside PISA) has no published numbers
one_liner: Research-grade in-memory C++ inverted-index search engine; trades blows with Lucene 10.4 on top-k ranked queries, loses on counting.

name: wepoll
baseline: Winsock select() as used by the JDK's legacy select-based Windows Selector (WindowsSelectorImpl); measured through the JDK NIO Selector, not wepoll against raw select()/WSAPoll in C
one_liner: Linux epoll API for Windows sockets on the AFD driver; flat 1.4 us select cost where select() grows linearly.

name: Pistache
baseline: C++ REST SDK (cpprestsdk) v2.10.15, also Restbed v4.6
one_liner: C++17 HTTP/1.1 REST server library; in a 2020 shootout it beat C++ REST SDK by 3.2x and Restbed by 1.26x on small POSTs.

name: Zef
baseline: QuickJS-ng 0.14.0 (release binary qjs-linux-x86_64), Lua 5.4.7 (built with GCC 11.4.0), CPython 3.10 (Ubuntu 22.04 package)
one_liner: Toy AST-walking interpreter tuned with inline caches; its leaky Yolo-C++ build beats CPython 3.10 and QuickJS-ng on four benchmarks.

name: libcbor
baseline: tinycbor (Intel TinyCBOR 0.6.0)
one_liner: Full RFC 8949 CBOR library in C99; its low-level encoder writes CBOR 1.2x to 1.6x faster than Intel tinycbor in one third-party C shootout.

name: bare-metal (hand-optimized SASS/CUDA ML kernels for RTX 3070 Ti Laptop)
baseline: cuBLAS (local reference harness; cuDNN and cuSPARSELt rows also measured and lost)
one_liner: Hand-tuned sm_86 CUDA/SASS ML kernels; FP16 HGEMM roughly ties cuBLAS on one laptop GPU, other kernels trail vendor libraries.

name: fclones
baseline: jdupes / fdupes / rdfind (duplicate finders built on POSIX read)
one_liner: Parallel, device-aware Rust duplicate file finder; 4-10x shorter wall time than jdupes, fdupes and rdfind on a 316 GB SSD scan.

name: prng-test-bench (aes_ctr_128 and clmulrand PRNG headers)
baseline: std::mt19937 (also std::mt19937_64, pcg64, xoshiro256**, wyrand in the same table)
one_liner: Header PRNGs from an x86 test bench: 3-round AES counter and carry-less-multiply generators, about 4x std::mt19937 per call.

name: randp (AES-CTR Random Pool)
baseline: glibc arc4random / arc4random_buf / arc4random_uniform (glibc 2.36+ getrandom-based); also getentropy, RDRAND, RDSEED
one_liner: Linux C library with arc4random-style API backed by a thread-local 3-round-AES pool; 2-21x faster than glibc arc4random.

name: vtprotobuf (protoc-gen-go-vtproto)
baseline: protoc
one_liner: protoc plugin generating reflection-free Marshal/Unmarshal/Size/Equal/Clone helpers for Go protobuf APIv2; ~1.7x faster unmarshal than stock protoc-gen-go.

name: Coz causal profiler
baseline: gprof
one_liner: Causal profiler for C/C++/Rust that predicts the whole-program effect of speeding up each line; far lower overhead than gprof.

name: DoubleTake
baseline: Valgrind Memcheck and AddressSanitizer
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD heap-error checker (overflow, use-after-free, leaks) using checkpoint/replay; few-percent overhead versus ASan's 30%+ and Valgrind's ~17x.

name: Mesh
baseline: jemalloc (Firefox, Redis) and glibc malloc (SPEC CPU2006, Ruby)
one_liner: Drop-in malloc that compacts fragmented C/C++ heaps by page remapping; 16% less memory than Firefox's jemalloc, 39% on Redis.

name: grpc_homa (Homa transport plugin for gRPC)
baseline: gRPC (default TCP transport)
one_liner: gRPC C++ transport plugin that replaces HTTP/2-over-TCP with the Homa kernel RPC protocol; reports ~40% lower short-RPC round-trip time.

name: Homa (HomaModule) — Linux kernel implementation of the Homa RPC transport protocol
license: BSD-2-Clause OR GPL-2.0+ (per-file SPDX headers on the module and benchmark sources; a few test/tool files are BSD-1-Clause or GPL-2.0; no top-level LICENSE file)
baseline: TCP (and DCTCP)
one_liner: Linux kernel module for Homa, a message-based datacenter RPC transport with far lower short-message tail latency than TCP.

name: NanoLog (PlatformLab)
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Binary, printf-style C++ logger from Stanford PlatformLab with about 7-14 ns call-site latency, 20-40x below spdlog.

name: RAMCloud
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Distributed, durable in-DRAM key-value store with kernel-bypass RPC; beats Redis 2.6 on read-heavy YCSB, not on writes.

name: jsoniter-scala
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: Scala macro-generated JSON codecs; decoding straight into case classes edged out RapidJSON's DOM (0.147 vs 0.154 s) in kostya/benchmarks.

name: zspell
baseline: Hunspell and Nuspell (C++) through the-mikedavis/ffi-dictionaries
one_liner: Pure-Rust Hunspell-format spellchecker that pre-expands affixes for near-constant 47-63 ns word checks, about 4-27x faster than Hunspell on en_US.

name: blip_mp
baseline: GMP 6.3.0 (mpz_t; built with assembly and with --disable-assembly)
one_liner: Pure-Zig arbitrary-precision integers stored as variable-length BLIP bytes; beats GMP mpz on Apple M4 at i64-sized and 128-8192-bit add/sub/mul.

name: bzip2z (Zig bzip2 with SA-IS block sorting)
baseline: system bzip2 1.0.8 (C); pbzip2 1.1.13 reported as a third column
one_liner: Clean-room Zig bzip2 with SA-IS block sorting; compresses 1.7-1.8x faster than bzip2 1.0.8 on a synthetic periodic input, decompresses slower.

name: fastapprox
baseline: libm expf/logf/powf (single-precision libm; the repo's tests use them as the accuracy reference, libm is never timed)
one_liner: Header-only C/C++ single-precision approximations of exp, log, pow, sigmoid, trig, erf, lgamma and Lambert W, with SSE2 variants; no measured speedup over libm.

name: Sophia
baseline: LevelDB 1.17 (HyperLevelDB also in the gist)
one_liner: Abandoned C MVCC key-value engine (append-only, RAM-disk hybrid); self-reported 2.6x LevelDB random reads in 2013, never reproduced.

name: PngEncoder (Java)
baseline: javax.imageio PNG writer (ImageIO, JDK built-in encoder)
one_liner: Pure-Java PNG encoder that beats javax.imageio's PNG writer by compressing image segments in parallel on a thread pool.

name: pocketpy
baseline: CPython 3.8.10
one_liner: Embeddable Python-subset interpreter in C11 for game scripting; about 1.2x CPython 3.8 on one old benchmark, slower than Lua.

name: Polars
baseline: pandas (CSV write path; independent benchmarks separately report CSV read speedups)
one_liner: Rust DataFrame engine with lazy query optimization and SIMD execution; ~45x faster CSV writing than pandas.

name: trueform
baseline: CGAL (EPICK kernel; also libigl, MeshLib, VTK, nanoflann, Coal/FCL)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 mesh-processing library (booleans, intersection curves, spatial trees, remeshing) that the vendor measures 2-233x faster than CGAL, libigl, MeshLib and nanoflann.

name: ISpMV
license: MIT (interfaces, examples, benchmarks) plus proprietary ISpMV Binary License for compiled core
baseline: cuSPARSE SpMV (CUDA 13 / cuSPARSE 12.8.6.72)
one_liner: Closed-binary GPU SpMV SDK with per-matrix plans; 1.3-2.2x faster than cuSPARSE SpMV on H100 (fp64).

name: poor-circle/radix_sort
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Header-only C++20 LSD byte-radix sort for ints/floats/pointers/pairs/structs; drop-in call syntax beats std::sort.

name: FN-DSA (Rust, Falcon-based post-quantum signatures)
baseline: OpenSSL RSA-2048 signing
one_liner: Pure-Rust, no_std FN-DSA (Falcon) post-quantum signatures whose author reports faster signing and keygen than OpenSSL RSA-2048.

name: PostgreSQL
baseline: MySQL 8.0 (InnoDB, sysbench; MySQL figures are Oracle's published 'extreme config' sysbench numbers as tabulated in the pgtpc repo)
one_liner: Client-server SQL RDBMS; one advocate's durability-off sysbench run beats MySQL 8.0's published point-select peak, not read-write.

name: Turbo-Base64
baseline: base64 (RFC 4648 encode/decode)
one_liner: GPL-3 C base64 codec with SSSE3/AVX2/AVX-512 VBMI/Neon kernels; author's tables beat Chrome's codec 7-11x, aklomp 11-70%.

name: Turbo-Histogram (TurboHist)
baseline: Naive single-table byte histogram loop (hist_1_8), plus Ryg's histogram variants and Countbench; the histogram is the counting stage of Huffman, FSE and rANS encoders
one_liner: Scalar C byte-histogram routines for entropy-coder front ends; 1.5x the naive loop on text, up to 22x on runs.

name: TurboRC (Turbo Range Coder)
baseline: Other range/arithmetic and adaptive ANS coders (unnamed in the README; listed only on an external benchmark page); BWT section compares head-to-head with bzip2, bsc and bzip3
one_liner: GPL C library of adaptive range coders, adaptive-CDF rANS and a BWT compressor that beats bzip2 on ratio everywhere and on speed on some files.

name: TurboPFor Integer Compression
baseline: Simple-8b, FastPFor (FP_VByte/FP_SimdFastPFor), varint-style VByte
one_liner: GPL C library of SIMD bit packing, PFor, variable-byte and Elias-Fano integer codecs; README tables beat Simple-8b, FastPFor and VByte.

name: TurboRLE (TRLE and SRLE)
baseline: rle8 (rainerzufalldererste/rle8 as of 2019, an SSE/AVX2 8-bit run length encoder, one configuration 'rle8 1'; that repository has since become hypersonic-rle-kit) and Mespotine RLE (MRLE); memcpy shown as a reference row. None of the general-lossless category baselines (zlib, zstd, lz4, brotli, xz) appear in the README tables.
one_liner: Block run-length encoder (TRLE, plus escape-based SRLE for 8/16/32/64-bit runs) that out-compresses and out-runs rle8 and Mespotine RLE.

name: mlkem-native (pq-code-package)
baseline: mlkem-native's own portable C backend (CI 'no-opt' rows, native backends disabled); that C code is a C90 fork of the pq-crystals/kyber ref implementation and is what liboqs ships as its portable C ML-KEM since 0.13.0
one_liner: Formally verified C90 ML-KEM (FIPS 203) with AArch64 Neon and x86-64 AVX2 assembly, about 2-3x faster than its portable C.

name: ffjson
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Go code generator that emits static per-struct MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON methods to replace encoding/json's reflection-based codec.

name: Protocol Puffers (protopuf)
baseline: Google protobuf C++ (libprotobuf with protoc-generated classes; version not stated)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 protobuf-wire-compatible codec with messages as template types; encodes a tiny message 2-4x faster than libprotobuf.

name: stealpool
baseline: self-written central-queue thread pool (std::deque behind a mutex), serial code, and std::sort (not TBB/OpenMP/Rayon)
one_liner: Small C++17 work-stealing fork-join scheduler (Chase-Lev deques, eventcount parking). It beats a mutex-queue pool on fine-grained tasks.

name: fast.cu (H100 BF16 matmul and sum-reduction kernels)
baseline: cuBLAS (cublasGemmEx, BF16 inputs, FP32 compute, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT) for matmul; CUB for sum reduction
one_liner: From-scratch Hopper BF16 GEMM (TMA + WGMMA) beating cuBLAS by 2-7% on square H100 matmuls, plus a CUB-level reduction.

name: PIQP
baseline: OSQP
one_liner: Header-only C++14/Eigen proximal interior-point convex QP solver; fastest and most robust on Maros-Meszaros, well ahead of OSQP.

name: picoquic
baseline: quiche
one_liner: Minimal C QUIC/HTTP3 research stack; beats quiche by ~6-7% on bulk upload and connection setup in one loopback harness.

name: ArenaAllocator (privateMwb)
baseline: std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource (stdArena in benchmarks/*/support/reference.h)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 fixed-capacity bump arena with frame rollback; about 1.2-1.8x faster per allocate() than std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource.

name: FluxIO
baseline: Boost.Asio C++20 file I/O and Go os.O_DIRECT with goroutines (not POSIX pread/pwrite)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 io_uring (SQPOLL, fixed files and buffers) O_DIRECT block I/O engine; out-runs Boost.Asio file I/O and Go on 4 KiB writes.

name: ThreadPool (progschj)
baseline: std::async(std::launch::async), one thread per task (labelled 'C++ thread' in the benchmark)
one_liner: Single-header C++11 fixed-size thread pool returning futures; not shown to beat std::async thread-per-task overall.

name: Ne10 (NEON FFT)
baseline: FFmpeg libavcodec FFT (assembly); also tricl_fft and CkFft
one_liner: ARM's NEON-optimized C library whose FFTs (float, Q31, Q15) beat FFmpeg's assembly FFT on an Android phone.

name: zix
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG); same suite rows for libreactorng (C, io_uring), libioma (C), h2o (C), mongoose (C), agensio (C++), Drogon (C++) and userver (C++)
one_liner: Pure-Zig network library with io_uring HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 engines; beats nginx, h2o and Drogon in HttpArena.

name: protobuf-c
baseline: nanopb
one_liner: Wire-compatible Protocol Buffers runtime and protoc plugin for C; about 5x nanopb's encode+decode throughput on host CPUs.

name: utf8_range (SIMD Range-based UTF-8 validator)
baseline: Lemire's SIMD UTF-8 validator (github.com/lemire/fastvalidate-utf-8, the algorithmic ancestor incorporated into simdutf)
one_liner: SIMD range-based UTF-8 validator bundled in protobuf; edges out Lemire's SSE/NEON validator, mostly on ARM.

name: protostuff
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Java serializer using a protobuf-style tagged binary format; serializes about 1.4x faster than protobuf-java but deserializes slower.

name: mr_blackwell (native Miller-Rabin GPU kernel)
baseline: GMP (CPU Miller-Rabin probable-prime test with GMP modular exponentiation)
one_liner: CUDA base-2 Miller-Rabin kernel with PTX-carry Montgomery multiplication; replaces CGBN in prime-gap and runs about 9x faster than the CPU/GMP pipeline.

name: lz4_flex
baseline: lz4 (C reference 1.9.3, via the lzzzz Rust binding)
one_liner: Pure-Rust LZ4 block and frame codec that matches or slightly beats the C reference lz4 when built with its unsafe paths.

name: Psi4
baseline: GAMESS-US 2020
one_liner: Open-source C++/Python quantum chemistry suite; in one 2020 community benchmark its non-DF B3LYP run edged out GAMESS-US.

name: Indexicon R-tree
baseline: Boost.Geometry R-tree (boost::geometry::index::rtree)
one_liner: Single-header C++17 dynamic N-D R*-tree for points or boxes; matches or beats Boost.Geometry's R-tree, by up to about 35%.

name: colortwist
baseline: Intel IPP ippiColorTwist (and a plain C reference loop)
one_liner: Small BSD-2 C++ library for 3x4 colour-matrix transforms on interleaved RGB24/RGB48; 2.6-4.9x faster than IPP's ColorTwist32f.

name: Box64 DynaRec
baseline: Box64 interpreter mode (no DynaRec)
one_liner: User-mode x86-64 Linux emulator for Arm64, RISC-V and LoongArch hosts whose dynamic recompiler beats its own interpreter 5-10x.

name: Box86 (x86 userspace emulator for ARM with dynarec)
baseline: QEMU user-mode (x86 guest) and FEX; also Box86's own interpreter
one_liner: 32-bit x86 Linux userspace emulator for armhf with a dynarec; author's 2022 7-Zip test: about 4.5x QEMU, 2.6x FEX.

name: CVR (Compressed Vectorization-oriented sparse Row)
baseline: Intel MKL CSR SpMV; also MKL CSR(I) inspector-executor, ESB, VHCC and CSR5
one_liner: CGO 2018 AVX-512 SpMV format for Xeon Phi Knights Landing that beats MKL CSR SpMV, especially on scale-free graphs.

name: Puma http11_parser (Mongrel/Ragel-based HTTP/1.x parser)
baseline: http-parser
one_liner: Mongrel's Ragel-generated C request/header tokenizer, vendored in Puma; ~1.26x faster than joyent http_parser in a 2016 test.

name: mpedb
license: LicenseRef-mpedb-1.0 (custom source-available license: free except a one-time USD 0.07/device fee for organizations over $5B revenue/valuation)
baseline: SQLite
one_liner: Rust embedded SQL database (mmap'd copy-on-write B+tree, MVCC, sqlite3 C-API shim) that beats SQLite on in-process point operations.

name: blazingio
baseline: iostream (std::cin/std::cout, with sync_with_stdio(false))
one_liner: Header-only mmap+SIMD std::cin/cout replacement, ~5x faster than libstdc++ iostream for competitive-programming I/O.

name: Pyccel
language: Python (transpiler that emits Fortran or C)
baseline: CPython 3.12 for the dev-branch table (the workflow installs it with actions/setup-python python-version '3.12'); separate tables for pyccel 2.2.3 from PyPI under CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14
one_liner: Ahead-of-time transpiler from type-annotated Python to C or Fortran extension modules; 5x-2000x faster than CPython on scalar-loop numeric kernels.

name: jiter
baseline: serde_json
one_liner: Rust JSON parser from Pydantic: borrowed-string DOM, pull iterator and Python parser; ~2x serde_json::Value DOM throughput.

name: Monty (pydantic/monty)
baseline: CPython-based sandboxes (WASI/wasmtime with precompiled CPython 3.14.7, local Docker python:3.14-alpine, Pyodide in Deno via mcp-run-python, a Daytona sandboxing service) and starlark-rust; the same page also times plain unsandboxed CPython (in-process eval/exec and a python -c subprocess). No CPython execution-throughput claim in the repo docs.
one_liner: Rust Python-subset sandbox for LLM-written code; sub-millisecond sandbox checkout versus 16 ms to 2.7 s for WASI, Docker, Pyodide and hosted sandboxes.

name: Pyodide (NumPy inv in WebAssembly vs math.js)
baseline: math.js (JavaScript) in Chrome and Safari
one_liner: CPython plus NumPy and SciPy compiled to WebAssembly; one informal test inverted a 200x200 matrix about 20x faster than math.js.

name: re2jit
baseline: RE2
one_liner: JIT-compiles RE2's NFA to x86-64 machine code; beats RE2 on capture groups and Unicode classes.

name: PyPy
baseline: CPython 3.14.6 (kostya/benchmarks); CPython 3.11.7 (plb2)
one_liner: Alternative Python interpreter with a meta-tracing JIT; runs pure-Python CPU-bound code 1.5-42x faster than CPython.

name: TgCrypto (pyrogram/tgcrypto)
baseline: OpenSSL AES-256-IGE / AES-256-CBC (no comparison found)
one_liner: Archived C extension for Python giving Pyrogram AES-256-IGE/CTR/CBC; replaces pure-Python pyaes, does not beat OpenSSL.

name: Pyston
license: Python-2.0 (CPython license stack: PSF License Version 2 with BeOpen, CNRI and CWI agreements; root LICENSE is CPython's)
baseline: CPython 3.8
one_liner: CPython 3.8 fork plus pip-installable JIT module (DynASM baseline JIT, quickening, inline caches); about 10-30% faster than stock CPython 3.8.

name: Pillow
baseline: ImageMagick 6.9.7-4 (via Wand)
one_liner: Python's standard imaging library (C core): 3-4x faster resizing and 10-30x faster grayscale/3D-LUT than single-threaded ImageMagick 6.9.

name: CPython tail-calling interpreter
baseline: CPython computed-goto interpreter loop (same source, default dispatch)
one_liner: Opt-in CPython 3.14+ interpreter loop in which opcodes tail-call each other; 3-5% faster than computed-goto (Clang 19), 15-20% faster than switch dispatch (MSVC).

name: CPython copy-and-patch JIT
baseline: CPython standard interpreter (tail-calling interpreter on AArch64 macOS), built with all optimizations
one_liner: CPython's built-in experimental copy-and-patch trace JIT; 7.5% (x86-64 Linux) to 11% (macOS arm64) geomean over the plain interpreter.

name: mypyc
baseline: CPython 3.10.7
one_liner: mypyc: compiles type-annotated Python modules to CPython C extensions; about 1.5x geomean on unannotated code, 2.4-22x on tuned code.

name: trigrep
baseline: ripgrep
one_liner: Rust CLI that pre-builds a disk-backed trigram index of a repo, then searches only candidate files, beating ripgrep in a first-party benchmark.

name: FBGEMM
baseline: Intel MKL FP32 GEMM (via a cited Microsoft paper), caffe2/perfkernels (embedding SpMDM), a prior 64-bit GEMM implementation
one_liner: Meta's x86 low-precision GEMM, convolution and embedding kernel library behind PyTorch quantized CPU ops; INT8 reported 2x MKL FP32 at batch 1.

name: PyTorch
baseline: TensorFlow
one_liner: PyTorch: eager-mode C++/CUDA tensor and autograd framework; old community benchmarks show faster CNN forward+backward than TensorFlow 1.x.

name: Qbix Server (PHP webserver)
baseline: php-fpm
one_liner: Pure-PHP HTTP/WebSocket server that forks copy-on-write workers after preloading the app, aimed at php-fpm's worker-count limit on I/O-bound PHP.

name: frg (fastripgrep)
baseline: ripgrep
one_liner: Rust CLI that indexes a codebase with sparse n-grams to search faster than ripgrep on every tested pattern.

name: cinatra
baseline: nginx
one_liner: Header-only C++20 coroutine HTTP/1.1 server and client library. On the project's own plaintext test it beats nginx by about 3%.

name: iguana (struct_pb)
baseline: Google protobuf C++ (SerializeToString / ParseFromString)
one_liner: Header-only C++17/20 reflection serializer whose struct_pb mode writes protobuf proto3 wire format from plain structs; claims 2.4x/3.4x over protobuf.

name: rest_rpc
baseline: brpc (Apache bRPC); gRPC only transitively, via brpc's own benchmark page
one_liner: Header-only C++20 coroutine RPC over raw TCP; its 2019 C++11 version beat brpc 1.2-1.9x on same-machine echo.

name: evpp
baseline: libevent 2.0.21 (libevent's own sample TCP ping-pong server and client)
one_liner: Qihoo 360's muduo-style C++11 TCP/UDP/HTTP library on top of libevent. In its own echo test it beats libevent 2.0's bufferevent sample by 1.1-2.4x.

name: mph (qlibs)
baseline: std::unordered_map (std::hash), std::map, boost::unordered_flat_map (Boost 1.85), frozen::unordered_map, gperf, if-else and switch-case chains
one_liner: C++20 compile-time perfect-hash lookup built on BMI2 pext; 2.4-10x lower latency than std::unordered_map on 5-100-key string sets.

name: Yao.jl (Julia quantum circuit simulator) in Roger-luo/quantum-benchmarks
baseline: Qulacs 0.1.9 (C++ library driven from Python through pybind11, one Python call per gate or circuit) and QuEST via pyquest-cffi 0.1.1 (C library driven from Python through cffi, one Python call per gate), single-thread full-amplitude state-vector simulation
one_liner: Julia quantum-circuit framework with state-vector simulation; its author's 2020 suite shows it beating QuEST through Python, not qulacs.

name: Quarkus (Vert.x/Netty, JDK 21)
baseline: nginx (C, hand-written handler module compiled -O3 -march=native, per HttpArena frameworks.json) in the HttpArena suite; h2o, Drogon, Mongoose, libreactorng and other C/C++ rows come from the same results directory
one_liner: Java framework (Jakarta REST on Vert.x/Netty) that beats nginx's HTTP/2-over-TLS path on HttpArena but loses every scored HTTP/1.1 profile.

name: QuestDB
baseline: ClickHouse
one_liner: Java/C++/Rust time-series database whose QWP protocol streams query results into Arrow 1.55x faster than ClickHouse's fastest client path.

name: Tantivy
baseline: Lucene
one_liner: Embeddable Rust full-text search library, architecturally close to Lucene, ahead on phrase/negated/count-heavy queries.

name: Whichlang (Rust language detection)
baseline: CLD2 (Google Compact Language Detector 2, C++), called through the deprecated cld2 1.0.2 crate (emk/rust-cld2), whose cld2-sys build.rs compiles the bundled CLD2 sources plus a thin C++ wrapper with the gcc crate and -std=c++03; the Rust side calls CLD2_ExtDetectLanguageSummary4 over FFI. Whatlang (Rust) and Lingua (Rust) are also compared.
one_liner: Dependency-free Rust language detector for 16 languages; about 5x faster than Google's CLD2 (C++) per sentence in Lingua's benchmark.

name: JSON3.jl (Julia) vs nlohmann/json, json-c and Boost.PropertyTree in kostya/benchmarks JSON
baseline: nlohmann/json (C++), json-c (C library called from a C++ driver) and Boost.PropertyTree (C++) as built by kostya/benchmarks; JSON3 does NOT beat RapidJSON (all variants), Boost.JSON, simdjson, yyjson, yajl, gason or DAW JSON Link in the same table
one_liner: Deprecated Julia JSON reader built on a lazy tape; beats nlohmann/json, json-c and Boost.PropertyTree in kostya/benchmarks, loses to every fast C/C++ parser.

name: PhastFT
baseline: FFTW 3.3.8 (via the Rust fftw crate); also RustFFT
one_liner: Safe-Rust, in-place, power-of-two FFT with low memory and optional threads; beats RustFFT at mid sizes and a scalar FFTW build.

name: FlashQLA
baseline: FLA Triton kernels (flash-linear-attention chunk_gated_delta_rule) and FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel
one_liner: TileLang-built fused CUDA kernels for Gated DeltaNet chunked prefill; about 2x faster forward and 2.5-3x faster backward than FLA Triton.

name: ragg
license: MIT; bundled AGG 2.4 sources under a BSD-style license (LICENSE.note)
baseline: Cairo (R grDevices png(type = 'cairo') anti-aliased raster device)
one_liner: R raster graphics devices (PNG/JPEG/TIFF/WebP) on AGG 2.4; about 1.3x faster than R's anti-aliased cairo png() on a composite ggplot2.

name: vroom
baseline: R base read.delim (utils)
one_liner: Lazy, ALTREP-backed delimited-file reader for R; indexes then reads on demand, beating base R's read.delim/readr/data.table.

name: ltalloc
baseline: operator new/delete (CRT/C runtime malloc)
one_liner: Single-file source drop-in overriding operator new/delete; thread-local free lists speed up many small (<256B) allocations vs CRT malloc.

name: RabbitMQ
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: Erlang multi-protocol broker; unbatched per-message delivery gave ~2.5x lower median latency than Kafka at 500 msg/s.

name: pqR (a pretty quick implementation of R)
baseline: GNU R (derived from R-2.15.0; the NEWS compares with R-3.4.0)
one_liner: Radford Neal's fork of GNU R 2.15 with a faster interpreter, GC and builtins; beats R-3.4/3.5 on many operations.

name: Adaptive Radix Tree (rafaelkallis/adaptive-radix-tree)
baseline: std::map (red-black tree, libstdc++) -- the closest stdlib ordered-index analog to the assignment's B-tree baseline
one_liner: Header-only C++11 adaptive radix tree for C-string keys; 1.5-2.4x faster than std::map<std::string> in author's microbenchmark.

name: wavelib
baseline: discrete-wavelets (npm pure-JavaScript 1D DWT package, ^5.0.15); PyWavelets under Pyodide also measured
one_liner: Plain C wavelet library (DWT, SWT, MODWT, packets, CWT); its WebAssembly build beats pure-JS discrete-wavelets by 82-154x on wavedec.

name: A*PA2 (astar-pairwise-aligner)
baseline: Edlib (C++) and BiWFA / WFA2-lib (C) exact global aligners
one_liner: Rust exact global DNA aligner using A*-guided band doubling over SIMD bit-parallel blocks; beats Edlib and BiWFA on long, similar sequences.

name: PtrHash
baseline: BBHash and CMPH (CHD) in the arXiv 2506.06536 survey; PTHash and PHOBIC (plus CMPH CHD) in the SEA 2025 paper arXiv 2502.15539
one_liner: Rust minimal perfect hash with 8-bit pilots (PTHash descendant); queries 2.7-3.8x faster than BBHash, ~7.6x faster than CMPH CHD.

name: QuadRank / BiRank
baseline: sux-rs Rank9 and RankSmall (Rust implementation of sux), qwt RSNarrow/RSWide/RSQVector, bitm RankSelect101111 and genedex rank structures; for the FM-index: genedex and AWRY
one_liner: Rust rank structures for bit vectors and 2-bit DNA, one cache miss per query; about 2x sux-rs Rank9 throughput with prefetching.

name: SimdQuickHeap
baseline: Rust std::collections::BinaryHeap
one_liner: SIMD-accelerated Rust priority queue, ~12x faster than std::collections::BinaryHeap on large monotone-key workloads; i32/u32/i64/u64 only.

name: Sassy (SIMD approximate string matching)
baseline: Edlib (C++ Myers bit-vector aligner); parasail (C) and SWOffinder also compared in the paper
one_liner: Rust SIMD library and CLI that finds all k-edit occurrences of short DNA/ASCII patterns in long texts, 4-15x faster than Edlib.

name: hypersonic-rANS
baseline: FSE (Finite State Entropy, tANS), FSE Huff0 (Huffman), htscodecs rANS (scalar/SSE/AVX2/AVX-512); also TurboANX (closed source)
one_liner: Research C++ rANS codecs with AVX2/AVX-512 decoders reaching about 3 GiB/s, about 3.1x FSE and 1.27x htscodecs.

name: LibTorrent (rakshasa)
baseline: official BitTorrent client (the original mainline client; not named more exactly in the claim)
one_liner: C++ BitTorrent engine behind rTorrent that writes mmap'ed file pages straight to sockets; old first-party claim of 3x the mainline client's seeding speed.

name: SPRAL SSIDS
language: Fortran (with C interface; GPU build via CUDA)
baseline: Not verified from an opened page. Per search snippets only: the ACM TOMS 2016 GPU paper compares against 'a state-of-the-art multifrontal solver on a multicore CPU' (not named in the snippet); the Duff-Hogg-Lopez a-posteriori-threshold-pivoting paper (RAL-TR-2016-017 / NLAFET Working Note 21) compares SSIDS v2 with HSL_MA86, HSL_MA97 and PARDISO on a multicore machine. MUMPS is not named in either snippet.
one_liner: BSD-licensed multicore/GPU sparse symmetric indefinite LDL^T solver (SSIDS); paper claims beat HSL and PARDISO, unverified here.

name: Botan
baseline: OpenSSL 3.6.0 (openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm)
one_liner: Broad BSD-licensed C++20 crypto toolkit; maintainer reports faster small-message AES-128-GCM than OpenSSL 3.6.0 on one Skylake.

name: libspng
baseline: libpng 1.6.37 (Debian Bullseye)
one_liner: Small C PNG decoder/encoder with a simpler API than libpng; decodes 1.02-1.07x faster on most images, 1.36x on 32bpp.

name: Superscalar Sample Queue (S3Q)
baseline: std::priority_queue
one_liner: Header-only C++17 cache-efficient priority queue beating std::priority_queue via batched, sample-sort-style bucket classification.

name: font-rs
baseline: FreeType 2.6.5 (glyph rasterization), per search snippets of the author's post; freetype-go is mentioned qualitatively in the README
one_liner: Small Rust TrueType glyph rasterizer (dense accumulation buffer plus prefix sum); 2016 author numbers claim 4-7.6x over FreeType 2.6.5.

name: RapidFuzz
baseline: FuzzyWuzzy (Python fuzzywuzzy package)
one_liner: Header-only C++ FuzzyWuzzy-style string similarity scorers on bit-parallel LCS/Levenshtein; its Python package runs 13-28x more pairs/s than FuzzyWuzzy.

name: cuDF (cudf.pandas)
baseline: pandas
one_liner: NVIDIA GPU DataFrame library; cudf.pandas runs unmodified pandas code on NVIDIA GPUs, 50-290x faster in vendor join/groupby benchmarks.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico SDK hand-coded RP2040 float and memory routines (pico_float, pico_mem_ops)
baseline: the compiler's soft-float library (libgcc) and C library memcpy/memset on the Cortex-M0+ cores of the RP2040
one_liner: Pico SDK's ROM-backed float, double and memcpy/memset replacements for RP2040, faster than libgcc soft-float and newlib libm on Cortex-M0+.

name: GPU_FFT (Raspberry Pi VideoCore IV, hello_fft in raspberrypi/userland)
language: C with VideoCore QPU assembly kernels
baseline: FFTW (FFTW_MEASURE) running on the Raspberry Pi 1 ARM CPU
one_liner: Andrew Holme's GPU_FFT: power-of-two complex FFTs on the Raspberry Pi VideoCore IV GPU, about 10x FFTW on the Pi 1 ARM.

name: eFFT (event-based FFT)
baseline: FFTW (fftw_plan_dft_2d, full N x N 2D FFT recomputed after every event or event packet)
one_liner: Header-only C++17/Eigen incremental 2D FFT for event cameras; updates an exact spectrum per event instead of rerunning FFTW.

name: hilbert_curves (rawrunprotected)
license: public domain (README statement, no LICENSE file)
baseline: classic iterative xy2d Hilbert index loop with per-level quadrant rotation (Wikipedia-style loop; measured as loop_rotation in the Rust port benchmark), not literally the Hacker's Delight code
one_liner: Branchless public-domain 2D/3D Hilbert index encode/decode; a Rust port encodes about 5.4x faster than the classic rotation loop.

name: wasmz
baseline: Wasmtime Pulley interpreter and WAMR fast interpreter
one_liner: Zig WebAssembly interpreter with a C API; roughly level with WAMR fast-interp and ahead of Wasmtime Pulley, behind wasm3.

name: Rayon
baseline: OpenMP parallel for (C++ with static and dynamic scheduling)
one_liner: Rust work-stealing data-parallelism crate (par_iter, join, scope); beats OpenMP only in fine-grained dynamic-schedule cells of a competitor's benchmark.

name: roxmltree
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Read-only, zero-copy Rust XML DOM parser; 2-3.5x faster than libxml2, no mutation or writing.

name: data.table (R)
benchmark_url: https://duckdblabs.github.io/db-benchmark/ (current DuckDB Labs continuation, report generated 2026-08-17; raw timings in https://github.com/duckdblabs/db-benchmark/blob/main/time.csv); original 2021 H2O run: https://h2oai.github.io/db-benchmark/
baseline: pandas
one_liner: R's in-memory data.frame replacement with C/OpenMP radix grouping and joins; ~3-4x faster than pandas on db-benchmark groupby.

name: zenjson
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: Single-header, in-situ C++ JSON DOM parser/serializer in the gason style; parses 1.8-3.6x faster than RapidJSON.

name: Cuik (C compiler with the TB backend)
baseline: clang 22.1.8 (LLVM) and gcc 16.2.1 / gcc-15 15.3.0, compile and build time at their default optimisation level
one_liner: MIT C11/C23 compiler and sea-of-nodes backend library (TB); about 2x clang -O0 and 12x gcc -O0 compile speed on a synthetic benchmark.

name: REAL (real-regex)
baseline: std::regex
one_liner: Header-only C++20 linear-time regex engine with lookaround support, beating std::regex 8x-152x and RE2 on every supported pattern.

name: Redpanda
license: BUSL-1.1 (core; converts to Apache-2.0 four years after each release) + Redpanda Community License (enterprise features); GitHub reports no SPDX id
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: Kafka-API-compatible streaming broker in C++ on Seastar; vendor OMB runs show 12-70x lower p99.99 latency than Kafka.

name: H264Sharp (native SIMD color converter)
baseline: OpenCV cv::cvtColor (RGB <-> YUV)
one_liner: AVX2/SSE4.1/NEON RGB<->I420 converters inside a .NET OpenH264 wrapper; about 2.4x OpenCV cvtColor single-threaded, 3x multithreaded.

name: remade_ffmpeg_rs
baseline: FFmpeg libavcodec native MP3 decoder and native AAC encoder; libvorbis
one_liner: Pure-Rust, Apache-2.0 FFmpeg rebuild whose MP3 decoder and frame-parallel AAC/Vorbis encoders beat FFmpeg's CLI on wall clock.

name: rusty-av1-toolkit
baseline: stock rav1e (AV1 encoder); decoder side is a fork of rav1d, itself a Rust port of dav1d
one_liner: rav1e fork whose default AV1 encode is byte-identical to stock rav1e and about 1.10x faster single-threaded; bundles a rav1d fork.

name: rusty-opus
baseline: libopus (C reference encoder); also FFmpeg's native Opus encoder
one_liner: Pure-Rust Opus codec (opus-rs performance fork) claiming 1.5-1.6x libopus single-core CELT encode speed; SILK 4% slower.

name: rusty_alloc
baseline: mimalloc v2.4.5 (also jemalloc, glibc malloc, dlmalloc on wasm32, esp-alloc on ESP32-S3)
one_liner: Pure-Rust rebuild of mimalloc's design; slightly fewer instructions than mimalloc, jemalloc and glibc malloc under callgrind.

name: rusty_flac
baseline: FFmpeg 8.1.2 native flac encoder and decoder (libavcodec)
one_liner: Pure-Rust FLAC encoder and decoder claiming 17% faster encode and 23% faster decode than FFmpeg 8.1.2's flac.

name: rusty_gif
baseline: FFmpeg 8.1.2 GIF encode via palettegen/paletteuse (dither=none, high-quality path) and FFmpeg's GIF decoder
one_liner: Safe-Rust fork of the image-rs gif crate whose census-routed k-means quantizer claims faster GIF encode than FFmpeg palettegen/paletteuse.

name: rusty_h265
baseline: FFmpeg 8.1.2 native hevc decoder (libavcodec, hand-written assembly)
one_liner: Pure-Rust, memory-safe HEVC decoder: about 5% faster than FFmpeg's hevc decoder on one stream, 1.1-1.67x slower on three.

name: rusty_jpeg
baseline: FFmpeg 8.1.2 native MJPEG encoder and decoder (not libjpeg-turbo)
one_liner: Pure-Rust JPEG/MJPEG decoder and encoder with AVX2/NEON kernels; by its own measurement at parity with FFmpeg's native MJPEG codec, not faster.

name: Kairos / rusty_rtos_kernel (FreeRTOS kernel remade in Rust)
baseline: FreeRTOS V11.3.1 kernel (C), unmodified, with its first-party GCC RISC-V port, built with clang -O2
one_liner: FreeRTOS V11.3.1 scheduler rewritten in safe no_std Rust; fewer instructions per rv32 tick and cooperative switch, less RAM per task, more flash.

name: rusty_xml (Remade-With-Rust)
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Pure safe-Rust rewrite of libxml2 (parse, DOM, SAX, XPath, DTD, C14N) whose CLI parses faster than xmllint as shipped.

name: bigfft
baseline: Go math/big (README also benchmarks GMP, which is faster)
one_liner: Pure-Go Schonhage-Strassen multiplication for math/big integers: 3-25x faster than math/big from 1 Mbit, 1.2-3x slower than GMP.

name: fph-table (Flash Perfect Hash)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only C++17 dynamic perfect-hash map/set with unordered_map-like API: lookups 1.2-7.6x faster than std::unordered_map, inserts far slower.

name: HyperLevelDB
baseline: LevelDB
one_liner: HyperDex's LevelDB 1.17 fork with parallel writers and cheaper compaction; about 3.4x faster bulk writes than LevelDB, but slower reads.

name: COROIO
baseline: libevent (epoll backend; libevent commit 4c993a0, its bench.c methodology)
one_liner: C++23 coroutine networking library with compile-time epoll/kqueue/IOCP/io_uring backends; lower dispatch latency than libevent at small descriptor counts.

name: Reindexer
baseline: SQLite 3.17.0 via mattn/go-sqlite3 and sqlx, opened with DSN '/tmp/foo.db?mode=memory&cache=shared' (no 'file:' prefix, so go-sqlite3 drops the query string and SQLite runs as an on-disk /tmp/foo.db with default settings, not in memory), with indexes on name and year and an FTS5 table; also compared with Redis, Tarantool, MySQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Sphinx, ArangoDB, RethinkDB and (web only) ClickHouse
one_liner: Embeddable in-memory document database (C++ core, Go API) with secondary and full-text indexes; first-party benchmarks show 3-6x SQLite on indexed reads.

name: opus-rs
baseline: libopus 1.6.1 (C reference encoder)
one_liner: Pure-Rust, no_std, zero-dependency port of libopus 1.6; first-party tables show parity on SILK and 5-28% gains on 48 kHz CELT encode.

name: rustrtc
baseline: webrtc-rs 0.17.1 (Rust) and pion/webrtc v3.3.6 (Go); no C or C++ stack (libwebrtc, libdatachannel, usrsctp) was compared
one_liner: Pure-Rust WebRTC/RTP/SRTP stack with its own ICE, DTLS and SCTP; first-party data-channel loopback runs 3.3x webrtc-rs and 3.2x pion.

name: svc-hook (ARM64 system call hook by binary rewriting)
baseline: ptrace-based system call interception (README headline, no numbers); ASC-Hook, another ARM64 binary-rewriting syscall hook (Documentation/README.md, with numbers)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD library that rewrites every ARM64 svc into a branch to a trampoline, hooking system calls in-process instead of via ptrace.

name: CvsAssemblyBenchmark
language: Assembly (GNU as, AVX2/FMA) with C harness
baseline: GCC 12.2.0 -O3 compiled C i-k-j dense matrix multiply (double precision)
one_liner: Toy benchmark: hand-written AVX2/FMA GNU-as i-k-j double matmul beating a GCC -O3 build restricted to SSE2.

name: cjson.cpp
baseline: nlohmann::json
one_liner: Header-only SIMD index/tape JSON parser for C++26 on the micron runtime, ~9-31x faster than nlohmann::json.

name: micron.cpp (cmemory memcpy/memset/memmove)
baseline: glibc memcpy / memset / memmove (system libc, called as ::memcpy in the harness; glibc version not stated)
one_liner: Header-only inline memcpy/memset/memmove from the freestanding micron libc/STL rewrite; 1.13-1.91x fewer cycles than glibc on SPEC2017-size random copies.

name: libcsv
baseline: Ruby's stdlib CSV parser (bench.rb does require 'csv' and labels it FasterCSV, which became Ruby's stdlib csv in 1.9); a pure-Ruby parser, not a C or C++ incumbent
one_liner: Small streaming ANSI-style C CSV reader/writer with callbacks; only speed evidence is a 2012 Ruby wrapper beating Ruby's csv.

name: AVR-AES-faster (rgrgrg)
language: AVR assembly (.S files) with C/C++ wrappers
baseline: AVRAES (point-at-infinity.org, rijndaelfast.asm), Osvik et al. 'Fast Software AES Encryption', AVR CryptoLib, AVR-Crypto-Lib, the tiny version of uclouvain lightweight cipher code, and any pure C/C++ implementation
one_liner: Constant-time AES-128/192/256 block functions in AVR assembly, about 2,100 cycles per AES-128 block on ATmega328P.

name: DirectLUSolvers (MultifrontalQR, SupernodalLDLT)
baseline: Eigen::SparseQR (MultifrontalQR); also Eigen::SimplicialLDLT and Eigen::SparseLU for the LDLT/LU solvers
one_liner: Header-only Eigen add-on: rank-revealing sparse QR far faster than Eigen::SparseQR, plus supernodal LDL^T beating SimplicialLDLT.

name: Ribbon Filter (ribbonGo)
baseline: Bloom filter, xor filter
one_liner: Pure-Go static Ribbon filter (Dillinger-Walzer 2021) storing 7.3-7.5 bits/key at 0.78% FPR, below textbook Bloom and Xor sizes.

name: bc7enc (rgbcx BC1 and bc7enc16 BC7 encoders)
baseline: libsquish (BC1 cluster fit); Intel ispc_texcomp (BC7); also AMD Compressonator and DirectXTex CPU BC7
one_liner: Scalar single-file BC1-5 (rgbcx.h) and modes-1/6 BC7 encoders; first-party tables beat ispc_texcomp, independent tests mostly do not.

name: fpng
baseline: libpng
one_liner: Single-file C++ PNG writer/reader for 24/32bpp: about 35x libpng's default encode speed, files about 29% larger.

name: LZHAM (lzham_codec)
license: Public domain (LICENSE dedication dated 2020-09-15; no SPDX id)
baseline: LZMA (lzma 26.03 as built in lzbench)
one_liner: Asymmetric LZ77 codec with near-LZMA ratio whose decoder runs about 3.5x faster than 7-Zip LZMA; compression is slow.

name: miniz
baseline: zlib
one_liner: Single-file MIT zlib/Deflate replacement with ZIP and PNG helpers; measured slower than zlib, chosen for portability, not speed.

name: sserangecoding (SSE 4.1 interleaved range coder)
baseline: Finite State Entropy (FSE) demo by Yann Collet (tANS) and its Huff0 mode; length-limited Huffman; Fabian Giesen's SSE 4.1 interleaved rANS (ryg_rans)
one_liner: SSE 4.1 16-stream interleaved 24-bit range decoder for order-0 bytes; on book1 it decodes about 1.6x faster than FSE tANS.

name: libzling
baseline: zlib (gzip)
one_liner: Small C++ ROLZ + Huffman compressor (Baidu, archived) that compresses about 3x faster than zlib -6 with a better ratio.

name: orz
baseline: xz -6, zstd -19/-15/-10, brotli -9/-8/-7, bzip2 -9, lzfse, gzip -6 (GNU gzip CLI)
one_liner: Rust ROLZ compressor: near-xz -6 ratio on enwik8 text with about 13x faster single-threaded encode; decode slower than zstd.

name: libdivide
baseline: hardware integer division (compiler-emitted DIV/IDIV with a runtime divisor)
one_liner: Header-only C/C++ library replacing division by a runtime-invariant integer with multiply-shift sequences; about 6.7x over hardware DIV.

name: CharConv.h (rigtorp)
baseline: iostreams (std::stringstream); std::to_string; std::stoi/atoi/strtol
one_liner: Header-only base-10 int32/int64 to/from-string conversion; beats stringstream, to_string, atoi/strtol, stoi.

name: rigtorp/HashMap
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only open-addressing hash map with backshift deletion, up to ~5x faster than std::unordered_map on delete-heavy workloads.

name: ringline
baseline: tokio (multi-thread work-stealing runtime, epoll/mio-based)
one_liner: Thread-per-core io_uring runtime for Rust servers: 4-71% faster than default tokio on TCP echo, -10% to +9% versus tuned tokio.

name: tuc (Rust cut replacement)
baseline: the system cut binary (C; GNU or BSD and version not stated), also awk, uutils cut, hck and choose in the same table
one_liner: Rust cut alternative with reordering, negative indices and multi-character or regex delimiters; about 5x faster than the system cut on comma-split field extraction.

name: risechain/pevm (parallel EVM on revm)
baseline: sequential revm (pevm's own execute_revm_sequential path)
one_liner: Block-STM parallel executor for whole EVM blocks on top of revm; about 2x sequential revm on mainnet blocks.

name: Rive Renderer (rive-runtime)
baseline: Skia (and Flutter Impeller, per the same post); Skia backend and configuration unstated
one_liner: Rive's C++ runtime and GPU vector renderer (Metal, Vulkan, D3D, GL); vendor claims 66x Skia on animated tiles.

name: rivet-h26x (rivet-h26x-codecs)
license: Open Encoding Attribution License v1.0 (source-available, royalty-free with commercial attribution; not OSI-approved; no SPDX id confirmed)
baseline: libavcodec (FFmpeg) native H.264 and H.265 decoders
one_liner: Pure-Rust H.264/H.265 decoders, conformance bit-exact; beats libavcodec only on all-thread WPP HEVC, at parity or behind elsewhere.

name: Adept-2
license: Apache-2.0 (library); GNU all-permissive license for test and benchmark code
baseline: CppAD (measured in the benchmark); autodiff (autodiff/autodiff, measured); ADOL-C and Sacado (named in the user guide, qualitative)
one_liner: Expression-template reverse/forward-mode C++ AD library with Fortran-like arrays; tapes faster than ADOL-C, CppAD and Ceres in third-party benchmarks.

name: Staccato
baseline: Intel TBB 4.3 and Intel Cilk Plus 7.3
one_liner: Header-only C++11 work-stealing scheduler storing task objects inside its deques; lower spawn overhead than TBB 4.3 and Cilk Plus.

name: rkyv
baseline: Cap'n Proto, FlatBuffers, Protocol Buffers (via prost/protobuf crates), MessagePack (via rmp-serde/msgpacker/zerompk)
one_liner: Rust zero-copy serialization crate; faster serialize and in-place reads than Rust FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto, prost and rmp-serde.

name: tinyfft (rluts/tinyfft)
baseline: fft.js (pure JavaScript, f64)
one_liner: no_std Rust radix-4 FFT shipped as 16 KB SIMD wasm; 1.2-1.4x fft.js complex-FFT throughput in Node.

name: picoflann
baseline: nanoflann (also OpenCV FLANN)
one_liner: Tiny single-header exact kd-tree (knn and radius search) claiming 1.25-4x over nanoflann; unlicensed, claim disputed.

name: CRoaring (Roaring Bitmaps)
baseline: std::unordered_set<uint32_t> and sorted std::vector<uint32_t> with STL set algorithms (std::set_intersection/union/difference, std::binary_search) from the standard library bundled with GCC 5.4; also an uncompressed bitset (the authors' portable C 'cbitset', same word-array layout as std::bitset/std::vector<bool>)
one_liner: Compressed bitmap for sparse 32/64-bit integer sets; set-algebra ops beat std::unordered_set/vector by 3x-800x, loses on dense data.

name: nanomp3
baseline: minimp3 (SIMD and scalar builds)
one_liner: Safe, no_std Rust port of minimp3 (MP3/MP2/MP1 decode), bit-exact, 6-21% faster than minimp3's SIMD build.

name: lsr
baseline: GNU ls 9.7 (readdir/stat syscalls); also eza, lsd, uutils, busybox
one_liner: Zig ls(1) clone that batches directory open, statx and passwd/group/localtime reads through io_uring; beats GNU ls -al.

name: SPARKNaCl
baseline: TweetNaCl (C), compiled into the same binary with the same GNAT compiler at the same -O level
one_liner: SPARK/Ada re-implementation of TweetNaCl with proven absence of run-time errors; the author reports Ed25519 Sign about 3x faster than TweetNaCl C on a RISC-V board.

name: prio_queue (rollbear)
baseline: std::priority_queue
one_liner: Header-only B-heap priority queue storing priority/payload in separate arrays; faster than std::priority_queue on cache-friendly workloads.

name: icy
baseline: std::map, std::unordered_map, std::set, std::unordered_set
one_liner: C++23 consteval perfect-hash map/set for fixed keys; ~1.6-1.8x faster string_view hits than std::unordered_map in the author's benchmark.

name: Fastor
baseline: Eigen 3.3.7 / Blaze 3.7 / MKL JIT 2021.01 / LIBXSMM (small fixed-size GEMM, single-threaded)
one_liner: Header-only C++ fixed-size tensor library whose small-GEMM kernels match MKL JIT and beat padded Blaze.

name: QWT (Rust quad wavelet tree)
baseline: SDSL 2.1.1 wavelet matrix/tree (also Pasta, sucds, simple-sds)
one_liner: Rust 4-ary wavelet matrix (rank/select/access over integer sequences), about 2x lower query latency than SDSL wavelet trees.

name: tcFFT
baseline: NVIDIA cuFFT (half precision)
one_liner: Research FP16 FFT kernels that run radix-16 butterflies on NVIDIA tensor cores; beats cuFFT half precision on V100/A100.

name: ser20
baseline: cereal, boost::serialization
one_liner: C++20 fork of cereal with a buffered binary archive: 1.3-2.1x faster than cereal, 1.1-2.8x than Boost, on small-field data.

name: al-dente (dent)
baseline: GNU find (readdir/fts directory traversal); also fd
one_liner: Small multithreaded C directory walker on raw getdents64 that prints every path; beats GNU find and fd on a synthetic tree.

name: rpclib
baseline: gRPC (also Apache Thrift and Cap'n Proto RPC in the same suite)
one_liner: Small C++11/14 msgpack-rpc client and server with no IDL; its author's 2017 benchmark has small calls 2.5x faster than gRPC 1.1.0.

name: NetJSON
baseline: Json.NET (Newtonsoft.Json)
one_liner: C# JSON serializer that emits per-type IL at runtime; ~3.4x faster serialization than Json.NET in a 2014 benchmark.

name: memlz
baseline: LZ4 (with acceleration around 32 to 64), Snappy, FastLZ, LZO
one_liner: Header-only C/C++ word-hash compressor that compresses about 4.8x faster than LZ4 --fast -17 at similar ratio; decompresses slower.

name: Trio / ArckFS
baseline: NOVA, PMFS, WineFS, Strata, SplitFS, ODINFS (kernel and user-space NVM file systems; ext4 DAX)
one_liner: SOSP '23 research userspace NVM file system (ArckFS) on Optane PM that outscales NOVA, WineFS, OdinFS and ext4-DAX at high core counts.

name: markdown-wasm
language: C (md4c) compiled to WebAssembly with a JavaScript API
baseline: markdown-it ^10.0.0 (commonmark preset, IDNA link encoding disabled), marked ^0.7.0, commonmark.js ^0.29.2 and showdown ^1.9.1 (JavaScript) in Node.js 14.11 / V8
one_liner: md4c CommonMark parser and HTML renderer compiled to 31 kB-gzipped WebAssembly; about 2.3-2.4x markdown-it throughput.

name: dnspython
baseline: c-ares
one_liner: Pure-Python DNS toolkit; gevent's wrapper for it beat gevent's c-ares resolver on the maintainer's macOS, but lost on Linux.

name: xrandom (rtmigo/xrandom_dart, Dart random number generators)
baseline: Dart core dart:math Random
one_liner: Pure-Dart PRNG classes (xorshift, xoshiro, splitmix64, mulberry32) implementing dart:math Random; Xrandom is 1.4-1.7x faster than Random on AOT.

name: YJIT (CRuby)
baseline: CRuby 4.1.0dev bytecode interpreter (same commit, JIT off); the report also shows CRuby 3.4.7 and YJIT 3.4.7
one_liner: CRuby's built-in Rust JIT; about 2x the CRuby interpreter on Rails-style apps after warmup on x86-64, 1.7x on Graviton4.

name: NanoSVG2 (RudjiGames fork)
baseline: The fork's own pre-PR master, not a category incumbent: a 2024-08-15 copy of memononen/nanosvg whose rasterizer matches upstream nanosvgrast.h apart from later upstream fixes (paint order, NaN clamping, dash stroke preparation). Skia, Cairo and Blend2D are not measured, and upstream nanosvg HEAD is not measured either.
one_liner: Copy of the two-header NanoSVG parser and rasterizer with SSE2 blending and span-delta coverage, 2.5-3.7x faster than its own previous rasterizer.

name: mold
baseline: lld
one_liner: Drop-in ELF linker beating LLVM lld and GNU ld via pervasive data-parallelism across the whole link pipeline.

name: Apex memmove (Trevor Herselman): SSE2 memcpy and memmove for x86 and x64
baseline: C library memcpy and memmove (the README names no baseline; the repo's source has no comparison)
one_liner: Unlicensed 2016 mirror of Trevor Herselman's 2014 SSE2 memcpy/memmove with CPUID dispatch. Claims to beat the C library but ships no numbers.

name: Run:ai Model Streamer
baseline: Hugging Face safetensors loader (mmap/read) and Tensorizer
one_liner: Concurrent C++ safetensors reader with a Python API that loads model weights to GPU faster than Hugging Face's safetensors loader.

name: CTL (C Container Template Library)
baseline: libstdc++ containers (std::vector, std::list, std::deque, std::set, std::unordered_set, std::string) from g++ 10.2.1
one_liner: Header-only macro-templated C99/C11 copies of the STL containers; benchmarks show parity with libstdc++, not a general speedup.

name: LibBF (Fabrice Bellard)
baseline: GNU MPFR (mpfr_mul, via the Rust rug 1.30.0 crate: GMP 6.3 / MPFR 4.2)
one_liner: Fabrice Bellard's tiny MIT-licensed C arbitrary-precision float library; NTT multiplication edges MPFR only at very high precision.

name: Perfect::Hash / pperf
baseline: gperf
one_liner: Perl generator (pperf) that emits C perfect-hash lookup tables; builds 100k-key tables in 1-2 s where gperf times out.

name: copy-fast
baseline: project's own naive sequential read/write backend (backend_naive.c); 1-worker run for the multi-file test
one_liner: Student C11 Linux file-copy tool with threaded pipeline and io_uring backends, compared only against its own naive read/write loop.

name: selectolax
baseline: libxml2 (via lxml.html.fromstring used directly)
one_liner: Cython bindings to the Lexbor/Modest C HTML5 engines, giving CSS-selector DOM parsing faster than lxml/libxml2.

name: nom (Rust parser combinator library)
baseline: Handwritten C HTTP parsers Joyent http-parser and h2o picohttpparser (parser_benchmarks/http); the MP4 benchmark compares against hammer (UpstandingHackers), a C parser-combinator library rather than a handwritten parser.
one_liner: Rust parser-combinator library; its own benchmarks show parity at best with handwritten C HTTP parsers, not a win.

name: Tako (per-thread server)
baseline: Drogon 1.9.13 (C++, trantor event loop; the-benchmarker cpp/drogon, cmake release build); also agoo-c 0.7 (C) in the same table
one_liner: Rust multi-transport web framework on hyper; its thread-per-core HTTP/1.1 server out-served Drogon 1.12-1.24x in the-benchmarker.

name: packed_simd
baseline: ISPC (ispc and ispc_tasks builds of the stock ISPC example programs)
one_liner: Archived, nightly-only Rust SIMD vector crate that preceded std::simd; with rayon it roughly matches ISPC on ISPC's examples.

name: Rust portable SIMD (std::simd / portable-simd)
baseline: scalar loops (Rust for-loop and Rust iterator version; also a C for-loop and NumPy as reference rows)
one_liner: Rust nightly's std::simd: one portable Simd<T, N> type that beat scalar and autovectorized Rust loops 5-13x in a byte count.

name: regex (Rust regex crate)
baseline: PCRE2 (interpreter and JIT) and RE2 (C/C++ regex engines); Hyperscan also measured
one_liner: Rust's linear-time finite-automata regex engine; faster than PCRE2 JIT and RE2 on most search benchmarks, slower to compile.

name: rustc-hash (FxHash)
baseline: SipHash-1-3 (Rust std DefaultHasher, the default hasher of std::collections::HashMap/HashSet)
one_liner: rustc's own tiny multiply-based hasher and FxHashMap/FxHashSet aliases. Much faster than std SipHash-1-3 on integer-heavy keys, but not DoS-resistant.

name: rustc_codegen_cranelift (cg_clif)
baseline: rustc
one_liner: Drop-in Cranelift codegen backend for rustc that replaces LLVM to cut debug-build compile times.

name: rust-phf (compile-time perfect hash maps)
baseline: std::collections::HashMap (Rust) populated at runtime from statically bundled (code-generated) data
one_liner: Rust crates that bake immutable perfect-hash maps and sets into the binary at compile time, removing runtime HashMap construction.

name: rsloop
baseline: uvloop (libuv-based asyncio event loop)
one_liner: Rust/PyO3 asyncio event loop on io_uring, IOCP or kqueue; beats uvloop on TLS, bulk and TCP round-trips, not plaintext WebSockets.

name: simdutf8
baseline: Rust std::str::from_utf8 (also compared against simdjson's UTF-8 validator)
one_liner: SIMD-accelerated UTF-8 validator for Rust, a drop-in replacement for std::str::from_utf8, up to 23x faster.

name: rustls
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Memory-safe Rust TLS 1.2/1.3 library on AWS-LC crypto; beats OpenSSL 3.6.1 per core on handshakes, resumption and AES-GCM bulk.

name: CCAN htable (ccan/htable)
baseline: Judy arrays (JudyL, the Judy integer-key sparse array library)
one_liner: Compact C open-addressing hash table of object pointers with hash bits folded into spare pointer bits; beats JudyL on random lookups.

name: oxsv
language: Assembly (NASM x86-64 AVX2) with a C build wrapper
baseline: xsv (BurntSushi's Rust CSV toolkit, version and build unstated) for the command-level table; naive scalar C loops (byte count, byte find, comma walk) built with gcc -O2 in test/bench.c for the SIMD microbenchmark, not glibc memchr or an -O3 build
one_liner: Linux x86-64 NASM/AVX2 CSV command-line tool with xsv's command names; reports 5.7-76x over xsv on a 1 GB unquoted CSV.

name: turbovec (Rust TurboQuant vector index with Python bindings)
baseline: FAISS IndexPQFastScan (C++) at a matched bit rate (m = d sub-quantizers, 4-bit codes in the published 4-bit script); FAISS IndexPQ (LUT256, nbits=8) for the recall comparison
one_liner: In-process Rust/Python vector index on 2-4 bit TurboQuant codes; searches 2-5x faster than FAISS IndexPQFastScan at equal bits.

name: fast64 (FAST: Fast Architecture Sensitive Tree, 64-bit)
baseline: B-tree (STX B-Tree)
one_liner: Rust/C AVX-512 static search tree for sorted u32/u64 keys; about 10% faster lookups than STX B-Tree in SOSD.

name: ryg_rans
baseline: Scalar (non-interleaved) rANS in the same repo (rans_byte, rans64)
one_liner: Public-domain reference rANS coders in C/C++ headers; interleaved and SSE 4.1 decoders run 1.6-3.7x the scalar decode.

name: tinyfft
baseline: FFTW3 (FFTW_MEASURE planner)
one_liner: Two tiny C files for power-of-two complex FFT and real convolution; author says the AVX version beats FFTW_MEASURE at 2^17-2^20.

name: Darts-clone
baseline: Darts (Double-ARray Trie System, original header library by Taku Kudo)
one_liner: Single-header static double-array trie with 32-bit units; half the size of Darts and faster on cache-bound lookups.

name: marisa-trie (libmarisa)
baseline: darts-clone (compacted double-array trie) and tx-trie (LOUDS-based trie)
one_liner: Static LOUDS-based recursive (nested Patricia) trie dictionary; about 7.4x smaller than darts-clone and 2.5x smaller than tx-trie.

name: netbsd-curses
baseline: ncurses (wide-char build)
one_liner: Portable Linux build of NetBSD's widechar curses; builds 6.6x faster and installs far smaller than ncurses, with no runtime benchmark.

name: pytorch-qrnn (QRNN CUDA kernels)
language: Python (CUDA kernels compiled at runtime via CuPy and pynvrtc)
baseline: NVIDIA cuDNN LSTM
one_liner: Archived PyTorch QRNN layer with a runtime-compiled CUDA recurrence kernel; trained language models about 2x faster per epoch than cuDNN LSTM.

name: sgemm.c (salykova)
baseline: OpenBLAS 0.3.26 (sgemm)
one_liner: Compact pure-C, OpenMP, AVX2/FMA SGEMM in BLIS style that claims parity with OpenBLAS on two desktop CPUs.

name: sgemm.cu (hand-tuned FP32 GEMM for NVIDIA GA102/Ampere GPUs)
baseline: cuBLAS SGEMM (CUDA 12.6)
one_liner: Hand-tuned row-major FP32 SGEMM kernels for Ampere; about 4-7% above cuBLAS SGEMM at large square sizes on an RTX 3090.

name: VectorVisor (GPU binary translator for WebAssembly)
baseline: Same Wasm modules on CPU with Wasmtime embedded in VectorVisor (--wasmtime=true) and native x86-64 Rust builds (cargo run --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu), on 4-vCPU AWS c5.xlarge (Intel) or c5a.xlarge (AMD) instances; hand-written CUDA versions (cuda-blockhash, cuda-blur) on the GPU for imagehash and imageblur.
one_liner: Binary translator that runs thousands of copies of a single-threaded Wasm program on an OpenCL GPU; per dollar it beats native x86 CPU VMs only on some compute-bound workloads.

name: LunaSVG
baseline: cairosvg 2.9.1 (Python, renders through Cairo 1.18.4) and resvg-py 0.5.0
one_liner: Small C++17 SVG 1.1/Tiny 1.2 renderer on the plutovg rasterizer; converts icons to PNG about 2x faster than cairosvg through Python.

name: plutovg
baseline: Cairo, Skia, Blend2D (category baselines; no comparison found)
one_liner: Small MIT C 2D vector library with a Cairo-like canvas API; no published speed comparison against Cairo, Skia or Blend2D.

name: Chorba (table-less CRC32)
baseline: zlib (zlib 1.3.1.1 CRC32 'braiding' implementation)
one_liner: Table-less software CRC-32 using sparse zero polynomials; about 2x zlib 1.3.1.1's braided CRC on large buffers.

name: Escargot
baseline: QuickJS (Bellard release 2026-06-04); the same dashboard also runs V8 d8 and V8 --jitless
one_liner: Samsung's embeddable no-JIT JavaScript interpreter (ES2026, Intl, Temporal); about 1.2-1.3x QuickJS speed on ARM64 suites, with lower RSS on large workloads.

name: htscodecs (32-way interleaved SIMD rANS)
baseline: Scalar 4-way rANS4x16 codec in the same library (r4x16 -o0) and FSE order-0 (tANS), both rows on the PR's tables
one_liner: CRAM 3.1 codec library whose 32-way SIMD rANS decodes about 2.7x faster than its 4-way rANS and 3.8x faster than FSE.

name: htslib
baseline: Samtools 0.1.19 (the original libbam-based implementation HTSlib grew out of)
one_liner: C library for SAM/BAM/CRAM/VCF/BCF I/O; 5x faster BAM read-write and 13x faster BAM-to-SAM than Samtools 0.1.19 at 16 threads.

name: musql
baseline: SQLite (C, via mattn/go-sqlite3); Turso's Go driver is also compared
one_liner: Pure-Go SQLite-dialect engine on its own columnar format; JIT filter/aggregate kernels beat C SQLite on read-mostly scans.

name: wazy
baseline: wazero (the Go runtime it descends from; the repo's three-way benchmark arms against wasmtime-go exist but the README states no wasmtime numbers)
one_liner: Pure-Go WebAssembly runtime hard-forked from wazero; about 1.3x faster compiled codegen on a 6.5 MB module, up to 9x on instantiate and interruptible loops.

name: Chipmunk (column-sparse attention and MLP kernels for diffusion transformers)
baseline: FlashAttention-3 (attention layer) and cuBLAS / torch.compile'd nn.Sequential (MLP layer); torch.compile'd reference repos for end-to-end
one_liner: Training-free dynamic column-sparse attention and MLP kernels for diffusion transformers; about 2.16x end-to-end on HunyuanVideo over torch.compile'd dense.

name: sanity-lint (groq-wasm)
language: Rust (groq-lint, groq-format) compiled to WebAssembly; TypeScript
baseline: The TypeScript implementation of the GROQ lint rules in @sanity-labs/groq-lint (named as 'TypeScript' in packages/groq-wasm/README.md; also the automatic fallback when WASM is unavailable)
