one_liner: GROQ query linter whose 13 pure-GROQ rules run in a Rust-to-WASM build; claims 5-10x over its own TypeScript rules, with no measurement.

name: cisv
baseline: csvkit
one_liner: SIMD-accelerated C CSV parser/writer (AVX-512/AVX2) beating csvkit and PapaParse; monorepo now deprecated.

name: epoll-httpd
baseline: nginx
one_liner: Small Linux-only C++17 static-file HTTP/1.1 server on raw epoll; ~1.4-1.6x single-worker nginx on 1-8 KB files.

name: faer
baseline: OpenBLAS, LAPACK and Eigen (paper text); Intel MKL not claimed as beaten
one_liner: Pure-Rust dense (and sparse) linear algebra whose multithreaded QR and mid-size eigensolvers outrun OpenBLAS and Eigen; MKL still leads.

name: h0_bv (H0-compressed bitvectors)
baseline: SDSL rrr_vector (and SDSL hybrid bitvector)
one_liner: Research C++ RRR-style H0-compressed bitvectors with faster block decoding; beat SDSL rrr_vector on access at block size 63.

name: MagicScaler (PhotoSauce)
baseline: ImageMagick via Magick.NET-Q8-AnyCPU 12.2.0 (also System.Drawing, ImageSharp, SkiaSharp, NetVips/libvips 8.13.2)
one_liner: .NET image resizing pipeline (MagicScaler) that makes JPEG thumbnails 5-9x faster than Magick.NET in its author's runs.

name: Register-Blocked SIMD Bit-Pattern Bloom Filter (bloomfilter_benchmarks)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Benchmark header of AVX2 bit-pattern Bloom filters: 19-22x a naive Bloom filter's throughput on small filters, at ~6% FPR.

name: vectorized_find (AVX2 find experiments)
baseline: std::find on a raw array and on std::vector (plus a naive loop)
one_liner: Personal AVX2 experiment: a 2x-unrolled cmpeq/movemask find for int and float, about 3.2x std::find on 4096 L1-resident ints.

name: zigmark (Zig CommonMark parser and renderer)
baseline: cmark and cmark-gfm (C); the same table also lists lowdown and discount (C) and pandoc (Haskell).
one_liner: Zig CommonMark+GFM parser and HTML/Typst renderer; README shows it ahead of cmark only through a shell-wrapped baseline.

name: Scala.js WebAssembly backend
baseline: Scala.js JavaScript backend output run in V8 / Node.js (JS emitted code)
one_liner: Scala.js's WasmGC backend: the same Scala code linked to WebAssembly instead of JavaScript, claimed 30% lower geomean run time.

name: golang-fifo
baseline: lru-hashicorp / lru-groupcache
one_liner: Go generic in-process cache implementing SIEVE and S3-FIFO eviction; about 16-18% fewer misses than hashicorp LRU, but no higher ops/sec.

name: scandum/binary_search (monobound / boundless binary search)
baseline: bsearch() (C standard library)
one_liner: C binary-search variants; monobound_bsearch() is a bsearch()-compatible drop-in ~1.4-2.35x faster than libc bsearch().

name: blitsort
baseline: std::stable_sort
one_liner: In-place, stable, adaptive C sort beating std::stable_sort via rotations instead of an O(n) swap buffer.

name: crumsort
baseline: pdqsort
one_liner: Branchless in-place unstable C quicksort/quadsort hybrid, ~1.4-1.5x faster than pdqsort on random 32/64-bit ints.

name: fluxsort
baseline: std::stable_sort
one_liner: Stable branchless quicksort/mergesort hybrid with a qsort-style C interface, claimed ~3x faster than std::stable_sort on random ints.

name: gridsort
baseline: std::stable_sort
one_liner: Stable C sort using a cache-friendly bucketed grid; qsort-compatible interface; 1.4x-2.6x faster than std::stable_sort on 1M-int arrays.

name: quadsort
baseline: std::stable_sort
one_liner: Stable branchless bottom-up adaptive merge sort in C, beating std::stable_sort on random and partially ordered arrays.

name: mogwai
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript (vanillajs-keyed)
one_liner: Rust/Wasm browser GUI crate without a virtual DOM; its 2023 benchmark build beats React 19.2 hooks, but not vanilla JS.

name: LB+-Trees (persistent B+-Tree optimized for 3D XPoint memory)
baseline: WB+-Tree and FP-Tree (state-of-the-art NVM-optimized persistent B+-trees)
one_liner: Persistent B+-Tree for Intel Optane PM; 1.12-2.92x faster inserts than WB+-Tree and FP-Tree, similar lookups.

name: CoDiPack (operator-overloading AD, expression templates)
baseline: ADOL-C and Adept (other C++ operator-overloading AD tools); none of the listed baselines (oneDNN, cuDNN, XNNPACK, Eigen tensor) apply
one_liner: Header-only C++17 operator-overloading AD with expression templates; peer-reviewed paper reports it beats ADOL-C and roughly matches Adept.

name: DiffEqGPU.jl (GPU ensemble ODE solvers in Julia, GPUTsit5) vs MPGOS
baseline: MPGOS (Massively Parallel GPU ODE Solvers), a CUDA C++ ensemble ODE solver library: RK4 (fixed step) and RKCK45 (adaptive), built with nvcc -O3
one_liner: Julia GPU ensemble ODE/SDE solvers that compile one trajectory per thread; against MPGOS (CUDA C++) results are mixed.

name: OrdinaryDiffEq.jl (DifferentialEquations.jl) ODE solvers vs Sundials, ODEPACK and Hairer codes
baseline: Sundials CVODE_Adams and ARKODE (C) and liblsoda (C port of ODEPACK lsoda), plus Hairer dopri5/dop853/odex (Fortran), called through Julia wrappers with a Julia right-hand side.
one_liner: Julia ODE solver suite whose Verner Runge-Kutta methods beat Sundials CVODE/ARKODE on small non-stiff work-precision benchmarks.

name: InstantTensor
baseline: safetensors loader (mmap-based file read to GPU); also compared with fastsafetensors and Run:ai Model Streamer
one_liner: C++/Python safetensors-to-GPU loader using O_DIRECT io_uring/AIO plus NCCL all-gather; beats the safetensors loader on cold loads.

name: ScyllaDB Rust driver (async Tokio CQL driver vs C++ driver)
baseline: DataStax Cassandra C++ driver ('cpp-multi', v2.16.0 .deb per the current Dockerfile, run with I/O threads = hardware_concurrency), plus the Scylla C++ driver fork ('cpp'), which the harness ran with a single I/O thread until commit 'Bump Scylla cpp driver to 2.16.2, remove single thread limitation for it' (2022-08-01)
one_liner: Pure-Rust async Tokio CQL driver for ScyllaDB and Cassandra; the vendor's insert benchmark shows it level with the multi-threaded DataStax C++ driver.

name: ScyllaDB
baseline: Apache Cassandra 4.0 (Java; cassandra-stress, CL=QUORUM)
one_liner: C++ rewrite of Apache Cassandra (CQL, plus a DynamoDB API) on a thread-per-core engine; vendor claims 3-8x Cassandra 4.0 throughput.

name: Seastar
baseline: libevent
one_liner: Shard-per-core C++ futures framework with optional DPDK userspace TCP; its memcached beat libevent-based stock memcached 2-4x (2015).

name: Kiddo (Rust k-d tree)
baseline: pykdtree, scipy.spatial.KDTree and sklearn KDTree (Python), nabo-rs and FNNTW (Rust); no C++ baseline (nanoflann, PCL, CGAL) is benchmarked
one_liner: Rust k-d tree for low-dimensional exact/approximate NN; 1.2-1.5x faster queries than nabo-rs; no C/C++ API.

name: httparse (Rust push parser for HTTP/1.x)
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: Rust's standard zero-copy HTTP/1.x push parser; beats picohttpparser only when pico is built without SSE4.2.

name: Cromulent-PRNG (seanwevans/Cromulent-PRNG, cromulent128 with AVX2 variant)
baseline: xoshiro256++, a 64-bit-state PCG variant labelled pcg64, and splitmix64 (reference copies in src/reference/, timed by the repo's own apps/bench_micro.c)
one_liner: Small MIT C library for a new 128-bit-state nonlinear PRNG; its own benchmark beats xoshiro256++ but loses to splitmix64.

name: spow
language: Rust (server crate, browser WASM and JS-only solvers)
baseline: the JS-only browser solver shipped in prebuilt/browser, and optimised native Rust (the wasm build is slower than native)
one_liner: Self-hosted Hashcash-style proof-of-work captcha in Rust with a browser WASM solver, about 20x faster than its own async-WebCrypto JS solver.

name: ferrocat (Rust Gettext PO catalog engine)
baseline: GNU msgmerge (gettext-tools 1.0, C), run as a separate process per iteration
one_liner: Rust Gettext PO parser and catalog merge/update engine; first-party runs merge a 10k-message catalog about 56x faster than GNU msgmerge.

name: ferromark
baseline: md4c (C); cmark (C) in a second report
one_liner: Rust CommonMark/GFM Markdown-to-HTML engine, about 3x faster than md4c and 5-6x faster than cmark in its own harness.

name: Ferroni (Rust port of the Oniguruma regex engine)
baseline: Oniguruma (C); also PCRE2 interpreter, PCRE2 JIT, Onigmo, Rust regex and fancy-regex measured
one_liner: Pure-Rust port of the Oniguruma regex engine and the vscode-oniguruma scanner; about 2.2x faster than C Oniguruma on everyday searches and 12x on TextMate highlighting replays.

name: noyalib
baseline: yaml-rust2
one_liner: Pure-Rust, zero-unsafe YAML 1.2 serde library that parses config-sized documents to a Value 1.11-1.36x faster than yaml-rust2.

name: zsv-ruby
baseline: CSV (Ruby standard library CSV parser)
one_liner: Ruby native-extension binding to the zsv C library; drop-in CSV stdlib replacement, 5-6x faster.

name: SeekStorm
baseline: Apache Lucene
one_liner: Rust in-process search engine with native lexical and vector indexes; claims sub-millisecond BM25 latency beating Lucene.

name: seelabs/nasm (AVX2 hex encoder and decoder for 256-bit values in NASM)
baseline: reference C++ hex encode and decode routines taken from rippled (compiled with g++ -O3 according to build.sh)
one_liner: Learning-project NASM AVX2 kernels that hex-encode 32 bytes and hex-decode 64 digits 5.6x and 8.4x faster than rippled's scalar C++.

name: segmentio/asm
baseline: the package's own pure-Go fallback implementations of the same functions, selected with the purego build tag (Makefile benchcmp target runs go test -bench with -tags purego as 'old' and without it as 'new'); for ascii a table-lookup unrolled EqualFoldString, for bswap an encoding/binary loop, for qsort the package's Go quicksort128 with Hoare partition. Not Go stdlib functions (strings.EqualFold, sort.Slice); no stdlib numbers are published.
one_liner: Go assembly (avo-generated AVX2) kernels for ASCII case-folding, byte swapping, fixed-size-key sort and base64; 6-13x over the package's pure-Go fallbacks.

name: segmentio/encoding (encoding/json replacement)
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Drop-in encoding/json replacement for Go that swaps reflection for unsafe-pointer codecs; ~1.7x marshal, ~5x unmarshal on typed structs.

name: zimg
baseline: FFmpeg 4.0.2 filters (README column label 'swscale 4.0.2'): the swscale scale filter for the Lanczos resize and the libavfilter colorspace filter for the BT.709 to BT.2020 conversion
one_liner: C++ library for scaling, colourspace and bit-depth conversion of video frames; its 2018 README shows about 2x FFmpeg 4.0.2's filters.

name: PcapPlusPlus
baseline: libtins v4.5 (C++ packet parsing and crafting library)
one_liner: C++ packet capture, parsing and crafting library; parses pcap TCP/DNS traffic 1.06-1.26x faster than libtins in its maintainers' run.

name: RustyBox (Rust BusyBox-style userland)
baseline: GNU coreutils sort and GNU sed (versions not stated); BusyBox, Toybox and FreeBSD native tools for the other rows
one_liner: Single-binary Rust multicall userland (sort, sed, grep, cut, wc and about 45 more) claiming small wins over GNU sort and sed.

name: serde_json (typed, #[derive(Deserialize)])
baseline: RapidJSON (DOM parser) and nlohmann/json; simdjson is faster
one_liner: Rust's standard JSON crate; typed derive decoding beat a RapidJSON DOM parse 1.4-1.8x in kostya's suite, but not simdjson.

name: serde (serde_derive typed deserialization)
baseline: RapidJSON DOM parser and nlohmann/json (JSON libraries in the same suite; no Cereal or Boost.Serialization comparison found)
one_liner: Rust's compile-time derive (de)serialization framework; through serde_json it beat a RapidJSON DOM parse 1.4-1.9x on kostya's JSON test.

name: IResearch (SereneDB)
baseline: Lucene
one_liner: C++ inverted-index search library (ex-ArangoSearch) embedded in SereneDB; claims 5x over Lucene, real gains are 1.0x-1.7x.

name: frozen
baseline: std::unordered_map (arXiv 2602.22506 demos); std::set and std::unordered_set in the author's first-party 2018 Quarkslab microbenchmark
one_liner: Header-only C++14 constexpr immutable set/map/unordered_map built on compile-time perfect hashing; beats std::unordered_map on fixed key sets.

name: Pythran
baseline: CPython 3.12 (interpreted Python; the dev-branch workflow sets python-version 3.12 via actions/setup-python, so the version is stated, not inferred; tables for 3.10, 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14 use the PyPI Pyccel 2.2.3 run)
one_liner: Ahead-of-time compiler from a NumPy-flavoured Python subset to C++17 extension modules; 11x-2096x faster than CPython on loop kernels.

name: Goofy (realtime DXT1/ETC1 encoder)
baseline: stb_dxt (ryg DXT1, STB_DXT_NORMAL); also rgbcx 1.08, icbc 1.0 and rg_etc1 1.04
one_liner: Header-only SSE2 BC1/ETC1 encoder, about 1.4 GP/s per core, trading about 4 dB PSNR for 24-400x speed.

name: smmalloc
baseline: CRT malloc/free (C runtime heap, the allocator under default operator new)
one_liner: Lock-free, thread-cached proxy allocator for small (16-992B) game allocations; passes everything else through to CRT malloc.

name: Pathfinder 3
baseline: Unnamed 'best CPU rasterizers' (README). FreeType, stb_truetype and font-rs are named as comparison points only in the 2017 Pathfinder 1 blog post (pcwalton.github.io), which is blocked here and is known only from a search snippet.
one_liner: Rust GPU rasterizer for glyphs and vector paths (OpenGL, Metal, WebGL 2); claims to match or beat CPU rasterizers, with no numbers.

name: Stylo (Rust parallel CSS style engine in Firefox Quantum) vs Gecko's previous C++ style system
baseline: Gecko's previous sequential C++ style system (CSS selector matching and cascade) in Firefox before Quantum
one_liner: Firefox's and Servo's Rust CSS style engine; its parallel cascade replaced Gecko's sequential C++ style system in Firefox 57.

name: WebAssembly vs JavaScript Animation Demo (sessamekesh/wasm-3d-animation-demo)
baseline: TypeScript skeletal-animation implementation running in the browser JavaScript engine
one_liner: 2017 WebGL demo running one naive skeletal-animation system in TypeScript and in Emscripten-compiled C++/Wasm; Wasm hit 60 FPS where JS managed 5-10.

name: Talc
baseline: DLmalloc (Rust wasm default), RLSF, Galloc, FRuSA, system allocator
one_liner: Rust no_std and WebAssembly heap allocator; about 2x DLmalloc's throughput on wasm at under a third of its code size.

name: dft_simd (vertical-SIMD FFTW codelets)
baseline: FFTW 3 (planner/execute API with its SSE/AVX codelets, single and 8-transform advanced interface)
one_liner: Recipe and test code that runs FFTW genfft codelets on AVX2/AVX-512 vectors, 8 or 16 short DFTs per call; beats FFTW on bulk short transforms.

name: SFML
baseline: raylib (DrawTexture, C)
one_liner: C++ window, input, audio and sprite library; one hobby benchmark draws static sprites 1.29x faster than raylib, slower than SDL2.

name: Sphinx
baseline: DHT (Delta Hash Table, a dynamic perfect hash table) / RSQF / Aleph Filter / Adaptive Aleph Filter (state-of-the-art fingerprint and perfect-hash indexes for log-structured hash tables / key-value stores)
one_liner: Dynamic succinct perfect hash index (~4 bits/key) for log-structured KV stores; paper reports ~2x lower latency than DHT/Aleph Filter.

name: libqoi
baseline: qoixx (wx257osn2/qoixx)
one_liner: Small C++14 port of the QOI reference codec; a single informal user report says faster than qoixx, which the code does not support.

name: WebDSP
baseline: its own JavaScript fallback implementations of the same image and video filters (in-browser)
one_liner: 2017 C++-to-WebAssembly image/video filter set (Sobel, 3x3 convolutions, colour tweaks) with a pure-JS fallback; faster only on the heavy filters.

name: arena-allocator (ShortAlloc)
baseline: operator new/delete (GNU/glibc malloc via std::vector's default std::allocator)
one_liner: Single-file bump-pointer arena allocator with an STL-compatible wrapper; beats glibc malloc via std::vector, especially above the mmap threshold.

name: MELG-64 (MELG19937-64)
baseline: MT19937-64 reference C code (algorithmically std::mt19937_64)
one_liner: Maximally equidistributed 64-bit Mersenne-Twister-type generators in C; MT19937-64-class speed with optimal high-dimensional uniformity.

name: diskus
baseline: GNU du -sh
one_liner: Parallel Rust replacement for du -sh that prints one directory total; author measured 10x faster cold-cache, 2.2x warm.

name: fd
baseline: GNU find (findutils, C)
one_liner: Rust parallel, gitignore-aware replacement for GNU find; 13-23x faster wall time on one regex name search, by using every core.

name: frxml
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Archived zero-copy C++17 XML parser; its old chart shows ~1.8-9x faster than libxml2 DOM but slower than pugixml and RapidXML.

name: RapidKV
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Single-threaded C++20 RESP server with 13 string commands; ties Redis unpipelined, 1.45-4.2x faster when pipelined.

name: MadFS
baseline: ext4-DAX and NOVA persistent-memory filesystems (POSIX file API)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD userspace persistent-memory file layer over ext4-DAX; FAST '23 reports up to 3.6x ext4-DAX concurrent throughput.

name: markdown_yo (Yo-language Markdown renderer, WASM build)
language: Yo (new systems language) compiled to WebAssembly via Emscripten and to native
baseline: markdown-it (JavaScript Markdown parser on Node.js/V8)
one_liner: Markdown-to-HTML converter in the Yo language (native and WebAssembly) that outputs markdown-it-compatible HTML 4.5-7.6x faster natively.

name: Shed Skin
license: GPL-3.0 (compiler); MIT/Expat, BSD-3-Clause and BSL-1.0 for the C++ runtime library; examples individually licensed
language: Python (transpiler) generating C++; runtime library in C++
baseline: CPython 3.14 (headline claim); CPython 3.10.6 and 3.11.0 in the sieve timing
one_liner: Ahead-of-time transpiler from implicitly statically typed Python 3 to C++; README claims 12x median over CPython 3.14.

name: GLU (GPU-accelerated sparse LU solver for circuit simulation)
baseline: KLU and UMFPACK (SuiteSparse)
one_liner: CUDA sparse LU numeric factorization for circuit matrices; papers report 19.56x over KLU (numeric phase only, float32).

name: Caladan
baseline: Parties (authors' reimplementation, 'Parties*', because the original source was unavailable); also compared with Linux (kernel TCP, BE task at SCHED_IDLE) and Shenango
one_liner: Interference-aware core scheduler and kernel-bypass runtime; memcached 99.9% latency 52 us vs 580 ms under Parties* during GC.

name: Shenango
baseline: ZygOS (a state-of-the-art kernel-bypass network stack) and standard Linux kernel networking
one_liner: Kernel-bypass runtime reallocating cores every 5 us; ZygOS-level tail latency, 6.3x Linux DNS throughput, idle cores freed for batch jobs.

name: json.h
baseline: nlohmann/json (C++11, v2.0.3 as pinned by nativejson-benchmark); the same table also has JsonCpp 1.0.0, Jansson and cJSON
one_liner: Public-domain single-header C/C++ JSON parser into one read-only allocation; out-parsed nlohmann/json v2.0.3 in a 2016 shootout.

name: SLEEF (SIMD Library for Evaluating Elementary Functions)
baseline: <cmath> (scalar libm, represented in the paper by FDLIBM as the reference scalar implementation)
one_liner: Vectorized C library of libm math functions (sin, cos, exp, log, pow); beats scalar <cmath>/libm when call sites are SIMD-batched.

name: TLFloat
baseline: GNU libquadmath (GCC __float128)
one_liner: Constexpr C++20 template library for IEEE half to octuple floats; inlined Quad beats libquadmath on add/mul/fma/sqrt/casts, loses on div/exp/log/pow.

name: sy_callback.hpp
baseline: std::function
one_liner: Header-only type-erased callback wrapper beating std::function on construct/destroy, move, and assign; no SBO.

name: libfacedetection (Highway-optimized facedetect_hw_cnn and Rust crate)
baseline: libfacedetection original C++ implementation (facedetect_cnn, AVX2 build with _ENABLE_AVX2) from the same repository
one_liner: Dependency-free YuNet CNN face detector; its 2026 Highway build is 2.8-3.9x faster single-thread than the project's own AVX2 original.

name: TurboFFT
baseline: NVIDIA cuFFT (also VkFFT)
one_liner: Code-generated batched 1D FP32/FP64 GPU FFT kernels with fused ABFT fault tolerance; matches or beats cuFFT, beats VkFFT.

name: libcsp
baseline: Go goroutines (Go 1.14, sync.WaitGroup); pthreads also run at a reduced size
one_liner: Go-style M:N process scheduler for C (GCC plugin, x86-64 Linux); about 10x faster than Go 1.14 at spawning short-lived tasks.

name: Mini-Attention (FlashAttention-2 from scratch in CUDA C++ for SM120)
baseline: cuDNN fused attention via PyTorch SDPA (SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION)
one_liner: Hand-written FlashAttention-2 forward kernel for RTX 5090 (SM120); beats cuDNN SDPA at N<=1024, 3-5% slower beyond.

name: veque
baseline: std::vector; std::deque
one_liner: Header-only C++20 double-ended vector: std::vector's contiguous storage plus std::deque's fast front growth.

name: SHOGUN (k-means)
baseline: scikit-learn 0.8 (scikits.learn KMeans)
one_liner: Large C++ machine-learning toolbox whose 2011 k-means beat scikit-learn 0.8 about 2x; that edge did not survive.

name: milo
baseline: llhttp
one_liner: Strict Rust HTTP/1.1 parser (crate, C++ lib, WASM) meant to replace llhttp in Node.js; ~1.07x llhttp in one test.

name: UltrafastSecp256k1
baseline: OpenSSL (ECDSA_do_sign/ECDSA_do_verify, secp256k1); also benchmarked against libsecp256k1 (bitcoin-core)
one_liner: C++20 secp256k1 ECDSA/Schnorr engine: about 1.5x faster CT signing and 1.1x faster verify than libsecp256k1, and 11-22x faster than OpenSSL.

name: Arc (Arc Gateway)
baseline: nginx (C) as an HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 reverse proxy; version, build and the configuration behind the README table are not stated (the repo's benchmark script uses worker_processes auto and upstream keepalive 1024)
one_liner: Young Rust io_uring reverse proxy claiming 2.05-2.30x nginx's HTTP/1.1 proxy throughput on a 2-vCPU WSL2 box.

name: RANLUX++ (sibidanov/ranluxpp)
baseline: std::ranlux (GCC libstdc++ RANLUX) in the repo README and tests/std_random_test.cxx; ROOT's TRandom1 (James' RANLUX implementation) in the independent ROOT measurement
one_liner: RANLUX recast as a 576-bit LCG with x86-64 assembly modmul; about 8x faster than classic RANLUX implementations.

name: Bloomsday (blocked/split-block Bloom filter, Rust)
license: MIT (declared in Cargo.toml; no separate LICENSE file detected by GitHub)
baseline: Bloom filter (sbbf-rs Split Block Bloom Filter crate)
one_liner: Safe-Rust Parquet-style split-block Bloom filter whose inlined, auto-vectorized lookups ran ~2.3x faster than sbbf-rs in its own benchmark.

name: fast_vector (sigerror/fast-vector)
baseline: std::vector
one_liner: Header-only C++17 vector without zero-init, exceptions, or a real allocator; beats std::vector on trivial-type push_back workloads.

name: Silkenweb
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust/Wasm signals-based web UI library (no VDOM); about 1.6x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark, not faster than vanilla JS.

name: PochiVM (copy-and-patch baseline compiler)
baseline: LLVM 10.0.0 JIT backend of the same metaprogramming system at -O0 (also -O1/-O2/-O3) for code-generation time and generated-code speed, plus an in-house AST interpreter (about 1.5x faster than the Peloton interpreter)
one_liner: C++-embedded JIT DSL whose copy-and-patch backend generates code about 100x faster than LLVM -O0, with 14% faster output.

name: WasmNow (copy-and-patch WebAssembly baseline compiler)
baseline: Google Chrome (V8) Liftoff baseline WebAssembly compiler; also Wasmer Singlepass named in README
one_liner: Research copy-and-patch WebAssembly baseline JIT; OOPSLA 2021 paper: 4.9-6.5x faster compiles, 39-63% faster code than V8 Liftoff.

name: TinyORM (TinyDrivers MySQL driver)
baseline: QtSql with the QMYSQL driver
one_liner: Qt-based C++20 ORM whose own MySQL driver layer replaces QtSql/QMYSQL; measured gain is marginal (~40 ms per 620 queries).

name: Photon (photon-rs)
baseline: libvips (vips CLI, Windows vips.exe)
one_liner: Pure-Rust image-effects library that also ships as WebAssembly for browsers and Node; one mixed first-party result against the libvips CLI.

name: Simbody
baseline: ODE and Bullet Physics, through Gazebo-classic's ODE and Bullet plugins (DART was measured in the same run)
one_liner: Featherstone-style O(n) multibody dynamics library; measured slower than ODE and Bullet for free boxes, so a not-faster entry.

name: SIMD Everywhere
baseline: unvectorized (scalar) implementation of the same program (VVenC/VVdeC ported from x86 SSE/AVX to Arm)
one_liner: Header-only C99 library implementing x86 (MMX to AVX2, parts of AVX-512), Neon and WASM SIMD intrinsics on any target, beating scalar ports.

name: simd-json (Rust)
baseline: serde_json
one_liner: Rust port of simdjson with serde support; 1.2-2.7x faster DOM parsing than serde_json in json-benchmark.

name: CLHash
baseline: CityHash (CityHash64WithSeed, the paper's C port of v1.1.1); secondarily xxHash (xxh3) via SMHasher
one_liner: Keyed 64-bit universal string hash built on carry-less multiply; about 40% faster than CityHash64 on inputs over 64 bytes.

name: simditoa
baseline: std::to_chars
one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA int64/uint64-to-decimal conversion; 2.8x std::to_chars throughput on 12-19 digit integers, slower at 1-4 digits.

name: simdjson experimental_json_builder (C++26 reflection-based JSON serializer)
baseline: nlohmann/json
one_liner: Obsolete 2024 prototype of a C++26 reflection JSON serializer; about 20x nlohmann/json throughput. Now part of simdjson's builder.

name: simdjson
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: SIMD-accelerated JSON parser with full UTF-8 validation; ~4x faster than RapidJSON, ~25x than nlohmann.

name: SimdUnicode
baseline: .NET runtime's built-in UTF-8 validator (Utf8Utility.GetPointerToFirstInvalidByte; private in the runtime, benchmarked through a vendored MIT copy in benchmark/UTF8_runtime.cs)
one_liner: Drop-in faster UTF-8 validator for .NET, beating the runtime's private SIMD validator on non-ASCII text.

name: simdutf Base64 (WHATWG forgiving-base64, ignorable-character SIMD decoding)
baseline: base64
one_liner: SIMD WHATWG forgiving-base64 codec in the simdutf C++ library; its fastbase64 CLI decodes 100 MB 3.5–27x faster than system base64.

name: simdxml
baseline: pugixml
one_liner: Rust SIMD XML parser and XPath 1.0 engine using a flat structural index; beats pugixml on large, attribute-dense files.

name: copies-and-fills (libcofi_rpi.so)
baseline: generic libc memcpy and memset on Raspberry Pi (ARM)
one_liner: ARMv6 assembly memcpy and memset for the original Raspberry Pi, LD_PRELOADed over the generic libc versions.

name: VROOM (RNS Montgomery arithmetic with AVX-512 IFMA, BLS12-381 and BN254)
baseline: BLST (supranational/blst at 8065152, a modified vendored copy in blst/ with benchmark wrappers); GMP is used only for parameter generation and validation, not timed
one_liner: Header-only C++20 RNS Montgomery arithmetic on AVX-512 IFMA; BLS12-381 pairing 3.9x faster than BLST on Sapphire Rapids.

name: ProxQP (ProxSuite)
baseline: OSQP (also compared against Gurobi, MOSEK, qpOASES, quadprog)
one_liner: Header-only C++ QP solver (ProxQP) on Eigen; 3.5-18x lower shifted-geomean solve time than OSQP on random QPs.

name: vphilox
baseline: std::mt19937 (also compared with xoshiro256++ and PCG64)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 SIMD Philox4x32-10 engine; bulk fill runs 1.3-4.6x std::mt19937 throughput, seekable and reproducible.

name: Sirius
baseline: DuckDB
one_liner: DuckDB extension that runs DuckDB's SQL plans on NVIDIA GPUs via libcudf; vendor TPC-H hot runs 2.7-5.7x faster than DuckDB.

name: SixLabors.Fonts
license: Six Labors Split License 1.0 (non-OSI: Apache-2.0 only for open-source or source-available use, transitive dependencies, non-profits and for-profits under 1M USD annual revenue; commercial license otherwise)
baseline: HarfBuzz via HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1.1 (native HarfBuzz called from .NET, single-run text shaping)
one_liner: Pure managed C# OpenType shaper and text layout engine; on .NET 10 it is within about 8% of native HarfBuzz overall, beating it on four of ten scripts.

name: ImageSharp (SixLabors)
license: Six Labors Split License 1.0 (not an SPDX id, non-OSI): Apache-2.0 for open-source or source-available use, transitive dependency use, for-profit under 1M USD annual gross revenue and non-profits; paid Six Labors Commercial License otherwise
baseline: Magick.NET (ImageMagick) and System.Drawing

name: ImageSharp.Drawing

name: aeronet
baseline: Boost.Beast and Go net/http

name: PowerInfer
baseline: llama.cpp

name: ska::flat_hash_map / ska::bytell_hash_map

one_liner: Header-only Robin Hood open-addressing hash map/set beating std::unordered_map on lookups, inserts, and erases.

name: ska_sort
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Header-only radix/American-flag sort beating std::sort by ~2x on ints, floats, structs and strings via key extraction.

name: ChaCha20-BLAKE3
baseline: XChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-256-GCM via RustCrypto's pure-Rust crates (chacha20poly1305 0.11.0-rc.2 and aes-gcm 0.11.0-rc.2 per benchmarks/Cargo.toml), not OpenSSL or libsodium
one_liner: Rust committing AEAD (ChaCha20 + keyed-BLAKE3 MAC); about 2x RustCrypto XChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-256-GCM on 1-10 MB messages.

name: stdx-go ChaCha20 (Go simd/archsimd)
license: MIT (per LICENSE.txt and GitHub detection); the README contradicts this, saying 'The code is licensed under AGPL-3.0 (see LICENSE.txt)'
baseline: golang.org/x/crypto/chacha20 (the Go project's x/crypto module, not the std library proper). It is pure-Go scalar on amd64: the package has assembly only for arm64, ppc64x, s390x and loong64.

name: re2c
license: Public Domain (dedication, not a formal OSI license)
baseline: Ragel

name: High-performance pub/sub (uWS broadcast-coalescing prototype)

name: zeemo
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG); same suite rows for libreactorng, libioma, mongoose, h2o (C) and Drogon, agensio, userver (C++)
one_liner: Zig io_uring HTTP/1.1 benchmark server and young library; 1.35x nginx's HttpArena baseline rate, ties libreactorng.

name: Skytable
baseline: Redis
one_liner: Multithreaded in-memory Rust NoSQL server with a SQL-like query language; one unaudited 2022 benchmark shows ~6x Redis GET/SET throughput.

name: FastMemcpy
language: C (header-only FastMemcpy.h using SSE2/AVX intrinsics, no assembly)
baseline: System memcpy of gcc 4.9 and MSVC 2012
one_liner: Header-only SSE2/AVX intrinsics memcpy from 2015 that beat the gcc 4.9 and MSVC 2012-era memcpy but not modern glibc.

name: KCP
baseline: ENet (libenet) reliable UDP; README also claims a gain over TCP
one_liner: Two-file C reliable-UDP ARQ library. It spends extra bandwidth to get much lower tail latency than ENet or TCP under packet loss.

name: sfl-library small and static containers (sfl::small_vector, sfl::static_vector, sfl::small_flat_map)
baseline: std::vector
one_liner: Header-only C++11 small_vector, static_vector and small_flat_map that avoid heap allocation for up to N elements; no benchmark numbers.

name: Sleipnir
baseline: CasADi 3.8.0 (autodiff and NLP frontend) with Ipopt 3.14.20 and MUMPS 5.8.1

name: slick-logger
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Header-only C++20 async logger: lock-free ring, formatting deferred to a writer thread; 2-5x spdlog async on producer-side throughput.

name: SLOTHY
baseline: unscheduled 'clean' hand-written assembly and prior hand-optimized implementations of the same kernels (ML-KEM and ML-DSA NTTs, FFT, X25519); no compiler baseline stated on the pages opened

name: libcr
baseline: kernel (OS thread) task switches

name: rpcx
baseline: gRPC (grpc-go 1.39.0); also Go standard library net/rpc (Go 1.16.6)

name: zxml
baseline: pugixml

name: WFA2-lib

name: K2 (smartnic/superopt, BPF superoptimizing compiler)

baseline: clang BPF output: -O3 per the abstract, and the best of the clang -O1/-O2/-O3 variants per benchmark in the throughput runs (the artifact example's best clang variant for xdp_map_access is O1); clang version not stated on the pages opened

name: cxx-ziggurat

name: BEAM.com (Erlang/OTP + Elixir single Cosmopolitan binary)

name: FlashTP (SNU-ARC)
baseline: e3nn o3.TensorProduct (uvu, with torch_scatter) and NVIDIA cuEquivariance
one_liner: Fused, sparsity-aware CUDA kernels for e3nn's channelwise (uvu) tensor product; paper reports up to 41.6x over e3nn.

name: RFUSE

baseline: FFTW 3.3.5 (planning excluded from run time), Intel MKL (version not stated), PFT (snudatalab/PFT, KDD 2021) and FFTW's pruned FFT (fftw.org/pruned.html); all single precision, with tolerances set so every method keeps relative l2 error below 1e-6.

name: sockudo-ws

one_liner: Rust WebSocket library (Tokio/Compio; HTTP/1.1, /2, /3) that self-reports 2-3% higher echo throughput than uWebSockets.

name: bitcode

one_liner: Rust-only columnar, bit-packed serializer; on string-heavy logs it encodes 5-14x faster than prost, FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto, rmp-serde.

name: Quantum++
baseline: Qiskit (QFT) and QuTiP (partial trace, memory ceiling)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 quantum-computing library on Eigen; its 2018 paper says single-core runs beat Qiskit (QFT) and QuTiP (partial trace).

baseline: Apache Thrift (binary protocol)

name: Sogou C++ Workflow (HTTP Server)
baseline: nginx

baseline: std::lower_bound (primary), std::set (bench code binsearch/set.cc actually uses std::multiset), absl::btree

one_liner: Rust RFC 5322/MIME e-mail parser with SIMD scanning and lazy zero-copy decoding; 9x to 31x GMime, VMime, libEtPan!, Dovecot.

name: RESTinio
baseline: Restbed v4.6 (also compared against C++ REST SDK v2.10.15, Crow v0.1, cpp-httplib v0.5.8, Pistache v0.0.002 in the same table)

name: STM32 Low Layer (LL) driver library
baseline: STM32 HAL drivers (HAL_GPIO_WritePin)
one_liner: ST's Low Layer (LL) drivers: static inline register-access calls that replace HAL calls such as HAL_GPIO_WritePin.

name: CHT (Compact Hist-Tree)
baseline: RMI, PGM-index, RadixSpline (learned index baselines)
one_liner: Header-only C++ compact Hist-Tree: a flattened radix-histogram table over sorted integer keys, beating RMI/PGM/RadixSpline lookup latency.

name: PLEX / TrieSpline
baseline: B-tree (and ART, PGM-index)
one_liner: Read-only learned index for sorted integer keys: error-bounded spline plus auto-tuned radix tree; ~2x faster lookups than B-tree.

name: hsvbench (branchless HSV to RGB)
baseline: the repo's own hsv_to_rgb in hsv.h: the common 6-way switch formula seen in StackOverflow answers (calls double-precision floor() and branches on the hue sector); a naive in-repo baseline, not an incumbent library
one_liner: Branchless, expression-only HSV-to-RGB float function in a public-domain C header, about 5.7x faster than the textbook 6-way switch on random input.

name: DRPC
baseline: gRPC
one_liner: Storj's small Go replacement for grpc-go, using its own framed protocol instead of HTTP/2; not wire-compatible with gRPC.

name: strager/perfect-hash-tables
baseline: gperf
one_liner: Research generator of CRC32-hashed perfect hash tables for 80 JS/TS keywords; beats gperf ~1.2-1.4x except on keyword-only input.

name: IsoAlloc
baseline: glibc malloc only (the 'jemalloc' row of PERFORMANCE.md actually times IsoAlloc)
one_liner: Security-hardened C11 malloc replacement (size-isolated zones, guard pages, canaries) that runs near glibc ptmalloc speed.

name: zaw (Zero-Allocation WASM)
language: Zig and Rust (WebAssembly) with TypeScript host
baseline: Plain JavaScript loop and Rust wasm-bindgen
one_liner: Fixed-buffer JS-to-WASM call protocol (TypeScript host, Zig/Rust modules); 3.3-6.9x faster than wasm-bindgen on 100+ element typed-array calls.

name: submilli-wasm
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift), Wasmer (Cranelift) startup
one_liner: Safe-Rust Wasm 3.0 interpreter with a wasmtime-shaped API; compiles modules about 90x faster than Wasmtime's Cranelift JIT.

name: sonnet
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Pure-Go rewrite of encoding/json with the same API; decodes typed structs about 4x faster than the stdlib in author benchmarks.

name: LRB (Learning Relaxed Belady) / webcachesim2
baseline: LRU
one_liner: ML (LightGBM) CDN cache-eviction policy approximating relaxed Belady; cuts simulated WAN traffic 4-25% vs Bloom-filter LRU.

name: AmgT (tensor-core AMG)
baseline: HYPRE (GPU build calling cuSPARSE)
one_liner: Modified HYPRE 2.31 whose BoomerAMG SpGEMM and SpMV run on tensor cores; beats stock GPU HYPRE with cuSPARSE.

name: DASP (dense-tensor-core SpMV)
baseline: cuSPARSE CSR SpMV (CUSPARSE_SPMV_ALG_DEFAULT); also CSR5, TileSpMV, LSRB-CSR and cuSPARSE BSR in the paper
one_liner: CUDA SpMV that repacks CSR rows into 8x4 tiles for FP64/FP16 tensor-core MMA; beats cuSPARSE CSR SpMV on A100.

name: PanguLU
baseline: SuperLU_DIST
one_liner: Distributed MPI+CUDA sparse LU direct solver using regular 2D sparse blocks; reports up to 11.7-18x over SuperLU_DIST on 128 GPUs.

name: TileSpGEMM (tiled GPU SpGEMM)
baseline: cuSPARSE, bhSPARSE, NSPARSE and spECK SpGEMM
one_liner: Research CUDA SpGEMM on 16x16 sparse tiles; PPoPP '22 reports wins over cuSPARSE on 139 of 142 large matrices.

name: TileSpMV
baseline: Merge-SpMV (Merrill and Garland), CSR5 and BSR SpMV on NVIDIA GPUs, as named in the IPDPS 2021 abstract. The BSR implementation is presumably cuSPARSE bsrmv, but the snippets do not say so, and whether cuSPARSE CSR was also compared is unconfirmed.
one_liner: CUDA SpMV on 16x16 sparse tiles with per-tile format choice; paper beats Merge-SpMV, CSR5 and BSR on most SuiteSparse matrices.

name: SupXML (sup-xml)
license: Proprietary source-available (Supported Source; LICENSE requires a paid or free-tier license certificate to use the code; not OSI)
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: Source-available Rust XML stack with a libxml2-compatible C ABI; the vendor reports ~2.1x median DOM-parse throughput over libxml2.

name: sst-basic-blocks LanczosResampler (Surge)
license: MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later (LanczosResampler.h is dual licensed; the rest of sst-basic-blocks is GPL-3.0-or-later)
baseline: libsamplerate sinc resampling (SRC_SINC_FASTEST in the NonIntegerSRC harness); the issue says only 'Sinc interpolation'
one_liner: Surge's 8-tap table-driven SSE Lanczos stereo resampler for real-time audio; claimed about 2x faster than libsamplerate's fastest sinc.

name: SurrealKV
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: SurrealDB's pure-Rust async LSM key-value engine with OCC transactions; vendor benchmark shows ~3x RocksDB fsync'd write throughput.

name: Glyd
license: BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0 (codec); glyd-store and GPU package under BUSL-1.1
baseline: zstd -3 (also LZ4, zstd -19)
one_liner: Rust LZ/entropy codec with a C ABI whose blocks decode in parallel; mixed one-core result against zstd -3, wins multicore reads.

name: Kaoken (baked-weight C code generation for CPU transformer inference)
baseline: PyTorch CPU layers (transformers GPT-2 building blocks)
one_liner: Python generator that emits GPT-2 layers as straight-line C with baked weights; first-party per-layer timings beat PyTorch CPU.

name: libdill
baseline: Go goroutines (also gccgo)
one_liner: C structured-concurrency library with stackful coroutines; project numbers show roughly 20x cheaper switches than Go goroutines.

name: libmill
baseline: Boost.Context (boost) and libco in the same shootout
one_liner: Go-style coroutines and channels for C; in a third-party switch shootout it beats libco and sometimes Boost.Context.

name: Duktape
baseline: MuJS 1.3.8 (embeddable JavaScript interpreter); QuickJS 2026.06.04 is faster than Duktape in the same table
one_liner: Compact, portable embeddable ES5.1 JavaScript interpreter in C; about 1.6x MuJS on Linux/macOS, about half QuickJS's speed.

name: fcp
baseline: GNU cp
one_liner: Parallel Rust replacement for the common cp -R cases; about 10x faster than GNU cp on a Linux kernel tree on SSD.

name: FastTanhSinhQuadrature.jl (Julia tanh-sinh quadrature)
baseline: Cubature.jl (wrapper of the C cubature library, h- and p-adaptive) and Cuba.jl (wrapper of the C Cuba library: Vegas, Divonne, Cuhre) for 2D and 3D integrals; QuadGK.jl and FastGaussQuadrature.jl (Julia) for 1D
one_liner: Julia tanh-sinh (double-exponential) quadrature for 1D-3D boxes; beats Cubature/Cuba C wrappers on endpoint-singular and low-order integrands.

name: swenson/sort (sort.h)
baseline: qsort (C standard library)
one_liner: Single C89 header that macro-generates type-specialised quick, heap, tim, merge and shell sorts that beat libc qsort.

name: WasmKit register-based interpreter (swiftwasm/WasmKit)
license: MIT (runtime modules); the GDBRemoteProtocol and WasmKitGDBHandler modules are Apache-2.0 with a Runtime Library Exception
baseline: WasmKit's own previous (second-generation) stack-based interpreter; also charted against wasm3, stitch and wasmi
one_liner: Pure-Swift embeddable WebAssembly interpreter; register-based VM scores 7.5x its old stack interpreter on CoreMark, roughly level with wasm3.

name: SWIG
baseline: SWIG's own default Python proxy-class wrappers (same tool, default code generation mode)
one_liner: Interface-file-driven C/C++ binding generator; its -builtin and -fastproxy Python modes roughly halve SWIG's own default per-call overhead.

name: Sycamore
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust/Wasm fine-grained-reactive UI library; its 2023 beta ran the keyed DOM benchmark about 1.4x faster than React 19.2 hooks.

name: benchmark-rngs PhiloxSIMD (AVX Philox4x32-10)
baseline: xoshiro256**, PCG64 and std::mt19937 (also an at::mt19937 implementation shipped in the repo)
one_liner: AVX2 8-lane Philox4x32-10 engine in a 2019 benchmark harness; 3.7x xoshiro256** and 9x std::mt19937 single-thread.

name: Cacheus
license: reference (no LICENSE file found in repo)
baseline: LRU
one_liner: Research Python simulator of Cacheus (FAST'21), a learned two-expert page-cache eviction policy that competes with ARC/LIRS/DLIRS on hit rate.

name: SYLT-FFT (fixed-point FFT for Cortex-M4)
license: MHG (Moral High Ground) license: the Unlicense text released 'under the single condition that good moral standards are maintained in its use', plus non-binding requests; custom, not an OSI/SPDX license (the README calls it GPL-compatible)
baseline: CMSIS-DSP arm_cfft_radix2_q31 (arm_cortexM4I_math.lib 1.4.2)
one_liner: Header-only 32-bit fixed-point radix-2 (I)FFT for Cortex-M4; 15-26% faster than CMSIS-DSP arm_cfft_radix2_q31 on a 256-point inverse.

name: SymEngine
baseline: SymPy (pure Python, called through PythonCall.jl)
one_liner: C++ symbolic algebra core (expand, diff, series, subs, lambdify) that runs SymPy-style workloads 10x to 1000x faster than pure-Python SymPy.

name: UnQLite
baseline: SQLite (Python sqlite3 module, one INSERT then commit per key; one SELECT per key)
one_liner: Single-file embedded C key/value and JSON document store (linear hashing); faster than SQLite only for point lookups in one informal Python test.

name: Sympiler
baseline: Eigen sparse (triangular solve, Cholesky); CHOLMOD
one_liner: Sparse-matrix code generator and kernel library; SC17 Cholesky 3.8x average over Eigen, 1.5x over CHOLMOD on fixed patterns.

name: rkvdec-vdpu383 HEVC/H.264 read-cache fix
baseline: Mainline Linux rkvdec-vdpu383 HEVC and H.264 backends (upstream driver without read-cache configuration); vendor MPP stack as reference
one_liner: Linux kernel patch that turns on the RK3576 VDPU383 decoder's read caches, cutting mainline HEVC/H.264 hardware decode time several-fold.

name: FastFormat
baseline: C stdio snprintf (printf family), plus C++ IOStreams and Boost.Format
one_liner: Type-safe C++ formatting library (positional fmt and concatenating write) that beats IOStreams and Boost.Format; mixed against printf.

name: tir (tiny image resize, in tinyexr)
baseline: stb_image_resize2 (successor of stb_image_resize, matched filter, float32 path); also tinyexr's own exr_resize_float
one_liner: Pure-C11 separable float resizer in tinyexr's tools/resize; 2.2-3.6x tinyexr's own resizer, roughly level with SSE2-built stb_image_resize2.

name: rv32emu (tiered JIT)
baseline: QEMU v9.0.0 (RV32 user-mode emulation)
one_liner: RV32 RISC-V emulator in C with an interpreter, template JIT and LLVM tier; charted 1.25-2.85x faster than QEMU 9.0 user mode.

name: MANGO image codecs
baseline: libpng (via find_module(PNG), version and zlib build not stated); 'libjpeg' is whatever jpeglib.h find_module(JPEG) linked, used through the libjpeg API one scanline at a time. one_liner: C++20 graphics library whose multi-threaded PNG/JPEG codecs beat single-threaded libpng and libjpeg, mostly on mango-encoded files.

name: Tachyon JSON (Rust, TachyonConcepts)
baseline: serde_json
one_liner: Tiny unsafe Rust JSON writer for compile-time-constant objects into a fixed stack buffer; claims 8 ns vs serde_json's 23 ns.

name: FP-ASM (FP_ASM_LIB_DEV)
language: Assembly (NASM x86-64 AVX2) with a C API
baseline: Scalar C reference loops compiled with gcc 13 -O3 -march=native
one_liner: NASM AVX2 kernels with a C API for float reductions, dot products and batched vec3/mat4 math; beats strict-order scalar C loops.

name: LWMalloc
baseline: glibc ptmalloc
one_liner: 618-line single-file C malloc for embedded Linux, injected via LD_PRELOAD; paper claims up to 53% faster than glibc ptmalloc.

name: quick-xml
baseline: libxml2 and pugixml
one_liner: Rust StAX-style XML pull reader/writer; streams real-world XML 1.84x faster than libxml2 SAX, serializes 1.22x faster than pugixml.

name: llama2.mojo
baseline: llama2.c (karpathy/llama2.c, OpenMP build); also llama.cpp CPU
one_liner: Single-file Mojo port of karpathy's llama2.c fp32 CPU inference; 1.1-1.5x llama2.c tok/s in the author's same-session runs.

name: katsu
baseline: Node.js 26.8.1 (V8); Bun 1.4.0 and Deno 2.9.6 are also measured
one_liner: Pre-alpha JavaScript runtime in Rust (bytecode interpreter today) that starts a hello world about 16x faster than Node and 3x faster than Bun.

name: taoJSON
baseline: nlohmann/json (Nlohmann v2.0.3 row in nativejson-benchmark)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 JSON/CBOR/MsgPack/UBJSON value-and-events library; beat nlohmann 2.0.3 in a 2016 run, mainly on number-heavy JSON.

name: PEGTL (JSON grammar)
baseline: nlohmann/json (nlohmann::json::accept validation)
one_liner: Header-only C++ PEG parser-combinator library; its JSON grammar validates 1.7-5.5x faster than nlohmann::json::accept in lexy's benchmark.

name: TDengine
baseline: InfluxDB 2.0 and TimescaleDB 2.6.0 (PostgreSQL 12)
one_liner: Clustered C time-series database for IoT; about 8.5x InfluxDB 2.0 and 5.6x TimescaleDB ingest in one rival-run shootout.

name: SampleRateTap (async engine)
baseline: libsamplerate 0.2.2 (Secret Rabbit Code, MEDIUM and BEST converters)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 near-unity ASRC for clock-drift bridging; its datapath beats libsamplerate MEDIUM/BEST at near-unity ratios.

name: libdart
baseline: nlohmann/json (version not stated); the same run also has RapidJSON, sajson, YAJL and Jansson
one_liner: C++14 JSON library whose finalized flat binary packets parse 9.2x faster than nlohmann/json and read with zero parsing.

name: RA-SpMM (regime-aware GPU SpMM router for GNN workloads)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpMM (FP32, cusparseSpMM)
one_liner: Rule-based GPU SpMM dispatcher (five CSR/tensor-core kernels) for GNN graphs, 1.70x warm geomean over FP32 cuSPARSE.

name: Taskflow
baseline: Intel oneTBB (FlowGraph task scheduler)
one_liner: Header-only C++ task-graph library that beats oneTBB FlowGraph on heterogeneous CPU+GPU DAG workloads.

name: bfs
baseline: GNU find 4.6.0 / fd
one_liner: Breadth-first, find-compatible directory search tool with parallel async I/O; about 3x faster than GNU find on full traversals.

name: args (Taywee)
baseline: Boost.Program_options (also TCLAP)
one_liner: Single-header C++11 command-line parser in the style of Python argparse; its 2016 benchmark ran 2.2x faster than Boost.Program_options.

name: tbox (coroutine switch)
baseline: Boost.Context (boost), libco (Tencent), libgo(boost), libmill, libtask, Go, cloudwu coroutine, acl libfiber
one_liner: glib-like C library whose stackful coroutine scheduler switches faster than Boost.Coroutine and libco in its author's benchmark.

name: during (D io_uring wrapper)
baseline: C liburing echo server (MarkReedZ/mrloop) and C++ epoll echo server (methane/echoserver), both built with -O3; in the httpbench suite also the C liburing HTTP-reply server
one_liner: Low-level D binding to Linux io_uring (no liburing); author's echo and HTTP microbenchmarks edge C liburing servers.

name: FlexTOE
baseline: Linux host TCP stack, TAS (TCP Acceleration as an OS Service), and the Chelsio Terminator hardware TCP offload engine
one_liner: Netronome Agilio SmartNIC TCP offload engine running the established-connection data path on-NIC; beats Linux, TAS and Chelsio TOE.

name: SpeedyXml (SpeedyXml-cpp)
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: C++20 streaming SAX-style XML push parser with zero-copy callbacks; author-measured 4.4x faster than libxml2's SAX2 streaming parser.

name: ibig
baseline: GNU GMP (mpz, via the Rust rug 1.30.0 crate; gmp-mpfr-sys 1.7.1 pinned in Cargo.lock)
one_liner: Pure-Rust big integers that beat GMP (via rug) only on one-word (<=64-bit) values and on string parsing.

name: tdewolff/canvas
baseline: Inkscape and Cairo (named in the README as 'existing solutions'; which Cairo-based tool was run, e.g. rsvg-convert or CairoSVG, is not stated on any readable page)
one_liner: Pure-Go vector drawing library (paths, booleans, text, raster/PDF/SVG/EPS output); claims 2x over Inkscape/Cairo, no published numbers.

name: Cuckoo-GPU
baseline: cuckoo filter
one_liner: Header-only CUDA cuckoo filter with lock-free batched insert/query/delete; outpaces multi-threaded CPU cuckoo filters and GPU TCF/GQF.

name: cuSBF (GPU Minimizer-Aware Super Bloom Filter)
baseline: Bloom filter (NVIDIA cuCollections GPU Blocked Bloom Filter, GBBF)
one_liner: Header-only CUDA Super Bloom filter for DNA k-mers; 7.6-9.1x faster than cuCollections' GPU blocked Bloom on RTX PRO 6000.

name: CharLS
baseline: WebP lossless via Pillow 10.1.0 (libwebp, quality=100, method 1 and 5), Pillow PNG plugin (zlib, not libpng) and Pillow JPEG 2000 plugin (OpenJPEG), all run in-process in Image-Compression-Benchmark; the CharLS README separately cites the original HP JPEG-LS code, JPEG-XR and JPEG 2000
one_liner: C++17 JPEG-LS (ISO 14495-1) lossless/near-lossless codec; encodes about 10x faster than libwebp lossless, decodes slower.

name: VectorJSON

baseline: Stock streaming/partial JSON parsers in the Vercel AI SDK, Anthropic SDK, TanStack AI and OpenClaw (JavaScript, run under Bun); JSON.parse for one-shot parsing
one_liner: Incremental streaming partial-JSON parser for LLM tool calls (Zig to WASM plus TypeScript); beats AI SDKs' re-parse-every-chunk loops.

name: Quicker ADC (faiss-quickeradc)
baseline: FAISS PQ ADC (IndexPQ-style m x 8 float lookup-table scan, FAISS as of mid-2018) and polysemous codes
one_liner: 2018 FAISS fork that scans PQ codes with quantized in-register lookup tables; about 4-5x faster than FAISS PQ ADC at equal recall.

name: PQ Fast Scan
baseline: PQ Scan (product quantization distance scan with lookup tables in L1 cache; the project's own reference implementation, also with SSE, AVX and AVX gather variants)
one_liner: Research C++ kernel for 8x8-bit product-quantization nearest-neighbour scans: keeps lookup tables in SSE registers, 4-6x faster than scalar PQ Scan.

name: Quick ADC
baseline: ADC (asymmetric distance computation in product quantization, lookup tables in L1 cache; the authors' scalar implementation)
one_liner: Research C++14 PQ search engine whose AVX2 scan uses 4-bit sub-quantizers and pshufb tables; about 3.8x faster scans than scalar ADC.

name: BlazeDiff core-wasm (@blazediff/core-wasm)
baseline: pixelmatch (JavaScript)
one_liner: Rust image diff compiled to wasm32 with v128 SIMD; pixelmatch-style YIQ diff counts, about 2-6x faster than pixelmatch on large differing images.

name: Tempesta FW (Tempesta TLS)
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Linux-kernel TLS 1.2 server stack in the Tempesta FW proxy; 6-83% more handshakes/s than Nginx+OpenSSL in vendor tests.

name: BqLog
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Tencent's C++ async logger with a real-time compressed binary format; much higher end-to-end throughput than spdlog async and glog.

name: FeatherCNN
baseline: Caffe2 with Eigen, Caffe with OpenBLAS, Caffe2 with NNPACK, TensorFlow Lite, ARM Compute Library, TVM
one_liner: Small dependency-free ARM CPU CNN inference library; 2017 wiki shows 2-13x lower latency than Caffe+OpenBLAS and Caffe2+Eigen.

name: TGFX (Tencent Graphics)
baseline: Skia (m136)
one_liner: Tencent's GPU-only C++17 2D renderer (PAG's engine), claimed 10-16x more animated rectangles per frame than Skia Ganesh m136.

name: TQUIC
baseline: quiche
one_liner: Tencent's Rust QUIC/HTTP3 library with C API: ~2.4x quiche on request and stream-churn rate, slower on bulk.

name: TACO (Tensor Algebra Compiler)
baseline: Eigen (sparse), Intel MKL, OSKI and pOSKI, uBLAS and Gmm++ for sparse linear algebra; SPLATT and the MATLAB Tensor Toolbox for sparse 3rd-order tensor kernels
one_liner: Compiler that generates fused C/CUDA kernels for any sparse/dense tensor expression; matches Eigen and MKL, beats uBLAS, Gmm++ and MATLAB Tensor Toolbox.

name: TensorBase
baseline: ClickHouse
one_liner: Abandoned Rust ClickHouse-protocol server on forked DataFusion; 3.1x faster than ClickHouse on plain sum, 6.7x slower on group-by.

name: TensorFlow
baseline: PyTorch (NGC PyTorch 1.5.0a0+8f84ded, container nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:20.03-py3)
one_liner: Google's ML framework; with XLA plus mixed precision (NVIDIA's 2020 TF 1.15 build) it out-trained NGC PyTorch on ResNet-50 and BERT-base.

name: TensorFlow.js WebAssembly backend (tfjs-backend-wasm)
baseline: TensorFlow.js plain JavaScript CPU backend in V8 (Chrome); also compared with the WebGL backend
one_liner: TensorFlow.js backend that runs XNNPACK C++ kernels compiled to WebAssembly; 3-20x faster than the plain-JS CPU backend for CNN inference.

name: ultraviolet
baseline: glam single-lane types (glam_f32x1) in mathbench; nalgebra wide types tie

name: Terra
baseline: Lua (PUC)

name: UASM
baseline: MASM (Microsoft Macro Assembler 6.15 and 10.0)
one_liner: Open-source MASM-syntax x86/x64 assembler descended from JWasm; forum timings put it modestly ahead of MASM, behind JWasm and AsmC.

name: MTGEMM-A
baseline: Apple Accelerate sgemm/dgemm (also OpenBLAS develop and 0.3.34, Eigen master, LIBXSMM, KleidiAI)
one_liner: SME2 FP32/FP64 GEMM for Apple M4 Pro, rebuilt from the MpGEMM paper: 1.18-1.26x Apple Accelerate on the paper's workloads.

name: Tesseract
baseline: EasyOCR (PyTorch CRAFT+CRNN, run on GPU with batch_size 16)
one_liner: Classic CPU OCR engine (LSTM line recognizer); with one process per core it out-throughputs single-stream GPU EasyOCR.

name: tsl::array_map / array-hash (Tessil)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only cache-conscious string hash map/set (Askitis array hash); about half the memory of std::unordered_map<std::string,T>, 1.3-2.3x faster lookups.

name: tsl::htrie_map (hat-trie)
baseline: std::unordered_map<std::string, int> (memory, and speed on the Askitis set) and cedar::da double-array trie (memory and speed on the Wikipedia set)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 HAT-trie string map/set using about 3x less memory than std::unordered_map<std::string, T>.

name: tsl::hopscotch_map (Tessil/hopscotch-map)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only C++17 hopscotch-hashing hash map/set, faster than std::unordered_map with dense_hash_map-like speed.

name: tsl::ordered_map (Tessil/ordered-map)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Insertion-order-preserving hash map/set beating std::unordered_map on inserts, misses, and iteration.

name: tsl::robin_map (Tessil/robin-map)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only robin hood open-addressing hash map/set beating std::unordered_map on insert, lookup, erase, and iteration.

name: pocketlang

one_liner: Zig/WASM polygon booleans and rounded buffer for web GIS; 2.7-3.3x faster than native GEOS on a 4,040-parcel union.

name: Ant (Ant Silver JavaScript engine)
baseline: QuickJS 2026-06-04 (also Duktape 2.99.99 / 2.7.0; its own README compares cold start against Node, Bun and Deno)
one_liner: Small JavaScript runtime with its own engine and a MIR-based JIT; about 1.8-2.0x QuickJS on the v8-v7 suite.

name: muFFT
baseline: KissFFT
one_liner: Small MIT C99 single-precision power-of-two FFT with runtime SSE/SSE3/AVX dispatch; 5-9x faster than KissFFT, near FFTW.

name: streamvbyte-simdgo
baseline: Go encoding/binary Uvarint/PutUvarint (LEB128 varint), via the repo's util.GetVarint/PutVarint wrappers
one_liner: Go port of Stream VByte with avo-generated AVX/AVX2 assembly; decodes uint32 arrays 8-14x faster than encoding/binary Uvarint loops.

name: rpp (TheNumbat/rpp) compile-time-oriented containers and allocators
baseline: std::vector, std::unordered_map and the other STL container headers (MSVC STL)
one_liner: Rust-style C++20 base library (Vec, Map, String, allocators, threads, async) that avoids STL headers to cut compile time.

name: sol2
baseline: Other C++ Lua binding libraries (LuaBridge, OOLua, Kaguya, luwra, Selene, SWIG, tolua++ and others); floor is the plain Lua C API
one_liner: Header-only C++17 Lua binding whose wrapper overhead sits closest to the raw Lua C API among 15 binding libraries.

name: rawscan
license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT OR GPL-2.0 (author's choice; PCG code in generate_input_data.c is Apache-2.0)
baseline: fgets, getline (glibc stdio)
one_liner: Small Linux C line reader over a raw fd; about 30-40% less user CPU than fgets or getline on large inputs.

name: micromalloc
baseline: glibc malloc
one_liner: Low-overhead general-purpose C/C++ malloc that usually beats glibc malloc on speed while using about as little memory.

name: Stenos
baseline: Blosc2 byte shuffle + Zstd and Blosc2 bitshuffle + Zstd
one_liner: C/C++ compressor for arrays of fixed-size numeric elements that picks its own filter; claims better ratio and speed than Blosc2+Zstd.

name: Exposed (reflectionless RPC for Go)
baseline: gRPC
one_liner: Go RPC library over one batched TCP connection, derived from valyala/fastrpc; README shows ~1.1-3x gRPC echo throughput.

name: gopus (pure-Go Opus codec)
baseline: libopus 1.6.1 (C reference encoder and decoder, SIMD build)
one_liner: Pure-Go (no cgo) Opus encoder/decoder whose SIMD build roughly matches, and in most tested encode cases beats, SIMD libopus 1.6.1.

name: haya32x64
baseline: xxHash (XXH64, via xxhash-wasm)
one_liner: 64-bit non-cryptographic hash built only from 32-bit operations. In pure JS it beats xxhash-wasm XXH64 on 4-8 byte keys.

name: hayahash
baseline: xxHash (XXH3-64 and XXH64)
one_liner: Portable scalar 64/128-bit C hash; beats XXH3-64 by about 1.35x on 1 MiB bulk in SIMD-less wasm32.

name: ocaml-curve448
baseline: OpenSSL 3.6.4 (`openssl speed`, EVP Ed448/X448)
one_liner: OCaml X448/Ed448 library whose optional fiat-crypto C backend roughly matches OpenSSL 3.6.4 on X448 and Ed448 signing; verification is slower.

name: verztable
baseline: absl::flat_hash_map/flat_hash_set, boost::unordered_flat_map/unordered_flat_set and ankerl::unordered_dense::map/set (src/cpp_hashtables_wrapper.cpp); integer keys use each library's default hash, string keys use std::string_view with a shared wyhash. The 'std' column is Zig's std.AutoHashMap/StringHashMap, not std::unordered_map.
one_liner: Zig port of Verstable's chained open-addressing hash table; edges Abseil/Boost/Ankerl on small and string-keyed tables only.

name: ChainHash
baseline: XXH3-64 (xxHash)
one_liner: Keyed 64-bit carry-less universal hash with a Lean-proved collision bound; beats XXH3-64 on long in-cache inputs.

name: minperf (RecSplit implementation)
baseline: CHD algorithm, implementation not named in the comment. The README says performance is 'very similar' to the Sux4J CHD and GOV algorithms, so the baseline is most likely Sux4J's Java CHDMinimalPerfectHashFunction. CMPH is not mentioned anywhere.
one_liner: Thomas Mueller's Java RecSplit minimal perfect hash: about 2 bits/key, lookups ~1.1x faster than CHD in one code comment.

name: fast-srgb8
baseline: naive powf-based sRGB transfer function (reference implementation inside the crate's own benchmark)
one_liner: Tiny no_std Rust crate: table-based linear-f32 to sRGB-u8 and back, several times faster than per-call powf.

name: ThorVG
baseline: Skia (CPU raster backend, Skia v148)
one_liner: MIT C++ SVG/Lottie vector engine; its CPU renderer averaged 2.9x Skia raster fps on 5k-shape scenes (4 threads vs 1).

name: Thruster (Rust, thruster-grpc)
baseline: gRPC C++ (grpc/grpc) servers cpp_grpc_st, cpp_grpc_mt and cpp_asio_grpc in the grpc_bench suite
one_liner: Koa-style Rust web framework whose experimental thruster-grpc server, on hyper/h2, out-served gRPC C++ in grpc_bench unary echo.

name: SageAttention (SageAttention, SageAttention2, SageAttention2++)
language: CUDA/C++ and Triton with Python API
baseline: FlashAttention2 (also FlashAttention3 and FlashAttention3-FP8)
one_liner: Quantized (INT8 QK, FP8/FP16 PV) forward attention kernels for NVIDIA GPUs that outrun FlashAttention2 and match FlashAttention3-FP8.

name: SpargeAttn (SpargeAttention)
language: C++ (CUDA) with Python bindings; Triton example
baseline: FlashAttention2 (Figure 2 legend 'FlashAttn'; Table 1 'Full-Attention' does not name the implementation)
one_liner: Training-free block-sparse, INT8/FP8-quantized attention kernels; 1.8-4.5x per-layer over full attention in model runs, approximate.

name: TriCache
baseline: mmap and Linux swap (OS page cache)
one_liner: User-space multi-level block cache over SPDK SSDs that runs unmodified in-memory programs out-of-core, beating Linux swap and mmap.

name: matmul-cpu (core_v5 GEMM kernels)
baseline: OpenBLAS (sgemm, C=A*B^T+C)
one_liner: Learning-project AVX-512 FP32 GEMM (row-major C += A*B^T) that edges past OpenBLAS at 4096^3 on 24 threads only.

name: TidesDB
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Embeddable transactional LSM key-value engine in C; the author's benchmark shows 4-5x RocksDB's iterator-seek throughput at about 3.5x the memory.

name: bluebox
baseline: redis-server (its epoll event loop)
one_liner: Toy Redis-protocol server (SET/GET/DEL/PING) showcasing Neco coroutines; first-party memtier run shows 2.4x redis-server throughput.

name: evio (Go epoll/kqueue event loop; Redis clone vs real Redis)
baseline: Redis 4.0.2 (C, single-threaded ae event loop on epoll) answering PING_INLINE; the same table also holds Go net/http, fasthttp and a Go net echo server, which are Go baselines and not counted here
one_liner: Go event-loop framework using raw epoll/kqueue; its toy Redis clone out-served Redis 4.0.2 on pipelined PING.

name: gjson
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Go library that reads single values from JSON by dot-path without unmarshalling; 3.2-5.7x lower latency than encoding/json structs.

name: llco
license: Unlicense OR MIT-0 (README: Public Domain or MIT No Attribution)
baseline: none named
one_liner: Single-file C stackful coroutine switch (minicoro-derived assembly) with bring-your-own-stack; no scheduler, no benchmark against any baseline.

name: Neco
baseline: none named (README claims fast switching; ucontext fallback only)
one_liner: Single-file C coroutine runtime with Go-like channels, deterministic scheduler and epoll/kqueue I/O; about 11 ns switches, no baseline measured.

name: Pogocache
baseline: Redis, Memcached
one_liner: Multithreaded C cache server speaking RESP, memcache, HTTP and Postgres; about 2x Redis and 1.2-2.3x memcached throughput (author-run).

name: Redcon (Go Redis-compatible server framework; clone vs real Redis)
baseline: Redis (C, single-threaded, started as 'redis-server --port 6379 --appendonly no'; version not stated)
one_liner: Go framework for writing Redis-protocol servers; its 136-line map clone out-ran redis-server about 2x on a 2016 laptop pipeline test.

name: redcon.c
baseline: Redis 6.0.6 (the README writes 'Redis 6.06'), single-threaded stock redis-server
one_liner: Small C framework for Redis-protocol (RESP) servers on epoll/kqueue; its toy clone outruns Redis 6.0.6 under deep pipelining.

name: tidwall/rtree.c
baseline: Boost.Geometry 1.90 R*-tree
one_liner: Single-file C dynamic R-tree with O(1) copy-on-write clones; inserts 20-40x faster than Boost.Geometry's R*-tree.

name: TG (tidwall geometry library)
baseline: GEOS (PreparedGeometry and plain geometry)
one_liner: Single-file C11 planar geometry library whose indexed point-in-polygon and intersects tests beat GEOS PreparedGeometry by about 1.1-2.7x.

name: Titan (RocksDB plugin)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: RocksDB plugin that moves large values into separate blob files (WiscKey-style) to cut write amplification versus plain RocksDB.

name: stilus
baseline: golang.org/x/image/vector (the Go project's rasterizer) and gogpu/gg v0.52.5 CPU rasterizer
one_liner: Pure-Go sparse 2D rasterizer; 2.0x x/image/vector on 20k short strokes (first-party); 477x hatch figure is harness-inflated.

name: TinyCC (tcc)
baseline: GCC at -O0 (gcc 16.2.1 in compiler-benchmark, GCC 3.2 in the bellard.org table); also Clang 22.1.8 at -O0
one_liner: Tiny self-hosting C compiler/JIT that compiles about 9x faster than gcc -O0, trading away optimization.

name: msgp
baseline: MessagePack
one_liner: Go code generator for MessagePack; about 6-7x lower marshal/unmarshal latency than reflection-based vmihailenco/msgpack on the same wire format.

name: pengyhash
baseline: xxHash64
one_liner: Tiny multiply-free 64-bit ARX hash; its v0.2 beat xxHash64 bulk speed in rurban/smhasher, current v0.3 does not.

name: Wizard Research Engine
baseline: Rewriting Wasm interpreters wasm3 and WAMR fast-interp (iwasm-fast), plus WAMR classic interpreter and JavaScriptCore's Wasm LLInt (jsc-int); V8 Liftoff/TurboFan and SpiderMonkey tiers also measured (OOPSLA 2022 artifact)
one_liner: Research WebAssembly engine in Virgil whose in-place interpreter sets up code about 6x cheaper than wasm3 or WAMR-fast, but executes slower.

name: simd-f128
baseline: GCC __float128 (libquadmath)
one_liner: Header-only C11/C++11 double-double (about 106-bit, 31-digit) type, claimed 1.5-3.4x lower latency than GCC __float128.

name: aHash
baseline: xxHash (XXH3 via xxhash-rust) and wyhash; also SipHash-1-3, the Rust std HashMap default
one_liner: Keyed AES-round Rust hasher for in-memory HashMaps; about 11x faster than SipHash-1-3, claims wins over xxh3/wyhash.

name: tlx::btree_map / btree_set / btree_multimap (STX B+Tree lineage)
baseline: std::map, std::multiset
one_liner: Header-only B+ tree implementing STL's map/set/multimap/multiset; beats libstdc++'s red-black tree at large n.

name: go-byte-test (tmthrgd)
baseline: Go gc compiler output for the loop that checks every byte equals a value (BenchmarkGoTest)
one_liner: SSE assembly predicate for Go that checks whether every byte of a slice equals one value; 5-42x a naive Go loop.

name: tmthrgd/go-hex (SSE/AVX assembly hex)
baseline: Go standard library encoding/hex
one_liner: Go hex encode/decode with SSE4.1/AVX assembly; about 19x encoding/hex on encode and 4.6x on decode against current stdlib.

name: go-memset (tmthrgd): Go amd64 assembly memset
baseline: Go's own fill loop (README benchmarks BenchmarkGoSet for non-zero fill and BenchmarkGoZero for the zeroing loop idiom)
one_liner: Go amd64 assembly Memset for non-zero byte fills; 8-31x a plain Go fill loop, slower than Go's zeroing loop.

name: go-popcount (tmthrgd)
license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT (portions copyright 2015 Hideaki Ohno under MIT, per the LICENSE file and the headers of popcount.go, popcount_test.go and popcnt_amd64.s)
language: Go (x86-64 POPCNT assembly, popcnt_amd64.s and popcount_amd64.s)
baseline: Go loop over math/bits.OnesCount64 (BenchmarkCountBytesGo and BenchmarkCountSlice64Go)
one_liner: Go amd64 POPCNT assembly that counts set bits in []byte or []uint64, 1.2-2.9x a math/bits.OnesCount64 loop.

name: libmsdf
baseline: msdfgen (CPU MSDF generator; the lead's msdfgl was not compared either); neither is in the listed HarfBuzz/FreeType baselines
one_liner: Rust/wgpu SDF and MSDF text renderer whose WGSL compute shader generates MSDF glyphs at runtime; no speed data versus msdfgen.

name: Tokio (1M concurrent tasks, peak memory)
baseline: Asio C++20 coroutines (awaitable tasks) and concurrencpp
one_liner: Rust's work-stealing async runtime; 1M sleeping tasks used 2.8x less peak memory than concurrencpp and 4x less than Asio.

name: tokio-uring (HttpArena minimal HTTP/1.1 server)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native) in the HttpArena suite; h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma (C) and Drogon, Cutelyst, hical, agensio, userver (C++) rows alongside
one_liner: io_uring-backed Rust runtime; a hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 server on it edges nginx 1.09x in HttpArena but loses to plain epoll tokio.

name: warp_cache
baseline: cachetools (Python LRU/TTL cache library)
one_liner: Rust/PyO3 memoization decorator for Python with SIEVE eviction, TTL, async and mmap cross-process backend; ~25x cachetools, slower than lru_cache.

name: Prefix Filter
baseline: Bloom filter, cuckoo filter
one_liner: Insert-only AVX-512 filter with a fixed ~0.37% false-positive rate; builds over 3.2x faster than cuckoo filters in similar space.

name: fastbloom
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Rust Bloom filter crate: classic non-blocked layout, faster lookups than other Rust Bloom crates, plus a lock-free atomic variant.

name: Shine (fixed-point MP3 encoder)
baseline: LAME 3.100 (M1 Pro run) and LAME 3.99.5 (outdated Raspberry Pi run) CLI, 128 kbps CBR, qval=3, joint stereo with psychoacoustic model
one_liner: Small fixed-point C MP3 (Layer III) encoder that runs about 2-4x faster than LAME by skipping most of LAME's quality work.

name: Topaz (Ruby on RPython)
baseline: CRuby (MRI) 2.7.7p221 and 3.2.1p31, interpreter without JIT
one_liner: Ruby 1.9.3 subset on PyPy's RPython meta-tracing JIT; in one shootout beats CRuby 2.7.7 on 12 of 13 programs.

name: ToplingDB
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: RocksDB 8.10 fork with a trie memtable and searchable compressed SSTs; about 5x RocksDB's in-cache random-read throughput.

name: Torch7
baseline: Caffe (BVLC) and Theano
one_liner: Lua-scripted C tensor library (TH) behind the Torch7 framework; a 2015-16 Bosch study found it fastest on CPU versus Caffe and Theano.

name: WasmBoy
baseline: The same emulator core compiled to JavaScript through the TypeScript compiler (ES6), run in the browser
one_liner: AssemblyScript Game Boy/Color emulator whose one core builds to both Wasm and JS; benchmark app compares them per frame.

name: TPDE (TPDE-LLVM back-end)
baseline: LLVM -O0 code generation (clang/llc back-end)
one_liner: Single-pass baseline back-end framework; its LLVM-IR back-end compiles 10-20x faster than LLVM's -O0 back-end at similar code speed.

name: go-flac
baseline: FFmpeg native flac encoder (libavcodec); the same README table also measures libFLAC and SoX, and libFLAC is faster than go-flac
one_liner: Pure-Go (no cgo) FLAC encoder and decoder with AVX2/NEON kernels; encodes slightly faster than FFmpeg's flac, about 1.5x slower than libFLAC.

name: tphakala/simd
baseline: pure-Go scalar loops (same binary with SIMD_DISABLE=all, or each operation's *Go reference function)
one_liner: Go assembly SIMD kernels (AVX-512/AVX2/AVX/SSE2, NEON) for slice math and audio DSP; 2-16x over the library's own pure-Go loops.

name: chgemm
baseline: gemmlowp (int8 GEMM); also reported against the fp32 single-core peak of the same CPU
one_liner: Symmetric int8 x int8 to int32 GEMM for ARMv8 (aarch64) NEON, hand-written assembly; reported above gemmlowp on RK3399.

name: NativeLink
baseline: local, non-distributed single-machine build (no remote cache / no distributed compilation)
one_liner: REAPI remote build-cache and execution server for Bazel/Buck2/CMake; beats local-only, non-distributed builds.

name: Traefik (Go reverse proxy; TLS latency vs Nginx and HAProxy)
baseline: Nginx 1.28.3 (C, official nginx:1.28.3 image) and HAProxy 3.3.6 (C, official haproxy:3.3.6 image) in Docker. Configs read: nginx worker_processes auto, epoll, multi_accept, upstream keepalive 64, TLSv1.2/1.3 with ECDHE AES-GCM ciphers, no ssl_session_cache, proxy_buffers 8 4k; HAProxy maxconn 20000, no-tls-tickets, http-reuse always, alpn h2,http/1.1. All proxies use the same self-signed RSA-4096 certificate.
one_liner: Go reverse proxy and load balancer; one small third-party Docker test shows lower TLS (HTTP/2) tail latency than nginx at 5k req/s.

name: yam
baseline: libyaml
one_liner: Zero-copy C11 YAML 1.2 event parser and emitter with an SSE4.2 scanner; parses 1.6-13x faster than libyaml.

name: intel-tex-rs-2 (intel_tex_2)
baseline: Intel's upstream ISPCTextureCompressor (ispc_texcomp) kernels as vendored on the crate's main branch (GameTechDev submodule, built with ISPC 1.20), plus the same upstream kernels rebuilt with ISPC 1.31 (PR #49 column) to isolate the compiler change; all through the same Rust binding and criterion harness, not a separately built Intel ispc_texcomp library
one_liner: Rust bindings over a maintained fork of Intel's ISPC texture compressor; BC6H/BC7/ETC1 encode 2-6x faster than Intel's kernels on Apple Silicon.

name: AWFM-index (AvxWindowFmIndex)
baseline: SeqAn3 FM-index (built on sdsl-lite)
one_liner: C FM-index for DNA/RNA/protein exact k-mer count and locate; paper reports 2-6x faster than SeqAn3's FM-index.

name: AWRY
baseline: AvxWindowFmIndex (C), SeqAn3 FM-index, SDSL
one_liner: Rust port of the AVX2 windowed FM-index (AvxWindowFmIndex); in the only third-party benchmark found it is slower than genedex.

name: flatty
baseline: Nim std/marshal
one_liner: Binary serializer for plain Nim types; ~38x faster serialize, ~36x faster deserialize than JSON-based std/marshal.

name: libbzip2-rs (libbz2-rs-sys, Rust port of libbzip2)
baseline: libbzip2 (C, original bzip2 library)
one_liner: Memory-safe Rust port of libbzip2 exposing the same C API; about 11% fewer compression cycles than C libbzip2 on x86-64.

name: Basker (ShyLU threaded sparse LU, in Trilinos)
baseline: KLU (SuiteSparse) and Intel MKL PARDISO
one_liner: Threaded sparse LU (Trilinos ShyLU-Basker) for low-fill circuit matrices; paper reports 5.9x geomean over sequential KLU on 16 cores.

name: Lace (trolando)
baseline: Intel TBB, Cilk Plus (Cilk++), OpenMP and Wool (Wool is the parity target, not a claimed loss)
one_liner: C11 fork-join work-stealing runtime (split deque, leapfrogging) from the Sylvan BDD author; claims Wool-level overhead, no reproducible numbers against TBB, Cilk or OpenMP.

name: uthash
baseline: std::unordered_map (libstdc++ from GCC 13.2.0)
one_liner: Header-only intrusive C hash table (macros); in one third-party benchmark it iterates and erases faster than std::unordered_map but loses most lookups.

name: TurboPython / tpy (typed Python to C++ without GC)
baseline: CPython (Shed Skin, Cython, mypyc, Nuitka and Codon appear in the README only as design contrasts, with no timings)
one_liner: Pre-1.0 compiler from annotated Python to C++23 binaries without GC or refcounting; no published speed numbers against CPython.

name: Rayon vs OpenMP (CMU 15-618 project)
baseline: C++ with OpenMP (and GNU parallel-mode sort) for Mandelbrot, matrix multiplication, sorting and reduction; C++ compiled with GCC per the report
one_liner: 2019 CMU course study timing Rust+Rayon against C++/OpenMP on four kernels; Rayon wins only large parallel stable sorts.

name: TrueAsync Server (PHP extension with a C core, HttpArena true-async-server entry)
language: C (PHP extension; HttpArena labels the entry PHP)
baseline: nginx (C, custom handler module compiled -O3 -march=native, per HttpArena frameworks.json); Drogon (C++, CMake Release build), h2o (C), agensio and proxygen (C++) rows from the same suite
one_liner: C HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server inside PHP (TrueAsync fork) that out-runs HttpArena's nginx on small-response HTTP/2.

name: flash-attention-minimal (forward-only FlashAttention in about 100 lines of CUDA)
baseline: naive PyTorch attention (eager matmul + softmax + matmul)
one_liner: Educational 100-line FP32 CUDA FlashAttention forward kernel; its 13x win over eager PyTorch attention is a cold-start profiling artifact.

name: ARM NEON Compositor
baseline: the same alpha-overlay routine without NEON intrinsics, compiled with GCC -O3
one_liner: Hand-written NEON straight-alpha BGRA overlay for Raspberry Pi; 3.5x its own scalar fallback on cache-resident images, 1.4-1.6x when memory-bound.

name: batmat (batched small-matrix linear algebra)
baseline: Intel MKL and OpenBLAS (per-matrix BLAS/LAPACK calls via the BLAS interface), BLASFEO
one_liner: C++20 SIMD kernels for batches of same-shape small matrices (gemm, syrk, trsm, trtri, Cholesky); claims wins over per-matrix MKL, OpenBLAS and BLASFEO, with no published numbers.

name: camaro
baseline: Pure-JavaScript XML parsers in Node.js/V8: txml, fast-xml-parser, xml-js, xml2js
one_liner: Node.js XML-to-JSON extractor (pugixml in Wasm) using XPath templates; about 5x txml, 24-37x other JS parsers on 60 KB.

name: JsonFusion
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: Header-only C++23 reflection-based JSON parser that parses, validates and fills your structs in one pass, beating RapidJSON plus hand-written mapping.

name: Flash Attention PTX/CUDA (hand-written PTX prefill attention for RTX 5080)
license: MIT (stated only in the README's License section; no LICENSE file in the repository, raw LICENSE returns 404)
baseline: FlashAttention-2 as bundled in vLLM 0.23.0 (vllm.vllm_flash_attn.flash_attn_varlen_func, FA2 path)
one_liner: Hand-written PTX flash-attention prefill and paged decode library for RTX 5080 (sm_120); edges out vLLM's FlashAttention-2 at small batch.

name: VectorFFT
baseline: Intel oneMKL 2025.3 FFT (DFTI, sequential)
one_liner: Double-precision x86 AVX2/AVX-512 FFT library in C, with generated codelets and a wisdom planner; median 1.29x Intel MKL on 1D c2c.

name: Cage (wasmtime-mte, MTE-based memory safety and bounds checking for 64-bit Wasm)
baseline: Plain 64-bit Wasm (wasm64/memory64) run in Wasmtime without MTE, where the sandbox relies on software bounds checks; the paper reports speedups 'over wasm64' (search snippet of arXiv 2408.11456; whether the baseline build is upstream Wasmtime or the fork with MTE off was not confirmed).
one_liner: Research fork of Wasmtime 16 that swaps wasm64 software bounds checks for Arm MTE tag checks and adds MTE/PAC memory safety.

name: LSQUIC-DPDK (tumi8 kernel-bypass fork)
baseline: msquic
one_liner: LSQUIC 4.2 fork with a zero-copy DPDK datapath; 1.3x kernel MsQuic (GSO+GRO) goodput on single-connection bulk downloads.

name: quiche-DPDK (tumi8 kernel-bypass fork)
language: C (DPDK kernel-bypass I/O layer added on top of upstream Rust quiche core)
baseline: quiche
one_liner: DPDK kernel-bypass client/server built on unmodified quiche; 1.83x the single-connection goodput of kernel-socket quiche on 100G NICs.

name: w2c2
baseline: Wasmtime (independent blog runs); native C for the README CoreMark figure
