one_liner: Ahead-of-time WebAssembly-to-C89 translator; the compiled output beat Wasmtime in two independent blog runs.

name: Quickenshtein
baseline: naive baseline Levenshtein implementation in the repo, and Fastenshtein (other fast .NET Levenshtein library)
one_liner: Allocation-free .NET Levenshtein distance with an SSE4.1/AVX2 anti-diagonal kernel; about 4.8-5.3x faster than Fastenshtein on long strings.

name: THST (Hierarchical spatial trees)
baseline: Boost.Geometry index (rtree)
one_liner: Header-only C++03 R-tree and 2D quadtree that compile about 25x faster than Boost.Geometry rtree code; runtime is not faster overall.

name: edge264
baseline: FFmpeg libavcodec H.264 decoder (README chart also shows LibAVC and OpenH264)
one_liner: Compact C H.264 (progressive High, MVC) decoder that beats single-threaded FFmpeg libavcodec by about 1.2x in its CI.

name: MuseAir (C++ port)
baseline: wyhash
one_liner: GPL-3.0 C++20 header port of deprecated MuseAir v0.4-rc4. Ties wyhash in bulk, slower on short keys.

name: minicbor
baseline: MessagePack
one_liner: no_std Rust CBOR codec whose derived encoders serialize 2.6-6.9x faster than rmp-serde (MessagePack); decoding is only on par.

name: PTMS (Parallel Tournament Merge Sort)
baseline: std::sort (1 thread) and tbb::parallel_sort
one_liner: OpenMP-task parallel merge sort for int arrays with AVX2/AVX-512 bitonic base cases; claims about 2.2x over tbb::parallel_sort.

name: MicroProfiler (micro-profiler)
baseline: AQtime Performance Profiler and Visual Studio Instrumenting Profiler (instrumenting profilers)
one_liner: Low-overhead real-time instrumenting C/C++ profiler; README chart shows 6-7x less slowdown than AQtime and the VS instrumenting profiler.

name: hypher
baseline: hyphenation crate 0.8 (embedded Liang/Knuth patterns, the common Rust hyphenation library)
one_liner: Allocation-free Rust Knuth-Liang hyphenator with patterns embedded as automata; about 2x faster per word than the hyphenation crate.

name: Typst
baseline: pdfLaTeX (pdfTeX 1.40.24, TeX Live 2022) and LuaLaTeX (LuaHBTeX 1.15.0); the same shootout also ran WeasyPrint 68.1, Apache FOP 2.11 and speedata Publisher 5.3.18 Pro
one_liner: Rust typesetting system (markup language, compiler, CLI) that built mail-merge PDFs 3-5x faster than pdfLaTeX in one shootout.

name: PH-tree (phtree-cpp)
baseline: Boost.Geometry R-tree (boost::geometry::index::rtree); libspatialindex R-tree also measured
one_liner: Header-only PH-tree (bitwise Z-order quadtree) spatial map; about 5x faster inserts than Boost.Geometry's R-tree, slower kNN.

name: TooManyCooks (TMC)
baseline: oneTBB (Intel/uxlfoundation Threading Building Blocks)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 coroutine thread pool with continuation-stealing scheduling; 1.1-3.8x faster than oneTBB on fork-join workloads.

name: TzdLanguage NTT BigInt multiplier
license: MIT (stated only in the README and badge; there is no LICENSE file in the repository: raw main/LICENSE and github.com blob/main/LICENSE both 404)
baseline: GNU GMP 6.3.0 (single-core mpz_mul)
one_liner: 3-prime NTT big-integer multiply (AVX2 CPU, CUDA GPU) inside a Windows hobby language; beats single-core GMP only on GPU or decimal I/O.

name: Boost.Text (tzlaine/text)
baseline: ICU
one_liner: Boost-style C++ Unicode library (transcoding, normalization, text types) faster than ICU only in narrow, now-degraded cases.

name: grpcxx
baseline: gRPC
one_liner: Small C++20 unary-only gRPC server on nghttp2 and libuv; author's hello-world h2load runs show ~2.3-3x gRPC C++ throughput.

name: uavs3e
baseline: HPM 4.0 (the AVS3 reference software) for encoding speed; x265 veryslow for compression at a roughly similar speed
one_liner: Open-source AVS3 (China's AVS3-P2 baseline) encoder with SIMD and fast mode decisions, far faster than the HPM reference encoder.

name: Pkd-tree (parallel kd-tree with batch updates)
baseline: CGAL kd-tree (Spatial_searching) and Boost.Geometry R-tree (also BHL-tree and Log-tree)
one_liner: Parallel ParlayLib kd-tree with batch insert/delete; builds 80-277x faster than CGAL's kd-tree on 10^9 points.

name: PSI-Lib / SpaceTreeLib (P-Orth tree, SPaC-tree; also contains the Pkd-tree)
baseline: Boost.Geometry bgi::rtree (quadratic, sequential); the repo also benchmarks CPAM and Zd-tree, and has a CGAL kd-tree harness (tests/cgal.cpp)
one_liner: Header-only parallel kd-, orth- and space-filling-curve trees with batch updates; 2-3x faster batch updates than a Zd-tree.

name: SocketPro
baseline: RabbitMQ
one_liner: C++ async RPC framework with a built-in persistent server queue; the vendor claims 3.6-54x RabbitMQ's enqueue/dequeue speed.

name: json-parser (udp/json-parser)
baseline: nlohmann/json v2.0.3 (same suite also: json-c 0.12.1, Jansson v2.7, JsonCpp 1.0.0)
one_liner: Two-file, non-recursive C89 DOM parser; parsed 1.5x faster than nlohmann/json 2.0.3 in a 2016 run, entirely on number-heavy input.

name: MaxMulSK
baseline: OpenBLAS (tuned build reaching its own SME kernels, one thread) and Apple Accelerate
one_liner: Single-threaded FP32 SME/SME2 GEMM for Apple M4; published v3 beats an SME-enabled OpenBLAS build, trails Accelerate.

name: cpp_prngs (QuarkBurst64, RomuDuoJr, Konadare192 engines)
baseline: std::mt19937 (also std::minstd_rand, std::default_random_engine and C rand())
one_liner: Header-only constexpr C++17 small-state PRNG engines (RomuDuoJr, QuarkBurst64, Konadare192 and others) with a game-oriented Random<E> API, faster than std::mt19937.

name: Ryu
baseline: printf (sprintf)
one_liner: Shortest round-trip float/double-to-string conversion beating sprintf, plus a faster %f/%e printf replacement.

name: UWVM2 (u2 interpreter)
baseline: wasm3
one_liner: C++26 WebAssembly runtime whose 'u2' direct-threaded interpreter reports about 1.7x lower geomean wall time than wasm3 on Apple Silicon.

name: Ultimate++ (U++ Core: VectorMap, String, Stream, heap)
baseline: std::map and std::tr1::unordered_map with std::string and std::ifstream (libstdc++ shipped with GCC 4.1.3)
one_liner: U++ framework's VectorMap/Index hash containers plus String and heap; 1.8-2.4x over std::unordered_map in a first-party word-index test.

name: UltraJSON
baseline: CPython json module (stdlib json)
one_liner: Maintenance-only CPython C extension for JSON; up to 2.5x faster than stdlib json on standard fixtures; Python-only.

name: Kvazaar
one_liner: BSD-licensed HEVC/H.265 encoder in C from Tampere University; papers report faster all-intra encoding than x265 at equal BD-rate.

name: uvgRTP
baseline: FFmpeg (libavformat RTP) and Live555 as RTP senders/receivers for HEVC video
one_liner: C++ RTP/SRTP/ZRTP library with built-in H.264/HEVC/VVC packetization; its authors report 4.4x FFmpeg's RTP goodput.

name: wc.apl (Dyalog APL wc, 'Beating C with Dyalog APL')
baseline: wc (the C wc shipped with the author's macOS)
one_liner: Short Dyalog APL wc (lines, words, bytes) that ran about 2.9x faster than the stock macOS wc in a 2019 blog test.

name: sh-syntax
baseline: mvdan-sh 0.10.1 (npm; archived GopherJS build of mvdan/sh, pure JavaScript)
one_liner: mvdan/sh (shfmt) shell parser and formatter compiled to WebAssembly with TinyGo; 4.3x faster than the GopherJS mvdan-sh package.

name: kigumi
baseline: CGAL Polygon_mesh_processing corefinement ('coref.'); also libigl igl::copyleft::cgal::mesh_boolean (CGAL exact), geogram, Manifold, MCUT
one_liner: Header-only, exact, multithreaded mesh Booleans for open, closed and non-manifold meshes; beats CGAL corefinement.

name: Undertow
baseline: nginx (echo module) plus Kore, libmicrohttpd, Onion (C) and Crow (C++) in the same table
one_liner: Embeddable non-blocking Java HTTP server (Red Hat); a 2014 build topped Kore, libmicrohttpd and a 4-worker nginx in a 2015 hello-world test.

name: uWebSockets (µWebSockets / uSockets)
baseline: Node.js (Fastify, run as a cluster)
one_liner: C++ HTTP/WebSocket server on the uSockets event layer; author measured 12x the req/s of clustered Node.js/Fastify.

name: uWebSockets.js
language: JavaScript (Node.js bindings over a C++ core)
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Node.js addon running the uWebSockets C++ server behind JS callbacks; 2.6x Fastify, about 1.06x actix-web on hello-world.

name: uni-algo
license: MIT OR Unlicense (LICENSE.md offers a 'Public Domain License' whose text is the Unlicense, or MIT)
baseline: ICU (word break and extended grapheme cluster break iteration over UTF-16 text)
one_liner: Header-only C++17 Unicode library (UTF conversion, case, normalization, UAX #29 segmentation); its grapheme iteration runs 2.7-3.0x faster than ICU's.

name: ICU (ICU4C collation)
baseline: glibc strcoll (glibc 2.12.3 in the ICU4C 3.8 chart, glibc 2.13 in the ICU4C 4.8 chart)
one_liner: ICU4C's RuleBasedCollator: locale-aware UCA/CLDR string comparison and sort keys, charted by its authors as faster than glibc strcoll.

name: ICU4X
baseline: ICU4C (line break and word break iterators)
one_liner: Unicode Consortium's Rust rewrite of ICU; a 2023 first-party post says its line and word segmenters beat ICU4C's break iterators by 19-52%.

name: uniwidth
baseline: mattn/go-runewidth v0.0.19 (the de facto Go terminal display-width library) and rivo/uniseg v0.4.7 StringWidth, both pinned in bench/go.mod; HarfBuzz, FreeType and ICU are not involved
one_liner: Pure-Go terminal cell-width library; CI shows 1.1-52x faster StringWidth than go-runewidth v0.0.19, with width bugs on symbols.

name: Unison
baseline: LLVM's register allocator and instruction scheduler (output quality, Hexagon, ARM and MIPS back ends)
one_liner: Constraint-programming register allocator and instruction scheduler for LLVM 3.8 that produces 1-10% faster or 1-4% smaller code than LLVM's heuristics.

name: Type-V
baseline: V8 (node --jitless) and CPython 3.12
one_liner: Hobby register-based bytecode VM for the Type-C language; beats CPython 3.12 on three microbenchmarks, roughly matches node --jitless.

name: UCall (formerly ujrpc)
baseline: epoll
one_liner: JSON-RPC 2.0 server library in C++ with C and Python APIs; io_uring backend beats FastAPI/uvicorn on small-call latency and throughput.

name: USearch
baseline: FAISS (HNSW index build; exact brute-force search via faiss.IndexFlatL2)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 HNSW vector-search engine with native bindings; first-party tables claim 2-10x faster index builds than FAISS.

name: UStore (UDisk engine)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Closed-source NVMe KV engine (UDisk) behind UStore's open C API; vendor numbers show 2-7x RocksDB throughput.

name: Pillow-SIMD
baseline: ImageMagick 6.9 (via Wand) in the pillow-perf results; ImageMagick 7.1.1 in the libvips wiki table. pillow-perf also compares Pillow, OpenCV, Skia, libvips and Intel IPP.
one_liner: SSE4/AVX2 fork of Python's Pillow; resizes 8-bit RGB images 11-23x faster than ImageMagick 6 via Wand, single core.

name: Ralloc
baseline: PMDK libpmemobj, Makalu
one_liner: Lock-free recoverable persistent-memory malloc (LRMalloc-based); about 10x faster than PMDK libpmemobj and Makalu on allocator microbenchmarks.

name: uriparser
baseline: Ruby standard library URI.parse (pure Ruby, Ruby 2.6); measured through the ruby-uriparser binding, not through uriparser's C API
one_liner: Strict RFC 3986 URI parser in C99; only evidence is a Ruby binding beating Ruby's URI.parse 4.5-5.5x.

name: ckmeans (Rust optimal 1-D k-means) vs Ckmeans.1d.dp C++
baseline: Ckmeans.1d.dp C++ implementation (kmeans_1d_dp, methods 'linear' (default) and 'loglinear'; the code behind the R package and the ckmeans-1d-dp Python package), vendored in bench_cpp
one_liner: Rust crate for optimal 1-D k-means (Wang and Song's Ckmeans); 1.6-2.1x faster than the Ckmeans.1d.dp C++ code on an M2 Pro.

name: Serenity Logger
baseline: spdlog
one_liner: Alpha C++20 synchronous logger (console, file, rotating targets) whose own crude benchmark beats spdlog's single-threaded sinks.

name: cereal
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Header-only C++11 serialization library whose binary archive round-tripped a 17 KB record ~2.2x faster than Protobuf in 2019.

name: wisp
baseline: wasmtime Winch (baseline compiler); wasmer Singlepass; wasmtime Cranelift on fib
one_liner: Compact Rust Wasm runtime whose single-pass AArch64 compiler compiles faster than wasmtime Winch and wasmer Singlepass.

name: Usuba (bitslicing language and compiler to C with SIMD intrinsics)
baseline: Hand-tuned reference implementations in SUPERCOP, compiled with the same C compilers at -O3: Kwan's bitsliced DES (C), Kasper-Schwabe SSSE3 AES-CTR and Kivilinna's AVX AES-CTR (assembly), Dolbeau AVX2, moon AVX/SSSE3 and e/ref ChaCha20, Linux C and avx2-16way/avx-8way/sse2-8way Serpent-CTR, and the Rectangle reference. Secondary: BSC 0.1 (Thomas Pornin's prototype bitslicing compiler, which emits C) on DES in results.org.
one_liner: Bitslicing DSL whose OCaml compiler emits SIMD C ciphers roughly on par with hand-tuned SUPERCOP references.

name: PebblesDB
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: LevelDB-API embedded KV store on a Fragmented LSM tree; several times RocksDB's random-write throughput with less write IO.

name: SplitFS
baseline: ext4 DAX (POSIX file I/O on persistent memory; NOVA also compared in paper)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD user-space persistent-memory file system layered on ext4 DAX; cuts POSIX data-path overhead versus ext4 DAX and NOVA.

name: WineFS
baseline: ext4-DAX, xfs-DAX and NOVA (kernel PM file systems); mmap workloads
one_liner: Linux kernel file system for Intel Optane persistent memory that keeps 2MB hugepage mappings after aging; beats ext4-DAX, xfs-DAX, NOVA on mmap workloads.

name: FreeGuard
baseline: DieHarder (secure allocator) and OpenBSD malloc; roughly parity with the default Linux (glibc) allocator
one_liner: Research secure malloc (CCS 2017) with near-glibc speed, far faster than the DieHarder and OpenBSD secure allocators.

name: NUMAlloc
baseline: default Linux allocator (glibc 2.28 malloc)
one_liner: NUMA-aware LD_PRELOAD malloc replacement, ~21% faster than glibc malloc and ~16% faster than mimalloc on 128-thread NUMA workloads.

name: uutils coreutils (Rust sort, nl, expand, base64)
baseline: GNU coreutils sort, base64, expand and nl (C)
one_liner: Rust reimplementation of GNU coreutils; release notes claim faster sort, base64, expand and nl than GNU, without a published harness.

name: uutils findutils (find, xargs, locate, updatedb)
baseline: GNU findutils find (C)
one_liner: Rust reimplementation of GNU find, xargs, locate and updatedb aiming at drop-in compatibility; never timed against GNU find.

name: oneDAL (oneAPI Data Analytics Library)
baseline: scikit-learn 1.8.0 (stock CPU implementation); the oneDAL README separately compares against Apache Spark MLlib
one_liner: Intel's C++ classical-ML library (k-means, SVM, kNN, linear models, PCA) behind sklearnex; beats stock scikit-learn on multi-core x86.

name: oneTBB concurrent_bounded_queue
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Bounded/blocking FIFO queue in Intel's oneTBB parallelism library; non-blocking try_push/try_pop mode cuts round-trip latency ~3.9x vs std::mutex.

name: V8
baseline: QuickJS (and Duktape in the same table)
one_liner: Google's JIT JavaScript and WebAssembly engine (Chrome, Node.js); about 36-44x QuickJS on the Octane v8-v7 suite.

name: Accelerated-Zig-Parser (compacting SIMD tokenizer)
baseline: Zig standard library tokenizer (hand-written, used by the Zig 0.14 self-hosted compiler)
one_liner: SIMD 'compacting' tokenizer for Zig source that beats the stdlib's hand-written tokenizer 2.75x on AVX-512 x86-64.

name: Valkey
baseline: Redis
one_liner: BSD-licensed fork of Redis OSS 7.2 whose async I/O threads give ~37% more SET throughput than Redis 8.0.

name: fasthttp (Go HTTP server/client package)
baseline: Go net/http
one_liner: Zero-allocation HTTP/1.1 server and client for Go; about 5x faster per request than net/http in its own benchmarks.

name: fastjson (valyala)
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Pure-Go schemaless JSON parser/validator with a reusable zero-allocation value tree; ~4-15x faster than encoding/json (2019 numbers).

name: valyala/fastrand (Go scalable per-CPU pseudorandom generator)
baseline: Go math/rand (global rand.Int31n and rand.New(...) instances)
one_liner: Tiny Go xorshift32 PRNG with a sync.Pool of generators; out-scaled the mutex-locked global math/rand under parallel load.

name: TurboRes
baseline: FFmpeg 7.1.1 native CLI (single- and multithreaded, plus VideoToolbox hardware decode) and ffmpeg.wasm
one_liner: Zig-to-WebAssembly Apple ProRes decoder for JavaScript runtimes; about 2.3-2.8x native FFmpeg 7.1.1 throughput on an Apple M4.

name: Firetrail (formerly skim)
baseline: lz4 (also zstd)
one_liner: Zig word-hash codec (Density-style) that encodes faster than lz4 --fast=20 and zstd --fast=5, at a lower ratio.

name: TinyKVM (Varnish KVM sandbox; per-request numbers come from libriscv/kvmserver)
baseline: per-request sandboxing by process fork, a new V8 isolate or WebAssembly (Wasmtime serve); native Linux process as the speed reference. kvmserver's examples/bench.ts has benchmark groups for Wasmtime serve (instance reuse on/off and release), Bun process forking and Node isolated-vm isolate-per-request, but the README publishes no results for them
one_liner: KVM-based userspace sandbox that resets a forked Linux program in tens of microseconds, versus milliseconds for process fork or V8 isolates.

name: Varnish Cache
baseline: NGINX 1.12.2 proxy_cache (worker_processes 1 and worker_processes auto on 12 cores) in front of an nginx origin
one_liner: Multi-threaded HTTP reverse-proxy cache programmed in VCL; beats a single-worker nginx proxy_cache but not nginx on all cores.

name: pixz
baseline: xz (XZ Utils), run multi-threaded by pRDS with the same core count as pixz (xz -zcT<cores> -6 to compress, xz -cdT<cores> to decompress)
one_liner: Parallel, block-indexed xz compressor CLI; roughly ties multi-threaded xz on speed, adds random access into .tpxz tarballs.

name: Vc (SIMD Vector Classes)
baseline: Sequential reference loop that calls an out-of-line scalar kernel per element (kernel_reference.cpp is compiled as a separate translation unit without LTO, so the loop cannot be auto-vectorized) using std::exp, std::log and std::sqrt from <cmath> (GCC 5.3.0 libstdc++ forwarding to glibc libm), built with -O3 -ftree-vectorize -ffast-math -mavx2 -mfma
one_liner: C++11 SIMD vector types (float_v, double_v) with vectorized math for x86 SSE2-AVX2; beats per-element scalar <cmath> loops.

name: vcflib (vcfputtogetheragain)
baseline: vcfcreatemulti zig implementation (vcflib's own earlier tool for merging overlapping VCF records)
one_liner: Plain C VCF tool merging overlapping records into multi-allelic records; claimed ~200x faster than vcflib's own zig vcfcreatemulti.

name: RapidProto
baseline: protoc
one_liner: Header-only codegen protobuf decoder for C++: arena and streaming models beating protoc's Arena decode and protozero.

name: Vectorscan
baseline: Snort 3 built without Vectorscan (the OpenWrt snort3 package sets -DENABLE_HYPERSCAN only when the vectorscan package is selected, so Snort falls back to its built-in non-Hyperscan fast-pattern search methods and PCRE; the commit message does not name the search_method used)
one_liner: Portable BSD fork of Intel Hyperscan multi-regex matcher for ARM, Power and x86; 1.4-3.6x faster Snort 3 on ARM routers.

name: Vector Class Library (VCL) version 2
baseline: standard scalar math function libraries (libm) and scalar code that the compiler fails to auto-vectorize
one_liner: Agner Fog's header-only C++17 SIMD vector classes for x86, with inline vector math meant to replace scalar libm loops.

name: Vector (Rust) vs Fluent Bit (C) in the Vector test harness
baseline: Fluent Bit (C log forwarder): 1.1.0 in the TCP to Blackhole, File to TCP, TCP to HTTP and TCP to TCP rows, 3.2.7 in the Regex Parsing row. The same table lists Filebeat (Go), Fluentd and Logstash (Ruby/JVM) and the closed-source Splunk Universal and Heavy Forwarders, whose implementation language was not verified here.
one_liner: Rust log and metrics pipeline whose 2019 first-party tests beat Fluent Bit 1.1.0; the current-version regex run loses.

name: fpnge
baseline: libpng
one_liner: Two-file AVX2/SSE4.1 PNG encoder; about 57x libpng's default encode speed on the QOI corpus, files about 15% larger.

name: Myelon / disruptor-mp (shared-memory ring-buffer IPC transport, Rust)
baseline: Boost.Interprocess message_queue ('Boost-MQ', C++) and an Open MPI shared-memory ping-pong (C, built with mpicc); the same chart also holds Rust and Java-ecosystem peers (iceoryx2, Aeron through rusteron, shmipc-rs, crossbeam, ZeroMQ).
one_liner: Rust LMAX-Disruptor-style shared-memory IPC ring for Linux and macOS; first-party 1 KB ping-pong chart beats Boost.Interprocess and Open MPI.

name: scriptc (Vercel Labs TypeScript to native compiler)
baseline: Node.js 24.18.0 (V8) and Bun 1.3.12; slower than both on sustained throughput per the same reports
one_liner: Ahead-of-time TypeScript-to-native compiler; executables start in about 2 ms against tens of milliseconds for Node and Bun, but run hot loops slower.

name: VerneMQ
baseline: Eclipse Mosquitto 2.0.15 (persistence disabled); also EMQX 4.4.16
one_liner: Clustered Erlang/OTP MQTT 3.1/3.1.1/5.0 broker that uses all cores, sustaining loads that saturate single-threaded Mosquitto, at far higher memory and latency.

name: SIMDNoise (simdnoise crate)
baseline: the crate's own scalar (non-SIMD) fallback implementation of the same noise generators
one_liner: Rust crate generating simplex, FBM, ridge, turbulence and cellular noise with SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2 runtime dispatch; beats its own 1-lane scalar path.

name: Clad (Clang-plugin source-transformation AD)
baseline: Enzyme (LLVM-level AD, run through Clad's own use_enzyme backend); Tapenade planned; none of the listed baselines (oneDNN, cuDNN, XNNPACK, Eigen tensor) apply
one_liner: Clang-plugin source-transformation AD for C++ generating derivative source code; no published timing against other AD tools.

name: emio
baseline: scanf (sscanf)
one_liner: Header-only C++20 format/scan library for embedded targets; claims integer scanning about 2x sscanf, binary about 38x smaller than {fmt}.

name: vlagent (Go log collector, VictoriaLogs): log-collectors-benchmark vs Fluent Bit
baseline: Fluent Bit (C), v5.0.9 in the 2026-09-17 run (v4.2.3 in the 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-16 runs), Helm chart fluent/fluent-bit 0.57.9, tail input with the kubernetes filter and an HTTP JSON-lines output with gzip, limited to 1 CPU and 1 GiB
one_liner: Go Kubernetes log collector for VictoriaLogs; about 4x less CPU than Fluent Bit per log at 10k logs/s in a vendor-run benchmark.

name: dav1d
baseline: libaom (AV1 reference decoder)
one_liner: VideoLAN's BSD-2 AV1 decoder in C and assembly; about 3x the 4K60 decode rate of libaom at equal thread counts.

name: MRG32k3a branchless implementation (Vigna)
baseline: L'Ecuyer's reference double-based MRG32k3a.c (also the equivalent 64-bit integer implementation)
one_liner: Branchless 64-bit-integer MRG32k3a in C and Java, about 4x faster per double than L'Ecuyer's reference code, same stream.

name: RecSplit (Sux C++ library)
baseline: CMPH
one_liner: Header-only RecSplit MPHF: 1.8 bits/key, smaller than CMPH's CHD and about 2x faster to build and query on 1e9 keys.

name: sux-rs
baseline: sucds Rank9Sel and vers-vecs RsVec (Rust crates; also succinctly BitVec), not SDSL directly
one_liner: Vigna's Rust succinct-structures crate; Rank9 plus SelectAdapt was fastest of four Rust crates on rank1 and select1.

name: Sux4J (GOV / GOV3Function minimal perfect hash)
baseline: CMPH (CHD algorithm)
one_liner: Java GOV minimal perfect hash (F3 linear systems, ~2.2 bits/key) with C lookup; about 2x faster lookups than CMPH's CHD.

name: vmcache (with exmap)
baseline: mmap-based buffer management (and OS page cache)
one_liner: Single-file C++20 database buffer manager that uses virtual memory for page translation; beats mmap-based LMDB and WiredTiger on TPC-C.

name: W-TinyLFU (C++ header-only, based on the TinyLFU paper)
baseline: LRU
one_liner: Small C++ header-only W-TinyLFU cache: frequency-sketch admission in front of segmented LRU, for higher hit ratios than plain LRU.

name: uring-sync
baseline: cp -r (read/write syscalls); rsync over SSH for network
one_liner: Linux io_uring directory copier and kTLS network sender for many-small-file trees; beats cp -r locally and rsync -az over SSH.

name: libjson (vincenthz)
baseline: nlohmann/json
one_liner: Tiny interruptible SAX-style (callback) JSON parser and printer in C; its suite wins over nlohmann/json come from harness code.

name: Vince's CSV Parser
baseline: fast-cpp-csv-parser (also rapidcsv and Glaze's CSV reader in the same suite)
one_liner: RFC 4180 C++ CSV reader/writer with mmap, SIMD and speculative parallel parsing; beats fast-cpp-csv-parser and rapidcsv on large-file ETL.

name: LuaBridge
baseline: luabind (Boost-based Lua binding library)
one_liner: Header-only C++11 Lua binding library without Boost; beat luabind on 8 of 13 rows of a 2018 shootout but trails sol2 and the raw C API.

name: YARA-X (Rust rewrite of YARA)
baseline: YARA (VirusTotal/yara, the C implementation; the blog calls it 'YARA (legacy)', version not stated)
one_liner: Rust rewrite of the YARA malware-pattern scanner; vendor reports 1.85x faster full-ruleset scans than C YARA since v1.16.0.

name: vek
baseline: pure-Go fallback of the same library (plain Go loops)
one_liner: Go float32/float64/bool vector library with AVX2+FMA assembly kernels, against its own pure-Go loops.

name: gason
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: ~450-line in-situ C++11 JSON DOM parser, 1.2-1.5x faster than default RapidJSON on kostya's number-heavy JSON test.

name: honeydiff (vizzly-testing)
baseline: none compared (candidates odiff and pixelmatch)
one_liner: Closed-source Rust image-diff engine for Node (CIEDE2000, AA suppression, SSIM/GMSD); no current benchmark against odiff or pixelmatch.

name: KPHP
baseline: PHP 7.4 with OpCache (Zend micro_bench.php and bench.php); PHP 7.2 for the vk.com page timings
one_liner: VK's ahead-of-time compiler from strictly typed PHP to C++; first-party 5-7x over PHP 7.4 on Zend benchmarks.

name: picohttpparser AVX2 fork (vkrasnov)
license: MIT OR Perl License (Artistic-1.0-Perl OR GPL-1.0-or-later), stated in source-file headers and README (no LICENSE file; GitHub spdx_id null); inherited unchanged from upstream
baseline: picohttpparser
one_liner: AVX2 bitmap rewrite of picohttpparser's header scanner; 1.7-1.8x the SSE4.2 PCMPESTRI version on Haswell.

name: pg_jitter
baseline: PostgreSQL LLVM JIT (llvmjit); also PostgreSQL's expression interpreter
one_liner: PostgreSQL JIT provider with sljit, AsmJit and MIR backends; compiles typical queries in 0.05-1 ms where llvmjit takes 20-60 ms.

name: udis86
baseline: Zydis, bddisasm and Intel XED (decode only); it loses to Capstone and Zydis in decode+format
one_liner: Small table-driven C x86/x86-64 decoder; in decode-only mode it beat Zydis, bddisasm and XED, but it formats slowest.

name: SplinterDB
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Embedded C key-value store for NVMe SSDs; paper reports 6-10x RocksDB insert throughput and 2-2.6x point-query throughput.

name: MIR / c2m (C2MIR)
baseline: GCC
one_liner: Lightweight JIT toolkit whose C11 front-end (c2m) compiles a header-free C function ~80x faster than gcc -O2.

name: MUM/VMUM hash
baseline: xxHash3, Google CityHash (City64), Bob Jenkins SpookyHash, SipHash24, MetroHash, t1ha2 — widely-used non-cryptographic hash functions used in place of std::hash for hash-table keys
one_liner: Header-only C multiply-mix hash family (MUM/VMUM) rivaling xxHash3, beating CityHash and SipHash24 on most key sizes.

name: CRuby RTL + MJIT (vnmakarov/ruby rtl_mjit_branch)
baseline: Ruby MRI 2.0 (primary) and Ruby MRI 2.5-development trunk the branch is based on ('base')
one_liner: 2017 CRuby fork with register-based (RTL) bytecode and a method JIT that emits C and runs GCC/Clang; beats MRI 2.0 and 2.5-dev.

name: Ichor
baseline: Boost.Beast (pure Beast http_server_fast-style server, beast_benchmark in the same repo)
one_liner: C++20/23 dependency-injection and event-queue framework with HTTP services on Boost.Beast; its 'faster than Beast' numbers come from a broken baseline.

name: kawipiko
baseline: NGINX (distribution package; configuration in the kawipiko examples/nginx folder), also darkhttpd
one_liner: Go static-site server that serves a prebuilt CDB archive from memory over fasthttp; author measured 1.22-1.34x NGINX request rate.

name: Monocoque
baseline: ZeroMQ (libzmq)
one_liner: Pure-Rust, ZeroMQ wire-compatible (ZMTP 3.x) async messaging library; about 3x lower REQ/REP latency than libzmq.

name: Vortex
baseline: Apache Parquet
one_liner: Rust columnar file format and compressed-array toolkit that aims to replace Parquet for scans, writes and random access.

name: ipnsort and driftsort (Rust std slice::sort_unstable and slice::sort)
baseline: C++ standard library sorts: std::sort and std::stable_sort of libstdc++ and libc++ (benchmark variants cpp_std_gnu / cpp_std_libcxx in the repo)
one_liner: Research home of ipnsort and driftsort, Rust's standard sorts since 1.81; ipnsort beats libstdc++ and libc++ std::sort on 10k u64.

name: vpxyz/xorshift (Go xorshift*, xorshift+, xoroshiro and splitmix64 generators)
baseline: Go math/rand (rand.NewSource Int63 source, and rand.New(source).ExpFloat64())
one_liner: Pure-Go ports of Vigna's xorshift/xoroshiro/xoshiro and SplitMix64 generators; raw calls 2-3x faster than math/rand's default source.

name: Cache-Aware and GPU-Accelerated SpMV (VSJ001)
baseline: cuSPARSE SpMV (CSR_ALG2)
one_liner: Coursework-scale CUDA CSR-vector SpMV kernel (one warp per row) that edges out cuSPARSE CSR_ALG2 on three regular SuiteSparse matrices.

name: libucl
baseline: jansson (C JSON parser and emitter)
one_liner: C parser and emitter for UCL, an nginx-style JSON superset; README shows it parsing JSON about 2x faster than jansson.

name: jpeg-encoder
baseline: image crate JPEG encoder (informal); libjpeg-turbo and mozjpeg not compared
one_liner: Pure-Rust baseline/progressive JPEG encoder with optional AVX2 DCT and color conversion; informally about 2x the image crate's encoder on x86.

name: Umka
baseline: Wren and Python (no Lua row)
one_liner: Statically typed, Go-like embeddable scripting language in C99; one old chart shows it beating Wren and CPython on matrix multiplication.

name: VTEnc
baseline: FastPFor (Delta+FastPFor128/256), Delta+BinaryPacking, Delta+VariableByte, Delta+VarIntGB
one_liner: C codec for sorted unsigned integer lists that beats Delta+FastPFor on compression ratio, and on speed only for clustered data.

name: ffpng
baseline: image-rs/image-png v0.18.1 (commit 4ab5484; the Rust png crate, already listed) built with --features=unstable at target-cpu=x86-64-v3. The same harness also times libpng + zlib, libspng, stb_image and ldpng (ffpng's front end with libdeflate inflate), but the README publishes no libpng, libspng or stb_image numbers
one_liner: Single-header C PNG decoder for x86-64-v3 (AVX2) that decodes 1.12-1.20x faster than image-png, the Rust png crate.

name: mmx sdefl/sinfl (single-header deflate)
baseline: zlib 1.2.11 (also miniz 1.0)
one_liner: Two tiny single-header C files for raw deflate and zlib: compressor about 1.8x zlib 1.2.11, decoder 1.2-1.4x (first-party).

name: kmeans-wasm
language: Rust (WebAssembly SIMD, simd128) with JavaScript wrapper
baseline: skmeans (JavaScript k-means library)
one_liner: Rust-to-WebAssembly k-means (Hamerly bounds, distinct-colour weighting) for colour quantisation and vectors; beats the naive JS skmeans.

name: gocrack (wa7nt)
baseline: Go standard library crypto/md5 and crypto/sha1 (single-stream hashing)
one_liner: Go program with hand-written 8-way AVX2 multi-buffer MD5/SHA-1 compression kernels; beats single-stream crypto/md5 and crypto/sha1 on aggregate throughput.

name: Wago
baseline: Wasmtime, Wasmer, V8 and wazero
one_liner: Pure-Go, no-cgo single-pass Wasm-to-native compiler; compiles about 3x quicker than wazero in-process and edges it on cold runs.

name: QtAV
license: LGPL-2.1 (library); the player example is GPL-3.0
baseline: VLC media player (CPU usage on Android, 10-bit H.264 playback)
one_liner: Qt plus FFmpeg playback library with hardware decoding and GPU YUV rendering; one author anecdote claims 10% less CPU than VLC.

name: low-latency-log
license: Apache-2.0 (some code from logflume under MIT, LICENSE-LOGFLUME)
baseline: quill (C++), spdlog-rs, fast_log, ftlog
one_liner: Small async Rust file logger with deferred formatting; higher backend throughput than spdlog-rs, fast_log, ftlog in its own harness.

name: FastGEMV (fp16/int8/int4 GEMV CUDA kernels)
baseline: PyTorch fp16 matrix-vector product (torch.matmul on a size x size fp16 matrix and size x 1 vector, baseline.py, kernel time via Nsight Systems)
one_liner: Three small CUDA GEMV kernels (fp16, int8, int4 weights x fp16 vector) beating 2023 PyTorch fp16 matmul by 1.1-2.7x.

name: fNBLI (NBLI lossless image codec)
baseline: PNG encoded and decoded through Pillow 10.1.0's own PNG codec (PngImagePlugin over Pillow's zlib-based 'zip' codec, not libpng), optipng 0.7.7 for optimized PNG encoding, and libwebp lossless via Pillow 10.1.0
one_liner: Single-threaded AVX2 lossless codec for 8-bit gray and 24-bit RGB; 7.8x faster encode than Pillow PNG with 33% smaller files.

name: wyhash
baseline: xxHash
one_liner: Header-only 64-bit non-cryptographic hash + PRNG; about 9% faster bulk throughput than xxHash's XXH3.

name: Bw-Tree (Open BwTree, wangziqi2013)
baseline: BerkeleyDB (B-tree mode)
one_liner: Open-source lock-free Bw-Tree (concurrent B+-tree multimap) from CMU; its own benchmarks show it slower than std::map and stx::btree.

name: libwebsockets
baseline: WebSocket++ (websocketpp) v0.7.0
one_liner: Pure C client/server library for WebSockets, HTTP/1-2-3 and MQTT; in a 2016 competitor table it used ~5.7x less memory per connection than WebSocket++.

name: wasm-bindgen with web-sys (hand-written benchmark implementation)
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: Rust-to-JavaScript binding generator; hand-written Rust DOM code built with it takes 0.58x React 19.2 hooks' time in js-framework-benchmark.

name: WARP WebAssembly compiler and runtime (wasm-ecosystem/wasm-compiler)
baseline: V8 Liftoff and V8 TurboFan; SpiderMonkey Baseline and Ion
one_liner: BMW's single-pass C++ Wasm-to-native compiler and runtime for embedded targets; its own chart shows compiles faster than Liftoff, runs near TurboFan.

name: wasm3
baseline: WAMR fast interpreter (iwasm); Wasmtime Pulley interpreter; WasmEdge interpreter
one_liner: Portable, dependency-free C WebAssembly interpreter; fastest of seven interpreters on scalar MVP code, about 1.6x WAMR fast-interp on Apple M4.

name: WasmEdge
baseline: Wasmtime, Wasmer (Cranelift, LLVM, Singlepass), V8 (Node.js) and wazero
one_liner: C++ WebAssembly runtime whose LLVM AOT mode ties Wasmtime and beats V8 and wazero on libsodium; its interpreter is slow.

name: Wasmer (LLVM backend)
license: MIT (repository); BUSL-1.1 for the LLVM and Singlepass compiler crates from Wasmer 6.0
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift) and V8 (Node.js)
one_liner: Rust WebAssembly runtime whose optional LLVM backend runs WASI code about 1.15x faster than Wasmtime and 1.34x faster than V8.

name: Wasmi
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift), Wasmer (Cranelift) and V8 for startup; WAMR fast interpreter and Wasmtime Pulley for execution
one_liner: Rust WebAssembly interpreter with near-zero startup through lazy translation; its v2 engine also out-executes WAMR, Wasm3 and Pulley interpreters.

name: Fizzy
baseline: Wasmtime (Cranelift), Wasmer (Cranelift) startup
one_liner: Dependency-free C++17 WebAssembly 1.0 interpreter whose eager parse-and-instantiate beats Cranelift JIT runtimes and WAMR fast-interp on startup.

name: AVX512-VAES2-PRNG (AVX-512/VAES/GFNI 8-way hybrid PRNG, proof of concept)
baseline: Mersenne Twister (mt19937), PCG32 / XorShift128+, ChaCha8 and ChaCha20 AVX-512 (rows in the README table)
one_liner: Single-header AVX-512/VAES/GFNI bulk PRNG proof of concept; author claims 0.093 cycles/byte versus about 4-6 for mt19937.

name: libopus-rs
baseline: libopus, Opus trunk commit 03647f524a40b05a1898522e92033810b58103c7 (static .libs/libopus.a from an autotools tree; configure flags not recorded), called through the full opus_encode/opus_encode24 and opus_decode/opus_decode24 API
one_liner: Archived pure-Rust Opus CELT-only codec (48 kHz); encodes 1-2% faster than trunk libopus at 5 ms, 192-320 kb/s.

name: WAVM
baseline: Wasmtime, Wasmer (LLVM, Cranelift, Singlepass backends) and V8 (Node.js)
one_liner: LLVM-based ahead-of-time WebAssembly runtime in C++; fastest total in the 2021 libsodium shootout against Wasmtime, Wasmer and V8.

name: blackwell-tensorcore-kernels
baseline: cuBLAS FP16-in/FP32-accumulate tensor-core GEMM (cublasGemmEx, which dispatches cutlass_80_tensorop_s16816gemm_f16_128x64 on sm_120)
one_liner: Teaching repo: raw mma.sync FP16 GEMM that edges past cuBLAS's tensor-core kernel at 4096-8192 on Blackwell sm_120.

name: jet_server
baseline: Drogon 1.9.13 (C++, trantor event loop; the-benchmarker cpp/drogon, cmake release build); also agoo-c 0.7 (C) in the same table
one_liner: Experimental pure-Dart HTTP/1.1 server driving epoll through dart:ffi; 1.36-1.46x Drogon's req/s in the-benchmarker.

name: Yeppp!
baseline: Julia Base log (pure-Julia Float64 implementation), measured through the Yeppp.jl binding
one_liner: Abandoned 2013-2015 SIMD array math library (log, exp, sin, dot, sum); hand-tuned assembly only for pre-2015 x86-64 cores.

name: WeavePy
baseline: CPython 3.14.8
one_liner: Experimental Rust Python 3.14 interpreter with a Cranelift JIT; about 2x CPython 3.14.8 on its own fixtures.

name: WebAssembly memory.copy (bulk-memory-operations proposal)
license: Per-directory (repo LICENSE): document/ W3C Software and Document Notice and License; interpreter/ and test/ Apache-2.0; papers/ CC-BY-4.0
baseline: Emscripten-generated wasm memcpy loop (aligned i32.load/i32.store) used in the Unity demo, plus manually unrolled i32 and i64 load/store loop variants
one_liner: WebAssembly memory.copy/memory.fill instructions; 2017 V8 prototype copied up to about 3-11x faster than Emscripten's wasm memcpy loop.

name: wasm2c (WABT)
baseline: Wasmtime, Wasmer (Cranelift, LLVM, Singlepass) and V8 (Node.js)
one_liner: wasm2c translates a Wasm module to portable C; compiled natively, it outran Wasmtime, Wasmer and V8 on libsodium.

name: wasi-libc SIMD string routines (opt-in, wasm simd128)
baseline: wasi-libc's own scalar string.h routines (musl-derived SWAR on a 32-bit size_t), i.e. the same library compiled to wasm without -DSIMD=ON
one_liner: Opt-in wasm simd128 versions of strlen, memchr, strchr, strrchr, memcmp, strspn and strcspn in wasi-libc, replacing musl's scalar loops.

name: libpas
license: BSD-2-Clause (per the Apple copyright header in libpas source files)
baseline: bmalloc (WebKit's previous allocator); HN thread also says it beats system malloc in WebKit and JSC
one_liner: Apple's libpas: isoheap-capable malloc toolkit behind WebKit's bmalloc, faster and leaner than the bmalloc it replaced.

name: Bstrlib (The Better String Library)
baseline: C standard library char* string functions (string.h strcat/strcpy/strstr) for the C API; std::string for the CBString C++ wrapper
one_liner: Paul Hsieh's original length-tracked C string library (plus CBString C++ wrapper) replacing string.h char* handling.

name: Crypto++
baseline: libgcrypt (CAST5 in CBC mode), also Botan 1.10 (CAST_128)
one_liner: Broad C++ crypto class library; a 2013 hobby benchmark had its CAST-128-CBC about 1.3-1.4x faster than libgcrypt.

name: BlockQuicksort
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: In-place Quicksort using block-buffered Hoare partitioning to avoid branch mispredictions; ~88% more elements/s than GCC std::sort on random ints.

name: bzip2gpu (weissenberger)
baseline: multicore CPU bzip2 decompressor (exact program not named in the search snippet; candidates bzip2, pbzip2, lbzip2)
one_liner: Research CUDA decompressor for standard .bz2 streams that runs every stage except parsing on the GPU; reported faster than multicore CPU bzip2.

name: CUHD / gpuhd (massively parallel Huffman decoding on GPUs)
baseline: Zstandard's CPU Huffman decoder (huff0)
one_liner: CUDA Huffman decoder (CUHD) that splits one unpartitioned bitstream across GPU threads by self-synchronization; reported 10x+ over zstd's CPU huff0.

name: multians (massively parallel ANS decoding on GPUs)
baseline: 64-thread multicore CPU tANS decoder, a SIMD-based decoder and Zstandard's entropy codec
one_liner: CUDA research decoder for a single unpartitioned tANS bitstream; paper claims up to 17x over 64 CPU threads.

name: misa77
baseline: LZ4 (lz4 1.10.0 and lz4hc)
one_liner: LZ77 codec built for decode speed: about 2x LZ4's decompression throughput on Silesia at a better ratio, with slow compression.

name: SPRK-tree (Sorted Projection Radius KD-tree)
baseline: Boost.Geometry R-tree (named among the paper's competitors in search snippets) plus KD-trees in several languages (Kiddo, nabo, Neighbourhood), a Rust VP-tree, scikit-learn BallTree, SNN and brute force. nanoflann and CGAL kd-tree are feature-gated backends in the rembed harness, but I could not confirm they appear in the paper.
one_liner: Rust SIMD kd-tree for fixed-radius queries with sorted LUT leaves; ESA 2026 paper reports fastest queries across 2-960 dimensions.

name: JTransforms
baseline: FFTW 3 through the ezFFTW Java wrapper (single-threaded)
one_liner: Pure-Java multithreaded FFT/DCT/DST/DHT library; beat a per-call-planned FFTW (via JNI) on smooth 2-D/3-D sizes, lost on primes.

name: flex
baseline: AT&T lex
one_liner: The standard lex-compatible scanner generator; table-driven DFA scanners its author timed 1.5-3.8x faster than AT&T lex in 1988.

name: stdext::inplace_function (WG21-SG14/SG14)
baseline: std::function
one_liner: Header-only, fixed-capacity callable wrapper beating std::function's invocation speed in 5 of 7 shootout categories.

name: wcp
baseline: GNU cp (cp -r); rsync also shown
one_liner: Experimental io_uring recursive file copier for Linux, about 2-3x faster than GNU cp -r on the author's NVMe box.

name: runiq (Rust duplicate-line filter)
baseline: GNU sort -u and uniq (coreutils; versions not stated); also uq and huniq
one_liner: Rust tool and library that drops duplicate lines with one hashing pass, no sort; beats GNU sort -u and uniq.

name: text-shaper
baseline: harfbuzzjs ^0.4.13 (HarfBuzz compiled to WebAssembly, called from JavaScript), not native HarfBuzz; opentype.js also compared; the rasterization rows compare with FreeType through the freetype2 (node-freetype2) Node native binding
one_liner: Pure-TypeScript OpenType shaper and rasterizer; about 1.2-1.5x harfbuzzjs (WASM) on simple-script shaping under Bun.

name: Wild (wild-linker)
baseline: lld
one_liner: Rust linker for Linux that beats LLVM lld on debug-build link time via mmap'd input and rayon-parallelized phases.

name: Vectis
baseline: scalar C++ loop (and the same loop with four independent accumulators, and the same loop built with -ffast-math), as the reference for an AVX2 intrinsics/assembly dot-product kernel
one_liner: New header-only C++20 vec<T,N> SIMD engine (scalar, AVX2, AVX-512) whose AVX2 dot kernels beat a naive scalar loop 13.9x.

name: SPIDER (Succinct Predictive InDEx for Rank and select)
baseline: pasta-flat and pasta-wide, poppy (cs-poppy), Vigna's rank9 and SDSL rank/select structures (competitor list from WebSearch snippets of the SEA 2024 paper; paper not opened)
one_liner: Research C code for a ~3.8%-overhead rank/select bit vector that interleaves rank counters with data and predicts select positions.

name: winnow
baseline: nom
one_liner: Zero-copy Rust parser-combinator crate, forked from nom, favoring API evolution and built-in features over strict compatibility.

name: wizzardo-http
baseline: lithium and cinatra (C++) in the TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext leaderboard
one_liner: Small Java HTTP server and web framework on a JNI epoll core; ties C++ cinatra and lithium in TechEmpower plaintext.

name: nanobind
baseline: pybind11 (also Boost.Python, Cython, cppyy)
one_liner: C++17/CPython binding library from pybind11's author; 2.3-3.1x faster builds, 3-10x lower call overhead than pybind11.

name: wjakob/pcg32
baseline: std::mt19937
one_liner: Tiny two-header PCG32 RNG beating std::mt19937 on speed, with an optional AVX2 8-wide variant.

name: GEMM_AVX2_FMA3
baseline: Intel MKL 2019 update 4
one_liner: Archived 2019 AVX2/FMA3 OpenMP sgemm_/dgemm_ for very large matrices, 2-6% faster than MKL 2019u4 on an i9-9900K.

name: GEMM_AVX512F (wjc404; AVX-512F SGEMM/DGEMM)
baseline: Intel MKL single-thread SGEMM/DGEMM
one_liner: Hand-written AVX-512F SGEMM/DGEMM with a Fortran-ABI entry point; claims 99% of one-thread MKL, which is parity, not a win.

name: wjr (WJR big integer and utility library)
baseline: GMP (mpn_* low-level functions in the repo's own benchmark)
one_liner: x64-tuned C++17 big-integer library with GMP-style mpn kernels, Toom-Cook and FFT multiplication; has a GMP harness but publishes no numbers.

name: uv-cpp
baseline: Boost.Asio 1.67 (TCP ping-pong echo); nginx 1.14.2 (HTTP, Apache bench, chart images only)
one_liner: C++11 callback wrapper over libuv with TCP/UDP/HTTP; ties Boost.Asio 1.67 on loopback echo, trails nginx on HTTP.

name: base64-avx512 (Muła & Lemire)
baseline: base64 (conventional/table-based scalar base64 codec, e.g. Chromium's)
one_liner: C artifact of the Muła–Lemire AVX-512 VBMI base64 codec; 10–20x faster than Chrome's table-driven codec.

name: Faster Base64 Encoding/Decoding using AVX2 (base64simd)
baseline: base64
one_liner: Muła's research harness of SSE/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/RVV base64 kernels; origin of the AVX2 algorithm measured 7-11x faster than Chrome's.

name: simd-sort (AVX2 and AVX-512F quicksort, Wojciech Mula)
baseline: std::sort (GCC toolchain; version not stated for the valid issue #8 run)
one_liner: Experimental AVX2/AVX-512F quicksorts for 32-bit keys; only Lemire's in-repo AVX2 variant beats std::sort on random data.

name: sse-popcount
baseline: scalar hardware POPCNT instruction loop (cpu / builtin-popcnt via __builtin_popcountll), plus lookup-table and bit-parallel scalar versions
one_liner: Reference SIMD popcount kernels (Harley-Seal, PSHUFB lookup) that beat the POPCNT loop 1.8x to 3.6x on kilobyte buffers.

name: sse4-strstr (SIMD-friendly algorithms for substring searching)
baseline: std::strstr / libc strstr (same problem as std::string::find and the default std::search)
one_liner: SIMD substring-search kernels (SSE2-AVX512, NEON) from a blog article; beats glibc strstr by ~1.3-1.8x on x86.

name: etcpak
baseline: Etc2Comp (effort=0, error metric rgba) and ETCPACK 4.0.1 (reference ETC2 encoder in Arm Mali Texture Compression Tool 4.3.0), as measured in the QuickETC2 paper (ACM TOG 2020); the current README only cites the NVIDIA in-driver ETC2 decoder (42.5 Mpx/s) for decompression, and the 2016-2018 README (etcpak 0.5) timed PVRTexToolCLI 3.5, Mali etcpack 4.2, etc2comp and crunch (rg-etc1) 1.04.
one_liner: SIMD multithreaded ETC1/ETC2/EAC/BC encoder: 500-1400x faster than Etc2Comp/ETCPACK multithreaded, 9-21x single-thread scalar, at lower quality.

name: Tracy Profiler
baseline: No perf, gprof or Valgrind comparison; manual compares profiled versus unprofiled run only
one_liner: Hybrid instrumentation plus sampling frame profiler for C/C++ with nanosecond rdtsc timestamps and a remote GUI; no measured win over perf, gprof or Valgrind.

name: VapourSynth-BM3DCUDA
baseline: VapourSynth-BM3D (original CPU plugin) and FFmpeg bm3d; no comparison against either found
one_liner: BM3D/V-BM3D denoiser for VapourSynth on CUDA, AVX2, HIP and SYCL; no published number against VapourSynth-BM3D.

name: wolfSSL
license: GPL-3.0 (the LICENSING file lets certain listed projects, e.g. MariaDB and OpenVPN, use it under GPL-2.0 instead)
baseline: OpenSSL
one_liner: Embedded-first C TLS 1.3 library, not an OpenSSL fork, that beat every OpenSSL version in HAProxy's 64-core Graviton4 tests.

name: Versor (geometric algebra library)
baseline: other C++ geometric algebra solutions: GluCat (framed and matrix), TbGAL, Garamon, Gaalet, Gaalop, GATL
one_liner: Template-metaprogrammed C++ geometric algebra library; within ~15% of GATL and 18-2,600x faster than Garamon, TbGAL, GluCat.

name: GeoRepair (geo-repair)
baseline: GEOS 3.14.1 (conda-forge libgeos, MSVC build) makeValid / UnaryUnion
one_liner: Rust crate (with a C API) for OGC validity checks and ST_MakeValid-style repair; faster than GEOS on most invalid-input classes.

name: torch_ans
baseline: torchac and CompressAI range coding (named as replacement target, no head-to-head numbers)
one_liner: PyTorch C++/CUDA extension for batched parallel rANS coding, pitched as a faster replacement for torchac and CompressAI range coding.

name: eventpp::SpinLock (eventpp GeneralThreading policy)
baseline: std::mutex
one_liner: Header-only spinlock policy for eventpp's EventQueue/EventDispatcher, swapping std::mutex for a std::atomic_flag test-and-set lock at <=core-count thread counts.

name: Wren
baseline: Lua 5.4.4 (PUC), Python 3.11.3, Ruby 3.0.5 in the re-run; Lua 5.2.3, Python 3.3, Ruby 2.0 on the original page
one_liner: Tiny embeddable class-based scripting VM in C; fastest on method-dispatch benchmarks, slower than Lua 5.4 elsewhere.

name: libslz (SLZ)
baseline: zlib
one_liner: Stateless deflate/zlib/gzip compressor in C, about 3.5x faster than zlib -1 at a much lower ratio.

name: wudream813/fastio
baseline: std::cin / std::cout (also scanf/printf, fread, getchar_unlocked as rows in the same table)
one_liner: Single-header C++17 fast integer reader/writer for competitive programming: mmap plus 2-digit lookup tables, about 7-8x faster than std::cin.

name: qAverageColor
baseline: serial (scalar C++) average-colour routine in the same repo
one_liner: SIMD (psadbw, AVX2, AVX-512) mean colour of an RGBA8 pixel buffer; AVX2 path 2.6-5.4x faster than a scalar loop.

name: qHilbert
baseline: Wikipedia d2xy/rot C implementation (in source/qHilbert.cpp), called once per index from tests/benchmark.cpp; the README table does not label it
one_liner: Batch Hilbert-curve index-to-point mapping (Hacker's Delight parallel prefix, SSE/AVX2/AVX-512); 10-50x over Wikipedia's d2xy loop.

name: qReverse
baseline: std::reverse (serial element-swapping reversal)
one_liner: Header-only SIMD/bswap array reversal for 1-16-byte elements; 8-16x faster than scalar libstdc++ std::reverse on bytes.

name: Vacuum Filter
baseline: Bloom filter, cuckoo filter
one_liner: Deletable cuckoo-filter variant allowing any table size; ~25% less space than cuckoo on average, smaller than Bloom below 3% FPR.

name: Wormhole (fast ordered index)
baseline: Skip list (extracted from LevelDB), STX B+-tree (fanout 128), Adaptive Radix Tree (libart from GitHub), Masstree (beta release)
one_liner: Concurrent in-memory ordered KV index in C fusing hash table, trie and B+-tree; lookups beat B+-tree, skip list, ART, Masstree.

name: qoixx
baseline: qoi.h (reference QOI implementation, phoboslab/qoi)
one_liner: Single-header C++20 QOI codec with an AVX2/NEON/SVE encoder, 1.4-1.8x faster than the reference qoi.h.

name: Rain
baseline: Tokio
one_liner: Small header-only C++23 coroutine runtime for Linux: per-thread epoll loops with SO_REUSEPORT, ~1.13x Tokio req/s on one loopback test.

name: Pare
language: C (x264, SVT-AV1, libvmaf) compiled to WebAssembly SIMD128 with Emscripten, TypeScript web app
baseline: ffmpeg.wasm 0.12 (x264 built without its assembly) single-threaded and multithreaded; native x264 as the ceiling
one_liner: In-browser video compressor: x264 with ~1,500 lines of WebAssembly SIMD128 kernels, 1.7-6.4x faster than ffmpeg.wasm end to end.

name: serde-zap
baseline: Protobuf (prost 0.14.4; Google's protobuf 4.36.1-release crate also on the page), FlatBuffers (flatbuffers 25.12.19), Cap'n Proto (capnp 0.27.0), MessagePack (rmp-serde 1.3.1); all are the Rust crates for those formats, not the C++ libraries
one_liner: Serde-trait binary serializer for Rust; serializes string-heavy logs ~5.4x faster than prost, ~9.7x faster than rmp-serde.

name: XenoAtom.Allocators (TLSF)
baseline: C runtime malloc/free (MSVC CRT on Windows)
one_liner: TLSF sub-allocator for .NET 8 over caller-supplied chunks; about 22% faster than CRT aligned malloc/free in its own micro-benchmark.

name: Bf-Tree
baseline: RocksDB (commit 54d6286); the authors' own conventional B-Tree and Bδ-Tree in Rust; Leanstore (commit 677126c); TwoTree
one_liner: Microsoft Research's larger-than-memory concurrent B-Tree for small records, with record-level caching; beats RocksDB and page-cached B-Trees.

name: OpenOnload (with ef_vi and TCPDirect kernel-bypass APIs)
baseline: Linux kernel UDP sockets (kernel network stack)
one_liner: AMD's user-level TCP/UDP stack that accelerates unmodified BSD-sockets apps by bypassing the Linux kernel network stack.

name: CB-SpMV / CB-Sparse (xing-cong)
baseline: cuSPARSE BSR SpMV (cusparse_bsrmv, cuSPARSE v12.4); also TileSpMV and DASP
one_liner: FP64 GPU SpMV on a 16x16 compressed-block format; about 3x faster than cuSPARSE BSR SpMV on SuiteSparse matrices.

name: rav1e
baseline: libaom (AV1 reference encoder)
one_liner: Rust AV1 encoder with dav1d-derived SIMD asm and a C API; its 'fastest' claim is unsupported: slower than libaom at equal quality.

name: xjb
baseline: Ryu (ulfjack/ryu, the double-to-shortest-string algorithm that std::to_chars uses in libstdc++, libc++ and MSVC STL; std::to_chars itself is not in the benchmark); also benchmarked against Dragonbox, Schubfach and fmt 12.1.0
one_liner: Schubfach-derived shortest double/float-to-string converter, about 2.4x faster than Ryu (the algorithm behind std::to_chars) on random doubles.

name: starknet-rs (WebAssembly build, Pedersen hash)
language: Rust (compiled to wasm32-wasi in the benchmark)
baseline: micro-starknet (paulmillr, pure-JavaScript StarkNet library) on Node.js
one_liner: Rust Starknet library whose starknet-crypto Pedersen hash, compiled to WebAssembly, ran 6.88x faster than pure-JS micro-starknet in Node.js (2022).

name: KangarooTwelve (XKCP)
license: CC0-1.0 for most files, with per-file exceptions: CRYPTOGAMS BSD-style/GPL (AVX2 and AVX-512 KeccakP-1600 asm), Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT (ARMv8-A cores), and Brian Gladman's permissive license (brg_endian.h)
baseline: SHAKE128 (FIPS 202), SHA-256 and SHA-512, using the fastest implementations available to the authors, cross-checked with eBASH; 'often' OpenSSL for the traditional hashes
one_liner: Keccak team's C package; its KangarooTwelve XOF hashes long messages 5-8x faster than SHAKE128 via SIMD tree hashing.

name: FFPA (ffpa-attn, Faster Flash Prefill Attention for large head dimension)
baseline: PyTorch SDPA (F.scaled_dot_product_attention); FlashAttention-2 supports head dim only up to 256, FP8/FP4 variants also compared with SageAttention 2/3
one_liner: Exact GPU attention kernels for head dims 320-1024 (beyond FlashAttention-2's 256); 1.5x-15x faster than PyTorch SDPA.

name: xmake
baseline: Make (via CMake-generated Makefiles)
one_liner: Lua-scripted cross-platform build tool with built-in package manager; beats CMake+Make, roughly matches plain Ninja.

name: libjson (xnacly)
baseline: encoding/json
one_liner: Minimal pure-Go JSON parser with dot-path queries; parses about 2x faster than encoding/json into any by mutating input.

name: xNVMe
baseline: DuckDB default synchronous file I/O (psync)
one_liner: Samsung's single C API for NVMe I/O over io_uring, io_uring_cmd, libaio, SPDK and more; DuckDB on it beats default sync I/O.

name: Xorbits
baseline: Dask (DaskDF)
one_liner: Distributed pandas/NumPy-API engine built on Mars. On 100 GB-1 TB TPC-H it beats Dask DataFrame, Modin and pandas-on-Spark.

name: XRP (BPF-KV, WiredTiger patches)
baseline: read() system calls and io_uring (also SPDK)
one_liner: OSDI'22 research kernel that lets an eBPF function in the NVMe driver chain dependent reads, beating read() and io_uring for on-disk B-tree lookups.

name: GEMMFIP (BLIS fork)
baseline: OpenBLAS, AMD BLIS/AOCL, ArmPL, Intel MKL
one_liner: Research BLIS fork whose DGEMM fuses packing into the first compute pass; paper plots show it ahead of OpenBLAS/ArmPL on medium sizes.

name: XS (xs-lang)
baseline: CPython 3.13 and Node 20 (V8), measured in the same README table; the Node column is dominated by Node's own 57 ms process startup
one_liner: New scripting language with VM and register-allocating x86-64/arm64 JIT; about 2x CPython on recursive fib, far behind V8.

name: Spaces
baseline: jemalloc (also snmalloc, tcmalloc, Hoard in the same table)
one_liner: Single-file C malloc replacement for Linux x86-64 with destroyable region heaps; README ranks it ahead of jemalloc on several mimalloc-bench workloads.

name: xsimd
baseline: std::transform / scalar loops
one_liner: Header-only C++ SIMD abstraction: portable batch<T,Arch> type replaces scalar loops across x86/ARM/RISC-V/WASM.

name: xtensor
baseline: NumPy (built from source with -O3 -march=native, called from the same C++ executable via embedded Python)
one_liner: Header-only C++ n-d arrays with NumPy-style broadcasting and lazy expressions; beats NumPy on SIMD transcendentals, loses on large reductions.

name: may
baseline: Tokio, pre-1.0 (tokio-core 0.1 / tokio-proto 0.1 era, via tokio_minihttp)
one_liner: Rust stackful-coroutine runtime with Go-style go! and blocking-style I/O; its may_minihttp demo beat pre-1.0 tokio_minihttp by ~15% req/s.

name: may_minihttp
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Bare-bones Rust HTTP/1.1 server on the may stackful-coroutine runtime; 1.19x actix-web on the-benchmarker's empty-body GET.

name: fast-md5-web
language: Rust compiled to WebAssembly with a TypeScript Web Worker pool
baseline: spark-md5 (pure-JavaScript MD5)
one_liner: Browser MD5 library: RustCrypto md-5 in WebAssembly plus a Web Worker pool, claimed 8-16x faster than spark-md5.

name: Optimizing Dilithium Implementation with AVX2/AVX-512 (PSPM)
baseline: pq-crystals/dilithium AVX2 implementation: the 'standard' branch (FIPS 204 ML-DSA) AVX2 code for the headline Table XI numbers, and the NIST Round 3 submission AVX2 code for Table IX. This is the upstream code that liboqs/PQClean also derive from; liboqs and PQClean were not benchmarked directly.
one_liner: Research AVX2/AVX-512 Round 3 Dilithium code using PSPM-TEE sparse c·s multiplication; paper reports 1.6-2.9x fewer cycles than pq-crystals AVX2.

name: ywasm (y-crdt, Rust port of Yjs compiled to WebAssembly)
baseline: Yjs 13.6.11 (pure-JavaScript CRDT)
one_liner: Yrs, the Rust port of the Yjs CRDT, as a WebAssembly npm module: loads Yjs documents faster but edits slower than Yjs.

name: HaloDB
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Java embedded key-value store for point lookups: append-only logs plus an off-heap hash index. Beats RocksDB on random writes and reads in IO-bound tests.

name: ultrachess (Rust chess library compiled to WebAssembly)
baseline: chess.js (pure JavaScript chess library in V8/Node)
one_liner: Rust chess rules core compiled to a 158 KB WASM module with a TypeScript API, aimed at replacing chess.js; its speedup over chess.js is cited, not measured.

name: asp (algebraic, staged parsing)
baseline: ocamlyacc/ocamllex
one_liner: Staged, typed OCaml parser combinators (MetaOCaml) that beat ocamlyacc/ocamllex throughput on 4 of 5 grammars.

name: flap (fused lexing and parsing)
baseline: ocamlyacc (also benchmarked against Menhir's table- and code-generation backends)
one_liner: Fuses OCaml lexer and parser via MetaOCaml staging, generating token-free code 2-6x faster than ocamlyacc.

name: LibYAML
baseline: yaml-cpp
one_liner: Portable C89 YAML 1.1 parser/emitter (the engine under PyYAML's C loaders); about 6-7x yaml-cpp's YAML::Load throughput.

name: toywasm
baseline: Wasmtime and Wasmer (Cranelift) startup
one_liner: Portable C11 in-place WebAssembly interpreter with eager validation; instantiates modules about 90x faster than single-threaded Wasmtime/Wasmer Cranelift.

name: Perforator
license: Apache-2.0 (eBPF unwinder and JVM parts GPL-2.0)
baseline: perf record (sampling profiler)
one_liner: Yandex's eBPF continuous CPU profiler that unwinds frame-pointer-less native stacks in-kernel; a perf record alternative, no measured win.

name: YaFF (Yet another Flat Format)
baseline: Protobuf
one_liner: Zero-copy wire format for existing .proto schemas. In-place field reads beat Protobuf parse-then-read ~25-50x and FlatBuffers ~2x.

name: arena-allocator (yaroslavaristov)
baseline: malloc/free (system C allocator; the benchmark calls malloc/free directly, not operator new/delete)
one_liner: Bump-pointer mmap arena for single-threaded HFT hot paths; O(1) allocate/reset, 10x-27x faster than malloc/free.

name: ACEAPEX
baseline: zstd (zstd -3); also zlib in lzbench
one_liner: Block-independent LZ77 with zstd-coded token streams; decodes in parallel on CPU/GPU and supports random-access reads, aimed at genomic archives.

name: zpoline (x86-64 system call hook by binary rewriting)
baseline: ptrace-based system call interception (README headline); Intel Pin System Call API (reviewer Q&A in Documentation/README.md)
one_liner: LD_PRELOAD library that rewrites every x86-64 syscall instruction into callq *%rax, hooking system calls in-process instead of via ptrace.

name: libevhtp
baseline: Boost.Beast
one_liner: Archived C HTTP/1.1 server library on libevent; about 1.15x Boost.Beast's async example on one plaintext wrk test.

name: Yew
baseline: React 19.2 hooks (react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed, JavaScript in Chrome/V8) in krausest/js-framework-benchmark; also compared with vanilla JavaScript
one_liner: React-style Rust/Wasm component framework whose keyed reconciler beats React 19 on row swaps; overall it ties React and trails vanilla JS.

name: PDFOxide (pdf_oxide, Rust PDF text extraction)
baseline: MuPDF (via PyMuPDF) and PDFium (via pypdfium2), C and C++ PDF engines measured through their Python bindings
one_liner: Rust PDF toolkit (text, Markdown, images, editing) whose README claims 5x PyMuPDF; its own owner's later runs show it slower on real text-bearing PDFs.

name: cpp-httplib
baseline: C++ REST SDK (cpprestsdk) v2.10.15 HTTP server
one_liner: Single-header C++11 HTTP/1.1 client and server; easiest to embed, but not shown faster than C++ REST SDK.

name: LeCo (Learn-to-Compress)
baseline: Frame of Reference (FOR), Delta encoding (fixed and variable partitions), Elias-Fano (thirdparty succinct) and rANS, all built inside the repo; Parquet default encoding and RocksDB default index blocks in the system experiments
one_liner: Research codec (SIGMOD'24): per-block linear regression plus bit-packed residuals for integer columns; better ratio than FOR and Elias-Fano, faster random access than Delta.

name: agensio
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (HttpArena nginx entry with a custom C handler module); HttpArena rows for h2o and Drogon also compared
one_liner: Pre-alpha C++ static-file, FastCGI and reverse-proxy web server on Asio; outpaces nginx on most HttpArena infrastructure rows.

name: xerg (xtreme-grep, Rust parallel grep)
baseline: system grep (implementation and version not stated; the test environment is macOS, so probably BSD grep)
one_liner: Small Rust learning-project grep (xerg) that searches files in parallel with rayon; claims 17.7-33.7x over macOS system grep on a target/ directory.

name: RapidUDF
baseline: native scalar C++ (GCC -O2 for the fib comparison; native loops for the vector cases)
one_liner: LLVM-JIT C-like expression/UDF engine for C++ with SIMD column ops; 6-10x over scalar native loops, scalar code slightly slower than native.

name: Spectra
baseline: ARPACK (ARPACK-NG)
one_liner: Header-only C++/Eigen implicitly restarted Arnoldi/Lanczos eigensolver; ARPACK redesign, modestly faster than ARPACK-NG in the author's dense tests.

name: yklua (Yk JIT retrofitted into PUC Lua)
license: MIT (PUC-Rio Lua notice in src/lua.h and doc/readme.html); no repository-level LICENSE file covering the Yk additions
language: C (Lua interpreter) with the Rust Yk JIT
baseline: PUC-Rio Lua 5.5.0 (stock lua.org tarball, the version yklua is based on) built with -flto as an LTO baseline
one_liner: PUC-Rio Lua 5.5.0 with the yk meta-tracing JIT bolted on; about 1.96x faster than stock Lua 5.5 on a 22-benchmark geomean.

name: funtrace
baseline: LLVM XRay and uftrace function tracers (not perf, gprof or Valgrind)
one_liner: Small flight-recorder function call tracer for C/C++ on x86-64 Linux; author reports 4.5-18x lower per-call cost than XRay and uftrace.

name: cpp-yyjson
baseline: RapidJSON
one_liner: C++20 JSON DOM library: header-only API over a bundled SIMD-patched yyjson fork; reads 1.4-4.6x, writes 2.6-8.1x faster than RapidJSON.

name: flacenc-rs
baseline: FLAC reference encoder: flac 1.4.3 command-line tool (-f -8, -f -8 --lax, -f -5), single-threaded (1.4.3 predates flac's -j threading)
one_liner: Pure-Rust embeddable FLAC encoder library and CLI; its multithreaded mode outruns single-threaded flac 1.4.3 at near -8 compression.

name: zapcc
baseline: GCC, Clang
one_liner: zapcc: a Clang fork with a persistent caching server that rebuilds template-heavy C++ 1.2-3.3x faster than GCC/Clang.

name: ROCCA-S
baseline: OpenSSL AES-128-GCM
one_liner: KDDI's reference C code for Rocca-S, a 256-bit-key AES-round AEAD; ~1.9-2.9x OpenSSL AES-128-GCM encryption throughput.

name: YugabyteDB
license: Apache-2.0 (core database: src/, java/, python/ and build tooling) AND LicenseRef-PolyForm-Free-Trial-1.0.0 (YugabyteDB Anywhere: managed/, troubleshoot/)
baseline: Apache Cassandra 3.11.1 (YCQL API against CQL, YCSB); not the assigned single-node PostgreSQL
one_liner: Distributed SQL database (PostgreSQL-compatible YSQL plus Cassandra-style YCQL) over a C++ Raft/RocksDB store; not faster than single-node PostgreSQL.

name: GopherLua
baseline: CPython 3.4.3 (also C Lua 5.1.4, go-lua, otto, anko)
one_liner: Pure-Go Lua 5.1 VM for embedding in Go programs; about Python-3.4 speed in 2016, now behind CPython.

name: rushdown (Rust CommonMark parser)
baseline: cmark (C reference CommonMark implementation, master built with its own Makefile)
one_liner: AST-based, extensible Rust CommonMark/GFM parser and HTML renderer, 9-14% faster than cmark on one 198 KB fixture.

name: wa-ulid
language: Rust compiled to WebAssembly (Cargo.toml in repo) with a TypeScript wrapper
baseline: ulid 2.x (ulid/javascript, the reference pure-JavaScript ULID generator; devDependency ^2.3.0)
one_liner: Rust-to-WebAssembly ULID generator with the ulid npm API; about 43x faster ulid() than ulid 2.3.0 in Node.

name: wasm-and-ffi-performance-comparison-in-node (Rust WASM Collatz)
baseline: JavaScript Number-based Collatz loop in Node (V8), and the same Rust function built as a native cdylib (cargo build --release, no LTO) called through ffi-napi 4.0.3
one_liner: One-commit Node benchmark: a Rust Collatz loop compiled to wasm runs 45.6x faster than a naive JS loop and 6.5x faster than an ffi-napi call.

name: rlsf
baseline: dlmalloc (also buddy-alloc, umm_malloc, wee_alloc)
one_liner: Rust no_std TLSF allocator with constant-time alloc/free; lower latency and far smaller code than dlmalloc on microcontrollers and wasm.

name: libgo
baseline: libco (Tencent), Linux ucontext
one_liner: Go-style stackful coroutine runtime for C++11 with multi-thread scheduler and syscall hooks; switches faster than libco and ucontext.

name: Optimizing DGEMM on Intel CPUs with AVX512F
baseline: Intel oneMKL DGEMM
one_liner: Step-by-step AVX-512 DGEMM tutorial whose final kernel roughly matches single-threaded Intel MKL on large square matrices.

name: ugrapheme
baseline: ICU's character BreakIterator called through PyICU (the Python binding to ICU's C++ library), driven by a Python generator; also pyuegc, uniseg and grapheme (the other Python grapheme splitters)
one_liner: Cython UAX #29 grapheme splitter for CPython; about 8x faster than ICU's BreakIterator driven through PyICU on a short string.

name: uwcwidth
baseline: jquast/wcwidth, the standard Python terminal-width package, which was pure Python when measured (most likely 0.2.13, the only wcwidth release between January 2024 and September 2025 per PyPI); cwcwidth, a Cython binding to the C library's wcwidth/wcswidth, was also measured; neither version is stated
one_liner: Cython wcwidth/wcswidth for Python with Unicode 16 emoji rules; beats pure-Python wcwidth 0.2.13 by 18-42x on short strings.

name: z88dk (Z80 development kit: C compilers, z80asm assembler and assembly libraries)
license: Clarified Artistic License (SPDX ClArtistic: FSF-libre and GPL-compatible but not OSI-approved per the SPDX license list), 'unless otherwise stated in the appropriate file'
baseline: SDCC 4.6.0 (also HI-TECH C 3.09 and 7.80 and IAR Z80 V4.06A in the same tables)
one_liner: Z80/8080-family C toolchain (sccz80, zsdcc, z80asm) whose assembly C and maths libraries run 1.1-5.4x fewer cycles than stock SDCC 4.6.0.

name: noodles (noodles-fasta FAI indexer)
baseline: samtools faidx (samtools 1.24 with HTSlib 1.24, C)
one_liner: Rust bioinformatics format libraries; noodles-fasta builds samtools-compatible .fai indexes about 6x faster than samtools faidx.

name: BaM (Big accelerator Memory)
baseline: CPU-orchestrated GPU storage access (cudaMemcpy over POSIX I/O / GPUDirect Storage)
one_liner: CUDA library and kernel driver that let GPU threads issue NVMe reads and writes themselves, bypassing CPU-orchestrated storage paths.

name: rapid-qoi
baseline: Two different QOI implementations, both already listed, and neither the category baseline: the README 'qoi' row is the phoboslab/qoi reference C implementation run through its own qoibench.c with --nopng (benches/m1/reference.md and benches/intel-msvc/reference.md carry qoibench.c's exact output format, with the 'rate' column and 'Grand total' line), measured in a separate run from the rapid_qoi row; the repo's Rust harness bench/src/main.rs compares rapid_qoi against the qoi crate 0.4 (aldanor/qoi-rust). Not libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp or libavif.
one_liner: Safe no_std Rust QOI encoder/decoder; decodes about 6% faster than the qoi crate but encodes about 14% slower.

name: zanazakaryaie/fastGaussianBlur (step-by-step optimised Gaussian blur)
baseline: OpenCV cv::GaussianBlur
one_liner: Unlicensed three-step tutorial for a fixed 5x5 float Gaussian blur; it beats OpenCV only on a Raspberry Pi 3B+, and only when using 4 threads.

name: iswasmfast
language: C++ compiled to WebAssembly and to an N-API addon, JavaScript harness
baseline: Pure JavaScript implementation (labelled 'Native' in the README) and the same C++ code built as a Node.js N-API addon
one_liner: Node.js demo that times five toy kernels as plain JS, a C++ N-API addon and C++ compiled to WebAssembly; WASM wins 2 of 5.

name: prometeo
language: Python (transpiler that emits C calling BLASFEO)
baseline: CPython 3.7 (also compared with Nuitka and PyPy)
one_liner: Typed-Python-subset DSL transpiled to self-contained C on BLASFEO; beats CPython, Nuitka and PyPy on a Fibonacci loop.

name: fast-hex (zbjornson)
baseline: hex (scalar hex string encode/decode)
one_liner: AVX2 hex encoder/decoder for C++ and Node.js, self-reported ~11-12x faster than its own scalar lookup-table codec.

name: zeebo/blake3 (Go BLAKE3 with avo-generated AVX-512, AVX2, SSE4.1, NEON assembly)
baseline: The same library built without its assembly (pure Go, compiled by the Go toolchain), plus the upstream Rust blake3 crate (single-threaded) shown in charts
one_liner: Go BLAKE3 with avo-generated AVX-512, AVX2, SSE4.1, NEON and SVE2 kernels; 6-8x its own pure-Go path on large inputs.

name: zeebo/xxh3 (Go XXH3 with assembly)
baseline: xxHash XXH3 (C reference implementation by Cyan4973), not benchmarked in the repository
one_liner: Go port of XXH3 64/128-bit hashing with avo-generated SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON accumulators; no measured win over C xxHash.

name: Spicy
baseline: binpac (Zeek's earlier protocol parser generator); not hand-written parsers
one_liner: Grammar-to-C++ parser generator for network protocols and file formats; Zeek's binpac successor, but slower than binpac on most microbenchmarks.

name: caprese
baseline: actix-web
one_liner: Nim HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket server with built-in TLS; about 30% more req/s than actix-web on an empty GET /.

name: chumsky
baseline: nom
one_liner: Rust parser-combinator library beating nom on JSON throughput, with error recovery and zero-copy output.

name: meshoptimizer (vertex codec used as a lossless float-image compressor)
baseline: OpenEXR 3.4.0 ZIP compression at level 4 (deflate through OpenEXR's bundled libdeflate, OPENEXR_FORCE_INTERNAL_DEFLATE ON); the same harness also runs EXR RLE, PIZ, HTJ2K_32/HTJ2K_256 (OpenJPH inside OpenEXR) and libjxl lossless at efforts 1/3/4/7/8. No standalone zstd, fpzip or zfp baseline in this harness.
one_liner: Mesh library whose lossless vertex codec, misused on float pixels, beat OpenEXR ZIP: 1.4x encode, 3.1x decode, 7% smaller.

name: pugixml
baseline: libxml2
one_liner: In-place, allocation-light C++ XML DOM parser with XPath 1.0, beating libxml2 on parse throughput.

name: ptar
baseline: GNU tar
one_liner: Go CLI that archives a directory tree into N independent tar files in parallel, much faster than GNU tar on parallel filesystems.

name: libuhttpd
baseline: nginx
one_liner: Small embeddable C HTTP/1.1 server library on libev for embedded Linux; one first-party wrk run shows 1.74x nginx req/s.

name: PipeYAML
baseline: yaml-cpp
one_liner: C++17 YAML parser/emitter with a yaml-cpp-style API; author reports ~10x faster Load, ~5x faster Dump on sub-1 KB configs.

name: sljit
baseline: PostgreSQL LLVM JIT (llvmjit) in the pg_jitter shootout
one_liner: Portable low-level C JIT assembler; as pg_jitter's PostgreSQL backend it compiles queries in microseconds, not LLVM's tens of milliseconds.

name: ZhiLight
baseline: vLLM and SGLang (versions not stated)
one_liner: Zhihu/ModelBest C++/CUDA LLM serving engine tuned for PCIe multi-GPU boxes; cut TTFT versus vLLM and SGLang on 4x AD102.

name: zig-js
baseline: JavaScriptCore (system framework on macOS, public C embedding API)
one_liner: JavaScript engine in Zig with a JavaScriptCore-shaped C API; ten small kernels run 2.3x faster than system JSC, which probably had its JIT off.

name: s2s (ziglibs)
baseline: Protocol Buffers (Arwalk/zig-protobuf 5.0.0, generated from the suite's shared benchmark_v2.proto); MessagePack (serde.zig 1.2.1 backend) also compared
one_liner: Single-file Zig binary serializer driven by comptime type reflection; 1.1-2x faster round trips than zig-protobuf in one benchmark.

name: Woodpecker
license: Apache-2.0 (server/ directory dual-licensed AGPL-3.0-only OR SSPL-1.0)
baseline: Apache Kafka
one_liner: Go WAL library storing append-only logs on S3/object storage or local disk; vendor test shows 3.5-5.8x Kafka single-stream write throughput

name: ZipNN (Huffman-based lossless compression of AI model weights)
baseline: Zstandard (ZSTD v1.5.6, as written 'ZSTD v1.56' in the README table)
one_liner: Lossless compressor for floating-point model weights; byte grouping plus Huffman beats plain zstd on bfloat16 speed and ratio.

name: Cynosure RingBuf (async-native SPSC ring buffer, Rust)
license: MIT (declared in Cargo.toml and the README; the repository has no LICENSE file)
baseline: rigtorp::SPSCQueue (C++ single-producer single-consumer ring buffer). The same table also holds a hand-rolled C11 cached-index ring, which is faster than Cynosure.
one_liner: Rust lock-free SPSC ring with built-in async push/pop; 1.29 vs 2.46 ns push+pop against rigtorp::SPSCQueue on Apple M4 Max.

name: cuniq (Rust unique-line counter)
baseline: GNU coreutils 8.32 `sort -u | wc -l` and `sort | uniq -c`, and GNU awk 5.3.2 (`a[$0]++`), all C programs.
one_liner: Rust CLI that counts distinct lines (or per-line occurrences) with a hash table instead of GNU sort -u / sort | uniq -c.

name: zlib-ng
baseline: zlib (including its CRC32/Adler32 checksum routines)
one_liner: Maintained zlib fork with SIMD deflate, inflate and CRC32/Adler32; about 2.2-2.5x faster compression and 1.5x faster decompression than zlib.

name: jsmn
baseline: nlohmann/json
one_liner: C89 zero-allocation JSON tokenizer; beat nlohmann/json on 8 of 14 benchmark files but trails RapidJSON.

name: zuu_string_view
baseline: std::string_view
one_liner: Header-only C++11 SWAR-accelerated string_view alternative; faster find/rfind/find_first_of than std::string_view, slower on not_of scans.

name: cmph / cxxmph (mph_map)
baseline: std::unordered_map (cxxmph's dense_hash_map / sparse_hash_map are its own flavors named after the sparsehash classes; cxxmph/bm_map.cc benchmarks only against std::unordered_map)
one_liner: C minimal-perfect-hash library (BDZ/CHD/BRZ) plus cxxmph::mph_map, claimed 10-50% faster than std::unordered_map on >100k URLs.

name: zwasm
baseline: wasmtime 43.0.1; wasmer 5.0.4; wazero 1.11.0; WasmEdge 0.16.1 (interpreter)
one_liner: Zig WebAssembly runtime (interpreter, single-pass JIT, AOT) that starts short WASI guests 2.2-3.6x faster than wasmtime, with less memory.

name: faster-utf8-validator
baseline: fastvalidate-utf-8 AVX2 validators (validate_utf8_fast_avx and validate_utf8_fast_avx_asciipath)
one_liner: Single-file AVX2/SSE4 UTF-8 validator in C; about 1.5-1.7x faster than fastvalidate-utf-8 AVX2 on random UTF-8.

name: DPTree (Differential Indexing for Persistent Memory)
baseline: FAST+FAIR (also FPTree, WORT)
one_liner: Research persistent-memory index that buffers writes in DRAM; up to 1.82x faster point lookups than FAST+FAIR on Optane.

name: Enchantum
baseline: magic_enum (compile-time enum reflection to string); simple_enum and conjure_enum also compared
one_liner: Header-only C++17 enum reflection (to_string, cast, iteration, bitflags); author-measured builds up to 6.4x faster than magic_enum with default settings.

name: Zydis

baseline: virtual member function call through a base-class pointer
one_liner: Book example: CRTP base-class call versus a virtual call through a base pointer; about 5.8x per 32-call loop.

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: type-erased ScopeGuard with a fixed inline buffer (chapter 11)
baseline: ScopeGuard holding its cleanup in a std::function<void()>
one_liner: Book example: type-erased scope guard with a 16-byte inline buffer, under 1 ns faster than a std::function guard.

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: local-buffer type-erased Function
baseline: std::function<int(int,int,int,int)>
one_liner: About 60-line std::function-style wrapper for trivially copyable callables of up to 16 bytes; the book reports cheaper calls than std::function.

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: type-erased smart pointer with local-buffer deleter (smartptr_te_static / smartptr_te_vtable)
baseline: std::shared_ptr<int> with a custom deleter (and std::make_shared<int>)
