name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: small_queue, a fixed-capacity circular-buffer queue with local storage
baseline: std::queue<int>
one_liner: A 20-line fixed-capacity ring-buffer int queue stored inside the object, benchmarked against std::queue<int> (std::deque); buggy as published.

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: template ScopeGuard instead of a std::function-based guard (chapter 11)
baseline: ScopeGuard holding its cleanup in a std::function<void()> (the book's type-erased guard)
one_liner: Book example: a scope guard templated on its cleanup lambda, removing std::function type erasure and its per-guard overhead.

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: virtual function call instead of dynamic_cast (chapter 1)
baseline: dynamic_cast<Derived*> on a base-class pointer (type test to select behaviour)
one_liner: Teaching idiom: replace a dynamic_cast type test with a virtual member call; book example code, not a library.

name: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook 3rd ed.: parallel map and fold with std::async tasks
baseline: Sequential std::transform and std::accumulate (the std::thread version is a second reference)
one_liner: Cookbook recipe: chunked parallel map and fold with std::async tasks, beating sequential std::transform and std::accumulate on large vectors.

name: Modern C++ Programming Cookbook 3rd ed.: parallel map and fold with std::thread
baseline: Sequential std::transform and std::accumulate
one_liner: Book recipe running std::transform and std::accumulate on one std::thread per hardware thread; about 2.2x at 50M ints.

name: Qt 6 C++ GUI Programming Cookbook 3rd ed.: raw heap array instead of std::vector and QVector
baseline: std::vector<int> filled with push_back (no reserve) and summed with at()
one_liner: Book sample timing a presized new int[] against std::vector and QVector filled by push_back without reserve, read with at().

name: Rust-for-CPP-Developers: matrix_multiply_indexing_opt (accumulator hoisted into a local sum)
baseline: naive nested-loop matrix multiply with in-place accumulation (out[i][j] += a[i][k]*b[k][j]), same language (the repo's matrix_multiply_original)

name: Rust-for-CPP-Developers: matrix_multiply_simd (std::simd f32x4 inner product)
baseline: same-language scalar unsafe-indexing matrix multiply (the repo's matrix_multiply_unsafe_indexing)
one_liner: Book example: nightly std::simd f32x4 inner product in a naive Vec<Vec<f32>> matrix multiply, book-reported 1.7x over its scalar loop.

name: Rust-for-CPP-Developers: matrix_multiply_unsafe_indexing (get_unchecked bounds-check removal)
baseline: same-language safe indexed matrix multiply with the hoisted accumulator (the repo's matrix_multiply_indexing_opt)
one_liner: Book example: naive Rust f32 matrix multiply that swaps safe indexing for get_unchecked, about 1.5x over the safe loop (book figure).

name: Software Architecture with C++ 2E: binary search (std::ranges::lower_bound) versus linear scan (std::ranges::find) in a sorted vector
baseline: std::ranges::find (linear scan) on a sorted std::vector<int>
one_liner: Book benchmark: std::ranges::lower_bound beats std::ranges::find on a sorted vector<int>, O(log n) against a linear scan.

name: Software Architecture with C++ 2E: computed-goto bytecode dispatch versus a single switch
baseline: switch-based bytecode interpreter loop (single large switch in a while loop, same repo)
one_liner: Book sample: computed-goto (labels-as-values) dispatch for a toy 7-opcode VM, reported about 1.29x faster than a switch loop.

name: Software Architecture with C++ 2E: tail-recursive Fibonacci with musttail versus naive recursion
baseline: naive double-recursive Fibonacci (same repo; also iterative Fibonacci as a second reference)
one_liner: Book microbenchmark of musttail tail recursion against loops and plain recursion; shows parity, no speedup from musttail.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: std::atomic counter increment instead of a mutex-guarded counter
baseline: std::mutex with std::lock_guard around ++x
one_liner: std::atomic fetch_add on a shared counter in place of a std::mutex-guarded ++x; a book idiom, not a library.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: cache-line padding of per-thread partial sums
baseline: Per-thread counters stored adjacent in a plain unsigned long array (false sharing)
one_liner: Per-thread counters spaced 128 bytes apart instead of in adjacent array slots, removing false sharing; book demo, not a library.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: preallocate-once buffer instead of new[] and delete[] every iteration
baseline: Per-iteration new char[N] / delete[] (system operator new)
one_liner: Book sample: allocate a scratch buffer once at its maximum size instead of new[]/delete[] on every loop iteration.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: publishing pointer (ts_unique_ptr) instead of an atomic std::shared_ptr
baseline: std::shared_ptr accessed through std::atomic_load_explicit and std::atomic_store_explicit
one_liner: Book sample: single-writer publishing pointer over std::atomic<T*> versus atomic_load/atomic_store on a std::shared_ptr; never frees replaced objects.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: signed int loop index in substring comparison
baseline: std::sort with a hand-written substring comparison that uses an unsigned int index (bounded and unbounded variants)
one_liner: Book idiom: signed int index in a hand-written string-compare loop beats unsigned-index versions inside a std::sort benchmark.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: spinlock-guarded thread-safe stack
baseline: std::stack guarded by std::mutex (mt_stack1)
one_liner: Book example: std::stack behind a test-and-test-and-set spinlock, about 2.3x the single-thread push/pop rate of a std::mutex-guarded stack.

name: The Art of Writing Efficient Programs: contiguous std::vector instead of std::list for sequential traversal
baseline: std::list<unsigned long>
one_liner: Book benchmark: traverse a contiguous std::vector instead of a node-based std::list; about 8x faster sequential reads.

name: Cache-blocked double-precision matrix multiply with tile accumulator (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 4)
baseline: naive i-j-k triple-loop dgemm (dgemm_basic in the same repo, no blocking); OpenBLAS cblas_dgemm is measured as a reference and is far faster than the blocked code

name: Clamp loop with conditional store instead of std::min (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 4)
baseline: std::min-based clamp loop (ct::clamp_min, branch-free/cmov form), same function with auto-vectorisation disabled on both sides
one_liner: Book micro-idiom: an if-guarded store clamp loop beats a std::min (cmov) clamp loop by about 1.2x, vectorisation off.

name: Hash maps versus ordered maps, random-access lookup (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 5, Table 5.1)
baseline: std::map
one_liner: Book benchmark: hash maps find random int64 keys 6-9x faster than std::map and other ordered maps at 256-1,024 keys.

name: OpenMP parallel all-pairs nearest-neighbor distance (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 4)
baseline: sequential nested-loop version of the same all-pairs minimum-distance computation (nearest_neighbor_distance_seq, one thread)
one_liner: Book sample: one OpenMP 'parallel for' min-reduction pragma on an O(n^2) closest-pair loop, about 4x over one thread.

name: SAXPY function multiversioning with per-ISA builds and CPUID dispatch (The C++ Programmer's Mindset, ch. 4)
baseline: default-target build of the same scalar saxpy loop (saxpy_default, x86-64 SSE2 baseline, no runtime dispatch); OpenBLAS cblas_saxpy measured as a reference
one_liner: Book sample: one scalar saxpy loop compiled per ISA (SSE4.2, AVX2, AVX-512F) with CPUID dispatch; 1.27-1.35x over default build.

name: BVLSM
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Research RocksDB variant that splits big values out at WAL-write time. Paper reports 7.6x RocksDB random-write throughput at 64KB.

baseline: header-based includes (#include); whether precompiled headers were in the baseline is not confirmed
one_liner: Field report: moving Alibaba's Hologres code base from #include headers to C++20 named modules cut its compile time 42%.

name: dups (c-blake/bu, Nim duplicate-file finder)
baseline: jdupes (C)
one_liner: Nim exact-duplicate file finder; claimed ~2x over jdupes when RAM-cached, though the author's 2019 timing favored jdupes by 7%.

name: mk1 (c-blake/bu, Nim up-to-date check for 1-to-1 build rules)
baseline: ninja (C++) and GNU make (C); the table also times a bash while-read loop
one_liner: Nim freshness checker for 1-input-1-output rules; ~3x ninja's no-op check and ~40x GNU make on 40k pairs.

name: Cascaded Learned Bloom Filter (CLBF)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Learned Bloom filter: pruned boosted-tree cascade plus Bloom filters; less memory than Bloom/PLBF, faster rejects than PLBF.

name: Code Generation of Faster Formally Verified NTT with Plantard Reduction
baseline: NIST PQC / pq-crystals reference C implementations of ML-KEM (Kyber ref) and ML-DSA (Dilithium ref) for end-to-end and NTT results, plus formosa-mlkem Jasmin (NTT only); mlkem-native/mldsa-native scalar C (OPT=0 AUTO=0) is compared only at NTT level

name: CompassDB
benchmark_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18099 (arXiv v1 preprint, 26 Jun 2024; no journal reference listed)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: Paper-only RocksDB-derived KV engine that replaces SST indexes with in-memory two-tier perfect hashing; reports 2.5-4x RocksDB YCSB point-op throughput.

name: Cuckoo Filter (efficient/cuckoofilter)
baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: Reference C++ cuckoo filter from the CoNEXT'14 authors: a Bloom-filter replacement that supports deletes and does faster positive lookups.

name: DigitsOnTurbo (DoT)
baseline: GMP 6.3.0 (also OpenSSL 3.5.2 bignum)
one_liner: Research SIMD (AVX-512/IFMA) kernels for bignum add/sub and base-case multiply, patched into GMP and OpenSSL.

name: EASTL hash_map / hash_set (eastl::hash_map)
baseline: std::unordered_map (directly in Ankerl's map_benchmark, Linux build); EASTL's own tables used the pre-standard stdext::hash_map of VC++ 7.1 (Dinkumware) and STLport's hash_map, and N2271 used GCC 4.1 libstdc++
one_liner: EA's chained hash table (eastl::hash_map/hash_set), about 1.3x faster than libstdc++ std::unordered_map in Ankerl's 2019 suite.

name: EASTL sort algorithms (eastl::sort / quick_sort, eastl::radix_sort)
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: EA's introsort (eastl::sort) plus an LSD radix_sort; beat the VC++ 7.1 Dinkumware std::sort 1.7-1.9x on random 10k arrays.

name: EASTL string (eastl::basic_string / eastl::string, eastl::fixed_string)
baseline: std::string
one_liner: EA's non-COW, SSO basic_string and inline-buffer fixed_string; beat the VC++ 7.1 Dinkumware string on push_back and swap.

name: Exgen-Malloc
baseline: dlmalloc, mimalloc
one_liner: Single-threaded malloc built by stripping mimalloc's thread machinery; paper reports 1.03-1.05x over mimalloc and 1.17-1.19x over dlmalloc on SPEC CPU2017.

name: FlashAttention-4 (CuTeDSL, Hopper/Blackwell)
baseline: cuDNN 9.13.0 fused attention (also benchmarked: cuDNN 9.19.1.2, Triton 3.6.0, Gluon 3.6.0, FlashAttention 2.8.3)
one_liner: Blackwell/Hopper exact attention kernels in CuTe-DSL; beat cuDNN 9.13 by 1.04-1.29x on B200, roughly tie cuDNN 9.19.

name: FreeBSD libmd md5block.S (amd64 baseline, BMI1 and AVX-512 MD5 kernels)
baseline: libmd's C MD5 block function: the 'orig' build (previous md5c.c) and the new 'generic' C build measured in the same review

name: FT-BLAS

one_liner: Research double-precision BLAS for AVX-512 Intel CPUs with built-in soft-error checks; paper reports small wins over OpenBLAS, BLIS, MKL.

one_liner: Parallel Rust cp for Linux directory trees; about 3.4-4.8x faster than GNU cp -r on nested small-file trees.

name: rmz (FUC, Rust multi-threaded rm)
baseline: GNU rm -r (coreutils, C); the same table also lists find -delete and rsync --delete

name: GL-Cache

baseline: OpenBLAS, Apple Accelerate, LIBXSMM, KleidiAI

baseline: MessagePack

one_liner: Lean-verified peephole optimizer for Skia command streams; 1.12x geomean raster speedup over Skia Graphite on Chrome-generated pictures.

name: Mycelium (TE-LSM)
baseline: RocksDB
one_liner: RocksDB fork that splits columns, re-encodes values or builds secondary indexes during compaction, for faster analytic reads than RocksDB.

name: NV_path_rendering (NVpr)
language: C (OpenGL extension in the NVIDIA driver)
baseline: Cairo 1.9.6, Skia (circa May 2010, CPU raster backend), Qt 4.5.x, Direct2D and the OpenVG 1.1 reference implementation (the nvpr_svg comparison backends in the NVprSDK)

name: fast-noble-hashes (@r1ck404/fast-noble-hashes)
language: WebAssembly (SHA-2, SHA-1, MD5, PBKDF2 loop, scrypt ROMix) with JavaScript, drop-in for @noble/hashes
baseline: @noble/hashes 1.8.0 (pure JavaScript)
one_liner: @noble/hashes 1.8.0 drop-in with SHA-2, SHA-1, MD5, PBKDF2 and scrypt in WebAssembly; 1.7-7.8x faster than noble's JS.

language: Rust compiled to WebAssembly (zlib port) with JavaScript wrapper
baseline: pako 2.1.0 (pure JavaScript zlib port)

name: Rewrite it in Rust: A Computational Physics Case Study (Veytsman, Zhai, Ding, Sefkow)

name: Romu (RomuTrio/RomuQuad/RomuMono)

one_liner: Pure safe-Rust WebP codec (image-webp fork): lossless encode 1.6-2.8x faster than libwebp m4, decode faster than FFmpeg.

baseline: LRU

baseline: Bloom filter
one_liner: AVX2 split-block Bloom filter: one 32-byte block per key, about 2-3x faster queries than a standard Bloom filter.

baseline: OpenSSL SHA-256 (v1.0.1)
one_liner: Multi-buffer SHA-256 that hashes 4 independent messages per AVX register with standard digests; 3.42x OpenSSL 1.0.1 on 4KB messages.

name: SNOW-V-GCM
baseline: OpenSSL AES-256-GCM
one_liner: SNOW-V stream cipher plus GHASH AEAD; ~13% faster than OpenSSL AES-256-GCM at 16 KB on an i7-8650U laptop.

name: SpeedMalloc
baseline: mimalloc, jemalloc, TCMalloc
one_liner: Hardware proposal: a small in-order support core runs malloc/free for all cores; simulated 1.15x over mimalloc and 1.75x over jemalloc at 16 threads.

name: Squares counter-based RNG
baseline: Philox 4x32-10 (Random123 counter-based RNG)
one_liner: Stateless counter-based RNG built from 4-5 rounds of middle-square squaring; author reports ~1.7x Philox4x32-10 throughput.

name: StreamTok (Static Analysis for Efficient Streaming Tokenization)
baseline: flex
one_liner: Rust streaming tokenizer using static max-lookahead analysis for O(1)-per-symbol maximal-munch tokenization vs flex's backtracking

name: SynapServe
baseline: httparse
one_liner: Closed-source zero-allocation Rust HTTP/1.1 parser inside the SynapServe io_uring server; claims 1.11-1.25x faster tokenization than httparse.

name: Task-based nested multithreaded CHOLMOD for A64FX (OmpSs)
baseline: CHOLMOD with multi-threaded BLAS
one_liner: Research OmpSs/OpenMP-task parallelization of CHOLMOD's supernodal Cholesky with selective nesting; 1.95x over multi-threaded-BLAS CHOLMOD on A64FX.

name: Tiaoxin-346
baseline: AES-256-GCM
one_liner: Tiaoxin-346, an AES-round AEAD with 3 AES rounds per 16 bytes in AES-NI C; 1.8-5.6x faster than SUPERCOP's AES-256-GCM, unmaintained.

name: Umbra
benchmark_url: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickBench/blob/main/umbra/results/20260918/c6a.4xlarge.json (baselines in the same repo: clickhouse/results/20260926/c6a.4xlarge.json and duckdb/results/20260511/c6a.4xlarge.json)
baseline: ClickHouse
one_liner: Closed-source TU Munich research SQL database (HyPer successor) that runs ClickBench about 2.4x faster than ClickHouse on one node.

name: WojciechMula/toys avx512-string (AVX512F strlen, strchr, strrchr, strcmp)
baseline: libc strlen/strchr/strrchr/strcmp via <cstring> (labelled 'std' in the harness; libc version not stated)
one_liner: 2016 AVX512F SWAR versions of strlen, strchr, strrchr and strcmp; 4-16x over a 2016 glibc on Knights Landing.

name: toys strstr (SWAR SIMD-friendly Rabin-Karp substring search)
baseline: std::string::find (strstr-stdstring.cpp) and libc strstr (strstr-libc.cpp), both included in the harness; library implementation not stated
one_liner: 2014-2016 prototype of Mula's first/last-byte SWAR substring filter, claimed 2-3x over std::string::find; buggy, superseded by sse4-strstr.

name: fastcpp::phf (developer source)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Compile-time perfect hash table for fixed string-key sets (keywords, opcodes); 5.8-7x faster lookups than std::unordered_map.

name: fastcpp::arena (developer source)
baseline: new/delete
one_liner: Header-only bump/arena allocator for same-lifetime objects; 5.4x faster than glibc new/delete when a whole batch is freed at once.

name: fastcpp::flat_hash_map (developer source)
baseline: std::unordered_map
one_liner: Header-only SwissTable-style hash map: 1.8-5.5x faster than std::unordered_map on 1M uint64 keys, but slower than phmap on lookups.

name: fastcpp::io::buffered_writer (developer source)
baseline: unbuffered write(2) per call (about two write(2) calls per line)
one_liner: Header-only C++ output buffer that coalesces small writes into 64 KiB flushes instead of issuing write(2) per call.

name: fastcpp::str::parse_u64 / u64_to_chars (developer source)
baseline: strtoull (parse_u64), snprintf (u64_to_chars)
one_liner: Header-only uint64 decimal parse (SWAR) and format (two-digit table): ~3x strtoull/snprintf, 1.5x from_chars, 1.2x to_chars.

name: fastcpp::algo::lower_bound (branchless / Eytzinger) (developer source)
baseline: std::lower_bound
one_liner: Three header-only lower_bound variants (branchless cmov, cmov+prefetch, Eytzinger layout); 5.8x std::lower_bound in L1, 1.9x from DRAM on ints.

name: fastcpp::small_vector (developer source)
baseline: std::vector
one_liner: C++ vector with N inline slots (default 8). It skips std::vector's heap allocation while the vector stays small.

name: fastcpp::algo::sort / radix_sort (developer source)
baseline: std::sort
one_liner: Header-only pdqsort-style quicksort and LSD radix sort; 2.3x libstdc++ std::sort on random int64, 6.6x sorted, loses nearly-sorted.
